title: Commanders CB Amik Robertson to miss second straight game
summary: The Commanders got a win over the Bengals without cornerback Amik Robertson and they'll try to do it again when they face the Cardinals on Sunday.
full_text: ' The Commanders got a win over the Bengals without cornerback Amik Robertson and they'll try to do it again when they face the Cardinals on Sunday. Robertson remained out of practice this week with an ankle injury and head coach Dan Quinn told reporters on Friday that he will not travel with the team to Arizona. Quinn said the team does not have any long-term concerns about Robertson's injury at this point. Robertson has 53 tackles, a forced fumble and 10 passes defensed in nine games this season. The Commanders will release a full injury report later in the day, but Robertson is the only player who has missed practice this week.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bears call Colston Loveland week-to-week with a knee injury
summary: Bears tight end Colston Loveland went for tests on his injured knee after leaving Thursday's game in the first quarter and the team updated his condition on Friday.
full_text: '' Bears tight end Colston Loveland went for tests on his injured knee after leaving Thursday's game in the first quarter and the team updated his condition on Friday. The Bears say that Loveland is considered week-to-week as the team heads toward a Week 13 game against the Jaguars. They did not comment on the specific nature of Loveland's injury. There was also no mention of injured reserve, which is a positive given reports earlier in the day that indicated Loveland was going to go on the list. Loveland has 41 catches for 397 yards and three touchdowns. With Cole Kmet on injured reserve, the healthy Bears tight ends are Sam Roush and Stephen Carlson.
author: Josh Alper

title: Aaron Rodgers got no support from the Thanksgiving broadcasts
summary: The day after former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers went on TV and aired dirty laundry from the Pittsburgh locker room, none of the former quarterbacks (or other former players) who appear on TV supported him.
full_text: The day after former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers went on TV and aired dirty laundry from the Pittsburgh locker room, none of the former quarterbacks (or other former players) who appear on TV supported him. Across the board, the reaction from the NFL's analysts and broadcasters was negative. Former Steelers quarterback and Fox analyst Terry Bradshaw went off . Fox's Michael Strahan agreed that Rodgers shouldn't have gone public with his complaints — calling him a "narcissist" and a "rich jerk" and a "rich bad teammate." Fox's Howie Long said that the moment "defines who [Rodgers] is." "He's a guy that I think picked the wrong sport," Long said. "He probably should have played tennis." Fox's Rob Gronkowski said that, even if a contender loses its starting quarterback, there's "too much smoke" to justify bringing Rodgers in. The CBS pregame crew offered similar views . Nate Burleson said Rodgers " didn’t handle this right ." Bill Cowher said he hates to see a Hall of Famer go out this way . Russell Wilson said, "It's about Aaron Rodgers's legacy. . . . If I'm his family members, if I'm somebody close to him, I'm his significant other, whatever it may be. ' Is this how you want to go out? ' After all the success he's had, is this how you want to go out? . . . This is a disappointment." During the Eagles-Cowboys game, Fox's Tom Brady criticized Rodgers for violating the " sanctity " of the locker room. The irony, if I'm using the term correctly (I never know), is that Rodgers has previously railed about leaks from the locker room. “I think it’s chickenshit at its core , and I think it has no place in a winning organization," Rodgers said about the Jets. "One thing I really love — and it’s kind of the antithesis of where I was — is there’s not really any leaks in the boat,” Rodgers told reporters during his first year with the Steelers. “Every year, you have difficulties and adversity, both on the field and off the field, and to go through a season like this, and to be able to focus on football and not have a lot of other little bullshit out there has been really nice.” Rodgers didn't leak anything. He said it directly, bluntly, unapologetically. He took the team's focus off of football, at a time when the team was otherwise trying to fight through "difficulties and adversity." Again, he isn't a whistleblower. He's a troublemaker. He didn't get his way, so he set the house on fire as he walked out the front door. As one PFT reader put it, ultimatums and "blackmail" are close cousins. For Rodgers, it wasn't just "let me call the plays or cut me." It was, whether he said it this way or not, "let me call the plays or I'll tell the world all the stuff you don't want the world to know."
author: Mike Florio

title: Falcons rule out WR Jahan Dotson, LG Matthew Bergeron
summary: The Falcons have ruled out a couple of offensive starters for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
full_text: The Falcons have ruled out a couple of offensive starters for Sunday's game against the Vikings. Wide receiver Jahan Dotson (hamstring) and left guard Matthew Bergeron (back) will not play this weekend. The Falcons also ruled out rookie Zachariah Branch with a hamstring injury, so Drake London, Olamide Zaccheaus, Beaux Collins, and Chris Blair are the available wideouts on the 53-man roster. Kyle Hinton is likely to get the start in Bergeron's place. Safety DeMarcco Hellams (foot) will also miss the game with Sydney Brown set to start in his place. Defensive back Billy Bowman (hamstring) is the fifth and final player who was ruled out by the Falcons on Friday.
author: Josh Alper

title: LB Cole Holcomb inactive for the Steelers on Friday
summary: The most notable absence on the Steelers side of the field on Friday afternoon will be Aaron Rodgers, but the team also has players still on their roster who will not be playing against the Broncos.
full_text: '' The most notable absence on the Steelers side of the field on Friday afternoon will be Aaron Rodgers, but the team also has players still on their roster who will not be playing against the Broncos. Linebacker Cole Holcomb was the only player on either team listed as questionable heading into the game and he will sit out with a heel injury. Holcomb has been a core special teamer for Pittsburgh this season. With Rodgers gone, Will Howard moved up to the No. 2 quarterback spot. Drew Allar is inactive as the emergency third quarterback and wide receiver Kaden Wetjen, cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting, running back Eli Heidenreich, linebacker Alex Highsmith, and defensive end Gabe Rubio are also out. The Broncos' inactives are quarterback Sam Ehlinger, wide receiver Lil'Jordan Humphrey, safety Taylor Rapp, offensive lineman Gavin Ortega, offensive lineman Kage Casey, and tight end Dallen Bentley.
author: Josh Alper

title: Denzel Boston listed as questionable after missing Friday's practice
summary: The Browns will be on Sunday Night Football this weekend, but it remains to be seen if rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston will be in their lineup.
full_text: ' The Browns will be on Sunday Night Football this weekend, but it remains to be seen if rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston will be in their lineup. Boston missed his third straight practice on Friday with a quad injury and the team listed him as questionable to face the Raiders. The second-round pick has not missed a game this season and has 33 catches for 523 yards and three touchdowns in 10 contests. Defensive end Derek Barnett (hamstring) also missed practice all week and has been ruled out for this Sunday. Right guard Austin Barber (knee) and running back Raheim Sanders (hip) are listed as questionable. Sanders will need to be activated from injured reserve in order to play against Las Vegas.
author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos, under Bo Nix, are much better at home than on the road
summary: Lost in the ongoing drama in Pittsburgh is that they play the 8-2 Broncos today.
full_text: ' Lost in the ongoing drama in Pittsburgh is that they play the 8-2 Broncos today. Lost in that is that the Broncos, with Bo Nix at quarterback, are a much better team at home than they are on the road. After playing 23 games in Denver, Nix has a 20-3 record with 43 touchdown passes and averaging 242.6 passing yards per game. Playing 23 games elsewhere, the Broncos are 13-10, with Nix throwing 27 touchdowns and averaging 195.9 passing yards per game. The Steelers, in contrast, are 4-0 at home this year and 2-4 on the road. With the forecast for the game similar to the conditions that played out in Buffalo on Thursday night, that could even things out, from a talent standpoint. And it could give the Steelers a chance to rebound from two days of total dysfunction with a season-altering win. However it goes, the pressure is on Steelers coach Mike McCarthy. The best way to turn the page is to win. A loss (particularly an ugly one) will give even more credence to the things Aaron Rodgers said publicly on Wednesday.
author: Mike Florio

title: Christian Barmore questionable for Patriots, Alijah Vera-Tucker will travel to L.A.
summary: Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore was added to the team's injury report on Friday and his status for Sunday's game against the Chargers is uncertain as a result.
full_text: ' Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore was added to the team's injury report on Friday and his status for Sunday's game against the Chargers is uncertain as a result. Head coach Mike Vrabel said that Barmore is dealing with a knee injury and he will be listed as questionable for this weekend. Barmore was not on the field during the open portion of Friday's practice. Guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) has not been activated from injured reserve, but Vrabel said that he will travel with the team to Los Angeles. Vera-Tucker will need to be activated by Saturday afternoon to play on Sunday. Wide receiver Romeo Doubs (shoulder) has also been designated for return. Vrabel indicated he will not play and wide receiver A.J. Brown (hamstring), cornerback Carlton Davis (knee), and quarterback Drake Maye (fibula) have officially been ruled out.
author: Josh Alper

title: Brian Schottenheimer on failed fourth-down try: "I trust our quarterback and our offense"
summary: The Eagles' path to erasing a 31-10 third-quarter deficit included many favorable twists and turns.
full_text: The Eagles' path to erasing a 31-10 third-quarter deficit included many favorable twists and turns. The last one was a gift from the Cowboys. With 55 seconds left — and with the Eagles having no timeouts — the Cowboys faced fourth and one from the Philadelphia 39. After attempting to get the Eagles to jump offside, the Cowboys took a timeout and decided to go for it. The Cowboys lined up in shotgun formation. Quarterback Dak Prescott looked to the right, presumably to connect on a slant to receiver CeeDee Lamb. Lamb was jammed hard by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. Prescott waited for Lamb to get free. When Prescott decided to pursue another option, he was sacked. The play lost nine yards, giving the Eagles the ball at their own 48. Why not punt? Why not force quarterback Joe Milton III to drive into field-goal range, with less than 50 seconds to play and no timeouts? Coach Brian Schottenheimer was asked about the decision after the game. "Really felt good about the drive we had going, and felt really good that we were gonna put the game away there," Schottenheimer told reporters. "And I wanted the ball in Dak's hands. And, unfortunately, we weren't able to make it work." Does Schottenheimer ever second-guess himself? "All the time," he said. "Not in that situation. Absolutely not in that situation." Why not? "I trust our quarterback and our offense," Schottenheimer said. That's fine. But it's not about "trust." It's about whether it makes sense to assume the offense will execute in that moment, and what the consequence will be if the defense executes a little better. It's about making an assessment, based on years of watching, playing, and coaching football, as to whether the risk of not converting outweighed the risk of the Eagles driving from their own 20 (or perhaps deep inside their own 20) into field goal range. Maybe the truth is that Schottenheimer didn't trust his defense to keep that from happening. Regardless, his "trust" in the offense was ultimately misplaced. And the Cowboys lost another game when they scored 30 or more points.
author: Mike Florio

title: Mike Tomlin on current Steelers situation: "It's a dumpster fire"
summary: Former Steelers coach speaks at length about this week's events.
full_text: '' Many folks in and around football have had opinions about the recent brouhaha between former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and Steelers coach Mike McCarthy. Few have the insight and perspective that former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin brings to the table. Appearing on NBC's Chiefs-Bills halftime show on Thanksgiving night, Tomlin shared his thoughts on the situation in a conversation with Mike Tirico. (A portion of it was on the live broadcast; the full interview is here .) "I had a range of emotions watching those course of events yesterday," Tomlin told Tirico. "I think the prevailing one is just general sadness. Sad on a micro level, sad on a macro level. And by that, I mean, you know, just from an individual perspective, sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career of the quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, and just on the macro level, whether it's organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum. "Those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football. So, just a lot of emotions, but probably more than anything, man, general sadness on a lot of levels." Tirico asked Tomlin if he was shocked by Rodgers's decision to air dirty laundry in a public forum. "It certainly did," Tomlin said, "but, you know, and particularly because I know both men involved, certainly had a lot of intimate work and development of relationship with Aaron over the last couple of years, and have known and competed against Mike, you know, respected and appreciated him as a coach for a long time. But I don't — what I acknowledge is I don't know them as a collective, the nature of their relationships, and so certainly I was surprised by that." Regardless of Rodgers's conduct on the way out the door, Tomlin explained that Rodgers was viewed favorably by his teammates in 2025. "He was beloved, and I'm not, you know, over-exaggerating that," Tomlin said. "He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture, to be engaged with teammates, and particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times they lose a little patience for the process, or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, et cetera. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real, natural way. He was a tireless worker regarding the process. "I called early-morning quarterback meetings on Wednesday and Thursday. He was always early and engaged. Did a heck of a job in terms of engaging and developing, assisting in the development of young players. Specifically, Will Howard was always in that meeting, and, shoot, man, [Rodgers] and I were shoulder-to-shoulder in terms of the development of Will and challenging Will to develop professional habits. And so, you know, it was early and extremely consistent during my time with him, in terms of his willingness to work in those areas, and I think that's why he's so beloved in that locker room, as been reported by multiple sources in light of this incident. That is real. The guys in that locker room love and appreciate Aaron Rodgers." Had Tomlin gotten any sense that things were so close to breaking down? "Absolutely none, but it's a really specific reason why, to be honest with you, man," Tomlin said. "One of my cultural mantras, when I worked there for the 19 years, is don't talk to people about your problems unless they can be a component of the solution. Because if you do, it's counterproductive, and people know where I stand there. And by that I mean if you have a problem with your playing time, don't talk to your teammate about it. Talk to somebody that can do something about it. That's problem solving. "And so everybody understands my posture on some of that stuff, and so although I have really good, fluid communication with many of those guys, particularly, the more veteran guys, they know me and know me well enough to know that I didn't want to hear about any potential issues, because I'm not a component of the solution. And so although, particularly, like, Cam Heyward, he and I spent a little time together doing his bye week. Man, we had no mention of anything bubbling under the surface, if you will." Can McCarthy effectively lead the team, given what Rodgers said? "You know, it certainly created some challenges and challenges is probably an understatement if all of those things are true," Tomlin told Tirico. "And certainly the '1-2-3 Packers' is, because he acknowledged that. But his ability to overcome that or inability to overcome that in my opinion is based on relationships and the depth of those relationships and how those guys feel about him, or how those guys buy into what he's selling. And so, certainly, he's been there a short period of time. And so it makes you wonder, the level of that challenge. But it'll be relationship-based, his ability to overcome the things that you mentioned." How does Tomlin think the Steelers will fare against the Broncos on Friday? "Based on my knowledge of the men, particularly the leaders, the longstanding guys, they'll do a great job of getting hyper-focused on what really matters, and that's that football game," Tomlin said. "They'll use it as a mantra to bring them together. I expect those guys to fight. Now, fight and quality play are two different things. I'm certainly not gonna expect those guys not to fight. I think they're gonna fight and fight extremely hard. What I'm interested in is quality of play, quality of execution. And those are things that could be impacted by the level of distraction that they had on a short week in particular." Tirico then asked Tomlin how he feels, overall, about what has transpired this week. "I'm upset about it, you know, it's a dumpster fire," Tomlin said. "And I don't say that in a judgmental way. I presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I'm sure Steeler Nation is upset." If owner Art Rooney II calls Tomlin for advice, what would Tomlin say? "Hey, Mike, that's a hypothetical, because I know he wouldn't and, and because I know how he's trained," Tomlin said. "You know, Art is a guy that's not a hedge fund guy that bought a football team. He's not a, you know, artificial intelligence guy that bought a football team. This is a family business. It's generational. Any advice or thought process in that way, I imagine he just says, 'What would my dad do?' Or, 'What would my grandfather do?' Their mode of operation is time tested, it's generational. And so, I doubt, very, very seriously, that he called anyone for outside advice." Finally, Tirico asked whether Tomlin believes Rodgers will get another NFL opportunity this season, if he wants one. "There's certainly a possibility for that," Tomlin said. "And I just say that based on the 19 years that I held the position that I held. It's a 32-team league. All it takes is one. Over time, I've laughed and watched that people talk about, you know, 'No, that could never happen.' In a 32-team league, when everybody is highly competitive and there's some real challenges, particularly as you get to this portion of the journey from a player availability standpoint, there's certainly a possibility if he desires that he could play again, because all it takes is one suitor." Having cleared waivers, Rodgers is available to that one suitor, if/when that one suitor calls. Still, that one suitor will need to be willing to accept the risk that, if Rodgers doesn't have things go the way he wants, he'll choose to do again the same thing he did this week.
author: Mike Florio

title: T.J. Edwards: Fourth down pass to Jahmyr Gibbs a look we saw all week
summary: The Bears had a hard time stopping Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs throughout Thursday's game in Detroit, so it made sense that the Lions put the ball in Gibbs's hands on fourth down with just over two minutes left to play.
full_text: '' The Bears had a hard time stopping Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs throughout Thursday's game in Detroit, so it made sense that the Lions put the ball in Gibbs's hands on fourth down with just over two minutes left to play. Gibbs caught a short pass with forward momentum and one player between him and a first down that would have pushed them much closer to a home win. That player was Bears linebacker T.J. Edwards and Edwards was able to corral Gibbs short of the sticks for a tackle that gave them a chance to steal a win with three seconds left on the clock. After the 39-35 win, Edwards said he "knew it was going to be me" when he saw how the Lions lined up for the play. “I knew that there’s gonna be a play that we would have to make ,” Edwards said, via Kevin Fishbain of TheAthletic.com. “And we made a play when we needed to. I was happy to do it, grateful for it, man. It was a look that we saw all week, and I was able to make it.” Gibbs picked up 252 yards on Thursday, but Edwards's recognition and execution meant the few he didn't get made all the difference.
author: Josh Alper

title: Abdul Carter returns to Giants practice on Friday
summary: The Giants welcomed linebacker Abdul Carter back to the practice field on Friday.
full_text: The Giants welcomed linebacker Abdul Carter back to the practice field on Friday. Carter was out of practice on Wednesday and Thursday due to illness and a calf injury, but reporters at the open portion of Friday's workout noted that he was working with the rest of the team. The Giants will release injury designations later in the day, but head coach John Harbaugh downplayed concern about Carter's availability earlier this week and Friday's change in status suggests he'll be ready to go against the Colts. Carter had two sacks and five quarterback hits in last Sunday's win over the Jaguars. He was named the NFC defensive player of the week in recognition of that effort. Reporters also noted that cornerback Dru Phillips was practicing after missing the last two days with an illness. Defensive tackle Shelby Harris has also been sick and was not spotted during the open portion of practice.
author: Josh Alper

title: Carson Beck ruled out for Week 12, Josh Johnson to start
summary: Josh Johnson will once again start at quarterback for the Cardinals.
full_text: ' Josh Johnson will once again start at quarterback for the Cardinals. Head coach Mike LaFleur formally ruled out rookie Carson Beck for Sunday’s game against the Commanders, as Beck continues to deal with a back issue. LaFleur noted in his Friday press conference that Beck may be able to return for Week 13 when the Cardinals host the Eagles. Johnson started for Arizona in last week’s loss to the Chiefs, completing 18-of-31 passes for 155 yards with one touchdown. The Cardinals have also ruled out offensive lineman Jon Gaines II.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Art Rooney II expresses support for Mike McCarthy, calls Aaron Rodgers not a "good teammate"
summary: Steelers owner speaks about Wednesday's insanity.
full_text: After Wednesday's unprecedented chaos, it had to happen. And it did. Steelers owner Art Rooney II has addressed the events that resulted in the benching and then the firing of quarterback Aaron Rodgers. “A change had to be made , and I certainly agree with the change and the way it was handled," Rooney told Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette in a Thursday interview. The change was sparked by the notion that Rodgers gave coach Mike McCarthy an ultimatum: “Either let me call all the plays or just release me.” Instead, McCarthy benched him. It went to the next level when, as many expected, Rodgers scurried to the McAfee show to take shots at McCarthy for missing meetings, showing up late to meetings, and falling asleep in meetings — among other things, including the ultra-embarrassing "1-2-3 Packers!" moment from halftime of Sunday's loss to the Eagles. “There’s maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload,” Rooney said. “He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don’t do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that’s for sure. . . . “In general, I think, historically, what’s in the locker room stays in the locker room. That’s the way it’s always been. That’s the way it should be as far as I’m concerned.” Rooney also confirmed that the team supports McCarthy, despite Rodgers's rant and reports confirming the facts underpinning the petty delivery of them. “I just want to say that I have 100 [percent] confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney told Dulac. “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.” Rooney also was asked whether Rodgers raised with the owner supposed concerns about McCarthy's health. “Nothing,” Rooney said. “Mike’s as healthy as the rest of us. Health was not an issue. I’m not sure where that part comes [from].” Rooney also addressed something that has been largely overlooked during the fast-moving drama: Rodgers's subpar performance. “The sad thing is Mike took some of the bullets for Aaron in terms of some of the plays that were called, particularly in the red-zone troubles that we had,” Rooney said. “Mike took some of the bullets for things that were going wrong down there. He tried to protect him, and it just wasn’t working.” They should have known it wouldn't work between Rodgers and McCarthy. It's still unclear why either one of them thought it would. McCarthy shouldn't have wanted a reunion with Rodgers. And Rodgers shouldn't have wanted a second act with McCarthy. Then again, it's not as if Rodgers had many choices. In 2025, he had few takers. In 2026, he had fewer. If he was going to ensure that his final NFL throw wasn't a pick-six by playing another year, Pittsburgh wasn't just the best place. It was likely the only place.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jerry Jones on Mike McCarthy: "He was outstanding as the head coach"
summary: The recent remarks from former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers regarding Steelers coach Mike McCarthy have raised plenty of questions, posed to plenty of people.
full_text: The recent remarks from former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers regarding Steelers coach Mike McCarthy have raised plenty of questions, posed to plenty of people. After Thursday's 39-38 loss to the Eagles, Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones was asked about McCarthy, who coached Jones's team for five seasons, from 2020 through 2024. "I offered him to stay at least another year when he left," Jones told reporters. "And so I thought he was outstanding as the head coach and had a great command of, frankly, quarterback, offense. Can't say enough good things about him. He's, frankly, one of the finest people that around football that I've been around. And I can't say enough about him. I never had the type of thing that is being said about him. I never had that in consideration in any of my time with him, extending his contract. Any of that, that was never on the table. And we never had an issue within the organization." That conflicts, obviously, with the things Rodgers said on Wednesday. Regardless, Jones no longer employs McCarthy. While Jones possibly chose to take the high road, a former employer vouching for a coach is fundamentally different than his current employer vouching for him. McCarthy took the Cowboys to the playoffs three times in five years, advancing to the divisional round in 2022. The Cowboys failed to qualify for the postseason in the first year after McCarthy left. Thursday's loss to the Eagles makes it harder for them to get there the second post-McCarthy season.
author: Mike Florio

title: Aaron Rodgers clears waivers
summary: Rodgers becomes a free agent.
full_text: '' It's official. Aaron Rodgers is a free agent, again. For the third time since March 2025, Rodgers can sign with any team at any time. The soon-to-be 43-year-old cleared waivers on Thursday, per multiple reports. He can sign whenever he chooses, either to a practice squad or a 53-man roster. He can wait until the postseason, if he chooses. Of course, someone will have to want to sign him. In the 2026 offseason, only the Steelers did. At this point, an injury to a starter on a contending team will be the one thing that could create immediate interest in his services. As long as that team is willing to risk Rodgers eventually dialing up McAfee for another elongated monologue of grievances. At this point, any other outcome would be a surprise.
author: Mike Florio

title: Zach Ertz: People don't understand how good DeVonta Smith is
summary: Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith missed five games with a hamstring injury earlier this year and the Eagles lost all five of them, which doesn't feel like much of a coincidence after watching him in Dallas on Thursday.
full_text: Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith missed five games with a hamstring injury earlier this year and the Eagles lost all five of them, which doesn't feel like much of a coincidence after watching him in Dallas on Thursday. Smith caught 11 passes for 200 yards and two touchdowns in Philadelphia's remarkable 39-38 comeback win. The touchdowns came on 50- and 45-yard strikes from quarterback Joe Milton and Smith shook off a hard landing on his tailbone in the fourth quarter to finish out the game. The 11 catches tied Smith's career best and the 200 yards were a personal record, but the big day didn't come as a shock to tight end Zach Ertz. “It’s not surprising , honestly,” Ertz said, via Dave Zangaro of NBCSportsPhiladelphia.com. “I watched him when he was at Alabama, winning the Heisman. Comes in here right away, his game is just so smooth. I don’t think people understand how good of a player he truly is until he gets his opportunities. I don’t know what the final stats were. I know over 200 yards, which is crazy. But he’s just a receiver that really has no weakness. The way he runs routes is so smooth, the way he can make plays on the balls in the air, yards after catch. I think he’s probably one of the most underrated players in the league. I saw him as a rookie so where he’s at now doesn’t surprise me at all.” The Eagles made Smith their No. 1 wideout when they traded A.J. Brown this offseason and the injury interrupted his bid to prove he's the right guy to fill that role on their offense, but Thanksgiving offered some proof of concept for the Eagles' passing game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bills benefited from extra seconds during Chiefs' final drive
summary: For the second time this week, the clock operator took center stage.
full_text: '' Every second counts. We saw it on Monday night, when the clock operator didn't press the button to save a second or two for the Bengals to try to pull out a win over the Commanders. It apparently happened again on Thursday night, in more subtle fashion. By our count, the Buffalo clock operator managed to preserve four seconds during what was the Chiefs' final drive of the game. I've watched it, several times. The Chiefs had first and 10 on their own 11. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes dropped the shotgun snap. By the time he recovered the ball, was touched, the whistle blew, and the Bills called a timeout (assuming they did it instantly), four seconds had elapsed. The clock, however, ultimately moved by only one second , from 26 to 25 — not 22. Then, after running back Emmett Johnson gained five yards on second and 15, 19 seconds remained when the whistle blew. The clock in the NBC score bug at one point shifted from 19 seconds to 20, presumably to match the official time on the stadium scoreboard. After the third-down incompletion, the clock showed 15 seconds. It should have been 11 seconds. Following the punt, which was partially blocked, and the return by Greg Dortch, there were four seconds to play. Four seconds. The same four seconds that apparently were preserved through creative clock operation. Of course, if the clock had shown 11 seconds and not 15 before the punt, the Bills may have not tried to block it. They may have opted to attempt a fair catch followed by a free kick. Regardless, there was more time on the clock than there should have been. And those extra seconds ensured that the Bills would have just enough time for Tyler Bass to make a walk-off 57-yard field goal. With so many games decided by such tight margins, there needs to be a better effort to ensure complete accuracy with the game timing, especially as the final seconds of a game tick, tick, tick away. So when it was time to divvy up the postgame turkey legs, here's hoping the Bills saved a drumstick for the timekeeper.
author: Mike Florio

title: The "carnival" came back to town on Thursday, and Joe Milton III won his "teddy bear"
summary: Cowboys' decision not to put Milton on the roster comes back to haunt them.
full_text: Fifty-two years after the Thanksgiving legend of Clint Longley was born, a guy who couldn't convince the Cowboys to give him a spot on the 53-man roster pulled a Reverse Longley on America's Team. On Thursday, former Cowboys practice-squad quarterback Joe Milton III returned to Dallas and made them regret not putting him on the roster when they had the chance. The Cowboys acquired Milton in April 2025 , sending a fifth-round pick to New England for Milton and a seventh-round pick. He appeared in four games last season before losing the training-camp and preseason competition with Sam Howell to be the backup to Dak Prescott. Milton was released in late August. He cleared waivers. He joined the Dallas practice squad. After Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts landed on injured reserve due to blood clots, the Eagles came calling with a spot on the active roster. The Cowboys could have attempted to add Milton to their own active roster, but they didn't. Milton's impressive performance has rekindled the comments made by Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer in the days before the 2026 rosters were cut from 90 to 53. "I first remember hearing about Joe Milton he was at [the] University of Michigan, and everyone applauded him for how hard and how far he could throw the ball," Schottenheimer said at the time, via Jane Slater of NFL Network. "Cool. That's awesome. You know, go be in a carnival somewhere . Like, that's not what playing NFL quarterback is. It's not, 'Yeah, I can throw the ball 85 yards.' You're throwing through small windows, you're throwing over people, you're changing arm slots. So, like, to me, arm strength is cool but, like, you know, go to the fair and win a teddy bear." In fairness to Schottenheimer, he then praised Milton's development. "But you got to play quarterback, you know, and that's what I think you see Joe learning is he's playing quarterback," Schottenheimer said at the time. "And he's playing quarterback at a high level. He's checking the ball down. He's making blitz adjustments. He's solving problems. He's reading, you know, from his first, second, to third and even fourth progression at times. And it takes time. I mean, it, you know, you don't stop. I mean, you don't stop learning as a quarterback and the only way to do it is to play and I'm really, really proud of him." Still, the Cowboys weren't sufficiently proud of Milton to give him a roster spot. And owner/G.M. Jerry Jones refused to admit that they made a mistake. "That is the best I've seen him play," Jones told reporters after the 39-38 loss. "And he picked a bad time to do it , from my standpoint." From Milton's standpoint, he picked the ideal time to do it. He'll now become a factor in the Eagles' future plans at quarterback. How could he not be after what he accomplished on Thursday, engineering a comeback in a game that saw the Eagles down by 21 points late in the third quarter? Still, it's just getting started for Milton. He needs to build on what he did. If he does, he'll become a long-time NFL starter. If he doesn't, he'll become another Clint Longley — whose Thanksgiving Day performance in 1974 wasn't the beginning but the end.

title: Patrick Mahomes on Harrison Butker: I try to have confidence in everybody, I know he's working at it
summary: Harrison Butker missed yet another field goal on Thursday night, which was a key factor in the Chiefs eventually losing to the Bills, 13-10.
full_text: '' Harrison Butker missed yet another field goal on Thursday night, which was a key factor in the Chiefs eventually losing to the Bills, 13-10. With a whopping eight missed field goals in 11 games so far this season — plus one missed extra point — it’s fair to question how much longer the Chiefs can stick with their longtime kicker. After the Thanksgiving loss, quarterback Patrick Mahomes offered some public support for the embattled kicker. “I try to have confidence in everybody on the team. That’s part of playing this sport, is believing in the guys around you,” Mahomes said in his postgame press conference. “And obviously, Harrison hasn’t had the season that he’s wanted this year. But he’s also been one of the best kickers in the game for a long time. “I know he’s working at it. I can tell you that. And he’s doing his best to be the best teammate he can be, and go out there and execute in those moments. Unfortunately, tonight it didn’t go his way. But, I promise you, he’ll come back and work at it again. And hopefully, the next time, he’ll be able to go out there and make it happen.” The Chiefs signed Justin Tucker to their practice squad with the hope of pushing Butker to improve. But at this point, if Tucker is going to be around, it might be time to try him in a game.

title: Friday's game gives Steelers fans a chance to chime in on recent events

title: Dan Campbell on calling late timeouts: I was hoping for a "chance for rebuttal"
summary: With 2:34 to play on Thursday, the Lions had the ball on the Chicago 39.
full_text: '' With 2:34 to play on Thursday, the Lions had the ball on the Chicago 39. It was first and 10. Detroit led, 35-32. In other words, Detroit had its ninth win in hand. But the drive ended when coach Dan Campbell decided to go for it on fourth and four from the Chicago 33, instead of attempting a 51-yard field goal that would have stretched the lead to six. Yes, the Bears would have gotten the ball back with more than two minutes to play, if Campbell had opted to kick (and if kicker Jake Bates had made it). Yes, a touchdown (and an extra point) would have won the game. By not converting, the Bears had a chance to play for overtime or, if they could gain enough ground, a game-winning touchdown. After the game, Campbell addressed the decision to go for it on fourth down. "I don't regret that, you know?" Campbell said. "I wish we would have made that. But, listen, sometimes that happens, you know?" While that decision becomes the obvious focus of postgame scrutiny, a subsequent decision deserves some focus, too: As the Bears drove for what ultimately was the game-winning touchdown with three seconds left, Campbell called a pair of timeouts. He called one after the Bears got a first down at the Detroit 31, with 1:12 to play. He called another after the Bears got a first down at the Detroit 21, with 52 seconds to play. At the time, the Bears had only one timeout. Given the Thanksgiving Day debacle from 2024, when the Bears got greedy and blew their shot at a field goal that would have forced overtime (and coach Matt Eberflus got fired the next day), they undoubtedly wouldn't have gotten cute as the final minute ticked away. Two years later, those two timeouts allowed the Bears to run the clock all the way down to the last few seconds before taking the lead. Asked whether he took the timeouts to give the defense a "breather" or a chance to "regroup," Campbell said he was hoping for a "chance for rebuttal." The problem with that approach is that it was premised on the Bears tying the game with a field goal. The timeouts helped ensure that the Bears would have enough time to score a touchdown. There was still plenty of risk for Chicago. The Bears ran two plays with no timeouts, risking a sack or a tackle in the field of play that would have ended the game. The first play flirted with disaster. With 13 seconds left and the Bears at the Lions' six, quarterback Caleb Williams threw toward running back D'Andre Swift near the goal line. The ball was tipped by linebacker Derrick Barnes. If it had gotten through to Swift, he may have caught it and been tackled short of the end zone. And the Bears most likely would have been unable to rush to the line, get in formation, snap the ball, and spike it. Or the Swift catch could have been ruled a touchdown on the field and then overturned by replay review, with a 10-second runoff that would have ended the game. The Lions know that wrinkle all too well, thanks to an identical outcome in a 2017 game against the Falcons. Still, the Bears scored a touchdown and won. And they had enough time to do it in part because Campbell called not one but two timeouts as the Bears were driving.

title: On Our Way Home is free on Thursday and Friday
summary: The holiday season is here.
full_text: The holiday season is here. And I'm in the mood to give something away. (It must be the whiskey.) The On Our Way Home ebook is available for free on Thursday and Friday. Why not give something away? This is the week when everyone is trying to sell you something. No one is giving you anything, with zero strings attached. On Our Way Home is primarily a Christmas story. It's also a ghost story. I cranked it out between Thanksgiving and New Year's Day a few years back. In the interests of avoiding any spoilers, I'll just say this: Download it and give it a try. It's essentially about family and redemption and reconciliation. It's also about forgiving others, while finding a way to forgive yourself. It's funny at times. It's sad at times. If you make it to the end, you'll possibly shed a tear or two. The best feedback I've gotten came from a reader who had suffered from PTSD for years. Reading On Our Way Home unlocked his ability to feel emotions again. I never intended anything like that. I just had an idea for a story, years before writing it. One year, I got caught up in the spirit of the season and it flowed, one chapter, one page, one word at a time. The price is right. If you don't like it, delete it. If you like it, keep going. Speaking of free, Quarterback of the Future is being posted , one chapter at a time. Twenty-five chapters are up. A new one is coming every day until it's done. Someone asked recently why my break from writing consists of more writing. There's something magical and, frankly, fun about creating something out of nothing. It's even more fun when people read it and enjoy it. Whether you enjoy it is up to you. If you don't, that's on me. But it won't cost you a penny to find out, if you download On Our Way Home on Thursday or Friday.

title: James Cook touchdown gives Bills 7-0 lead over Chiefs
summary: There is some nasty weather in Western New York on Thanksgiving night.
full_text: There is some nasty weather in Western New York on Thanksgiving night. Will one touchdown be enough to win it? The Bills have at least scored one early in the second quarter, with James Cook going in for a 5-yard score. It took Buffalo 11 plays to go 49 yards, with the team getting great field positions as a result of one play on special teams. Chiefs returner Josh Downs let a punt fall and roll instead of fielding it in his team’s territory, which led the offense to start its second drive at the 4-yard line. Kansas City then went three-and-out, and the punt went out of bounds at the Kansas City 49. The Bills only needed to convert one third down on their ensuing drive, with Josh Allen hitting Khaliil Shakir for a 17-yard pass on third-and-6. While Buffalo got down to the 1-yard line, a false start backed them up. but Cook then erased that with his touchdown run. In three drives, Cook has 42 yards on 13 carries with one touchdown. Allen is just 3-of-6 passing for 30 yards.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Bills lead Chiefs 7-3 at halftime on Thanksgiving night
summary: Nasty weather in Western New York has limited offensive production for both Buffalo and Kansas City.
full_text: There is some nasty weather in Western New York for Thanksgiving night and the Bills look like they have a home-field advance over the Chiefs. Buffalo leads Kansas City 7-3 at halftime. With steady freezing rain falling throughout the first half, it was difficult for both teams to get much going offensively. The game-time temperature was 35 degrees but the feels like temperature was down to 21. The Bills have relied on running back James Cook for most of their offensive production. Cook rushed for 71 yards on 19 carries in the first half with a 5-yard touchdown. Josh Allen is just 5-of-10 passing for 41 yards with an interception. Safety Alohi Gilman picked off Allen in the end zone on second-and-8 from the Kansas City 9 midway through the second quarter. At that point, it seemed like if the Bills scored a touchdown, they might have an insurmountable lead. While the Chiefs didn’t score off of that interception, they at least kept Buffalo off the board. But Kansas City had several miscues from the wet ball. The team had trouble fielding kicks, punter Matt Ariza had trouble catching a long snap before a punt, and Patrick Mahomes had trouble fielding a snap. But Kansas City finally got a little something going late in the second quarter, with Harrison Butker sending a 26-yard field goal through the uprights to narrow Buffalo’s lead to four points. Through 30 minutes, Mahomes is 10-of-15 for 97 yards. Travis Kelce has four receptions for 71 yards, including a key 21-yard catch at the end of the first half to get Kansas City into scoring position. The Chiefs will receive the second-half kickoff.

title: Bears feared to lose another TE long-term as Colston Loveland looks for second opinion on knee injury

full_text:
The Chicago Bears won a Thanksgiving thriller over the Detroit Lions on Thursday, 39-35, but they did lose one of their top pass-catchers.
In the first quarter, tight end Colston Loveland exited with a knee injury and was eventually carted off the field. While ESPN's Adam Schefter initially reported that Loveland was expected to land on injured reserve with the injury, additional reporting noted that Chicago is waiting for Loveland to get a second opinion on his knee before any decision on injured reserve is made.
Until the decision is made, the team announced that Loveland is considered week-to-week with the knee injury. There is belief he will be able to return later this season regardless of IR placement, according to reports.
Loveland was rolled up on from behind during a D'Andre Swift rushing attempt early in Thursday's game against the Lopns. He caught just one pass for five yards, which he fumbled, before leaving the game. The former tenth overall pick out of Michigan has caught 41 passes for 397 yards and three touchdowns this season. He is Caleb Williams ' third-most-targeted receiver behind Luther Burden III and Rome Odunze .
Chicago may have to finish the regular season without its top two tight ends, as Cole Kmet was placed on injured reserve after suffering a knee injury in Week 7's win over the New England Patriots . Third-round rooke Sam Roush and undrafted veteran Stephen Carlson are the only other tight ends currently on the Bears' active roster. Roush has played situationally for the Bears this season, seeing 279 offensive snaps on the season while catching passes in each of his last three games, while Carlson has 13 career targets since entering the league in 2019 — four of which came against Detroit on Thursday. Undrafted rookie Qadir Ismail is on the Bears' practice squad. This year, Chicago's 92 targets to tight ends are the seventh-most of any team in the NFL, according to Next Gen Stats.
This is a massive loss for the No. 4 offense in the NFL. At 9-2, the Bears are not only looking to win the incredibly competitive NFC North, but also have their eyes set on the conference's No. 1 seed, currently held by the San Francisco 49ers .
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer on job security after latest disastrous loss: 'I don't worry about that'
summary: Schottenheimer is once again under fire in the wake of another brutal defeat
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys suffered an embarrassing loss on Thanksgiving afternoon, blowing a 21-point lead against the division rival Philadelphia Eagles and backup quarterback Joe Milton — whom the Cowboys themselves cut at the end of training camp.
Dallas is unfortunately no stranger to choking away games this season. The Thanksgiving upset was the Cowboys' second loss this season wherein they blew a multi-touchdown lead in the fourth quarter at home. It was also their second loss this season to a backup quarterback at home. Thursday evening's loss was the third game dropped on a game-losing field goal attempt either at the buzzer of regulation or in overtime, and the second of those three where their clock/game management decisions arguably cost them the win. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, the Cowboys have now posted the two highest win probabilities in a loss this season, with their 99.1% win probability against the Eagles topping their previous high of 98.3% in Week 8 against the Arizona Cardinals .
Unsurprisingly, given those calamitous results, the future of Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has been called into question. There are only so many games you can blow, so many mistakes you can make before the calls for your job start coming. And for Schottenheimer, those calls have been coming for some time now.
But Schottenheimer himself says he's unconcerned about the noise.
"I don't worry about that," Schottenheimer said when asked about his job security, according to The Athletic . "I worry about the guys in that locker room. That doesn't affect me."
He might have good reason not to worry about speculation regarding his job security. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones goes out there every week and defends Schottenheimer to the masses, insisting Schottenheimer will lead the Cowboys to a Super Bowl and that he is not considering any coaching changes. Incredibly, Schottenheimer's job appears safe, at least for now.
Schottenheimer did meet with both Jerry and Stephen Jones after the game to discuss the latest loss, but it sounds like the meeting was business as usual and pretty benign.
"Our conversations were shared disappointment, but we're also ready to get back to work," he said, per The Athletic .
The Cowboys have a whole lot of work to do. Whether that work ultimately leads to success is up for debate, and whether Schottenheimer should be in charge of directing it is another story entirely.

title: Jerry Jones, Brian Schottenheimer refute Aaron Rodgers' accusations: Mike McCarthy 'was outstanding'
summary: Rodgers accused McCarthy of being late to meetings, sleeping in meetings and being behind on film prep
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Aaron Rodgers nuked Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy's reputation after the Steelers benched him late Tuesday night.
In a scathing appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on ESPN on Wednesday, the four-time NFL MVP and Super Bowl XLV MVP ripped McCarthy, saying Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth told him of Pittsburgh's decision to make him inactive for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos, and he accused McCarthy of sleeping and being late to team meetings throughout the season. Rodgers raised numerous other accusations against McCarthy, including that he arrived late this week and slept during offensive meetings.
Rodgers said that the behavior McCarthy exhibited this season in Pittsburgh was present during their shared tenure with the Green Bay Packers, as well as during McCarthy's run as head coach of the Dallas Cowboys. The Cowboys employed McCarthy as their head coach for five seasons from 2020 to 2024, and they went 49-35 in that span, tied for the eighth-best record in the league with the Minnesota Vikings. Dallas won 12 games in the regular season for three consecutive years from 2021 to 2023, the first time the franchise accomplished that feat since their 1990s Super Bowl dynasty teams. The Cowboys went 1-3 in the postseason under McCarthy, advancing no further than the NFC divisional round.
"They know what's going on. Like I said, they all know. Everybody knows," Rodgers said on Wednesday . "Just like the guys in Green Bay knew. It's like the people in Dallas knew. Like they know what the deal is."
One of the people in Dallas who claimed not to know what Rodgers was talking about is Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones. Jones unequivocally refuted Rodgers' claims and said he tried to extend McCarthy when his original five-year contract expired at the end of the 2024 season. The two sides couldn't come to an agreement on a new deal, so McCarthy took a year off in 2025 before being hired by the Steelers this year.
"I never saw anything that would not ... I offered him to stay at least another year when he left," Jones said. "I thought he was outstanding as the head coach, and [he] had a great command of quarterback, offense. Can't say enough good things about him. He's frankly one of the finest people around football that I have been around. I can't say enough about him. I never had the type of thing that's being said about him, I've never had that in consideration at any of my time with him. [Whether it was] extending his contract or any of that. That [alleged behavior] was never on the table."
Current Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer worked as a consultant on McCarthy's staff in 2022 before becoming his offensive coordinator from 2023 to 2024, and he also backed up his old boss on a conference call on Friday.
"Well, No. 1, Mike McCarthy is an incredible man. He's a damn good football coach. I call him a friend," Schottenheimer said. "My experience with him here was awesome. He won a ton of football games here, and again, I think the world of Mike."
While Rodgers painted a picture of extremely erratic and irresponsible behavior by his longtime head coach, Jones and Schottenheimer claim none of that happened in Dallas. The Steelers have since released Rodgers, and he cleared waivers, thus making him a free agent.

title: Broncos at Steelers: Why the NFL isn't allowed to schedule the Black Friday game for primetime
summary: For the fourth straight year, the Black Friday game will kick off at 3 p.m. ET
full_text:
For the fourth straight year, the NFL is holding a Black Friday game, and for the fourth straight year, it will kick off at 3 p.m. ET, which makes it the most bizarre game on the NFL schedule . It's the only regular-season game all year that kicks off at 3 p.m.
With the Broncos and Steelers heading into a huge matchup , the NFL would probably prefer to put the Black Friday game in primetime — especially with all the Aaron Rodgers ' drama surrounding the game — but the league can't do that thanks to a 65-year-old law.
Under the Sports Broadcasting Act of 1961, the league isn't allowed to televise any games on Friday or Saturday from the second weekend in September through the second weekend in December. Instead, those two days have been earmarked for high school and college football . However, there is a loophole in this rule: the NFL is ALLOWED to schedule a Friday game as long as it ends before 6 p.m. local time , which is how the league settled on a 3 p.m. ET kickoff time. It's basically the latest the game could start without running afoul of the SBA.
The NFL has generally avoided this issue by just not scheduling any Friday games. Since the AFL-NFL merger in 1970, the league has only played a total of 16 Friday games and six of those have essentially been holiday games that were either played on Christmas Eve, Christmas or New Year's Eve. Those three holidays come AFTER the second weekend in December, so the NFL is allowed to put those games in primetime. For Black Friday, the game has to be in the afternoon.
The Black Friday game has worked out so well for the NFL that the league is actually kicking around the idea of adding a second game to the day . If that happened, it would likely be a doubleheader, with the first game kicking off at 12 p.m. ET and the second at 3 p.m. ET. Roger Goodell floated the doubleheader idea earlier this year, and although it didn't happen, it could still certainly be something we see on the schedule next year.

title: Did Chiefs get hosed by NFL clock controversy? Breaking down the final seconds of Bills' wild Thanksgiving win
summary: The Bills may have gotten a boost from a friendly clock operator in Buffalo
full_text:
The NFL gave us a wild day of football on Thanksgiving, and the action didn't end until late Thursday night when the Bills' kicker Tyler Bass hit a 57-yard field goal on the final play to beat the Chiefs 13-10. Although the Bills got the win, it appears they may have gotten some help from the clock operator, who might have given Buffalo a few extra seconds at the end of the game.
Let's break down exactly what happened.
After a punt by Buffalo, the Chiefs had a first-and-10 from their own 11-yard line with just 26 seconds left to play. The Chiefs couldn't simply kneel the ball and take the game to overtime because the Bills had all three timeouts, so Kansas City had to try to put together a drive.
On first down, Patrick Mahomes fumbled the shotgun snap, and that's where things started to get interesting with the clock.
After Mahomes fell on the ball, the Bills called a timeout, and the clock stopped at 19 seconds. However, before the Chiefs ran their next play, six seconds were added to the game clock, bringing it to 25 seconds. This means that the first-down play only took one second.
I am at a loss for words as how this first play only took *one* second off the game clock. Chiefs could have handled the ensuing sequence and punt differently and Buffalo potentially does not end up with enough time for the field goal attempt. pic.twitter.com/ILkv8LEXR7
The clip above was shared by Super Bowl-winning analytics consultant Ryan Paganetti, who used to make a living helping teams handle late-game situations like this. He was one of many people who were stunned that only one second came off the clock.
On the play, the whistle blew with 24 seconds left, and if you factor in that Bills head coach Joe Brady had to call a timeout, it seems like at least three seconds should have run off the clock.
On the next play, Emmett Johnson ran for a five-yard gain on second down. This play started with 25 seconds left on the clock and ended when the refs blew the whistle at 19 seconds. However, the officials added one more second to the clock, moving it to 20 before the start of the next play.
On third down, Mahomes threw an incompletion to Travis Kelce, which left just 15 seconds to play. At that point, it was total chaos: The Chiefs had to punt, and the Bills tipped the punt, making it more returnable for Greg Dortch, who took it 17 yards to Kansas City's 39-yard line. Dortch was tackled with four seconds left, which was just enough time for Bass to hit his game-winning field goal.
This final sequence is pure cinema. pic.twitter.com/jO4Fd8IOgu
The Bills definitely seemed to benefit from extra time here, but it's hard to say exactly how much. By my count, they got an extra three seconds, and in that case, Bass still would have been able to attempt the game-winning field goal with one second left. Other NFL reporters thought the Bills got even more time, with some believing Buffalo got anywhere from four to seven extra seconds .
If the Bills did get four to seven extra seconds, that would have created an interesting situation to end regulation. Matt Araiza's final punt would have come with just eight to 11 seconds left instead of 15.  In that situation, instead of returning the kick, Dortch could have called for a fair catch, and that would have set up a possible fair-catch free kick to win the game (this can be attempted even if the clock hits zero seconds on the play). The Chiefs also could have punted it out of bounds, or they could have had Araiza hit it low to ensure the ball would bounce so there would be no fair catch, but in either of those situations, the clock likely wouldn't have run out, and Buffalo still would have had time for one more play.
In the end, it does seem like the Bills got the benefit of a few extra seconds, but it's impossible to say whether that cost the Chiefs the game. Kansas City also had another controversy in the fourth quarter, when Rashee Rice made a catch for a first down on third-and-10 that was eventually overturned. Rice says he caught the ball , but the officials felt otherwise.
Although some NFL fans seem to think the Chiefs get every call, this game proves that not everything goes their way.
author: John Breech

title: A premature, unauthorized, tiered ranking of every possible Dallas Cowboys coach -- should Jerry Jones need it
summary: With Brian Schottenheimer on the hot seat after a disastrous 5-7 start, here is a look at who Jerry Jones could target, from big names like Bill Belichick to proven winners like Mike Tomlin
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are a disaster. After their latest calamitous loss, the Cowboys are 5-7 and their playoff "hopes" barely exist anymore.
They have suffered several embarrassing defeats this season, including two in which they blew multi-score fourth-quarter leads at home and two in which they lost to backup quarterbacks — again at home. The Thanksgiving loss to the division rival Philadelphia Eagles , of course, qualifies for both of those lists and is presumably the nail in the coffin for their season.
It should also probably be the nail in the coffin for head coach Brian Schottenheimer, who is clearly in over his head and who even Jerry Jones has admitted is learning on the job as a head coach and may not get to where he needs to to find success for years. Jones has stated several times that he is not considering a change at head coach and that he still feels that Schottenheimer is the right man for the job. But he should be considering a change, and he's pretty clearly wrong about Schottenheimer, who has shown in two seasons that he is not a difference-making coach — at least not in a good way.
It's probably time, then, to think about what might come next in Dallas. Jones is extremely reluctant to admit he's wrong and fire his hand-picked coaches — he let Jason Garrett and Mike McCarthy's contracts expire rather than fire them. He's even more reluctant to pay multiple coaches at once. And he's somehow even more reluctant than that to pay what it takes to land the best coaches on the market.
For some context: The Cowboys have only interviewed six coaches in total over the last two times they had an opening, and they basically rigged the processes for McCarthy and Schottenheimer. But that shouldn't stop us from thinking about who might be available, and how they might fit in Dallas.
That's why we're here: to speculate wildly about all the possible candidates for the Cowboys job, should it come open at some point. We're breaking things down by category and including every name we can think of that qualifies for each. Plenty of these potential hires don't make much sense, but Jones' past hires haven't made much sense either, so that shouldn't be disqualifying.
Former Alabama HC Nick Saban
North Carolina HC Bill Belichick
Let's be very, very clear: Neither of these hires would be a good idea.
Saban has been out of coaching entirely for several years and out of the NFL since a wildly unsuccessful tenure with the Miami Dolphins came to a close in 2006. He now spends most of his time shilling for SEC schools and the College Sports Protection Act on ESPN's College GameDay. The only reason to hire him would be that he is Nick Saban.
The end of Belichick's run with the New England Patriots was not great. His time with the Tar Heels has been largely unsuccessful so far, with a losing record in each season and scandal(s) off the field. He used to be the Super Bowl-winning Bill Belichick, though, so Jones could be enticed by the idea of bringing him in.
Former Steelers HC Mike Tomlin
Former Bills HC Sean McDermott
Tomlin is probably going to be the hottest candidate on the market this offseason, given his success in Pittsburgh. He's certainly a high-floor candidate, having shown the ability to rack up winning seasons, but he's probably not a particularly high-ceiling candidate, given he hasn't won a playoff game since 2016. He also hasn't shown much ability to identify good play-calling assistants on either side of the ball (Tomlin himself doesn't call plays).
Still, he's probably the safest potential hire on the board, and it would come with a lot of good press. Most of the credit for any wins in the future would go to Tomlin and not Jones, though, so I'd consider this one unlikely given Jerry's track record of wanting credit for everything.
McDermott is a similarly high-floor candidate. He showed the ability to rack up winning seasons in Buffalo — and not just when Josh Allen was his quarterback — the Bills went to the playoffs with Tyrod Taylor in 2017. McDermott's defenses during his time with the Bills were generally good but also not quite good enough when playoff time rolled around. He also was among the more conservative coaches when it came to game management, which isn't ideal in the modern NFL. But if you're looking for a safe hire, you could certainly do worse than McDermott, who has had a lot of success.
The only reason Shanahan is even being mentioned here is that he's who Troy Aikman has said he'd hire as his head coach if he ever got the opportunity, and a potential marriage between Aikman and the Cowboys has been floated several times this year. The 49ers are never going to agree to trade Shanahan, though, and certainly not to the Cowboys. That's why this section is titled "never-happening trade candidates" and not just "trade candidates."
Each of these coaches' teams has been disappointing this season, and at this point it wouldn't be that surprising if they weren't asked back for another year. Ryan has shown the ability to coach a top defense, which the Cowboys obviously desperately need. Steichen has coaxed top offenses out of questionable quarterback play before and could do good work with Dak Prescott . Moore was seemingly Jones' anointed successor to Mike McCarthy before that relationship blew up.
Oklahoma Sooners Interim OC Jason Witten
Colorado Buffaloes HC Deion Sanders
Witten might be the single-most likely candidate on this list to actually get the job, given his pedigree. He's a Cowboys legend. Jones loves him and has been praising him as a future NFL head coach for years. It would basically be like hiring Jason Garrett, but if the player was actually good when he was on the Cowboys. (That's not a comment on Witten's coaching acumen — just on Jones' thought process when it comes to hiring coaches.) Oklahoma's offense has actually improved since Witten took over play-calling duties, so maybe there is something there, but most of his success has come at the high school level.
Sanders is another former Cowboys player and a hire that would generate a massive amount of attention. Considering how his tenure in Colorado has gone since his team lost Travis Hunter and Shedeur Sanders , though, it's probably not a hire that would generate much enthusiasm. Still, Jerry loves a story, and Deion in Dallas would be arguably the biggest story out there.
Adams is highly respected, has shown the ability to design a good run game in both Dallas and Arizona, would probably come cheaply (which is important for Jones, as we know) and is right down the hall, which is where the Cowboys turned the last time they hired a head coach.
Durde was the Cowboys' defensive line coach under Dan Quinn before leaving to be the defensive coordinator under Mike Macdonald in Seattle. He doesn't call the defensive plays for the Seahawks, but he's been part of building one of the NFL's best defenses.
Rams Assistant HC Kliff Kingsbury
Texas Longhorns HC Steve Sarkisian
Much like Jones loves connections to the Cowboys, he loves connections to Texas.
Kingsbury was born and raised in San Antonio. He set records as a high school player in Texas, was inducted into the Texas High School Football Hall of Fame, started at Texas Tech, coached both Houston and Texas Tech to electric offenses and has worked with a lot of high-profile quarterbacks. He wasn't particularly successful as a head coach, but Schottenheimer wasn't particularly successful as an offensive coordinator, and Jones still hired him.
Sarkisian has been the head coach at UT since 2021. He seemingly generates NFL buzz every offseason. He does have NFL experience as an offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, but those tenures weren't exactly successful. And his run at Texas has included some high-profile bad losses, including a pair to unranked teams this year. Still, his name will probably come up in NFL circles again.
Notre Dame HC Marcus Freeman
Freeman is the hottest college-to-NFL name out there right…

title: Jaguars lose WR Parker Washington to shoulder injury as playoffs draw near
summary: Jacksonville's top target is evaluated week-to-week with a shoulder issue, while leading rusher Bhayshul Tuten is also banged-up
full_text:
The Jacksonville Jaguars will be without at least one of their most important playmakers when they host the Tennessee Titans this Sunday. Star wideout Parker Washington has been ruled out for Week 12 after suffering a shoulder injury during Thursday's practice session, according to a report from ESPN . Head coach Liam Coen said Washington is considered week-to-week.
Washington is the Jaguars' leading receiver this season, with 44 catches for 748 yards and six touchdowns through 10 games. He's less than 100 receiving yards away from a new career high, and his 17.0 yards per reception currently rank fifth in the NFL . The former sixth-round pick out of Penn State is coming off two straight 100-yard performances. He caught eight passes for 103 yards against the New York Giants last Sunday, and seven passes for 152 yards and a touchdown against the Titans in Week 10.
With Washington out of the lineup for at least one week, Trevor Lawrence will look to utilize Jakobi Meyers , Josh Cameron and Brian Thomas Jr . more in the passing game. Meyers is Jacksonville's second-leading receiver with 493 yards on 33 receptions.
To make matters worse for the Jaguars, they could also be without leading rusher Bhayshul Tuten this week. The second-year running back is dealing with foot and ankle injuries, and Coen says the team isn't sure he will suit up. Chris Rodriguez Jr . and Ameer Abdullah could see more work on Sunday.
The Jaguars had no problem with the Titans in their first matchup this season, defeating Tennessee 40-23 just two weeks ago. However, Washington becomes a crucial piece for a Jaguars team looking to make a serious playoff push. The Jaguars could still be without Washington as their schedule ramps up, with road games against the Chicago Bears and Houston Texans in two of the next three weeks.
While Jacksonville currently has a 94.3% chance to win their division, according to CBS Sports Forecasting & Projections, the Jaguars need to keep winning to maximize their postseason chances. Jacksonville is averaging more points per game (28.7) than any team in franchise history and entered Week 12 with the league's best points-per-game differential (+12.0). However, currently sitting at 7-3 behind the Denver Broncos and tied with the Cincinnati Bengals , the Jaguars hope to avoid a fourth-seed finish and a potential wild-card matchup with either the Broncos or the Kansas City Chiefs . Jacksonville dropped their Week 2 matchup against the Broncos, while they narrowly won their Week 5 matchup against the Chiefs in 2025.
