title: Steelers vs. Broncos prediction: Why Mason Rudolph can lead upset after Aaron Rodgers drama
summary: Rudolph is replacing Rodgers, who was surprisingly benched on Tuesday night and then went on a scorched-earth tirade against his now-former head coach
full_text:
This Black Friday showdown was already a must-watch before this week's stunning events in Pittsburgh, which led to Aaron Rodgers ' release. That news has added even more interest around a game that will have major playoff implications.
Despite this week's turmoil and a two-game losing streak, Pittsburgh (6-4) is still currently on the inside track in the AFC playoff picture. But the Steelers ' season is entering a pivotal stretch with upcoming games against Denver, Houston and Jacksonville.
Denver started the season slowly but has since won six straight games on the strength of an offense that has scored at least 23 points in five of those wins. However, now they'll have a new quarterback and plenty of baggage heading into Friday.
Here's how to follow the action in real time, along with a preview and prediction on how Mason Rudolph can pull off an upset.
Rodgers took every first-team rep during Tuesday's practice. By 11:10 that night, the Steelers had benched him and made him inactive for Friday's game. Fast forward less than 24 hours later, and the Steelers had released Rodgers after he scorched Mike McCarthy during an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show."
What caused the breakup? Rodgers did not feel that McCarthy should be the team's play-caller and gave him an ultimatum: Let either him or QB coach Tom Arth call the plays, or release him. McCarthy called his bluff.
The Steelers' offense will now be led by Mason Rudolph , a nine-year veteran with 20 career starts, including one postseason start.
Rudolph delivered when he was put in a similar spot back in 2023. He led the Steelers to three late-season wins that allowed Pittsburgh to clinch a spot in the playoffs.
Now 31, Rudolph doesn't exactly excel at anything, but he is a solid pro who can move an offense. He's largely accurate and has had success in the past on deep passes. Rudolph also has the respect of his teammates and coaches.
"I feel really good about Mason," McCarthy said on Wednesday . "I don't (want to) say pleasantly surprised, because that wouldn't be fair to him and what he's accomplished before we began working together. I think Tom Arth has done a great job with Mason and the young guys. He's done everything we ask as far as how to play, and has done a great job in the number two slot with the reps, and getting ready to play."
Rudolph will have some extra help against Denver. Michael Pittman , a former 1,100-yard receiver for the Colts , will play for the first time since Week 4. Roman Wilson made his return to the lineup last week and caught three passes for 43 yards. Fellow wideout Max Hurleman caught six passes for 61 yards and a touchdown on Sunday in his regular season debut.
Those players will help, but the Steelers' offense will need more production from wideouts DK Metcalf , Germie Bernard and running backs Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle if they are going to upset Denver. It's very possible that the Steelers' newfound depth at receiver should help open things up for Metcalf, Bernard and the Steelers' running back duo.
Rudolph and Co. will face a Broncos defense that is good but not great this season. The unit, which was third in the NFL in fewest points allowed in both 2024 and 2025, is 11th in points allowed this season. They're 24th in the NFL in passing yards allowed, 28th in average yards-per-carry allowed, 20th in third-down efficiency and 10th in red zone efficiency. Essentially, the Broncos have been a bend-but-not-break unit in 2026.
Pressure and opportunistic plays by the secondary have been Denver's calling card on defense. The Broncos have 31 sacks, with three players tied for the team lead at 5.0. Defensive back Ja'Quan McMillian has filled the stat sheet this season with 3.0 sacks, 39 tackles, two interceptions and eight pass breakups. He and safety Talanoa Hufanga have each returned interceptions for touchdowns.
Nix has faced Pittsburgh just once before, and it was his second career start back in Week 2 of the 2024 season. Nix and Co. were kept off the scoreboard for three quarters before getting two field goals in the fourth quarter. It wasn't enough as Pittsburgh left Denver with a 13-6 win.
Nix has mostly won since that game, but his play has regressed since his rookie season. This year, Nix is completing just 59.9% of his passes with 12 touchdowns and five interceptions. He has yet to throw for over 300 yards in a game and has been held three times under 200 passing yards.
It's fair to wonder if Nix is still working his way back from January's severe ankle injury, as it sometimes takes an athlete a full year to get back to where they were pre-injury. Whatever the reason is, it hasn't prevented Nix from winning the majority of his starts.
One of Denver's greatest strengths on offense is that it seldom turns the ball over. The Broncos have had just one game with multiple turnovers (Week 1) and have turned it over just two times in their last five games. The Broncos' offensive line also does a good job keeping Nix clean, as he has been sacked just 12 times.
The Broncos' offense has also been extremely good in the red zone, which has somewhat made up for their struggles on third down (they are 31st in the NFL in third-down efficiency). One of the reasons for Denver's success in the red zone has been their depth at receiver and the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman , who has run for a team-high six scores. Coleman will continue to be Denver's featured back on Friday as J.K. Dobbins has been suspended for conduct detrimental to the team.
Pittsburgh's game plan on defense will be to exploit Denver's porous third-down offense. Patrick Graham's unit will look to make the Broncos' offense one-dimensional by shutting down Coleman and the running game and putting the Broncos into obvious passing situations on third down.
The big question is whether the Steelers will play more man coverage after Joe Burrow and Joe Milton III have had success against their largely zone-based scheme over the last two weeks. It's safe to assume that if the Steelers continue to play heavy zone coverage, Sean Payton will give Nix a bevy of short, safe passes to negate Pittsburgh's pass rush.
As noted above, the Broncos have depth at receiver, but they don't have any elite wideouts, either. Because of that, the Steelers should play more man without the fear of getting beaten too many times over the top. Pittsburgh's secondary was outmatched two weeks ago in Cincinnati. That shouldn't be the case against Denver.
On paper, this is a win for the Broncos. They have the better team on both sides of the ball and haven't lost a game since Week 5. Conversely, the Steelers have lost two straight and are coming off a tumultuous week.
Football games aren't played on paper, though. Upsets happen all the time in the NFL (like the Eagles ' upset win in Dallas on Thanksgiving), so no one should be terribly surprised if the Steelers find a way to upset the Broncos at home, where they have yet to lose this season.
Rudolph isn't a typical backup. He has nine years of experience under his belt, including a playoff start. He has a deep understanding of the Steelers' offense and his offensive teammates. Rudolph will also have his full complement of playmakers, which is something Rodgers never really had this season.
More than that, Rudolph has risen to the occasion in similar situations in the past, and I expect him to do so once more against the Broncos.
Score: Steelers 24, Broncos 20
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: 2027 NFL Draft: Remaining games that will determine the draft order, including No. 1 overall
summary: A late-season clash between one-win teams Miami and Los Angeles leads a slate of critical showdowns with major quarterback dominoes and trade leverage at stake
full_text:
With seven weeks remaining in the regular season, the first-round draft order is far from settled. Several head-to-head matchups between teams near the bottom of the standings could have a significant impact on where each franchise ultimately selects. Which remaining games could have the biggest implications for the 2027 NFL Draft ?
Full draft order and needs, free agents for each team
The NFC South is heavily represented because three of the four teams have just three wins. With four games remaining among those three teams, the draft order will take care of itself in time.
When the two teams met earlier this season, Atlanta won by three touchdowns. It would be interesting to learn whether the Falcons would explore drafting another quarterback in the first round three years after taking Michael Penix Jr .
Tampa Bay has looked like a dominant team at times and lethally flawed at others. The health of Baker Mayfield has played a big role in the team's misfortunes, but the quarterback's stubborn tendencies also lead one to wonder if he may be too injured to help the team right now.
The Buccaneers dominated a prior meeting, 16-0.
If New Orleans were to lose out, difficult conversations may be had regarding head coach Kellen Moore . Kevin Stefanski has a longer leash in Atlanta. The two teams meet in Week 18 as well.
Tampa Bay has not picked Top-10 overall since taking linebacker Devin White No. 5 overall in 2019. Four of Atlanta's last six first-round picks have been within the Top-10 overall.
Los Angeles broke an eight-game losing streak two weeks ago against the Ravens . Will they find another victory by season's end? Among teams with just one win this season, Jim Harbaugh and the Chargers may be feeling the most pressure. Harbaugh is in his third season with the franchise, while the other two head coaches are in their first.
On the opposite sideline, Tampa Bay head coach Todd Bowles may also be coaching for his job over the remainder of the season.
Beyond the teams with a league-low one victory, the exercise meant taking a stance against certain teams. Arizona has fired its defensive coordinator and is now testing the depths of its quarterback position. Jacoby Brissett was traded, and Gardner Minshew and rookie Carson Beck suffered injuries. The Cardinals are not a threat down the stretch, so it is less likely they will string together some wins and fall outside the Top-10.
Philadelphia stole a win against in-state rival Pittsburgh, but quarterback Joe Milton is unlikely to stack multiple wins in the final weeks of the season. The Eagles also seemingly acknowledged the season was lost by trading defensive tackle Jordan Davis .
Arizona was feisty early in the season, but injuries to the offensive line and running back set them on a different course. The team lacks difference-makers in the passing game apart from tight end Trey McBride .
New Orleans was hot at the end of the 2025 season and carried that momentum into the offseason. However, injuries to key performers, such as running back Travis Etienne and wide receiver Jordyn Tyson , along with roster limitations, quickly set in.
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn came into the season knowing his job was on the line if the team didn't meet expectations. As a result, the team brought in veteran quarterback Geno Smith and several other veterans to raise the team's floor. Reality quickly set in for the franchise despite early-season hope. The Jets will once again have three first-round picks, but will Glenn be around to advise them?
One would assume Cardinals head coach Matt LaFleur is not in danger of losing his job, so an opportunity to build this team in his image lies ahead. The first order of business will be identifying and securing the correct quarterback.
These two teams are currently in position to draft Top-5 overall. If Miami wins, the same will be true next week. Although unlikely to get the No. 1 overall selection, New York has a vested interest in remaining near the top of the draft order so it isn't outside striking distance for a potential trade up for its quarterback of choice. In theory, such a move would cost less if the team only moved up a few spots.
Indianapolis is obviously not in possession of its own first-round pick, but the Jets will make that selection. As you're reading this, the Colts have moved on from Daniel Jones , so there isn't much upside left to the team's season. Indianapolis will almost certainly send a Top-10 overall pick back to New York as part of the Sauce Gardner trade.
Tennessee is currently in pole position and may be another team disinterested in taking a No. 1 overall quarterback if Cam Ward continues to show progress.
Three teams have one loss, and two of them will play in the final weeks of the regular season. Beyond affecting the draft order, this could also determine whether the No. 1 overall selection is available for trade. Los Angeles is presumably tied to quarterback Justin Herbert , whereas Miami is expected to be in the market for a quarterback. If the Chargers had the No. 1 overall pick, they could prioritize trading it to a franchise looking for a quarterback or to acquire Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith.

title: Thanksgiving Beef: Nick Sirianni vs. fan, Andy Reid vs. the refs, Aaron Rodgers vs. the world
summary: A thrilling holiday tripleheader delivered historic comebacks alongside heated sideline blowups, controversial officiating decisions and growing fan frustration
full_text:
This Thanksgiving in the NFL was arguably the best in football history, as it marked the first time every matchup featured a game-winning field goal or touchdown in the final five seconds of regulation, according to CBS Sports Research.
There were plenty of heroes from Thursday. Caleb Williams connected with Rome Odunze in the corner of the end zone with three seconds remaining to beat the Detroit Lions ; Jake Elliott of the Philadelphia Eagles capped the largest comeback (21 points) on Thanksgiving in NFL history with a 59-yard field goal to upset the Dallas Cowboys ; then Tyler Bass knocked through a 57-yard field goal as time expired to move the Buffalo Bills past the Kansas City Chiefs . It wasn't all sunshine and rainbows on this holiday, however.
There were sideline spats, questionable calls from the officials, upset fan bases, and then, of course, the grenade Aaron Rodgers lobbed at the Pittsburgh Steelers on his way out. Mike Tomlin finally gave his thoughts on that wild situation Thanksgiving night.
Below, we will power-rank all the "Thanksgiving Beef" we saw this week.
Cameras captured Eagles running back Will Shipley having a heated argument with head coach Nick Sirianni during Thursday's matchup in Dallas. It's true that Philly's lead man is known for his emotion, but this looked a bit weird.
Nick Sirianni And Will Shipley Getting Heated On The Sideline. Saquon Barkley Was Part Of This One Too. Not Exactly A Peaceful Thanksgiving In Philly. Something Clearly Has Them All Fired Up. pic.twitter.com/pCzsNMqcnz
After the Eagles' incredible 39-38 victory, Shipley told reporters that everything was fine, and cameras just happened to catch a Thanksgiving family argument.
"Emotions were running high. Like on Thanksgiving, all families are arguing about politics and the drunk uncle," Shipley said with a smile. "I've got so much love for coach Nick and him as the leader of this football team..."
Will Shipley on his sideline argument with Nick Sirianni pic.twitter.com/AUWxWgJ4An
Shipley isn't lying. Apparently he and Sirianni were acting like best friends in the locker room.
"They were loving each other up [in the locker room]," left tackle Jordan Mailata said, per ESPN . "I was like, 'Oh, how come I'm not getting hugged like that?'"
Thursday's edition of Patrick Mahomes vs. Josh Allen was a slugfest that featured just 23 total points scored. The bad weather made every play matter more.
With under two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter and the game tied at 10 apiece, Mahomes appeared to connect with Rashee Rice over the middle for a first down. However, the NFL headquarters in New York chimed in, saying it was actually an incomplete pass.
WOW... Refs called this a catch on the field but after review overturned the call and ruled this an incomplete catch for the Chiefs... Very little movement on this ball to overturn that pic.twitter.com/5yZ6sMQqTr
Chiefs head coach Andy Reid disagreed with the call and blamed "New York" for the reversal. The refs on the field had the correct ruling, but the league's headquarters did not, he said.
"Not one that I agreed with, but they said that this came from New York," Reid said. "It's not from these guys; our guys called it a completion — the guys who were working the game. I'm not quite sure what they saw. I saw he had control of the ball, and his elbow hit, then the ball hit. But he had control. Normally, in those kinds of situations, it's got to be clear and obvious. And to me, that was not clear and obvious."
This was a pivotal moment that forced the Chiefs to punt. Kansas City ended the game with two straight three-and-outs.
The 5-7 Cowboys fell to third place in the NFC East with their Thanksgiving loss to the Eagles. It's been an embarrassing season for Dallas, as the Cowboys are the only team in NFL history to average 30 points per game and have a losing record through 12 games. NFL teams are a combined 75-2-1 this year when up by 14 points or more in the fourth quarter.   The Cowboys have registered both of those losses.
Think about all the ways the Cowboys hurt their fan base:
How much worse can it get? After the loss to the Eagles, who's to say the Cowboys aren't the worst team in this stinky division?
Following the Eagles' game-winning field goal, Sirianni went to celebrate with some Philly fans near the field. However, it looked like he wanted to confront one of the fans, and he was yanked back by chief security officer Dom DiSandro and another staffer.
What is Nick Sirianni doing??? pic.twitter.com/vcJ8cIUmDd
Sirianni attempted to play this moment down , telling reporters that his staffers just wanted to get him back on the field to shake hands with Schottenheimer. I doubt that.
There was a ... let's call him a very vocal fan who would like Sirianni fired, in that section. Even after the Eagles won the game, he was flipping his head coach the bird.
Nick Sirianni was fired up after one of the best comebacks in Eagles history against their biggest rival in Dallas pic.twitter.com/PgDTrsRio4
There are other vulgar videos you can find online of this dude, but Sirianni definitely wanted a piece of him. Wouldn't that have been something? A head coach fighting one of his own fans moments after a massive game-winning field goal?
Rodgers was benched by the Steelers this week, so he went scorched-earth on the franchise. He didn't exactly throw a tantrum, but instead went a different, more calculated route — painting head coach Mike McCarthy as an old, unhealthy man totally incapable of leading an NFL franchise during an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show."
Rodgers accused his now-former coach of a lot, from falling asleep in meetings and failing to prepare for games to failing to connect with his players. The breaking point, according to Rodgers, was when McCarthy broke down the team saying, "1-2-3 Packers !" at halftime of last Sunday's loss to the Eagles. McCarthy last coached the Packers in 2018.
Rodgers' public undressing of his former boss will go down as one of the craziest "beefs" in NFL history — and it's generated plenty of response. There are former teammates of Rodgers who did not approve of what he did. T.J. Lang called it " despicable ," while Greg Jennings called it " distasteful. " Even Tom Brady said Rodgers violated "the sanctity of the NFL locker room ."
Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin spoke out on Thursday night, calling the situation a "dumpster fire."
"I'm upset about it; it's a dumpster fire," Tomlin said. "And I don't say that in a judgemental way; I've presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I'm sure Steeler Nation is upset."
This "Turkey Day Beef" could hurt Rodgers' legacy, and it's a story that's not over just yet.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Week 12 bold predictions: Vikings set season sack record, J.J. McCarthy has best game of career
summary: Plus, Derrick Henry gets back to his old ways against the Houston Texans
full_text:
Anything can happen in the National Football League, and the league's 2026 Thanksgiving actions emphasized that.
This year's Thanksgiving became the first day in NFL history with at least three games each with a go-ahead score in the final minute of the fourth quarter, per CBS Sports Research. All three games featured a game-winning field goal or touchdown in the final five seconds of regulation, the first such Thanksgiving ever. In the opening game of the day, Caleb Williams threw a six-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Rome Odunze with three seconds left to secure a 39-35 road win over the Detroit Lions . That marked the latest game-winning touchdown in regulation on Thanksgiving in the Super Bowl era (since 1966), per CBS Sports Research.
In the Dallas Cowboys ' home game, they blew a 21-point lead in a 39-38 defeat against the Philadelphia Eagles — the largest on Thanksgiving Day in NFL history. That game ended with Eagles kicker Jake Elliott hitting a 59-yard, game-winning kick with two seconds left. To close out the nightcap between the Buffalo Bills and the Kansas City Chiefs , Bills kicker Tyler Bass drained the longest game-winning field goal (57 yards) as time expired in Buffalo franchise history, according to CBS Sports Research.
What other attention-grabbing events could take place across the rest of the NFL's Week 12 lineup of games? Let's take a look at five bold predictions.
The Minnesota Vikings ' No. 1 defense got shelled in Week 11. Despite the 35-10 thrashing against the top-seeded 49ers (9-1) on "Sunday Night Football" last week, the Vikings' Brian Flores-led defense is still the NFL's best. They lead the league in the following defensive metrics through 11 weeks:
Flores, Minnesota's defensive coordinator, was asked earlier this week if San Francisco's grilling of his defense over the middle of the field is replicable by other NFL teams . Here's what he told reporters about that.
"It's certainly replicable. I think that's something our opponents have tried previously in games. This isn't the first time we have seen some of those things; we just didn't play them as well," Flores said. "But again, against a team like the 49ers, we have to be more precise."
The Vikings will be much more precise and sack Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . at least eight times, the most a quarterback has been sacked in a game this season. Yes, Penix has the second-fastest average time to throw (2.71 seconds) in the NFL this season, but the Vikings sacked Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love , who averages the fastest average time to throw in the entire league (2.69 seconds), eight times in Week 10. They'll get to Penix Jr. over and over again to release their pent-up frustration about the 49ers embarrassing them on "Sunday Night Football."
Quarterback J.J. McCarthy has been more along for the ride than driving the bus that is the NFC East-leading New York Giants (6-3-1). McCarthy has three total touchdowns and three turnovers in his past six starts, games in which the Giants have emerged victorious five out of six times.
Against the sagging Indianapolis Colts (3-8), McCarthy will throw a career-high four passing touchdowns. McCarthy's collegiate rival C.J. Stroud carved the Colts up (194 yards, three touchdowns and an interception on 21-of-27 passing) in a 26-3 "Thursday Night Football" win in Week 11. McCarthy will do so on Sunday and have the best game of his career.
All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr . is on an early tear for the Houston Texans , leading the NFL with 11.5 sacks through 10 games played. That's tied for the most sacks in the first 10 games of a season in Texans history, along with J.J. Watt (2012 and 2015). However, the rest of Houston's defense hasn't been at Anderson Jr.'s level this season. The Texans went from the league's No. 2 scoring defense in 2025 (17.4 points per game allowed) to average (22.2 points per game allowed, 16th in the NFL) in 2026.
That will spell doom for the Texans against their longtime boogeyman Derrick Henry . The Baltimore Ravens running back has the most career rushing yards of any player against the Texans with 1,611 yards against Houston in eight career games against them. Henry also has the most 200-yard rushing games of any player in NFL history (seven), and four of them have come against Houston. That makes him the only player in NFL history with more than two 200-yard rushing games against a single opponent, per CBS Sports Research.
Henry, who is 32-years-old and averaging a career-low 4.0 yards per carry, will turn back the clock to rush for over 150 yards against the Texans in Week 12. He averaged a season-high 7.2 yards per carry on 13 carries for 94 yards and a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers in Week 11, and Henry will build on that for a huge game against Houston on Sunday.
The 49ers (9-1) have the best record in the NFC, and it's not just because of their high-flying offense. San Francisco also has the NFL's best run defense, allowing a league-low 81.2 rushing yards per game this season.
However, Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet will have his first 100-yard rushing game of the 2026 season against San Francisco on Sunday. He tore his ACL against the 49ers in the divisional round of the playoffs in January, and he is set to play his fourth game of the season in 2026. Each week, his workload and production have increased. Charbonnet totaled 23 yards rushing on six carries in Week 8, 77 yards rushing on 16 carries in Week 9 and 94 yards rushing on 20 carries in Week 10.
"It's remarkable," Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters . "I'd say he's probably playing some of his best football, if not his best football of his career, which is again a tribute to him...I mean, you could argue he looks the best he's looked since we've been able to be here the last three years, which is saying something."
Charbonnet continues his upward trajectory with a 100-yard game against the NFL's No. 1 rushing defense in Week 12.
New Orleans Saints five-time Pro Bowl running back Alvin Kamara is on his last legs in 2026. He is 31 years old and playing out the final season of his Saints contract while averaging a career-low 3.2 yards per carry. New Orleans signed Travis Etienne Jr. away from the Jacksonville Jaguars on a four-year, $48 million contract to be their new bell cow back, but Kamara has scored all three Saints touchdowns in their past two games despite only having seven touches.
Despite facing the AFC North-leading Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) and Etienne back to having a full workload after his early-season hamstring injury, Kamara will find the end zone twice while having 10 or fewer touches.

title: Tom Brady torches Aaron Rodgers for 'private things becoming public' after Steelers' release
summary: The seven-time Super Bowl champion expressed disapproval of how Rodgers handled his beef with Mike McCarthy
full_text:
From one future Pro Football Hall of Famer to another, Tom Brady was disappointed by Aaron Rodgers' comments this week leading to his release from the Pittsburgh Steelers . After the team announced it was benching Rodgers for Mason Rudolph on Tuesday night ahead of Friday's game against the Denver Broncos, Rodgers publicly lashed out at coach Mike McCarthy, embarrassing him on a national stage.
Rodgers accused McCarthy of falling asleep during team meetings, not being on task on the job and failing to connect with players. Brady said "nobody wins when the family feuds" and disagreed with how Rodgers handled the situation.
"In response to that, the sanctity of an NFL locker room is a very sacred place, and we should never lose track of that as players," Brady said during the second half of Thursday's Eagles-Cowboys game. "It's a privilege to be in that locker room. You're fighting with your teammates. You're fighting coaches. You're always acting as a team together. It shouldn't always be the place for private things to become public; that's what I'll say."
Brady, who went 3–2 in his career against the former longtime Green Bay Packers quarterback, including a 31–26 victory in the 2021 NFC Championship Game, said Rodgers' admissions were selfish given his role on the team.
"Certainly a Hall of Fame career, and he's a tremendous player, and it has nothing to do with his play style," Brady said. "I was fortunate to be around a lot of great teammates over the years, and what made a great teammate to me was, you cared about your teammates and your coaches and you cared about what the team was trying to accomplish.
"And that supersedes any individual aspect of your game that you want to promote. I was in a great locker room. I played for my teammates, I played for my coaches."
McCarthy took the high road hours after Rodgers' remarks this week.
"He has a lot of opinions, and there's things we've always talked about. I considered those private conversations," McCarthy said before Friday's game with the Broncos. "There's a long history there. Clearly [a] difference of opinion."
McCarthy and Rodgers were part of a braintrust in Green Bay that lasted 13 seasons, including a Super Bowl XLV victory in 2011. McCarthy said his only focus this week was beating the Broncos and said this team had the "opportunity to grow today because of the things that were said" from Rodgers.
"And all those teammates have to — they're going to go and regroup, and that's going to hopefully galvanize them toward, you know, you feel like you're in the foxhole together," Brady said.
Former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin called the dispute between Rodgers and McCarthy a "dumpster fire" and expressed "general sadness" that the relationship between professionals would end this way.
"Sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career in the quarterback Aaron Rodgers, and just at the macro level whether it's organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum," Tomlin said Wednesday on The Pat McAfee Show . "Those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football."
author: Brad Crawford

title: Hope is now gone for Cowboys' season after historic Thanksgiving collapse vs. Eagles
summary: After two franchise-record meltdowns this season, the Cowboys can say goodbye to their NFC East title hopes
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- AT&T Stadium went from a full-throated roar to so deathly quiet that one could hear a scoop of cranberry sauce drop with two seconds remaining on the clock on Thanksgiving Day.
When Philadelphia Eagles kicker Jake Elliott's 59-yard field goal sailed through the uprights to complete a 21-point comeback, the largest Thanksgiving comeback in NFL history, the sensation Dallas Cowboys owner/general manager Jerry Jones felt when the stadium scoreboard read "Eagles 39, Cowboys 38" was numb. Nothingness. Emptiness. "Numbing" was the feeling Jones kept going back to outside the locker room postgame.
"The word is numbing. Numbing at the end," Jones said postgame. "I didn't expect to be having this kind of conversation with you guys about 10 minutes left in that game."
The Cowboys (5-7) desperately needed a win on Thanksgiving to get back to .500 and maintain a spot nipping at the heels of the NFC East-leading New York Giants (6-3-1). They were well on their way to doing so after quarterback Dak Prescott's 12-yard scoring strike out to running back Javonte Williams put Dallas on top 28-10 at halftime. Following kicker Brandon Aubrey draining a 59-yard field goal with 3:35 left in the third quarter, the Cowboys' lead ballooned to 21.
Then, everything came crashing down. Eagles fill-in quarterback Joe Milton, one of Dallas' backup quarterbacks up until October when the Eagles signed him off of the Dallas practice squad, carved the Cowboys up like Thanksgiving turkey, throwing for 331 yards and an interception on 21-of-31 passing with a 15-yard rushing touchdown. He hit on touchdown passes of 50 yards and 45 yards to wide receiver DeVonta Smith (200 yards receiving and two touchdowns on 11 catches) as well as on a 24-yarder to rookie first-round pick wide receiver Makai Lemon . No defense could have possessed a greater understanding of an opposing quarterback's tendencies than Milton, someone they worked against every day in practice as their scout team quarterback up until just over a month ago.
Oh, and this happened against an Eagles team (4-7) that is a husk of the squad that steamrolled the entire league en route to a Super Bowl title at the end of the 2024 season. They entered Thanksgiving Thursday without Super Bowl MVP quarterback Jalen Hurts (blood clots) and All-Pro linebacker Zack Baun (back). They also lost running back Saquon Barkley (stinger), cornerback Cooper DeJean (concussion) and tight end Dallas Goedert (shoulder) during the game. Six-time Pro Bowl right tackle Lane Johnson retired in-season a number of weeks ago. It didn't matter.
Aubrey, who signed a four-year, $28 million extension with $20 million guaranteed that made him the NFL's highest-paid kicker this past offseason, missed a 40-yard field goal that would have put the Cowboys up 11 with 3:42 left to play. A blocked punt returned for a touchdown made the Eagles believe they could come back with the margin trimmed down to seven, with 13:46 left to play.
After the special teams' shakiness, coach Brian Schottenheimer decided to put the football in Prescott's hands on a game-clinching fourth-and-1 at the Eagles' 39 with 55 seconds remaining. However, Prescott got sacked for a nine-yard loss, and the Eagles' next drive ended with Elliott's game-winner with two seconds left on the clock.
Prescott was left stunned and agreed with Jones that numb was an appropriate way to describe his postgame emotions. The light was clearly gone from the ever-resilient and optimistic quarterback's eyes at his postgame press conference. After all, his 2026 Cowboys are the only team in NFL history to average over 30 points per game (31.3 points per game, the second most in the NFL this season) and have a losing record through 12 games, according to CBS Sports Research.
"Pretty stunning," Prescott said. "[Numb is] a good description for how I'm feeling right now. Yeah, especially this soon after the game, understanding the plays left out there, the plays we could have made, should have made and the mistakes we had."
Perhaps the most deflating part of Dallas blowing a 14-plus-point lead at home against a team with a losing record is that this wasn't the Cowboys' first time doing so. Prior to November, Dallas was 202-0-1 when leading by that much in the fourth quarter at home in the 67-season existence of Cowboys football. Fast forward to Thanksgiving, and the Cowboys have lost twice this month in that situation against rebuilding teams with backup quarterbacks.
Dallas allowed Gardner Minshew and the NFC West bottom-feeding Arizona Cardinals (3-8) to dig out of a 24-10 hole and win 33-30 in overtime. That was the worst loss of the 2026 season until Thursday. The Cowboys don't play again for 11 more days when they suit up again in Seattle against the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks (6-4) on "Monday Night Football." This is one of the rare cases where having more time to process the grief from a letdown loss might be a bad thing.
"Hopefully it helps, but it's definitely going to sting during it and particularly these next couple of days," Prescott said of the 11-day layoff. "But as we get back into the building, we can't allow this to hold us back."
The problem for Dallas is that the Cardinals and Eagles home losses are hardly the only soul-crushing defeats of the year. Here's a quick rundown if you've lost count.
Days after the 49ers loss, Schottenheimer stripped first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker of defensive play-calling duties while still keeping him on the coaching staff. He gave defensive play-calling to Parker's mentor Mike Pettine, who was recently hired on staff out of retirement as a senior defensive assistant.
The hits just keep on coming, and this latest one prevented Dallas from getting back to .500 at 6-6 ahead of playing the NFL's second-toughest remaining strength of schedule. Their final five opponents have a combined winning percentage of .608, so this loss essentially erased all hope for an NFC East division title run.
"The message shouldn't have to motivate you, shouldn't have to inspire," Prescott said about how to keep the team together. "It shouldn't be the reason that you go win, or the message wasn't good enough, and it's the reason that we lost. So there's got to be a sense of accountability that doesn't fall on the messenger."
* First team ever with two home losses in a season up 14-plus points in the fourth quarter, per CBS Sports Research
Dallas surrendered 22 fourth-quarter points on defense to an Eagles team that hadn't scored more than that amount in an entire game since Week 2, Philadelphia's last game before their seven-game losing streak ended in Week 11 against the Pittsburgh Steelers, which ended up imploding that franchise .
The Cowboys' 2026 season isn't officially over, but it might as well be. Games at the 2025 NFC finalists — the Seahawks (6-4) and Los Angeles Rams (7-4) — loom, as do matchups with the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3), the Giants (6-3-1) and the surging Washington Commanders (4-5-1). Dallas has too much scar tissue, both mentally and physically, to realistically get back into the NFC East race.
"I mean, it's a gut check for sure. Told the guys that," Schottenheimer said postgame. "Division football. That's what we talked about in the locker room."
Prescott said everyone from the top down in the Cowboys franchise needs to take some time off this weekend before hitting the ground running.
"And [we have to] get back to it with more urgency and better than ever individually and collectively to give it our best chance," Prescott said.
But are these battered and scarred Cowboys able to successfully respond and bounce back from yet another gut-wrenching loss? The face of the franchise quarterback who is tasked with being Mr. Perfect on and off the field in Dallas couldn't answer that question definitively.
Prescott likely couldn't do so because, deep down, he already knows: The 2026 season will go down as…

title: NFL Week 12 grades for Thanksgiving: Cowboys choke their way to a 'D,' Bears earn 'B' for big win
summary: Caleb Williams delivers late magic to Rome Odunze in a wild shootout, while Detroit's defense collapses and Jordan Love struggles without Christian Watson
full_text:
Welcome to the Turkey edition of the Week 12 grades!
Playing on Thanksgiving is one of the NFL's longest running traditions, but this year, it's not just about Thanksgiving. The league is trying to take over nearly the entire week.
The holiday slate of games kicked off on Wednesday night with the Rams beating the Packers 26-13 in the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game. Hopefully you enjoyed the NFL's newest tradition, because it will be sticking around. The league is planning on making this game an annual event .
The game between the Rams and Packers served as the appetizer for possibly the craziest Thanksgiving slate ever. All three matchups were decided by a game-winning score in the final five seconds, marking the first time that's every happened on Thanksgiving in NFL history.
The Turkey Day action started in Detroit , where the Bears pulled off a dramatic 39-35 win in a game where Caleb Williams threw a touchdown pass to Rome Odunze with just three seconds left to help Chicago stun Detroit. The two teams combined for 1,007 yards of offense, which is the second-most ever in a Thanksgiving game.
The game in Detroit was crazy, but the second game of the day in Dallas might have topped it , with the Cowboys blowing a 31-10 lead in a 39-38 loss to the Eagles. It was the largest blown lead on Thanksgiving in NFL history. It also made the Cowboys the first team in NFL history to blow a lead of 14 points or more in the fourth quarter TWICE at home in a single season.
The Turkey Day nightcap took place in Buffalo, where the weather shut down the offensive shootout that we were all expecting to see. With temperatures under 40 degrees and a steady rain falling for the entire game, the Josh Allen vs. Patrick Mahomes showdown turned into a defensive struggle with the Bills coming out on top in a 13-10 thriller. The Bills might want to ask the NFL if they can play on Thanksgiving every year, because Josh Allen is now 4-0 on the holiday.
There will be one more game coming on Friday (Broncos at Steelers), but before we get to that, let's hand out some grades for the four games that have been played so far.
author: John Breech

title: NFL Thanksgiving overreactions: Bears a shoo-in for NFC North title? Should Joe Milton be a full-time QB1?
summary: Plus, is Jahmyr Gibbs truly an MVP candidate?
full_text:
You're probably on your second or third nap by now, right? No, we're not saying you're Mike McCarthy, nor are we saying you could coach the Pittsburgh Steelers (or Green Bay Packers , for that matter). We're merely pointing out that you've consumed enough tryptophan from the Thanksgiving turkey that you're probably a little lethargic. And if that means you dozed off during some of the NFL's Thanksgiving triple-header, that's alright. We're here to help you sift through what went down over the holiday slate and make you sound smart.
Given that all three games were in individual windows and the entire nation was huddled around the table to watch them, there will be a lot of opinions that spew out of them. Some will be justified, while others you'll rightfully tilt your head, squint your eyebrows, and judge silently. We'll make you the former.
Below, we'll go through some of the top storylines from each Thanksgiving game and determine if they're something to take seriously or if they're merely overreactions.
Overreaction vs. reality : Overreaction
When it comes to statement wins, you won't find many bigger than the Bears rolling into Ford Field and pulling off the 39-35 win over the Lions . Chicago scored the game-winning touchdown with just three seconds left in regulation and erased an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit. That victory puts the Bears at 9-2 on the season, and that has them atop the NFC North.
THAT'S A TOUCHDOWN!!!!!! 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/IOUvYvWOHa
Naturally, confidence is sky-high that Chicago will eventually secure the division title for the second straight year, and rightfully so. How can you not feel that way after such a marquee win? Should they be printing the hats and T-shirts, however? That's a different discussion entirely.
While Chicago owns the inside track, the NFC North is far from being solidified. The Bears still have three division matchups on the docket over their final six games of the season. Outside of facing NFC North rivals, they'll also square off against the Jaguars and Bills . The only sure-fire victory is when they visit the Miami Dolphins in Week 14. With the margins still razor-thin, and the Bears currently 1-2 in the division, they are not on as solid ground as this latest win would suggest.
Overreaction vs. reality : Overreaction
At the end of the day, the MVP is a quarterback's award. You may not like it, but that's the reality. Gibbs has been otherworldly this season and just put together a historic performance on Thanksgiving. He logged 21 carries for 205 yards, three touchdowns, and five receptions for 47 yards. Those are the second-most rushing yards on Thanksgiving in NFL history, and Gibbs tied Barry Sanders (1997) for the most rushing touchdowns on Thanksgiving by a Lions player in franchise history.
Gibbs has joined Eric Dickerson (1983) and Priest Holmes (2002) as the only players with at least 1,700 scrimmage yards and 18 total touchdowns in the first 11 games of a season in NFL history.
JAHMYR GIBBS 70-YARD TOUCHDOWN 🔥 pic.twitter.com/w7oihVzrsd
Again, these numbers are bonkers and will almost certainly give Gibbs the inside track at the Offensive Player of the Year award. Those who Jim Nantz pointed out were chanting "MVP" at Ford Field on Thursday, however, will be disappointed. That'll go to Joe Burrow , Brock Purdy , or whichever quarterback endears himself to the NFL at large.
He may deserve it, but the hardware Gibbs will be eyed for is OPOY and not MVP.
Overreaction vs. reality : Reality
Jalen Hurts is the obvious top option at quarterback once he returns to full health. We're not talking about Hurts' standing as QB1 in Philadelphia. However, Howie Roseman has once again pulled a rabbit out of his hat. He plucked Joe Milton III off Dallas' practice squad, and you can't deny that what we've seen out of Milton doesn't warrant a longer look as a full-time starter in the NFL.
JOE MILTON AND DEVONTA SMITH DO IT AGAIN PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hjaMzRC3ub
It might not be with the Eagles , but you can't deny the raw ability that Milton possesses. The arm talent is obvious, and he was able to hang in against Dallas in a high-profile Thanksgiving matchup on the road in just his third career start.
The Eagles have done a fantastic job at parlaying assets into future draft capital. It's not out of the realm of possibility that they do the same with Milton -- who'll be a restricted free agent -- this offseason. For a team searching for a long-term starter at quarterback, why wouldn't you roll the dice on someone like Milton, who is 26 years old? He has far higher upside than Kirk Cousins , Geno Smith , Kyler Murray , and Daniel Jones , who'll also be free agents (albeit unrestricted) this offseason.
Overreaction vs. reality : Reality
Nail, meet coffin. The Cowboys can put their playoff hopes to bed, unofficially. After blowing a 21-point lead to the Eagles on Thanksgiving, Dallas drops to 5-7 on the season. For the moment, they're in third place in the NFC East, and the path to the playoffs feels nonexistent, even if mathematically there's still a chance.
INTERCEPTED! EAGLES COMPLETE THE COMEBACK! pic.twitter.com/ymk4TF0H8K
They already are on the wrong side of the tiebreaker with the Giants after losing the season opener. They still have a Week 17 matchup to fully determine if that tiebreaker will be a factor. If not, it'll come down to division record, where New York has the advantage through Week 12 (2-1-1 vs. 2-2).
More dire for Dallas, the road ahead may make division and head-to-head tiebreakers moot. After falling to the Joe Milton-led Eagles, the Cowboys will now have to endure a three-game stretch of facing the Seahawks in Seattle, the Rams in Los Angeles (after the Week 14 bye), and then the Jacksonville Jaguars before they see the Giants. They'll, in all likelihood, be an underdog in all three of those games. If the oddsmakers are proved right, they're 5-10 before they kick off against the Giants.
After Thursday's showing, it's hard to have any confidence that they'll persevere and make a legitimate push to a division title.
Overreaction vs. reality : Overreaction
It's not that Buffalo won't eventually land the No. 1 seed in the AFC, but it's hardly secure at this point even after a critical head-to-head win over Kansas City. The Bills are 10-1 on the season, which has them on the inside track for the first-round bye at the moment. However, the upcoming month does present some challenges. After heading up to New England to face a Drake Maye-less Patriots , Buffalo will face the Packers (road), Bears, and Broncos (road). That could result in some losses that open the door for some other contenders in the conference.
Specifically, that Broncos matchup in Denver looms large on Christmas Day as Sean Payton's team is currently the closest to Buffalo for the top spot in the conference. Again, the Bills are in a great position to be the No. 1 seed, but we've got a long way to go before locking in first-round bye plans.

title: Prisco's Week 12 NFL picks: Browns over Raiders, Steelers overcome issues to upset Broncos
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 12 picks, including the Steelers to upset the Broncos on Black Friday
full_text:
That's three consecutive winning weeks for me, which is a big positive. I was 7-6 against the spread last week and 9-4 straight up. My straight-up record is now 104-58-1, while my ATS record is 75-85-3.
I can see .500 now after being buried under it at the start of the season.
This is Thanksgiving Week, which is usually a good week for me. And I feel good about the picks.
It starts Wednesday night with a good one between the Packers and Rams , and it ends Monday night with the Bucs against the Panthers . I really like the teams in both of those games.
We have NFL games Wednesday, Thursday (Thanksgiving), Friday, Sunday and Monday. What a feast.
I know I will as the climb to .500 ATS continues.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
This Friday game pits two teams who would be in the playoffs right now. But the Steelers have lost two straight and haven't looked good. Denver has won six in a row. But I think the Steelers will find a way to show up and win this one behind their running game. It won't be pretty, but the Steelers will find a way.
Pick: Steelers 21, Broncos 20
The Bengals are coming off a tough road loss at Washington, while the Saints are playing consecutive road games. The Bengals offense didn't score as it had in Monday's game, but that will change here. Joe Burrow gets back on track. Bengals big.
Pick: Bengals 37, Saints 20
The Giants are coming off an impressive victory over the Jaguars , while the Colts are coming off a bye. They released quarterback Daniel Jones , which means Anthony Richardson will be starting. The Giants' defense should dominate in this one. The Colts have packed it in, so the Giants take it.
The Jets are playing consecutive road games, while the Dolphins are home for the first time in three weeks. The Jets played well in beating the Chargers last week, while Miami lost to the Bills. The Dolphins are limited on offense, but the Jets' defense has struggled. Look for Miami to hang around.
Pick: Jets 23, Dolphins 21
The Vikings are home after getting blown out by the 49ers in Mexico. The Falcons are off a bye. The Minnesota offense struggled against the 49ers, but the Falcons have had defensive problems lately. Look for the Minnesota defense to get back on track as well. Vikings take it.
Pick: Vikings 28, Falcons 14
The Jaguars are coming off a bad showing in the loss to the Giants, while Tennessee gave up 51 to the Cowboys last week. Ouch. The Jaguars scored 40 against them two weeks ago. They won't get that many here, but it will still be ugly as Trevor Lawrence and the passing game get back on track.
Pick: Jaguars 33, Titans 13
This is essentially a playoff game of sorts for these two. The loser is pretty much done. The Texans are home off a Thursday game, while the Ravens are playing consecutive road games. Edge Houston. The Texans have played well on offense, and the Ravens' defense is a mess. Look for a big day for C.J. Stroud .
Pick: Texans 31, Ravens 23
This was once scheduled for prime time, but it was moved because both teams have flopped this year. The Patriots will start Tommy DeVito for the injured Drake Maye . That's a problem. The Chargers might not have Justin Herbert (concussion) either, which would put D.J. Uiagalelei in as the starter. He's thrown seven passes in his career. Even so, give me the home team here.
Pick: Chargers 23, Patriots 16
The Commanders are coming off an impressive home victory Monday night over the Bengals, while the Cardinals got rocked by the Chiefs last week. Arizona has big-time issues and fired the defensive coordinator this week. That defense will struggle to stop Jayden Daniels . The Commanders stay hot.
Pick: Commanders 30, Cardinals 19
The 49ers have the best record in the NFC and seem to be cruising to the division title. But Seattle can slow that talk down here with a victory. That will be tough to do on the road. Look for a lower-scoring game in the second division game between the two — the 49ers won the first — and San Francisco will win it late.
Pick: 49ers 21, Seahawks 17
This has been flexed to prime time because the Browns would be a playoff team right now. Plus, the Raiders have rookie Fernando Mendoza making his third start. The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, and Cleveland is off a bye. Big edge to the Browns as they win it behind their defense.
Pick: Browns 27, Raiders 19
The Panthers can take a stronghold on the division with a victory here.  They come in with defensive issues, but the Bucs have problems in the passing game. So what gives? I think the Tampa Bay defense will play well here and the Bucs will run it right at Carolina to win it like they did in the first meeting.

Dak Prescott has thrown nine touchdown passes and no picks in the past two weeks. The Dallas offense is rolling. The Eagles defense will be a challenge. Joe Milton, who was on the Cowboys ' practice squad, will start at quarterback for the Eagles. Dallas will play better defense against him this week. Cowboys big.

This is the game of the week. Patrick Mahomes vs. Josh Allen . What's not to like as two of the best in the league go at it? The Bills have played much better defense lately, but they've faced a bunch of backup quarterbacks. Not here. So look for both passers to have good days. title: NFL Week 12 picks: Our experts face off on Broncos at Steelers, Seahawks at 49ers and more
summary: CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games
full_text:
Welcome to the most special week in the NFL . We watched the Los Angeles Rams defeat the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night, and now, we have three exciting Thanksgiving matchups to digest this "Turkey Day."
Football fans suffered through many sleepy Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions Thanksgiving matchups over the years. Now, this 1 p.m. game on Thursday is expected to be one of the most exciting holiday matchups in recent memory. After that, the Dallas Cowboys will welcome Joe Milton III and the Philadelphia Eagles to AT&T Stadium. Both teams are coming off wins, and the Cowboys need this game if they want to keep pace in the NFC East. At the end of the night, we have a potential AFC Championship preview to watch when the Buffalo Bills host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs . This is just the second game in NFL history to feature two teams coming off at least three straight 17-point victories.
Which teams should you pick in Week 12, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 25 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.
Credit to CBS Sports Research
Dajani ( Broncos -3.5): Aaron Rodgers lobbed a grenade into the Pittsburgh Steelers facility as he exited it this week. Going on national television and calling your coach a narcoleptic, unhealthy, lazy person who doesn't even know the franchise he works for is insane. So, this is a moment that will ultimately rally the locker room, or cause them to completely fall apart. Pick which side you'd like. The Steelers have also won and covered in six straight home games. This seems like an appropriate time for that streak to end   … Prediction: Broncos 20, Steelers 13
Dubin (Broncos -3.5): After the disaster that hit the Steelers this week, I just can't see them keeping the game close against the Broncos. No, I don't think they'll get the backup quarterback bounce from Mason Rudolph . I don't trust the Broncos as far as Bo Nix or I can throw them, but given the state the Steelers' locker room has to be in right now, I think you have to roll with Denver to cover this one with relative ease.  … Prediction: Broncos 24, Steelers 10
Dajani ( Ravens +7): I have the Houston Texans winning this game, but seven points seems a bit high. C.J. Stroud is playing some great football, but his production has been overshadowed by a defense that has fallen from No. 2 in points allowed per game in 2025, to 17th this year. The Texans are 1-8 against the spread in their last nine home games following an ATS win. I'll take Baltimore to keep it close… Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 18
Dubin (Ravens +7): The Ravens have now lost six straight, but they've lost the two games in the Jacoby Brissett era by a combined five points despite turning the ball over six times in those contests. If they can just limit the giveaways, I think they might even be able to pull off an upset against a Houston team that hasn't exactly lit the world on fire this year. Either way, I think they can keep it close by throwing on a surprisingly vulnerable Texans pass defense.  … Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 20
Dajani ( 49ers -3): Sam Darnold is expected to return this week, and he's accounted for 10 touchdowns compared to nine interceptions in seven starts this season. If you throw out the season opener that Drew Lock finished and won, Darnold is 2-4 as a starter this season.
Believe it or not, San Francisco is 0-9 against the spread in its last nine home divisional games. With the number at a field goal, the 49ers have a good chance to end that streak this week. What they did to the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City last Sunday night was shocking. The 49ers should be headlining everyone's NFL power rankings if they weren't already. Their 0.19 EPA per play is the best mark since the 2018 Chiefs, and they have the best offensive success rate (54.8%) by any team in a season since at least 2000 … Prediction: 49ers 24, Seahawks 20
Dubin (49ers -3): I reserve the right to flip this prediction to Seattle if Brock Purdy is out with his ankle injury, but if he's in, I just think that this San Francisco offense is a buzzsaw that can't really be stopped — even by the Dark Side defense. Remember, they dropped 32 points on Seattle the last time out. And they've scored 35 or more in each of their three games since returning from the bye. I don't think they can be stopped when everyone is healthy.  … Prediction: 49ers 30, Seahawks 23
Dajani ( Raiders +4.5): Maybe part of me is rooting for Fernando Mendoza in his first primetime start? Last week against the Broncos, he threw for 267 yards, three touchdowns and an interception. It was a solid performance, even though the rookie was sacked five times. The Raiders certainly have their weaknesses. They are on pace to become the first team since the 2022 Texans to finish bottom two in both rushing yards per game and opponent rushing yards per game, but this 6-4 Cleveland Browns team hasn't won a game by five-plus points since LAST YEAR. That gives me some optimism Vegas can cover  … Prediction: Browns 24, Raiders 20
Dubin (Raiders +4.5): I will continue to stand on the idea that this Browns team is not good. Every one of Cleveland's wins has required a game-winning drive in the final minutes of the fourth quarter. The Browns have been out-gained in seven of their 10 games and are somehow 6-4. That is not remotely sustainable. I think the Raiders pull off the upset behind Fernando Mendoza and a returning Brock Bowers . … Prediction: Raiders 21, Browns 17
Dajani ( Panthers +3): I'm going to take the points with the Panthers because they are playing on the road. If you were unaware, Carolina is 3-2 away from Charlotte, and has a +8 turnover differential. The Panthers have a -4 turnover differential at home, and allow 37.4 points per game at Bank of America Stadium! For whatever reason, the Panthers are a better team on the road.
It's true that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers throttled the Panthers in Week 7, 43-13, but I think Carolina splits the season series. The Buccaneers are 1-9 against the spread in their last 10 home games, and 0-7 against the spread in their last seven home primetime games. Baker Mayfield is a shocking 1-13 in primetime since 2021, so I'll back Bryce Young … Prediction: Panthers 28, Buccaneers 27
Dubin (Buccaneers -3): The last time these two teams played, the Bucs racked up 258 rushing yards. The Panthers' run defense then limited the Packers, Broncos and Saints over the next three games, but the Ravens hit them up for 157 yards last week. I don't see much reason to believe that the Bucs will be slowed on the ground, and I don't trust Carolina's offense to score enough to get the Bucs out of their run-heavy orientation.  … Prediction: Buccaneers 20, Panthers 16
Dajani (Bears -1.5): I can't remember being more excited for a Thanksgiving Day game, as the Bears and Lions are two of the best teams in the NFL. What I keep going back to is that the Bears are 6-0 while averaging 33.7 points in games where Caleb Williams starts and finishes. Then, factor in how much improved this Chicago defense looks with the addition of Jeffery Simmons . In Weeks 1-7, they ranked dead last in both yards per play (6.3) and yards per attempt (8.7). Over the last four weeks, the Bears now rank in the top 10 in both categories. Chicago has been swept by Detroit in each of the last two seasons. I think the Bears are done with losing to Dan Campbell … Prediction: Bears 30, Lions 28
Dubin (Lions +1.5): These are two incredibly evenly-matched teams, but it seems like Detroit has more matchup advantages offensively against Chicago's improved defense than the Bears do against the Lions' own improved unit. With Detroit also getting the benefit of home-field advantage, we're rolling with the Lions to win a close one as a home underdog.  … Prediction: Lions 31, Bears 30
Dajani (Cowboys -8.5): I don't…
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin on Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy saga: 'It's a dumpster fire'
summary: Tomlin revealed his thoughts on the entire Rodgers-McCarthy mess on Thursday night
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are facing a unique kind of adversity as they prepare for their "Black Friday" matchup against the Denver Broncos . Late Tuesday night, the team announced it was benching future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph . On Wednesday, Rodgers appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" and lashed out against Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy. That led to his release.
Rodgers' attack of his head coach felt personal and unprecedented. On national television, he accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings, not putting in the work required to prepare for upcoming opponents, and failing to connect with players in his first season as the lead man in Pittsburgh. The breaking point, according to Rodgers, was when McCarthy, 63, broke down the team saying, "1-2-3 Packers !" at halftime of Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles . McCarthy last coached the Packers in 2018. The coach admitted using the wrong team name during a press conference on Wednesday.
Fans and former players have not been shy in voicing their opinions on this wild saga, but one man we all wanted to hear from about this situation was Mike Tomlin. The new NBC analyst spent 19 years as the head coach of the Steelers, winning Super Bowl XLIII with the franchise in 2009. He famously never registered a losing season with the Steelers, and coached Rodgers during his final year as coach in 2025. During halftime of the Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills matchup on Thanksgiving, he revealed what he thought about Rodgers' actions in an interview with Mike Tirico.
Tomlin said he had a range of emotions hearing what Rodgers had to say about his new head coach, but the prevailing emotion was "general sadness."
"Sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career in the quarterback Aaron Rodgers, and just at the macro level whether it's organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum," Tomlin said. "Those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football."
Did it shock Tomlin that Rodgers went this route?
"It certainly did," Tomlin said. "Particularly because I know both men involved. [I] certainly had a lot of intimate work and development of relationships with Aaron over the last couple of years and have known and competed with Mike and respected and appreciated him as a coach for a long time."
Tomlin was asked how Rodgers was viewed in the locker room during his one year in Pittsburgh.
"He was beloved, and I'm not over-exaggerating that," Tomlin said. "He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture. To be engaged with teammates, and particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times they lose a little patience for the process or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, etcetera. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real natural way."
Tomlin was asked whether McCarthy can effectively lead this team for the rest of the season?
"You know it certainly created some challenges and 'challenges' is probably an understatement if all of those things are true. Certainly, the '1-2-3 Packers' is because he acknowledged that. But his ability to overcome that or inability to overcome that in my opinion is based on relationships, and the depth of those relationships and how those guys feel about him or how those guys buy into what he's selling. And so certainly he's been there a short period of time, and so it makes you wonder the level of that challenge. But it will be relationship-based, his ability to overcome the things that you mentioned."
Tirico asked Tomlin what his emotions were being a coach that was involved with the Steelers franchise for nearly two decades
"I'm upset about it, it's a dumpster fire," Tomlin said. "And I don't say that in a judgemental way; I've presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I'm sure Steeler Nation is upset."
There were plenty of bewildering aspects of this story. Tom Pelissero reported that frustration had been building behind the scenes among some players and coaches about Rodgers, who was calling plays himself. The quarterback reportedly went to McCarthy and demanded more changes related to the play-calling process. The coach received feedback from players and coaches indicating that's not what they wanted. Rodgers then issued an ultimatum: "Run things my way, or I quit."
ESPN's Brooke Pryor also reported that "multiple league sources corroborated Rodgers' account" during his appearance on ESPN. According to Pryor, "One source texted: 'It's all true.'" Anonymous team sources acknowledged Rodgers' claim that McCarthy fell asleep in meetings, according to The Athletic.
With that said, Rodgers did violate "the sanctity of the NFL locker room," as Tom Brady mentioned during his broadcast of the Thanksgiving matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys . One of the best quarterbacks in NFL history dropped a grenade in his building and walked away.
“Nobody wins when the family feuds.” @TomBrady on Aaron Rodgers pic.twitter.com/qLtmKL5oif
The Steelers locker room was expectedly mum on the situation, but quarterback Drew Allar did say it was " kinda sad to see ," because of the respect he has for Rodgers.
There were plenty of others that did not hold their tongues , however. Former Packers offensive lineman T.J. Lang alleged Rodgers was a hypocrite for blacklisting players for telling the truth at other times, then going scorched-earth this week. Lang even said he's in a group chat with "a whole lot of former teammates" that feel the exact same way that he does.
"I think it's despicable," Lang said on 97.1 The Ticket in Detroit. "I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has bitched about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media. He has blacklisted, I don't know how many former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he just he was sick of it."
TJ Lang on his former teammate Aaron Rodgers pic.twitter.com/0oiS3PybCn
Former Packers receiver and teammate James Jones said something very similar.
"How do you jump on Pat McAfee's show and say all this? Come on, man," Jones said on the Speakeasy podcast . "My text thread is full of texts and group chats with a lot of my teammates right now, and none are on 12's side, especially the ones that know Mike."
Another former Packers wideout in Greg Jennings chimed in on "First Things First," saying he was surprised by a lot of Rodgers' comments, and called his decision to air out this dirty laundry "distasteful."
"If you truly cared about more than just yourself, then you don't do this to everybody in that locker room that you just called brothers," Jennings said. "They are playing for something. You are no longer playing for anything."
@GregJennings weighs in on Steelers releasing former teammate Aaron Rodgers: “It was very distasteful… If you truly cared about more than just yourself, then you don’t do this to everybody in that locker room that you just called brothers... They are playing for something.” pic.twitter.com/whPyBO7K2p
Steelers president Art Rooney II released a statement on Thursday saying he stands behind McCarthy despite Rodgers' criticisms.
"I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he'll be our coach this season, next season and beyond," Rooney told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette . "The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that."

title: Despite no confidence in the direction of the team, Arizona Cardinals fans want Mike LaFleur to stay
summary: It definitely has been a tough season for the Arizona Cardinals and their fans, once again. For the Cardinals they made decisions in January that didn’t seem to make sense. Firing Jonathan Gannon and most of his staff, while retaining Monti Ossenfort didn’t track, especially without a clear picture of what the future looked like […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 08: Head coach Mike LaFleur of the Arizona Cardinals looks on prior to a game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on November 08, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images It definitely has been a tough season for the Arizona Cardinals and their fans, once again. For the Cardinals they made decisions in January that didn’t seem to make sense. Firing Jonathan Gannon and most of his staff, while retaining Monti Ossenfort didn’t track, especially without a clear picture of what the future looked like at quarterback. You can move on to a new coach and quarterback, or bring in a new coach with an established quarterback, but doing things the way the Cardinals did never seemed right for LaFleur. That’s why I get that 82% of you think Mike LaFleur should be back even if they move on from Ossenfort (truth be told I don’t know if they will move on from Monti). However, what I don’t get is what 20% of you see in this product that makes you confident in the direction of the franchise. The Cardinals look lost on both sides of the ball, they don’t have a building block on either side of the ball, except for Trey McBride, and there’s really no clear path to improvement. FanDuel Sportsbook opened the season at 3.5 for the Cardinals win total. They have the second easiest schedule the rest of the way, but they start with the Washington Commanders on Sunday and sit as seven-point home underdogs. We will see if they can eclipse their win total and wins a game at home for the first time in over 14 months.

It is easy to pick one thing: Watching Trey McBride play every week. That has been something to enjoy and be thankful to watch. It seems like every iteration of the Cardinals has a McBride. Larry Centers back in the 90’s, when fullbacks were still a thing. Aeneas Williams and Simeon Rice. title: The young players to watch for the Falcons after the bye
summary: Coming off the bye week, the Falcons need to show urgency following three humbling defeats. The performances have been unacceptable after exceeding expectations during the early portion of the season. While nobody expects this team to compete for the divisional title, they must be more competitive with younger players emerging in these challenging matchups. Facing […]
full_text: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 08: Cincinnati Bengals running back Chase Brown (30) faces off against Atlanta Falcons safety Xavier Watts (31) during the NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons at Santiago Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid, Spain on November 8, 2026. (Photo by Bob Kupbens/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Coming off the bye week, the Falcons need to show urgency following three humbling defeats. The performances have been unacceptable after exceeding expectations during the early portion of the season. While nobody expects this team to compete for the divisional title, they must be more competitive with younger players emerging in these challenging matchups. Facing the Vikings and Lions over the next two weeks will be massive litmus tests to see what this team is made of, knowing those teams are much more talented than them. There is still plenty to watch for even if the losses will likely continue to pile up in Atlanta. The trade deadline showed the organization is looking toward the future. What the front office did should resemble how the coaching staff approaches the second half of the season. Younger players should receive more opportunities to prove they are ready to elevate the team long-term. There are also growing, well-acclaimed players who need to show more than they currently have this season. Here are four players who could make their mark to help the Falcons build toward the future. Xavier Watts It’s not that the playmaking safety has been a liability. It’s more about failing to build on last year’s tremendous rookie season. The high-impact plays haven’t been there. Poor angles in the open field and missed coverage assignments are happening more often than expected. It all feels underwhelming when assessing Watts this season. You don’t see him making his presence felt anywhere near as much by closing in on passes and bursting in to make standout open-field tackles. There have been moments when he’s been around the ball, with two forced fumbles against Carolina and San Francisco. He also produced an interception and a pass breakup against Green Bay. It’s hard to pinpoint many other signature plays. Meanwhile, his tackling was abysmal against Tampa Bay, and his positioning in coverage against Cincinnati was all over the place. After setting the bar so high in his rookie season, he is falling well short of being a potential defensive cornerstone. With Jessie Bates traded to Jacksonville, the time is now for Watts to set the tone as one of the players the defense can build around. A player with his ball skills and intelligence should be making a greater impact. It’s not as if he’s consistently lining up as a deep-lying safety 15 to 20 yards away from plays. Jeff Ulbrich is moving him around often between the box and the slot, while handling those deep-lying responsibilities. He needs to start impacting games like he did last season. Kendal Daniels The rookie linebacker hasn’t been underwhelming or underutilized. His inclusion on the list comes down to taking on greater responsibility and making progress as a three-down linebacker. That has happened following Divine Deablo’s recent injury troubles. Even with Deablo’s imminent return, it would be encouraging to see Daniels have more opportunities as a three-down linebacker and be challenged in coverage as a loop defender in zone or in man coverage against tight ends. The fourth-round pick does look far more comfortable accelerating downhill and closing down run gaps. That doesn’t mean he shouldn’t play in more obvious passing downs. More challenges are needed to determine whether he can be a three-down linebacker the coaching staff can trust next season. As well as Harold Perkins Jr. has flashed in glimpses and should continue to earn more playing time, Daniels needs to be prioritized as a player who needs all the reps to grow into a well-rounded linebacker. There is plenty to be excited about watching him on tape as a tone-setter against the run. His long arms and strong instincts can make a difference in coverage, as Brock Purdy learned in Atlanta’s upset win. Whether Daniels grows in an expanded role as one of the more valuable defensive pieces will be pivotal for the coaching staff for the rest of the season. Zachariah Branch Before suffering a hamstring injury against Tampa Bay, the dynamic dual playmaking prospect was starting to earn more playing time. He received 19 snaps against Chicago and 23 against San Francisco, up from averaging 12 to 14 snaps at the start of the season. While his production was minimal in those matchups, it shows the coaching staff is trusting him more as a wide receiver. Although Branch will need to regain trust as a returner after fumbling twice against Chicago, he should be able to bounce back and bring the necessary explosiveness to bolster the team. More opportunities could help spark a fragmented offense while putting them in better field position as a returner. More reps as a receiver should help the Falcons determine his place in the offense’s long-term outlook. The upside is certainly there, particularly after the catch, as he proved on a huge third-down conversion against the Ravens. His change-of-direction ability and feel for space can make a real difference for a team searching for production through the air. Michael Penix Jr. could use as many high-percentage looks as possible with how he’s played in recent games. Branch’s skill set can provide that while he’s finding his niche as a pass catcher. Ethan Onianwa This is a purely speculative selection based on potential opportunity. Avieon Terrell and DeMarcco Hellams were both considered, but there is skepticism about each player. Terrell may not get many opportunities given how crowded the defensive back room is. Hellams doesn’t seem like a long-term answer at safety with his limited range in coverage. With Jawaan Taylor’s maddening penalties increasing and poor run blocking becoming a greater issue, it wouldn’t be surprising to see the coaching staff bench him once the team is completely out of the NFC South race. Onianwa earned encouraging reviews from the coaching staff during training camp. His measurables stood out coming out of Ohio State. There is plenty of reason to see what he is made of in the final stretch of the season against more favorable opposition. There is no way you would throw a seventh-round rookie into the fire against Brian Flores’ defense. Seeing what he is made of against primarily NFC South teams would be a plausible move. Offensive tackle will be a critical need for the Falcons in 2027. Why not see what a young, intriguing talent is made of to see if he can help a positional flaw? Even if he ends up only being a swing tackle option, the opportunity to give a player with his attributes reps needs to be maximized when the time is right, especially under Bill Callahan’s guidance.
