title: 4 key matchups to watch in Cincinnati Bengals vs. New Orleans Saints
summary: The 7-3 Cincinnati Bengals will host the 3-7 New Orleans Saints. The Bengals better not be overlooking another team under .500 after the performance they put on the field against Washington this past week. While the Saints haven’t had the season they were expecting, they are like everyone else in the National Football League and […]
full_text: The 7-3 Cincinnati Bengals will host the 3-7 New Orleans Saints . The Bengals better not be overlooking another team under .500 after the performance they put on the field against Washington this past week. While the Saints haven’t had the season they were expecting, they are like everyone else in the National Football League and can spring the upset on any given Sunday. Let’s take a look at some of the key matchups to watch for in this one. Orlando Brown Jr. vs. Chase Young Chase Young is having an incredible season for the New Orleans Saints. He is up to 42 pressures and 8 sacks in the 2026 season. While the defense as a whole has been underwhelming for New Orleans, Young and Carl Granderson are two pass rushers that can get after it at a high level. Granderson doesn’t have as many pressures as Young, but he has 8.5 on the year. Both guys will be given opportunities to match up against Orlando Brown Jr. this week. Orlando Brown Jr. has been playing really good football, but he is still the guy that all pass rushers would rather face instead of Amarius Mims for the Bengals. Brown has allowed just 3 total pressures with 0 sacks over his last two games. He will need to continue playing at that level when facing off against Chase Young and Carl Granderson this week. DJ Turner and Dax Hill vs. Chris Olave and Jordyn Tyson This should be a big test again this week for the secondary. Turner and Hill will be tasked with going up against Chris Olave and Jordyn Tyson. Olave is a former first round draft selection who has over 850 receiving yards this season. Tyson was the Saints’ first-round draft selection this year. While he has dealt with injuries throughout parts of the season, just 2 games ago he put up 100 receiving yards in a game. After what rookie Antonio Williams just did against this secondary, these receivers could be a big problem for Cincinnati this week. It has felt like Turner is trending in the wrong direction the last couple of weeks. If he wants to get paid like one of the best corners in the league, he needs to start playing like it. The same goes for Dax Hill. With both guys up for potential big contracts in free agency, now is the time they start putting more consistent performances on the field. Chase Brown vs. Kaden Elliss The New Orleans Saints are ranked 27th in run defense so far during the 2026 season. The Saints are allowing 129.8 yards per game rushing this year. Meanwhile, the Cincinnati Bengals are ranked 30th in rushing yards per game offensively. They are averaging only 79.4 rushing yards per game. Something has to give in this one. Chase Brown is coming off one of his worst performances of the season. He caught 5 passes for 30 yards, but he had two crucial drops as a receiver. He also had just 6 carries for 6 yards, which is an abysmal 1.0 yards per carry. The Bengals need a better performance from their top running back, or questions will continue about Samaje Perine potentially taking on a bigger role in the offense. Kaden Ellis is the leading tackler for the Saints. The veteran linebacker is effective at rushing the passer as well. That should mean that when he blitzes, we will see him versus Chase Brown, but we will also see that matchup with Brown rushing and receiving the ball out of the backfield.

title: Bengals vs. Saints odds, expert picks, and our prediction for Week 12 matchup
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals will be looking to get the ship back in the right direction after laying an egg on Monday Night Football. That will come against the New Orleans Saints, who will be making the trip to the Jungle. The Saints are a sneaky team in that all but two of their games have […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (1) runs into the end zone for a touchdown with 2:10 remaining in the fourth quarter during an NFL Week 6 game against the New Orleans Saints, Sunday, Oct. 16, 2022, at Mercedes-Benz Superdome in New Orleans. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Cincinnati Bengals will be looking to get the ship back in the right direction after laying an egg on Monday Night Football. That will come against the New Orleans Saints, who will be making the trip to the Jungle. The Saints are a sneaky team in that all but two of their games have been decided by less than eight points. Yes, they are 3-7, but this is not a team that should be taken lightly. They have already beaten the Cleveland Browns and the Baltimore Ravens (when Lamar Jackson was still healthy). The Bengals looked disjointed Monday night. The offense looked clunky, even in the second half when the weather let up. The defense gave up way too many big plays. Almost all ended up as just field goals, but that added up. Especially when they had the Washington Commanders in long down-and-distance situations. Here is how the oddsmakers and experts see this playing out: Odds The Bengals are currently 9.5-point favorites over the Saints at home, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . This would only be the third time this season that New Orleans would lose by more than that margin if Cincinnati covers. That isn’t to say it can’t happen. Especially with the Bengals potentially refocused, but it seems not very likely. The point total is set at 49.5 between the two teams. That is tied for the second-highest total of the week. It seems oddsmakers expect Joe Burrow and company to pop back up while the defense may still be a bit leaky to reach that. Expert Picks All of ESPN’s 11 experts are going with the Bengals CBS Sports has all seven experts taking Cincinnati to win All five of NFL.com’s experts are expecting the Bengals to get back in the W column NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from across the web — has Cincinnati receiving 99% of the picks for this game. Cincy Jungle Pick It really was a rough loss last week, but it is the kind of loss that should reinvigorate a good team into playing to their standards. There wasn’t really anything that happened Monday night that wasn’t fixable for this team. Offensively, other teams have tried doubling Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins while trying to put pressure on Burrow. Sometimes, it has worked better than others. Can the Saints replicate that? I’d say probably not. Defensively, the big plays sprung back up. Running backs and receivers were easily picking up chunks of yards on runs and passes where the receivers were in open space. They managed to bend but not break, but some of that was also Washington making mistakes of their own. You would think the Saints offense wouldn’t scare you as much, but we kind of thought the same thing about the Washington offense. The Bengals get back to their winning ways, but in a game where it is much closer than it needed to be. Final Score: Bengals 31, Saints 25 Join the conversation! title: 3 keys to a Cincinnati Bengals victory vs. New Orleans Saints
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals will host the New Orleans Saints this Sunday at Paycor Stadium. The Bengals are 7-3 with a one-game lead in the AFC North over the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers. This […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals will host the New Orleans Saints this Sunday at Paycor Stadium. After multiple primetime games in a row, will the Bengals be ready for an afternoon matchup against the Saints at home? The Bengals are 7-3 with a one-game lead in the AFC North over the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers. This is the type of game you cannot drop on your home field. Let’s take a look at a few keys to the Bengals defeating the Saints this week. Cover Somebody!! Antonio Williams went off for over 120 yards against the Bengals on Monday Night Football. Another talented rookie, Jordyn Tyson, is next up. Tyson is more talented than Williams, and so is his running mate at receiver, Chris Olave. The Bengals cannot let these guys get behind them for chunk plays as we saw late in the Commanders game. It starts with Dax Hill and DJ Turner performing better than what we saw this past week, but the same is true about Jordan Battle, Bryan Cook, and Josh Newton in that secondary. Tyler Shough is throwing for almost 240 yards per game, and is likely salivating at the thought of facing the defense we all saw on Monday night in Washington. Feed Mike Gesicki and Jack Endries The top two Bengals receiving tight ends combined for 9 catches and 110 yards against Washington. The Commanders were trying to double both Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins throughout the game. I would imagine, with the relative success of Washington, that we will see a similar plan from the Saints defense. That means that the Bengals tight ends will once again need to step up and produce. While Gesicki and Endries had solid performances on Monday Night Football, there were a lot of times that Burrow still missed open passing opportunities to them. If that is what the defense continues to give you, stay patient and keep taking it. These two guys could be in for another highly productive week. Execute in late-game situations The Saints have lost 5 games by one score this season. That is a team that continually hangs around, even if they do not pull out the victory. The Bengals have to do a better job than they did executing offensively in critical moments. It will be paramount to turn one-score leads into two-score leads when you can, because the Saints will keep on coming. If you let a team that is underperforming on the season hang around, it will end up costing you the game. The Bengals defense did not do their job either, but I want to see Burrow and this offense close out games better. If you have a lead, you need to continue scoring and growing that lead. Do not take your foot off the gas, and you should give yourself an opportunity to improve to 8-3 this season.

title: Bengals Film Room: Boye Mafe continues his breakout season in Cincinnati
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals blew an opportunity to improve to 8-2 on the season by losing to Washington 22-20 on Monday Night Football. While the defense struggled in the second half, Boye Mafe was a bright spot throughout the game. Mafe recorded three first-half sacks of Jayden Daniels. Mafe brought pressure all night, with a team […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals blew an opportunity to improve to 8-2 on the season by losing to Washington 22-20 on Monday Night Football. While the defense struggled in the second half, Boye Mafe was a bright spot throughout the game. Mafe recorded three first-half sacks of Jayden Daniels. Mafe brought pressure all night, with a team leading 7 pressures for the game. He is now up to 50 pressures on the season, which ranks 5th overall for pressures in the entire league. With those three sacks, Mafe moves up to 3rd overall in the league in sacks with 9.5 on the season thus far. Let’s take a look at a few of the most impressive plays for Mafe from Monday Night Football. Mafe got his first sack of the night during the Commanders’ first possession of the game. He first went out to jam Chig Okonkwo before making his way after Daniels. While Daniels initially slipped out of his grasp, Mafe was able to finish off the play, ultimately forcing a punt on that first series. Boye Mafe had a strong performance on MNF pic.twitter.com/UiGf03nEje — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 It didn’t take long for Mafe to find his way to Jayden Daniels once again. This time, Mafe beat Josh Conerly around the corner and notched his second sack of the game. This ended up leading to another Washington punt, coming off of the Commanders getting a 4th-down stop of Joe Burrow right before that near midfield. Boye Mafe beats Josh Conerly for his second sack of the game pic.twitter.com/Jzywf62NNW — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 Jonathan Allen gets the assist for Mafe’s third sack of the night. His patented bull rush forces Jayden Daniels to step up in the pocket, allowing Mafe time of his own to get to the quarterback. Mafe finished the night with 7 total pressures and those 3 first-half sacks. It felt like during the second half there was a lot of bear hugging going on against Mafe, but it was something that was not being called against them. Boye Mafe’s third sack of the night on Jayden Daniels. Mafe is now up to 5th overall in pressures in the league with 50, and 3rd in the NFL with 9.5 sacks. pic.twitter.com/Ckf3jQrpYX — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 It was certainly a disappointing loss, but I do not want to take away from the performance of Boye Mafe. He has been giving this team good performances week in and week out all season long. As someone who was a big Trey Hendrickson fan, I can already say that the Bengals’ decision to get rid of him and bring in Mafe was the correct call. Now, can he help the Bengals get back in the win column this week when they face the New Orleans Saints?

title: Browns vs. Raiders: A matchup that could be key to a win
summary: The Cleveland Browns have been a bit of an adventure on offense through the first 10 games of the season. Bumble around for three quarters, make plays when they need to in the fourth quarter, and pull out a last-minute win. It’s a script that, while exciting, is also not one that feels sustainable on […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have been a bit of an adventure on offense through the first 10 games of the season. Bumble around for three quarters, make plays when they need to in the fourth quarter, and pull out a last-minute win. It’s a script that, while exciting, is also not one that feels sustainable on a week-to-week basis. Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders appears to be a prime opportunity for the Browns to get something going on offense, as the Raiders defense is: 30th in total defense 31st in run defense 26th in pass defense 32nd in points allowed 30th in RZ TDs allowed 29th in third-down stops But if Cleveland is going to get its offense untracked for a full season, they will need to contend with defensive end Maxx Crosby, who needs just a half-sack to hit 75 career sacks. And with Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson having taken 37 sacks, the second-most in the league coming into Week 12, Crosby could be in line for a big day. Crosby’s ability to disrupt an offense was on offensive coordinator Travis Switzer’s mind during his weekly media appearance : “I think Crosby is probably as disruptive of a player as there is on defense in this league. And really, this is not a knock; this is a credit to him. It starts with his relentless effort. Not that he’s not talented; he’s very talented, and he’s long, but I’ve always respected him. I think he plays the game the right way. He only knows one speed, and he’s going full speed at all times. “I think it’s an every-down disruption. Like some guys, they seem to show up maybe a little bit more on pass downs. I mean, he’s making plays on every down, whether it’s run or pass; he’s knifing the C-gap. He’s a guy that you just have to be aware of on every down, not just passing situations. And like I said, it starts with his physical ability, his length, his quickness, but also just his relentless play style.” Tytus Howard sealing off the defender on the game winner vs his old team #revengegame pic.twitter.com/2Jg6lGngum — Brandon Thorn (@BrandonThornNFL) November 16, 2026 One of the players who will be tasked with slowing down Crosby is right tackle Tytus Howard, as Pro Football Focus highlighted the matchup as one of the 10 best to watch this weekend : A revamped Sunday night showdown gives rookie Fernando Mendoza another big opportunity against the Browns under the lights. In this matchup between playoff hopefuls, Crosby vs. Howard will be defining. Crosby hasn’t been affected by a bad overall season by Las Vegas’ defense. His 86.1 overall PFF grade is the fifth-highest among qualified edge defenders, including tying for fifth at the position with 50 pressures. Howard has helped revitalize Cleveland’s offensive line since arriving from Houston. Although he’s surrendered 21 pressures, only two have been converted into sacks. That’s lifted him to a 77.9 PFF pass-blocking grade, tying for 16th among qualified tackles this season. Howard hasn’t let up a sack in 248 snaps, with his last coming in Week 4. Crosby, who was slowed by Mike McGlinchey and help against the Broncos in Week 11, will look to end that in another hostile road atmosphere. The NFL gave the Browns a primetime stage on Sunday night to showcase to the nation that they are serious about staying in the AFC playoff race. Keeping Crosby in check and out of the backfield will be a major step toward achieving that goal. Bring the Dawg Pound with you on the SB Nation app! title: Brian Schottenheimer report card: Is it finally over for the head coach?
summary: There was a lot of talk this week about the Dallas Cowboys attempting to make a run at the NFC East after dismantling the Tennessee Titans in week 11. All of that talk seems silly now, given what we know about this football team. Through 28 games as the Cowboys head coach, Brian Schottenheimer’s team […]
full_text: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images | Getty Images There was a lot of talk this week about the Dallas Cowboys attempting to make a run at the NFC East after dismantling the Tennessee Titans in week 11. All of that talk seems silly now, given what we know about this football team. Through 28 games as the Cowboys head coach, Brian Schottenheimer’s team has won back-to-back games just twice (weeks 11-13 last season). Since then, the Cowboys have alternated wins and losses or lost consecutive games. This is now a large enough sample size to see the writing on the wall. The Cowboys held a 31-10 lead late in the third quarter on Thanksgiving before the Cowboys abysmal defense and conservative play-calling on offense saw their lead squander with just minutes to go in the fourth quarter. After a quick three-and-out from the Cowboys defense to kickoff the second half, the Cowboys offense responded with a five-play, three-minute drive that led to a punt. On that drive (one that could have pretty much put the game away), the Cowboys ran the ball on first down for two yards, connected on a 22-yard passing play on second down, then followed it up with a run of negative five on first down, an eight-yard run on second down, and then a Dak Prescott sack on third down. That drive encapsulates everything that is wrong with the Schottenheimer offense. After Prescott torched the Eagles defense for the entire first half, and the officials calling defensive pass interference at a high rate, the Cowboys elected to start their run-heavy, clock-killing offensive approach that would ultimately cost them the game, and practically end their season. After the Cowboys first drive of the second half, the Cowboys kicked a field goal on 4th-and-11 to push the score to 31-17. Their first drive in the fourth quarter was three straight runs for nine yards. Schottenheimer had his offense on the field with a 21-point lead on 4th-and-1 from the Dallas 35-yard line. Instead of going for the kill, Schottenheimer did his trademark thing of attempting to get the defense to jump offsides, before taking the delay of game and punting. One issue, the punt was blocked and returned for a touchdown to cut the lead to 31-24. The Cowboys offense responded with a touchdown drive on a 14-yard rushing touchdown from Prescott taking the score to 38-24. The Eagles would respond with a touchdown of their own three plays later, cutting the lead back to 38-30. Their next offensive drive started with a first down run, a holding penalty, an incompletion to Kavonte Turpin, and then an illegal forward pass penalty that called back an 84-yard touchdown. A Brandon Aubrey missed 40-yard field goal with 3:27 left in the fourth quarter put every Cowboys’ fan watching in the worst place. After yet another quick, four-play drive for a touchdown, the Cowboys offense had the football with a two-point lead with 2:10 left to close out the game. The Cowboys started off the drive with a two-yard run to take the clock to the two-minute warning (smart!). They would come out of the two-minute warning with Prescott firing a dart into Brevyn Spann-Ford for a gain of 15 (smart!). After that play, Schottenheimer called three straight run plays that did not move the chains and elected to go for it on 4th-and-1 to ice the game. The decision to go for it over attempting another long field goal with a kicker who has struggled mightily this season was the correct one, but the play call could not have been worse. Needing just one yard to get to 6-6 on the season, Schottenheimer had Prescott come out in shotgun with no play-action running George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb on slants, with all other targets running hitches. No one was anywhere near open and with the Eagles bringing a blitz, Prescott was sacked for a loss of nine. The Eagles last-second field goal after that ended the game, and the season, for the Dallas Cowboys. Needing just one yard on fourth down, lining up in the gun and the non-use of play-action is just inexcusable for a play-caller who has been doing this for over two decades. No motion, no threat of a run, and no creativity in the design on the Cowboys biggest play of the game was as disappointing as possible. Schottenheimer called a good game in the first half, but he did so by being aggressive and allowing Prescott to run the offense through the passing game. In the second half, we saw a similar game script to the Arizona Cardinals game, where they attempted to bleed clock and settled for field goals and trusting the defense. What do you know? The end result was exactly the same. After so many embarrassing performances this year from the Cowboys, it’s just hard to even imagine a scenario in which Brian Schottenheimer could return next year. The fanbase lost a ton of interest towards the end of the Mike McCarthy experience, but this offseason would likely surpass that by flying colors if Jerry Jones announced Schottenheimer will return as head coach and/or play-caller in 2027. Play-Calling C- This was truly a tale of two halves for Schottenheimer the play-caller. It was a very good first half, but like he has done far too often this season, his conservative nature and faith in his defense ended up costing the Cowboys another win. Overall, he gets a C- due to the major fall off in the second-half and the disastrous 4th-and-1 play call on the biggest play of the game. Fourth-Down Decisions C- Similar to play calling, he made the correct decision to go for it on every fourth down that they did, but his decision to punt on the blocked punt was a major whiff in my opinion. Timeout Usage F Like we have seen so often this season, Schottenheimer’s use of timeouts in this game made no sense. Team Preparation D Again, a tale of two halves. The team looked great in the first half, but completely fell apart in the second half. For a coach who talks so much about consistency and playing all three phases in all four quarters, the Cowboys have been really poor at doing just that in Schottenheimer’s time as head coach. What grade would you give to Brian Schottenheimer on Sunday?
author: Connor Livesay

title: 10 thoughts on the Cowboys Thanksgiving loss to the Eagles
summary: If you think your stomach feels sick from eating too much, nothing could prepare you for the heartburn that the Dallas Cowboys subjected their fans to on Thanksgiving. For almost three full quarters, the Cowboys looked completely in control, giving fans plenty of good eats before everything completely collapsed in a heartbreaking 39-38 loss to […]
full_text: If you think your stomach feels sick from eating too much, nothing could prepare you for the heartburn that the Dallas Cowboys subjected their fans to on Thanksgiving. For almost three full quarters, the Cowboys looked completely in control, giving fans plenty of good eats before everything completely collapsed in a heartbreaking 39-38 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. We’ve been hurt plenty, but this team always finds a way to one-up themselves. Here are 10 thoughts on this very unfestive football game. 1. Epic collapse It is hard to put into words what we witnessed. The Cowboys led 31-10 with 3:35 left in the third quarter, and this game was supposed to be over. The Eagles then went 80 yards in just over three minutes to initiate the rally. On the Cowboys’ ensuing possession, they had a punt blocked that Philly returned for a touchdown, and suddenly it was a seven-point game. The Cowboys answered with a touchdown, but the Eagles answered right back with a touchdown of their own that took just 62 seconds. Suddenly, you could sense the bottom falling out, and it did not feel good. 2. A chance to ice it The Cowboys initially dodged the comeback after Cobie Durant picked off Joe Milton III with just over seven minutes to go. The offense burned off three minutes and drove down to the 22-yard line, setting up a chip-shot field goal that would have made it a two-score game, but Brandon Aubrey shanked it. Despite a late-game letdown, they still had an easy chance to escape, but no. It was as if the Cowboys just did not want to win this football game. 3. The fatal decision With all the chances the Cowboys had to put this game away, they were faced with one last tough decision late in the fourth quarter. With 55 seconds left on the clock, they faced a 4th-and-1 at the Eagles’ 39-yard line. Brian Schottenheimer faced the dilemma of trying to go for it to run out the clock or punting it away and relying on his defense to keep the Eagles from moving into game-winning field goal range with no timeouts left. They opted to go for it, and the gamble blew up in their face. Dak Prescott was sacked on the play, turning the ball over on downs and immediately putting the Eagles right on the cusp of field goal range. What a disaster. 4. Deja vu This is the second time this season that the Cowboys have opened up a big lead against a struggling NFC team, only to completely fall apart late. They followed an eerily similar script earlier this year against the Arizona Cardinals. Against a team filled with backups, Dallas held a huge lead and had multiple opportunities to ice the game with either a crucial first down or a field goal. Instead, they failed to do either and let the game slip right through their fingers. To fail once is disappointing, but to do it a second time in the same season is nothing short of shameful. 5. Taste of sweet revenge Eagles quarterback Joe Milton III went off on his old team in a major way. He threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns while adding a rushing touchdown for good measure. It was easily his best showing as a pro, as he thoroughly punished his former team. Thanksgiving leftovers always taste great, but for Milton, nothing tastes better than this victory. Every time the Cowboys looked like they might finally settle down and put him away, he made another huge throw to keep the Eagles alive. 6. Returning the favor Last year, when these two teams faced off against each other at AT&T Stadium, it was the Eagles who blew a massive 21-point lead. In that game, the Cowboys scored 24 unanswered points to pull off an epic comeback victory. Turnabout is fair play in the NFL, only this one feels even more disgusting for the Cowboys because they collapsed against a broken-down Eagles team. Do we really deserve this? 7. Aubrey’s struggles Brandon Aubrey has been a staple of consistency for this team, earning All-Pro honors in each of his first three seasons in the league. This year has not gone nearly so well for him, and it is not just the long 50+ yard kicks he occasionally misses. Aubrey has now reached a point where he is missing the easy ones. He has already missed two extra points this season, and on Thursday he missed a 40-yarder that would have essentially put the game away. This once-reliable fixture has now joined the party as part of the reason the Cowboys are not winning games. 8. Streaky offense It is crazy to realize that the Cowboys have scored at least 38 points in each of the last three games and somehow lost two of them, yet here we are. After starting last week’s game by scoring six straight touchdowns, the offense followed that up with four first-half touchdowns in this one. They looked unstoppable early on, moving the ball at will. Sadly, they could only muster 10 points in the second half, and with the way the rest of the team was unraveling, that simply did not cut it. 9. Sack streak stays alive The Cowboys have now put together four straight home games with five sacks. There are not a lot of good things you can say about this defense right now, but the pass rush continues to get after the quarterback. Five different players recorded a sack on Thursday as pressure came from all directions. It is just unfortunate that those big plays up front went to waste, as the team still fell victim to big plays. 10. Season slipping away Entering this week, the Cowboys were still alive in the divisional race, but they needed a lot of things to go well. At the top of that list was winning the easy games on their schedule, but this team just did not have it in them to finish the job against a shorthanded division rival. This loss serves as a harsh reminder that despite any brief inkling of an idea that this team might show glimpses of hope, they ultimately are not a team that can be taken serious.
author: Dan Rogers

title: 3 things we learned about the Cowboys against the Eagles
summary: The Dallas Cowboys hosted the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving afternoon. Here are three things we learned from the game. The offensive heater continues We came into 2026 expecting the offense to be great. And for the most part, they’ve been pretty solid. But there have been bumps in the road, including the lowest points of […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys hosted the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving afternoon. Here are three things we learned from the game. The offensive heater continues We came into 2026 expecting the offense to be great. And for the most part, they’ve been pretty solid. But there have been bumps in the road, including the lowest points of the year thus far against Tampa Bay and Green Bay. The last three weeks, however, Dak Prescott and the offense have been on fire. Scoring 40 against San Francisco, 51 against Tennessee, and now 38 against Philadelphia, the Cowboys offense might be the hottest in the NFL. Javonte Williams got the train rolling with the first touchdown of the day and finished with three total on the day. In totality, Dallas would put up 38 points in a shootout against their NFC East rival. Unfortunately, it was not enough, yet again losing after scoring nearly 40 points. The offense wasn’t as perfect as it needed to be, however. Failing to convert 4th-and-1 near the 50 to seal the game handed the Eagles the ball back close to striking range for the game winning field goal. It’s unfair to expect perfection, but the 4th-and-1 failure certainly hurts after an amazing day from Dak Prescott and the offense. The defensive issues are mind-numbing After beating a bad Titans team last week, the Cowboys faced another offense in a slump this week, going up against former Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton. While the defense started hot, this unit eventually allowed far too many explosive plays to an offense without a starting quarterback and with plenty of players missing elsewhere. The back end of the Cowboys defense seemed to disappear at times, especially when the pass rush didn’t get home. The edges also allowed Joe Milton to break contain throughout the day, successfully throwing the ball from outside the pocket on a consistent basis. The defense allowed a huge fourth quarter comeback in a game that Dallas should have walked away from without an issue. Going into half, the Cowboys were up 28-10. The game would end up 39-38 Eagles. A blocked punt in the fourth quarter certainly did not help matters. This was not good enough against a bad team and certainly won’t be good enough against adequate competition. This Cowboys defense is truly lost at sea with no hope for redemption this season. The Cowboys likely cost themselves a chance at a postseason run If Dallas was to stand a chance at catching the Giants for first place in the NFC East, they needed to win the games they were favored, plus steal one or two against better competition. With this loss against the Eagles, Dallas finds themselves in nearly insurmountable odds to win the East and make the playoffs. The Cowboys and Giants are headed in opposite directions with time running out for a recovery. With their playoff hopes hanging on by a thread, the defense rolled over in the second half, allowing Joe Milton and a banged up Eagles offense to make play after play. The special teams wasn’t any better. A blocked punt and a missed field goal were a ten point swing that amounted to the Eagles stealing one in Dallas. The high flying offense continues to dominate games while the defense gives them away. I’m not sure the league has ever seen such a disparity between the two sides of the ball in it’s history. It’s unfathomable that Dallas continues to lose games where they’re scoring 35 or more points, yet here we are again. The summary of the Cowboys season was on display Thursday afternoon for the world to see. And it likely cost Dallas any remaining, realistic hope for the playoffs.
author: Dyllan Rivers

title: Cowboys news: Playoff hopes come crashing down in  embarrassing loss
summary: There’s really no words to properly describe what we had to watch on Thanksgiving. The Cowboys had a 21-point lead in the third quarter and ended up losing to Joe Milton and the banged up Philadelphia Eagles 39-38 on a last second Jake Elliott field goal. With the playoffs seemingly out of the picture for […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images There’s really no words to properly describe what we had to watch on Thanksgiving. The Cowboys had a 21-point lead in the third quarter and ended up losing to Joe Milton and the banged up Philadelphia Eagles 39-38 on a last second Jake Elliott field goal. With the playoffs seemingly out of the picture for the Cowboys before we get to the month of December for the second straight year, and the New York Jets owning the Cowboys first-round pick, the hope for this franchise has reached a new low. Joe Milton has huge game as Eagles shock Cowboys – Todd Archer, ESPN.com This season has been filled with embarrassing losses, but this one takes the cake. This loss takes the Cowboys to 5-7 and their chances to make the playoffs are now less than 10% according to multiple sports books. Quarterback Joe Milton shined on the national stage, helping erase a 21-point third-quarter deficit to lead the Philadelphia Eagles to a thrilling 39-38 shootout win over the Dallas Cowboys to keep some hope alive in what’s been a trying season. Milton accounted for four touchdowns (three passing, one rushing) and made a number of “wow” throws with his howitzer arm, the bulk of which went to receiver DeVonta Smith , who erupted for 186 receiving yards and two scores. Milton did enough in the closing moments to set up a game-winning 59-yard field goal by Jake Elliott . Full coverage: Cowboys suffer late collapse in Thanksgiving shootout with Eagles – SportsDay Staff, The Dallas Morning News We have gotten used to the Dallas Cowboys defense collapsing, but giving up a 21-point lead with less than four minutes to go in the third quarter is just tough to stomach. Did this loss put the nail in Brian Schottenheimer’s coffin in Dallas? 6:45 p.m. It’s a shootout at AT&T Stadium. Shortly after Dak Prescott’s touchdown run, the Dallas defense forgot to account for Joe Milton’s rushing ability. After a big return on the kickoff, Milton found DeVonta Smith for a 23-yard gain. Milton then finished off the drive with a 15-yard touchdown run. Philadelphia’s ensuing two-point conversion attempt was unsuccessful. Cowboys lead 38-30 with 9:09 left in the fourth. Winners & 5 Losers From Cowboys’ Unforgivable Thanksgiving Loss To Eagles – Randy Gurzi, SI.com At the end of the day, we are all losers for having to watch that football game on Thanksgiving. But check out a couple of guys who stood our and a couple of guys who struggled in the Cowboys Thanksgiving day game loss. Special teams has been a sore spot for the Cowboys all season and that was the case again in Week 12. Dallas allowed a blocked punt in the fourth quarter, which was recovered by Kenny Moore for a touchdown. After Dak Prescott responded with a touchdown on offense, special teams again let them down by allowing a 55-yard kickoff return. That gave the Eagles a short field as they scored in 1:02 to cut it to one score again. As if that wasn’t enough, Brandon Aubrey missed another kick that could have put the game away. That’s an indictment of special teams coordinator Nick Sorensen, whose unit has been a mess all year. Don’t Forget These 5: Aubrey’s clutch FG miss – Nick Eatman, DallasCowboys.com Brandon Aubrey is no longer the trustworthy kicker he once was. With another chance to help pull away from the Eagles late in the fourth quarter, Aubrey pulled a 48-yard field goal wide left and handed the Eagles the ball right back near midfield. These misses have been an issues for almost two years now. Something has to give. Aubrey misses in the clutch – The Cowboys made Brandon Aubrey the highest-paid kicker in the NFL this offseason – not just for his ability to make long kicks but also the clutch ones. But Aubrey hooked a 40-yard field goal attempt late in the game that would’ve given the Cowboys a 10-point lead with 3:27 left. Yes, the hold wasn’t ideal as Bryan Anger didn’t get the laces turned around, but it was a bad miss that opened the door for the Eagles to score just over a minute later to get back in the game. NFC Playoff Picture: Cowboys and the NFC East standings after Thanksgiving – Dave Halprin, Blogging the Boys Is there any hope left for the Cowboys to make the playoffs? Maybe, a little, but it’s hard to buy into anything regarding this team winning their way to the playoffs with how they performed on Thanksgiving. The Dallas Cowboys are a broken football team. They had a win firmly in their hands and just handed back to the Philadelphia Eagles. Brian Schottenheimer fell apart in the fourth quarter with several awful decisions. Once again they played for a field goal late in the game instead of being aggressive and playing for the touchdown to win the game. Then they made a baffling call on fourth down – instead of kicking a field goal, or running the ball for one yard, they called a pass. Disaster when Dak Prescott was sacked leading to a long field goal from the Eagles to win 39-38. Download the SB Nation app today! DAK PRESCOTT CAN’T MAKE UP FOR DREADFUL DEFENSE – The Fantasy Footballers Dak Prescott has been playing at a MVP level over the last month. Unfortunately, that level of play still isn’t enough to win football games with his defense and coaching staff. Prescott completed 19 of 28 passes for 291 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Thursday’s 39-38 loss to the Eagles. He added 19 yards and a TD on two carries. The Cowboys held a 28-10 lead at the half and were up 38-24 early in the fourth quarter, but another abysmal effort by the defense and special teams squandered Prescott’s third straight game producing at least three touchdowns. It was the first time since Week 8 that he’d failed to reach 300 passing yards, but the 33-year-old QB is still on course for a career-best campaign. He’ll take a 27:7 TD:INT, along with three rushing scores, into a much tougher Week 13 tilt against the Seahawks.

title: Cowboys vs. Eagles: Brian Schottenheimer tops our losers list
summary: The Dallas Cowboys looked like they were going to run the Philadelphia Eagles out of AT&T Stadium on Thanksgiving.Then everything changed. Dallas built a commanding 31-10 advantage before allowing the Eagles to storm back, turning what should have been a comfortable victory into a frantic finish. There were some outstanding individual performances, but also several […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys looked like they were going to run the Philadelphia Eagles out of AT&T Stadium on Thanksgiving.Then everything changed. Dallas built a commanding 31-10 advantage before allowing the Eagles to storm back, turning what should have been a comfortable victory into a frantic finish. There were some outstanding individual performances, but also several familiar problems that ruined the afternoon and saw the Eagles secure a comeback victory. Losers: Brian Schottenheimer It’s hard not to lay a lot of the blame for this loss on the shoulders of head coach Brian Schottenheimer. His repeated inability to finish out games has crushed the Cowboys hopes this season. Late in this game, Schottenheimer had a chance to be aggressive and go for the killing touchdown with Dallas up 38-36. Instead, once he got in field goal position he got conservative and played for the three points. Brandon Aubrey missed the kick. Later in the fourth quarter, he had a 4th-and-1 decision to make. He chose about the worst avenue. Instead of punting, or kicking a long field goal, he went for it even though not converting would give the Eagles the ball close to field goal range. To make matters worse, while going for it, he didn’t use Javonte Williams, or got Prescott out on the edge with a run/pass option. Instead, he called a drop back pass which resulted in a sack. It was gross mismanagement of the end of the game. Loser: Cowboys pass defense Dallas stopped Philadelphia from running the football. Then Joe Milton and DeVonta Smith ripped the secondary apart. Milton threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns, averaging over 12 yards per attempt. Smith was even more damaging, producing 11 catches for 200 yards and two touchdowns, including scores of 50 and 45 yards, those numbers are insanely brutal. Dallas repeatedly allowed receivers behind the secondary and surrendered exactly the kind of explosive plays that have plagued this defense throughout the season. The Cowboys had Philadelphia buried at 31-10. The pass defense gave them a route straight back into the game. Loser: Cowboys special teams This might have been the single worst play of the afternoon. Dallas led 31-17 early in the fourth quarter and simply needed to get the punt away. Instead, Philadelphia blocked Bryan Anger’s punt and recovered it for a touchdown. Suddenly, a comfortable two-touchdown advantage became a seven-point game. A blocked punt returned for a touchdown while trying to protect a fourth-quarter lead is about as bad as it gets. Then, of course, there’s the missed Brandon Aubrey field goal that would have kept the game out of reach at the end of the fourth quarter. That field goal was crucial and he failed to connect the kick for three points. It’s a brutal miss but it was just another addition to the miscues on special teams this week. Loser: Closing games Dallas led 31-10, Philadelphia then scored 29 points while Dallas managed only seven. The Cowboys allowed a backup quarterback to turn what looked like a Thanksgiving demolition into a game that came down to the final minute. The blocked punt played a major part, but this wasn’t one isolated mistake. Explosive passes, penalties and defensive breakdowns all contributed. Dallas has shown repeatedly that it can build leads, but they haven’t learned how to finish opponents. We’ve failed to see this repeatedly so don’t expect it to change. Winner: Dak Prescott Dak Prescott gave Dallas everything it needed offensively. Prescott completed 19 of 28 passes for 291 yards and two touchdowns, while also adding a 14-yard rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter. He consistently attacked Philadelphia downfield, protected the football and kept answering whenever the Eagles threatened to take control of the game. Winner: CeeDee Lamb CeeDee Lamb continued his outstanding run of form. Lamb finished with seven receptions for 134 yards, averaging more than 19 yards per catch despite not finding the end zone. His ability to create explosive plays consistently stretched Philadelphia’s defense and opened opportunities elsewhere for George Pickens and KaVontae Turpin. Lamb has reached the stage where 100-yard performances almost feel routine. Winner: Javonte Williams Javonte Williams carried a massive workload and rewarded Dallas for sticking with him. Williams rushed 29 times for 101 yards and two touchdowns, while also catching a 12-yard touchdown pass from Prescott. His one-yard touchdown opened the scoring, his 12-yard run extended Dallas’ first-half advantage, and he later added the receiving score just before halftime. Three touchdowns on Thanksgiving is a pretty convincing way to land in the winner column.

title: Cowboys vs. Eagles recap: Dallas embarrassed by Philadelphia on Thanksgiving Day
summary: It will go down in history as one of the darkest Thanksgiving Day games ever for the Dallas Cowboys. Somehow, some way, the Cowboys threw away a 31-10 lead that they had in the third quarter. The Philadelphia Eagles won on what was basically a game-winning, 60-yard field goal. It is hard to fathom. On […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 26: Ceedee Lamb #88 of the Dallas Cowboys is tackled by Andrew Mukuba #24 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the second quarter at AT&T Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images It will go down in history as one of the darkest Thanksgiving Day games ever for the Dallas Cowboys. Somehow, some way, the Cowboys threw away a 31-10 lead that they had in the third quarter. The Philadelphia Eagles won on what was basically a game-winning, 60-yard field goal. It is hard to fathom. On the other hand it is actually very easy to fathom given everything we have seen from the Cowboys this season. They are not a good football team. They are poorly coached. They are talent-deficient. They are all of the bad things. On a day where we are supposed to be thankful it is hard to find a reason to be for this specific part of our lives. The Dallas Cowboys are a weekly embarrassment and Thursday was the latest example of it. What even happens now? First Quarter The Eagles won the toss and deferred which put the Cowboys offense to work first. Dak Prescott and the group did not waste the opportunity. Javonte Williams was served seconds, thirds, and then some as the team marched down the field, partly thanks to a huge 3rd and 18 conversion from Dak to CeeDee Lamb, but it was Williams who capped it off with the touchdown to give the home team an early 7-0 lead. JAVONTE TD pic.twitter.com/IFq12RHEEy — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 Things were looking rather impressive for Joe Milton and the Eagles. I’d imagine that many Cowboys fans were starting to assume a score was happening any minute across the first drive. Thankfully that was not the case. Right around field goal range the Eagles chose to roll the dice on fourth and short… and Quinnen Williams said no! QUINNEN!!! pic.twitter.com/Yz2K1cZsqi — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 Weirdly a sequence occurred on the next drive that did the first. Dak Prescott scrambled for a first on a third down, but the gain was negated by a penalty. This brought up third and long (16 here, 18 before) and Prescott connected with a star receiver (George Pickens here, CeeDee Lamb before) for the first down. After that KaVontae Turpin had a stellar catch where he turned on the boosters and reached the endzone in a flash. Dallas was up 14-0 early. TURP TD!!!! pic.twitter.com/8ihtwLzjs2 — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 The quarter ended with Philly holding the ball right after. Second Quarter The Eagles punted shortly after teams flipped the field which put the Cowboys offense back up. Given that they were already leading 14-0 this was a chance to really blow things open. Unfortunately they could not and wound up punting the ball for the first time in a while. A big 3rd and 12 conversion from Philadelphia put them within striking distance and while they were unable to fully get home they did give Jake Elliott a chance at a 48-yard field goal. It was good and the visitors had their first points on the day. The Cowboys offense did not miss this time around. KaVontae Turpin was involved again, this time on a jet sweep, and there was a big conversion from Dak Prescott to CeeDee Lamb. But it was Javonte Williams who cased in yet again. This marked his second score on the day and gave Dallas a 21-3 lead. JAVONTE WILLIAMS AGAIN pic.twitter.com/mbe4qovd3I — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 The dam finally broke, though. Joe Milton had been showing moments of promise to this point in the game and at long last he delivered. It was a classic Joe Milton throw… meaning it traveled quite a long ways. JOE MILTON'S ARM TALENT IS RIDICULOUS 🎯 PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2MLAir7i29 — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 The Cowboys received the ball with just over four minutes to go. It felt like an important possession as it would likely be their last one before the half and they received the ball to start the game. Points were essential. In all honesty it was a pretty penalty-filled drive. Officials were calling them left and right, many of them helping the Cowboys, but Dallas was moved back after an apparent touchdown to Brevyn Spann-Ford. On third and goal from the 12-yard line… Dak Prescott found Javonte Williams for a score to close the half. It also marked a hat trick of scores on the day for Williams specifically. JAVONT3 pic.twitter.com/9lMQ1ebII8 — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 The Eagles took a knee and it was Miranda Lambert time. Third Quarter Philadelphia went three and out to start the second half which is always great to see. The Cowboys took the field and once again with an opportunity to stretch their lead. Dallas punted it back themselves. This game truly felt over, but obviously with a lot of time left that was not the case in any real way. Football had to be played. Shemar James sacked Joe Milton which helped to ensure the punt streak continued. Philly booted it back and the Cowboys offense returned to the field. It was a little bit of the same for the Cowboys offense in terms of not being able to fully convert. They did score, but only 3 points by way of Brandon Aubrey. This was notable though as it was a 59-yard field goal that he drilled with ease which was great to see given how this season has gone. The FOX broadcast also noted that this was the longest ever field goal made on Thanksgiving all-time. Pretty neat. The third quarter ended right as Philadelphia crossed the 50-yard line… and then Joe Milton found DeVonta Smith again to get another touchdown on the board with 15 seconds left. It was suddenly 31-17, good guys. Fourth Quarter Things did not go particularly well for the Cowboys offense to start the fourth quarter. They faced a fourth and short on their side of the field and left the offense on the field. It was bold, but nobody really thought they were going to run a play. Thankfully they just fished for offsides and punted. Or so we thought. The Cowboys tried to punt… but it was blocked and returned for a Philly touchdown. Out of nowhere it was 31-24 with basically the entire fourth quarter left. EAGLES BLOCKED PUNT TD PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1mrM5lDeTK — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 It goes without saying that the pressure was high. The Cowboys were on the verge of blowing this game. Something had to happen. Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb specifically played like that was the case. They hooked up for a pair of big gains along the drive and then Dak put the exclamation point on things himself by running it on for a touchdown… thanks to some serious hops. DAK!!!! pic.twitter.com/1GdrVEJ8Ls — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 27, 2026 It seemed like this was going to essentially end the game. Have you seen the 2026 Dallas Cowboys, though Philadelphia traveled 42 yards in 3 plays to match the touchdown. Joe Milton literally did by rushing it in himself. Joe Milton takes it in himself! PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ERZiu9S8Kr — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 The Eagles missed the two-point conversion so it was 38-30 Cowboys. In the blink of an eye it was 3rd and 14 right past the team’s own 15-yard line. It appeared as if the Cowboys had pulled off something truly incredible. Dak Prescott found George Pickens for a modest gain, but then he threw a lateral across the field to Hunter Luepke and the fullback took it all the way to the house. He even jumped into the Salvation Army kettle. Unfortunately it was deemed to be a forward pass from Pickens and therefore a penalty which resulted in the loss of the down. Bryan Anger successfully got the punt off this time and the Eagles returned it past midfield. There was still half the fourth quarter remaining. It was then that the Cowboys defense made a play. On third and forever they…

title: Broncos vs. Steelers: 3 Things to Watch in Week 12
summary: The Denver Broncos and Pittsburgh Steelers battle on the gridiron this afternoon in a pivotal AFC matchup that has a lot at stake in the conference’s playoff chase. full_text: Nov 22, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos defensive tackle Malcolm Roach (97) and defensive end Zach Allen (99) sack Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) during the fourth quarter at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Denver Broncos and Pittsburgh Steelers battle on the gridiron this afternoon in a pivotal AFC matchup that has a lot at stake in the conference’s playoff chase. If the Broncos can take care of business on the road, they will earn their ninth victory of the season. Here are three major storylines I’ll be watching as the game transpires. Will Denver’s defense get pressure on Mason Rudolph? One of the big areas of focus today is what team can get the upper hand at the line of scrimmage. The Broncos had a standout performance in the trenches versus the Las Vegas Raiders last Sunday. A big key to the game will surround whether or not Denver’s defensive front seven can dominate the Steelers’ offensive line. Through ten games, Pittsburgh’s front five have already allowed 31 sacks—one of the worst marks in the NFL. With future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers being benched and subsequently released from the squad, longtime backup and veteran Mason Rudolph will be leading Pittsburgh on offense on Black Friday. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph needs to have a game plan that focuses on getting after Rudolph. The Steelers’ starting tackle duo of Troy Fautanu and Max Iheanachor have struggled this season. Each have surrendered five sacks. With that in mind, I believe the starting edge rushing duo of Nik Bonitto and Jonathon Cooper are poised to have big games. If they can dial up the heat, Denver’s odds of winning will skyrocket dramatically. Can Denver’s offensive line pave the way for Jonah Coleman and the Broncos’ rushing attack? Rookie running back Jonah Coleman had a standout performance against the Raiders. He rushed for 111 yards and had three touchdowns—proving he will be Denver’s bell cow back the remainder of the season. Today, Coleman and Denver’s offensive line face a much tougher battle going up against a formidable Steelers defense that is one of the best in the NFL at stopping the run. Can the Broncos’ offensive line hold their own against a Steelers’ defensive front at the point of attack? They need to protect quarterback Bo Nix and give him time to make some plays in the pocket. Additionally, they need to prove they can establish the run on the road. Pittsburgh has one of the league’s elite run defenses, but Denver has to get rookie running back Coleman going. With J.K. Dobbins sidelined due to a one-game suspension, expect a heavy dose of the rookie running back Per weather forecasts, this could be a rainy matchup . That means dictating the pace of the game on the ground will be mission critical for the Broncos to achieve victory. We all saw how important that was for the Buffalo Bills last night in their win over the Kansas City Chiefs in bad weather. Denver needs to get Coleman going and find a way to limit Jaylen Warren’s impact defensively. What team will win the turnover battle? Today’s matchup is going to have some wild weather if the weather forecast holds. That means protecting the ball will be extremely important for both teams. Both the Broncos and Steelers have done a good job forcing turnovers this season. In every game, winning the turnover battle is important. That usually winds up being a huge difference maker in the outcome. I think that’s going to play a big factor in today’s game. I’m eager to see what team is able to come ahead in this regard. I have a feeling Denver has the edge in this one. I don’t necessarily like to assume, but I’m not necessarily confident the Steelers are going to come out of the gate firing all cylinders. With all the Rodgers-McCarthy and team related drama this week, I could see them performing a bit flat. Though they are undefeated at home to start the season. I’m hoping Joseph and the Denver’s defense can find a way to make some noise and create some timely turnovers that change the momentum and tide of the game.

title: Broncos must build on recent offensive success
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos offense are starting to peak at the right time. And the biggest reason is rookie running back Jonah Coleman. It is a cliché, but when an offense can run the ball consistently and effectively, it sets up the rest of the offense for success. But […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 22: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos smiles after a Broncos touchdown during the third quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Empower Field at Mile High on November 22, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos defeated the Raiders 38-24. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos offense are starting to peak at the right time. And the biggest reason is rookie running back Jonah Coleman. It is a cliché, but when an offense can run the ball consistently and effectively, it sets up the rest of the offense for success. But more than that, Nix is taking care of the ball, the offense is taking shots down the field, and tight end Evan Engram is making an appearance. Over the last four games, Denver has averaged 30 or more points. Now it’s about staking these games. “Just off the top of my head, I think we’ve done a better job on third downs,” Nix said to the media earlier this week. “I think we’ve prolonged drives when we’ve gotten to extend some of those drives that we’ve had. At the same time, we’ve had more success in the run game and explosive plays. That’s going to help an offense score more points. “For us, we just have to continue to find ways to find explosives, continue to do well on third downs. I think one area we’ve really done well really all season is in the red zone; we’ve scored touchdowns. We’ve kept (kicker Wil) Lutz off the field until a PAT. We have to continue to do that. We feel like we’re in a good spot to continue to improve. Now we have the confidence that we can do it, we’ve done it for a couple weeks. Just have to stay on that track.” One of the most important developments is Engram. Getting the veteran tight end involved in the offense, as he was in the win over the Las Vegas Raiders, makes the Broncos that much more difficult to defend. Engram finished the game against the Raiders with six catches for 74 yards. More of that heading into the rest of the season will be massive for Denver. “He had a great game blocking and then catching,” Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb said to the media. “I think he might’ve been a leading receiver. You definitely noticed him if you were in the stadium, and he made some big-time catches on third down. Even the one that got the fourth-and-1 was an unbelievable catch. I think all of our guys are that way. “They’ve been ones everywhere they’ve been, in college and a lot of pro teams. So whatever the matchups allow you to have. That defense last week, we felt confident he was going to get the ball, and he played pretty well.” Added Broncos head coach Sean Payton: “Yes, those were some big plays that you’re getting some of that deep zone coverage. It’s hard sometimes to say, ‘Well, they have to get past the sticks.’ Well, that’s not really the case. Sometimes you’re going to have to throw it under, and he did a great job of that.” For the Broncos, it’s now about keeping the offense peaking. “It’s part of playing long seasons,” Nix said to the media. “You have to limit the distractions. Starve the distractions and feed your focus. That’s something that (Oregon head) coach (Dan) Lanning taught me a long time ago at Oregon. For us, it’s just about the next game and how we can win it.” New Jonah Coleman shirt BreakingT released a new Jonah Coleman shirt just in time for Black Friday. Coleman has taken to the history of running backs, namely Hall of Famer Terrell Davis and the Mile High Salute. The shirt? Coleman Mile High Salute . Broncos links

title: What everyone said about Detroit Lions, Jeffery Simmons false start controversy
summary: The CBS broadcast for the Detroit Lions vs. Chicago Bears Thanksgiving Day classic jumped all over an interesting controversy involving back-to-back false starts from Lions center Juice Scruggs in the second quarter. The two penatlies set the Lions behind the sticks, and they punted two plays later. But when the broadcast came back from commercial, […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 26: Jeffery Simmons #99 of the Chicago Bears smiles prior to an NFL football game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on November 26, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The CBS broadcast for the Detroit Lions vs. Chicago Bears Thanksgiving Day classic jumped all over an interesting controversy involving back-to-back false starts from Lions center Juice Scruggs in the second quarter. The two penatlies set the Lions behind the sticks, and they punted two plays later. But when the broadcast came back from commercial, they showed a replay that appears to show Bears defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons yelling out something loud that immediately resulted in Scruggs’ false-start flinches. Let’s break down the controversy by looking at the rulebook, and hearing everyone’s perspective about the situation via comments after the game. NFL rulebook on simulating snap counts Simulating a snap count—or trying to disrupt the offensive line verbally—is an unsportsmanlike conduct infraction that carries a 15-yard penalty. Here is the exact wording of the rule, which you can find in Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, subarticle i: There shall be no unsportsmanlike conduct. This applies to any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship. Such acts specifically include, among others: (i) Using acts or words by the defensive team that are designed to disconcert an offensive team at the snap. An official must blow his whistle immediately to stop play. So if Simmons was indeed yelling or screaming to intentionally get the Lions to jump, that should carry a 15-yard penalty in Detroit’s favor. CBS announcer (and former DL) J.J. Watt "It's a little defensive line trick. You normally can't ever get caught doing it because people can't see you." @JJWatt noticed something in the trenches 🔎 pic.twitter.com/6ECMxiHaY3 — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 26, 2026 J.J. Watt was the one to point this out on the broadcast, calling it out as a penalty. But he also described why it’s so easy to get away with as a defensive lineman. “He barks a little bit or he says something right here, and that’s when Scruggs moves. It’s a little defensive line trick. You normally can’t ever get caught doing it, because people can’t see you. But I think he is getting a little reason for Scruggs to be dropping back.” Bears DL Jeffery Simmons Simmons claims he was just calling a defensive alert to his teammate during those plays, and not trying to simulate the snap count. “If I say, ‘Run,’ I’m telling my defense, run. Think I care to tell them what they about to do? I’m talking to my guys. So all the crying that they’re doing, that’s a them problem, not me.” Lions guard Christian Mahogany Mahogany was the most outspoken of the group, blatantly calling out Simmons for the infraction—while also admitting it’s still on the offensive line not to false start. Via the Free Press : “They’re simulating the snap count. They’re using − they find out the snap count of the quarterback and they use it, and that’s it. They use the words. So like I said, no bitching and complaining, we self-inflicted those wounds and we can’t false start.” Lions coach Dan Campbell Campbell clearly wasn’t in the mood to talk about the controversy, initially shutting down the first question he got about it. When pushed, he said he has an idea on why the false starts were happening. But when asked why, he shut it down again. “No, I’m not going to share it. So, we’ll be good on that. We’ll be good. We’ve got to clean it all up and make sure that we just take care of our business. That’s all.“ Lions quarterback Jared Goff Goff was far more direct, accusing Simmons of indeed simulating the snap count. However, the Lions quarterback downplayed the impact of it, noting that it only happened once or twice and the team needs to handle it better. “I only think he did it really once that was really egregious to me – where they yell. It’s a really hard thing to officiate because at what point is he simulating the snap count? At what point is he just talking to his guys? And I understand it happens all across the league, this isn’t the first time it happened. But yeah, I’m just trying to make sure that they know that I’m not allowed to simulate snap count with my hands. He shouldn’t be allowed to do it with his voice. And that wasn’t the difference in the game. But yeah, that was early, and I don’t believe it happened more than once or twice.” Later adding, “We got to be able to handle that a little bit better than we did.”

title: Discussion: Are you feeling better, worse about Detroit Lions after loss to Bears?
summary: It’s never good to lose to a division rival. It’s even harder to swallow the loss when it feels like self-inflicted wounds turned a likely win into a painful loss. That’s what Detroit Lions fans are going through this Black Friday, as they try to cope with the Lions blowing a double-digit lead in the […]
full_text: Nov 26, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (4) is tripped up by Detroit Lions defensive back Andre Cisco (28) and cornerback Rock Ya-Sin (23) in the first quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It’s never good to lose to a division rival. It’s even harder to swallow the loss when it feels like self-inflicted wounds turned a likely win into a painful loss. That’s what Detroit Lions fans are going through this Black Friday, as they try to cope with the Lions blowing a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter to lose a pivotal game to the Chicago Bears. But after the sting of the loss wears off, we’ll have to assess the team and what Thursday’s loss means for the season. Maybe you’re still not over it. Maybe you’re still seething over certain plays or play calls. But for now, let’s assess where things are at. Today’s Question of the Day is: Do you feel better, worse, or the same after the Lions’ loss to the Bears? My answer: Thursday’s game confirmed a lot of good things I knew about the Lions. Their run game is back, their offensive line is playing their best football, and this team’s offense will keep them alive in just about any game. Jahmyr Gibbs is an insane weapon to have, and when Jared Goff is dealing, no one can stop them. Remember that going into this game, the Bears were considered one of the best defenses in football. Detroit just hung 549 yards and 35 points on them—and it probably should have been even more. For three straight weeks now, the Lions have played decent-to-great defenses, and they’ve hung at least 30 on each. That has to make you feel pretty good right now. Unfortunately, Thursday also presented the first real test of this defense in months, and they failed spectacularly. All of the problems that we saw earlier in the season—missed assignments, poor run defense, failure to capitalize on opportunities to get off the field—re-emerged. It begs the question as to whether all of Detroit’s defensive improvements over the past couple of months were real or the result of playing poor offenses. Particularly concerning is the play of the linebacking corps, where Detroit doesn’t seem to know who they can depend upon. With Jack Campbell out, there is no one linebacker that is the defense’s rock. Derrick Barnes barely played in the first half, Malcolm Rodriguez was a huge liability for most of the day, K.J. Britt’s magic seems to have worn off, and even Trevor Nowaske struggled. Additionally, while Derrick Moore had a fantastic first half, Detroit’s pass rush disappeared in the second. Aidan Hutchinson’s presence was certainly missed constantly in the final two quarters when the Lions defense just needed one more play. The good news is that Detroit’s defense was also missing a few key pieces that they’ll likely get back soon. Defensive end DJ Wonnum and safety Chuck Clark would’ve made a difference in this game. Detroit’s nickel and dime looks with Clark, Brian Branch, and Kerby Joseph at safety could alleviate some of the linebacker issues. And Wonnum can help with pass rush. So, ultimately, I feel a little worse. The defensive problems aren’t likely to completely go away soon. But with how the offense is playing right now, I still believe everything can be on the table for this team. How are you feeling after the Lions’ 39-35 loss? Vote in the poll below and share your thoughts in the comment section.

title: 12 winners, 7 losers from Detroit Lions’ loss to the Chicago Bears
summary: It was a Thanksgiving feast for offenses on this day. Unfortunately for the Detroit Lions, they were on the wrong side of a 39-35 barnburner. The Chicago Bears pulled ahead with a last-second touchdown pass, the culmination of a defense that could not find its footing. The Lions got some phenomenal performances from the offense, […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 26: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field on November 26, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was a Thanksgiving feast for offenses on this day. Unfortunately for the Detroit Lions, they were on the wrong side of a 39-35 barnburner. The Chicago Bears pulled ahead with a last-second touchdown pass, the culmination of a defense that could not find its footing. The Lions got some phenomenal performances from the offense, including Jahmyr Gibbs going over the 200-yard mark, but it wound up not mattering as the defense could not force Chicago off the field. This game was Detroit’s biggest test since Week 8, and while there were some positives, a lot has to go wrong to lose a game like this. Let us examine the winners and losers from this Thanksgiving Day tilt. Note: The label of “loser” is used to evaluate and contrast in-game performance and is not an indictment of a player’s ability, value, or character. The term is not intended to be disrespectful in nature. Loser: Kelvin Sheppard, DC The Lions defense had impressed over the last six games, but there was the caveat that they came against weak opponents. Detroit’s first game against Chicago would be their first true test—how could they handle a high-flying offense? The answer: they couldn’t. It was near-universal failure from the defense, specifically in the second half. The Bears turned two third quarter possessions into touchdowns. In the fourth quarter after the Lions scored a 70-yard touchdown to go up 35-24 with 8:20 left in the game—normally the dagger—the defense utterly collapsed. They gave up an uninspired, 71-yard touchdown drive in just one minute and three plays. Detroit was fortunate that the Bears had a turnover on downs on their next drive, but promptly allowed a 68-yard touchdown drive to end the game. The Lions were constantly getting beat in the flats, allowing D’Andre Swift to rack up a team-leading 97 receiving yards. Caleb Williams rarely had to make difficult decisions or throws because the flat was consistently open to attack. It’s difficult to say initially if there was a schematic issue or a performance issue, but both problems reflect poorly on Sheppard. This persisted throughout the game—it’s one thing to get beat like this early, but to get beat drive after drive on the exact same play is beyond frustrating, it’s incompetent. Couple this with the Lions opting to rush just three players on the pivotal final Bears goal line possession, and it was defensive malpractice from Detroit. Even if Detroit rebounds in the next weeks against the Atlanta Falcons or Tennessee Titans, how much faith are you actually putting in the defense? Detroit might not face another top-tier offense until their trip to Chicago in January, so my concerns about the performance of this defense will remain until then. Winner: Derrick Moore, DE No Aidan Hutchinson, no DJ Wonnum. Enter Derrick Moore. He was a game-changer early on Thanksgiving. In the first half, this was his stat line: four tackles, two sacks, and two forced fumbles, one of which resulted in a safety (and the ensuing drive ended with a touchdown). Chicago scored just 10 points in the first half and Moore’s performance was a key reason why. Moore was held off the stat line in the second half, but there are some extenuating circumstances. For one, Chicago started to attack the flats more and more, thus giving the Lions pass rush little time to attack. Considering that the Bears were in obvious passing downs for most of the second half, the pass rush largely fell on him, rookie Anthony Lucas, or the blitz. Secondly, it was noted that Moore had a heating pad on his knee, showing he was battling some kind of injury. Also, on the Lions’ lone second-half sack by Malcolm Rodriguez, Moore was a hair behind him and would have had the sack otherwise. All in all, you can see the difference Moore can make when things are clicking. Winner: Jared Goff, QB Goff was locked in on Thanksgiving. Last week against the Buccaneers, Goff had one of his best games of the year, and his encore performance this week was just as good. Play after play, Goff was making brilliant throws with pinpoint accuracy. He and Amon-Ra St. Brown had a telepathic-like connection—on multiple instances, Goff put the ball in the exact spot where St. Brown would be, even with a defender a hair out of place. Goff isn’t afraid to throw a block either . I don’t fault him for the interception, as it was tipped and bounced off the hands of Jameson Williams. Goff finished the day going 25-of-36 for 313 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. I don’t fault him for the interception, as it was tipped and bounced off the hands of Jameson Williams. Goff is as steady as they come. He will never outrun defenses, nor is he an incredible scrambler, but he is smart and poised. Those are two traits that are invaluable for an NFL offense. I did not love the failed second-down pass to Brock Wright late in the game, both in terms of play call or execution—that one play was the extent my complaints with Goff on the day. Joe Burrow and Brock Purdy are MVP frontrunners right now, but Goff should be on their heels. Although… Winner: Jahmyr Gibbs, RB …you can make a legitimate case that Gibbs is the MVP as well. Gibbs finally got his breakthrough run this week, scampering 70 yards down the field for his third score of the day. He finished the day with an absurd 205 rushing yards on 21 carries plus three touchdowns. He quietly added five catches for 47 yards as well. A performance like this would be a game-winner under normal circumstances, but the Lions defense wasted it. Week in, week out, Gibbs is the spark plug of the offense. He is the rare non-quarterback worthy of earning the title of Most Valuable Player. Unfortunately, having Gibbs and Goff on the same team arguably works against them with regards to MVP voting—quarterback is the more valuable position, yet Gibbs is playing at such a high level. I would personally have Gibbs ahead in that race, but we shall see come award season. Winner: Juice Scruggs, OC This is a hot take, I know. Three false start penalties should normally get Scruggs into the loser category, but I think there is a valid excuse for at least two of them: Bears defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons was seemingly yelling the snap. This is illegal, by the way . After the second false start, Simmons received a talking to by the officials during a commercial break. It is unclear if Simmons was again jawing to force Scruggs’ third false start, so I will dock him for that one at least. Aside from the penalties, Scruggs was dynamite as a blocker. The CBS commentary crew wouldn’t mention it, but Simmons was getting worked by the Lions interior and Scruggs specifically. On the pivotal 39-yard catch by Jameson Williams at the end of the first half, it was Scruggs putting Simmons on the ground: Goff to Jamo downfield for 39 yards! CHIvsDET on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/uzCbjt86qP — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 If you rewatch the game, I implore that you watch for Simmons’ orange sleeves. More often than not, it was Scruggs winning those battles, not the All-Pro defensive tackle. Simmons finished without a sack and per PFF’s live stats, just one pressure recorded. Considering that Scruggs had a tough time versus Vita Vea last week, seeing him succeed against Simmons like this is a massive win. Penalties can be cleaned up, especially when the other side should have been flagged for it instead. Loser: Malcolm Rodriguez, LB Normally one of the Lions’ most athletic cover linebackers, Rodriguez looked anything but on Thursday. In coverage, he looked incredibly sluggish. On a D’Andre Swift reception, his slow reaction led to him getting stiff-armed en route to a 33-yard reception. On the ensuing play, Rodriguez failed to stick…
