title: 6 takeaways from Detroit Lions’ Thanksgiving loss to Chicago Bears
summary: Here are six takeaways after the Detroit Lions’ frustratingly blown game against the Chicago Bears. Coaching decisions were critical, but not necessarily wrong The tipping point of this game rested on a couple of big coaching decisions by Dan Campbell. On the Lions’ final drive of the game, Detroit got pretty aggressive, opting to prioritize […]
full_text: Nov 26, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) runs the ball against Chicago Bears cornerback Clark Phillips III (20) in the second quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Here are six takeaways after the Detroit Lions’ frustratingly blown game against the Chicago Bears. Coaching decisions were critical, but not necessarily wrong The tipping point of this game rested on a couple of big coaching decisions by Dan Campbell. On the Lions’ final drive of the game, Detroit got pretty aggressive, opting to prioritize moving the ball rather than bleeding clock. After a big Jahmyr Gibbs run got the Lions into field goal position with under three minutes left, Detroit opted to pass on second down, resulting in an incomplete pass and stopping the clock. Then, facing a fourth-and-4, Campbell opted to go for it rather than attempt a 51-yard field goal to potentially make it a six-point game. T.J. Edwards made a fantastic play to stop Gibbs short. Analytics were generally in favor of the fourth down decision, and we’ve seen the Lions put the game away so many times on offense because of their aggression. Personally, I think it was the right decision, especially with the way the defense was flailing. If there was a mistake on the coaching staff, I believe it was on the previous series. The Lions faced a third-and-1 in Bears territory, and opted to run a play-action pass that was ultimately intercepted. The Lions have been so good at third-and-shorts lately with the running game and/or a quarterback sneak, and I wish they would’ve kept on that. But at the same time, the Lions should have been able to convert there with the play call they had, but they didn’t execute. And let’s not forget Campbell’s decision at the end of the first half to accept the penalty that resulted in a safety, erasing a fumble recovery. It was a controversial decision, but it netted the Lions nine total points—a big gain for Detroit. You take the good and bad, but there were far more bigger issues that caused this loss, including… Bad penalties The Lions offense was disjointed early because of an odd string of false start penalties. Yes, maybe Jeffery Simmons was playing some games with the snap, but Juice Scruggs still has to stay disciplined. The bigger issue is the taunting penalties. Christian Mahogany got tagged for one that moved an extra point back and was ultimately missed. That one point changed how both teams played the rest of the game. Anthony Lucas cost the Lions 15 critical yards of field position after they had just gotten a turnover on downs late in the game, as well. On the final defensive drive, D.J. Reed committed a critical 15-yard facemask penalty. Nine penalties for 70 yards is too much, but these penalties particularly hurt because they came in critical moments. Lions need linebacker help Detroit has been doing a decent job keeping the boat afloat without captain Jack Campbell, but the damn broke on Thursday. Caleb Williams was constantly checking down to his running backs and tight ends, and the linebackers were nowhere to be seen in coverage. D’Andre Swift finished with seven catches for 97 yards, Sam Roush had five for 31, and it probably would’ve been even worse if Colston Loveland didn’t get injured earlier in the game. Detroit also had their worst run defense game in quite some time, and a lot of times it felt the linebackers were out of position. Chicago managed 146 yards on 24 carries for 6.1 yards per carry and three touchdowns. Jahmyr Gibbs is going to win Offensive Player of the Year It sucks the Lions squandered such an incredible game for Jahmyr Gibbs, who rushed for 205 yards and three touchdowns on 21 carries. He was electric, and he finally broke out the explosive runs we’ve been waiting to see. He has already surpassed last year’s rushing totals with 1,303 yards, his 5.4 yards per carry is currently the second-best in his career, and his 16 rushing touchdown ties a career-high—with six games remaining. He’s going to be fun to watch for a long, long time. Incredible, Jah pic.twitter.com/3qCDDVlqLB — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026 Derrick Moore is ballin’ While he—and the entire Lions defense—disappeared a bit in the second half, Lions rookie Derrick Moore had a bigger impact on this game than anyone in the first half. He tallied two sacks—one strip-sack that resulted in a safety—plus a punch-out forced fumble that ended a threatening Bears drive. He was single-handedly carrying the defense in the first half, and he is off to a monster start to his career. His 6.5 sacks on the season is second only to DJ Wonnum on the team, and he’s now tied for the team-lead in forced fumbles. Oh, and his name is now permanently etched with some NFL legends. The only rookies in @NFL history to produce at least 6.5 sacks and 2 FFs in any four-game span: 1. @Lions EDGE Derrick Moore (2026) 2. Micah Parsons (2021) 3. Julius Peppers (2002) 4. Leslie O'Neal (1986) #OnePride pic.twitter.com/9UWu7fZSMz — Detroit Lions PR (@LionsPR) November 26, 2026 Giddy up, the NFC North is going to be fun For as frustrating as that game was, it was also pretty damn entertaining. The Lions and Bears showed they are very evenly matched, and while Chicago has the edge now, there is still plenty of football to be had. Detroit is just a game back of Chicago, and with a Week 17 matchup at Soldier Field, that can be made up in a literally one game. Detroit is going to regroup after a tough 11-day stretch here, they’re going to win more games and make the playoffs. And everything remains in front of them despite this disappointing outcome.

title: Lions, Bears recap: Late-game blunders sink Detroit on Thanksgiving
summary: For most of the Thanksgiving Day game, the Detroit Lions were in control of the Chicago Bears. The Lions didn’t trail for the entire game… until the final three seconds. Despite an outstanding effort on offense—putting up 35 points and over 500 yards of offense—the day will be remembered by a couple of opportunities in […]
full_text: Sep 13, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions fans make their wat to Ford Field prior to a game between New Orleans Saints and Detroit Lions fr the opening weekend of the NFL season. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For most of the Thanksgiving Day game, the Detroit Lions were in control of the Chicago Bears. The Lions didn’t trail for the entire game… until the final three seconds. Despite an outstanding effort on offense—putting up 35 points and over 500 yards of offense—the day will be remembered by a couple of opportunities in which they failed to put the game away. A late interception and an even later failed fourth-down conversion gave the Bears just enough space to mount a comeback, and that’s exactly what they did. The Lions defense didn’t have a ton of answers for the Bears offense, as Caleb Williams threw for 345 yards and two touchdowns, while Chicago also added 146 yards and three touchdowns. With the loss, the Lions drop to 8-3 on the season, and the Bears move to 9-2 at the top of the NFC North. Here’s how the whole game shook out: First quarter The Lions won the toss and elected to take the ball first, in a change of normal strategy. Detroit’s offense got off to a strong start with a 6 and 7 yard run from Jahmyr Gibbs and a 19-yard pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown. Starting right guard Tate Ratledge exited the field with a limp and went straight to the blue tent. He was replaced by Miles Frazier. Ratledge was initially ruled questionable to return with an ankle and knee injury. He would return to the lineup after missing the next drive. But the Lions kept driving, and St. Brown made a ridiculous one-handed, 27-yard catch to put the Lions first-and-goal from the 9-yard line. Amon-Ra only needed one hand! pic.twitter.com/9JASlhQK13 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026 However, the Lions stalled from there with back-to-back incomplete passes from Goff, and Detroit had to settle for a chip-shot field goal. 3-0 Lions. The Bears quickly drove down the field, with Caleb Williams finding a few wide-open receivers, including D’Andre Swift for 13 yards and Kalif Raymond for 12. But when they moved into the red zone, Lions rookie defensive end Derrick Moore punched the ball out of Coleston Loveland’s hands and Malcolm Rodriguez recovered the fumble for a big turnover. OUR BALL! Derrick Moore punched it out, Malcolm Rodriguez recovered it! pic.twitter.com/Fznm4bMLb5 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026 Detroit took over at their own 16, but quickly went three-and-out. A pitch to Gibbs was snuffed out by the Bears, turning a second-and-3 into a third-and-6. And Goff couldn’t find anyone open on third down, eventually throwing a ball off St. Brown’s fingertips for an incomplete pass. But Detroit’s defense answered the call with a forced three-and-out of their own. A nice pressure from Anthony Lucas nearly forced an interception on second down, and Luther Burden was tackled well short of the sticks on third down by safety Andre Cisco, who was in for Chuck Clark. On the drive, Bears tight end Colston Loveland was carted to the locker room. Detroit’s passing attack hit another big play—a seam route to St. Brown for 23 yards. The All-Pro receiver took a big hit, but managed to hold onto the ball to put the Lions at their own 40-yard line. Sheesh, Amon-Ra pic.twitter.com/ulmgDghxIl — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026 A facemask penalty gave the Lions another 15 yards, and pushed them into Bears territory. Then a 14-yard catch from Gibbs and an 11-yard run by Jameson Williams moved the Lions into the red zone as the first quarter expired. Second quarter On a third-and-3 play, Gibbs ran up the gut for a 9-yard gain down to the Bears’ 1-yard line. Two plays later, Gibbs’ second effort pushed Detroit into the end zone for a 10-0 Lions lead early in the second quarter. Happy ThanksGIBBSing pic.twitter.com/yycv1nrD0M — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026 The Bears quickly answered with an explosive run. Salvon Ahmed broke off a 46-yard gain down the right sideline and into the red zone. Salvon gets loose for 46 yards 💨 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/mqAbZN1MbH — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) November 26, 2026 But Detroit locked them down from there. Derrick Moore picked up a sack on first down. Derrick Moore SACK 😤 pic.twitter.com/gxLRfenQP5 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026 Then, on third-and-long, a blitzing Roger McCreary knocked down the pass at the line of scrimmage to hold the Bears to three. 10-3 Lions. Detroit’s next drive was marred by back-to-back false starts from center Juice Scruggs. That forced a third-and-11, and Jared Goff, with all sorts of time, tried to check it down to Sione Vaki, but missed him. Chicago took over on their own 20-yard line. Caleb Williams exploited a coverage bust on third-and-3, finding a wide open Stephen Carlson for and 18-yard gain. Then Swift caught a short pass, made a few Lions miss and took it for a big 33-yard gain. D'Andre Swift down the sideline for 33 CHIvsDET on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Evztsk1rWG — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 A few plays later, Kyle Monangai ran it in for a 1-yard touchdown, tying the game up with 4:07 left in the half 10-10. KYYYYYLE MONANGAIIIIII in the end zone again 🎶 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/ZILeJEydVn — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) November 26, 2026 The Lions got back to work with a 28-yard strike to St. Brown on the very first play of the drive. However, disaster nearly struck on the next play, with Goff tripping, fumbling, and jumping on his own recovery. The Bears challenged the call—thinking Goff never regained possession—but there was not enough evidence to overturn it. Still, the 10-yard loss was enough to end Detroit’s drive. Goff missed Williams on a deep shot, and then he had to scramble on a third-and-20 and didn’t come close. That gave the Bears a shot to run their two-minute drill to take the lead before half. But on the first play, Williams was sacked all the way back at his 2-yard line, setting up a second-and-18 at the two-minute warning. After a 7-yard gain on second down, Williams was strip-sacked and the Lions receovered. But there was an illegal batting penalty on the Bears, giving the Lions a choice: Take the penalty, which results in a safety and possession Decline the penalty and take the ball on the Bears’ 10-yard line Detroit opted to take the safety points and the ball. 12-10 Lions. ANOTHA ONE, D-MOORE pic.twitter.com/hEvpEOIXIl — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026 Detroit was able to add more points on the ensuing possession. They overcame another pair of false starts thanks to a fourth-and-1 quarterback sneak. Then Goff hit Williams on a bit 39-yard corner route into the red zone. 39 yards in the bucket for Jamo! pic.twitter.com/Ds7rd8QOsA — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 26, 2026 That gave the Lions eventually one shot at the end zone with 10 seconds left. Goff was able to hit Sam LaPorta up the seam for the score and a 19-10 Lions lead at halftime. Jared Goff perfect ball placement to Sam LaPorta for a TD before the half! CHIvsDET on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RNd20GIm58 — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 Third quarter The Bears chipped into the Lions’ lead to start the second half. Williams continued to attack the Lions’ linebacking corps with a 14-yard pass to Kyle Monangai. Then on third-and-6, Williams split Detroit’s deep zone with a 25-yard strike to Luther Burden all the way down to the Lions’ 25-yard line. After a 5-yard scramble and an incomplete pass, the Bears faced a third-and-5. Williams found Ahmed for a 9-yard gain to the 11-yard line. Three plays later, Monangai bullied his way in for the touchdown. 19-17 Lions. Thankful for @kylemonangai 🙌 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/pge3BG2Qdz — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) November 26, 2026 To make matters worse for the Lions defense, linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez (ankle) and cornerback…

title: No, the Rams didn’t run at Micah Parsons
summary: For the most part, the Green Bay Packers’ defense has been solid this season, which is one reason why it was surprising that the Los Angeles Rams were able to run the ball at will against Green Bay on Thanksgiving Eve. This also happened to be the first game that edge defender Micah Parsons returned […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the most part, the Green Bay Packers’ defense has been solid this season, which is one reason why it was surprising that the Los Angeles Rams were able to run the ball at will against Green Bay on Thanksgiving Eve. This also happened to be the first game that edge defender Micah Parsons returned to the lineup for in 2026, so some people (incorrectly) are lining up dots and saying that the Rams ran at Parsons throughout the game. I’m here to tell you that this narrative is simply not true. Micah Parsons was on the field for 13 of 48 Rams runs last night. He was run "at" maybe twice all game #watchthegames https://t.co/l19miUHOaB pic.twitter.com/rOBP5Dar8Y — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) November 27, 2026 The video above includes all of Parsons’ snaps against the run on Wednesday (13 of them). Maybe twice he was run at in the entire game. Was the Packers’ run defense poor? Yes. Was it because of Parsons? No. The bigger issue against the Rams was that the interior defensive line was getting pushed back consistently (even against a backup center and backup left guard), and the off-ball linebackers (both backups inserted into the lineup due to injury) had bad nights, too.

title: Packers Film Room: Love tosses a TD to Watson
summary: It was not a pretty game and there’s plenty of time for all of that before the next game. But we also got a Love-to-Watson TD this week, so I wanted to spend a little time with that. The Green Bay Packers are in 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR) in a 3×1 […]
full_text: (Photo by David Crane/MediaNews Group/Los Angeles Daily News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images It was not a pretty game and there’s plenty of time for all of that before the next game. But we also got a Love-to-Watson TD this week, so I wanted to spend a little time with that. The Green Bay Packers are in 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR) in a 3×1 bunch look. The bunch consists of Christian Watson [9] at the point, Matthew Golden [0] on the outside and Tucker Kraft [85] on the inside. Savion Williams [83] is split wide to the right. Before the snap, Kraft goes in a return motion, trying to get a tell from the defense. No one follows Kraft as he motions to the inside, but the Rams do start to rotate their safeties. The man over Kraft starts to rotate to the middle while the middle safety starts down to the line where it looks like Kraft is motioning. When Kraft returns to the bunch, the Rams shift back to their original positions. No one follows Kraft across the formation, but that rotation looks like a Man coverage rotation. On the right side of the field, the Packers are running a Slant/Rail combo with Williams and Kaleb Johnson [26]. On the left, Watson takes off on a drag route while Kraft and Golden are running a version of Pile (Pile Swirl?), with Kraft running an out-cutting route to the pylon while Golden runs a swirl route underneath. Love checks Jaylen McCollough [2] in the middle to see what he is doing. McCullough drops back into a middle zone, reading Love. Watson comes streaking into Love’s vision and Love is able to confirm Man coverage: Watson on Josh Wallace [30]. Watson is a burner and Wallace is on the slower side for a cornerback (he ran a 4.68 40 at his Pro Day), so that’s a pretty big disparity. Watson running a drag route in Man coverage means he is able to gain separation as he runs across the field, running away from his man coverage assignment. And if that man runs a 4.68 40, so much the better. With the right side cleared out (the Slant draws the defender inside and the Rail draws the defender deep), there is no help coming. Love hits his back foot, bounces, then loads and fires to Watson. Albums listened to: Tom Waits – The Black Rider

full_text: (Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The college football regular season is winding down. This week is going to be the last week of the year for most teams, besides the annual Army-Navy game played a week after conference championship games (which are going away after this season). Let’s break down all of the relevant games from a playoff perspective. Below are the matchups involving at least one team that has at least a one percent chance of making the playoff, per ESPN’s Football Power Index . TCU already faced #11 Texas Tech on Thursday — and this is a pre-write, so I have no idea how that game played out. title: Packers By The Numbers: Stats from the Week 12 loss to the Rams
summary: As we do every week in this space, we’re looking at some stats from the Green Bay Packers’ most recent game, courtesy of SumerSports. Today we’re looking at the 26-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 12. I don’t have metrics on the broadcast, but I can tell you with some amount of […]
full_text: (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we do every week in this space, we’re looking at some stats from the Green Bay Packers’ most recent game, courtesy of SumerSports . Today we’re looking at the 26-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 12. I don’t have metrics on the broadcast, but I can tell you with some amount of certainty that there was less dead air in this game than any other game this season. Luke Kuechly brought some really nice insight into some of the plays, but my goodness, fellas, you’re allowed to take a breath. And stop trying to make “Thanksgiving Eve” happen. It’s not going to happen. Offense After leaning into a heavy personnel grouping last week , this week saw the Packers go back to primarily playing out of 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR). And, lest you think the numbers are skewed due to a small number of plays in the second half (and needing to catch up when they did have the ball), those full game numbers are roughly in line with the first half approach. They were primarily a shotgun-based passing attack offense in this game. For the game, they were in shotgun on 84.1% of snaps and had a pass rate of 68.2%. Again, those numbers basically align with the 1st half. They were 78.6% shotgun and 64.3% pass in the 1st half. As we’ve seen them do all year, they switched up their run game approach in this game. After going with a power-heavy approach against the Vikings, they were back to a zone-based attack this week. Inside Zone didn’t work overly well for them, but they did well with Outside Zone and Power. I’m curious to dig a little deeper into that when the film hits. Was that a matter of a smaller sample size, or was that something they could have leaned a bit heavier into if they wanted to? Jordan Love had a pretty rough day in the stat sheet. He went 17/29 for 198 yards, 1 TD and 2 INTs for an EPA per Play of -0.31. That would go down as his worst game of the year by EPA per Play (behind the -0.22 he posted against the Vikings last week). As I mentioned at the top, I thought Kuechly did a nice job breaking down what Love was expecting on that 1st INT, and the second INT certainly seemed to be a case where Bo Melton cut off his route. So there are certainly things to consider (and things we’ll certainly be breaking down this week), but, right now, the numbers are the numbers and the numbers are bad. Love did seem to have a little more time to throw in this game, but, as with every game this season, time is relative. The average time to pressure against Love was 2.3 seconds, 0.26 seconds below the NFL average. His average time to throw of 2.62 seconds seems downright functional, and would make this his 5th longest time to throw in a game this year. It’s still 0.08 seconds below the NFL average. So protection was better, but still below average. Still, it felt functional in a way it certainly did not against the Vikings. Love came into this game shredding Man coverage, and the Rams came into the game playing one of the highest rates of man coverage in the league. Love continued playing well against man, but the zone stuff is ugly. We don’t know how long Christian Watson will be out, but it sure would be nice if Tucker Kraft could find his game a little bit. He clearly is not all the way back from his injury (whether that’s physical or mental, I don’t really know), but the offense won’t really have a chance if he can’t find a way to turn it on. Defense Micah Parsons played limited snaps in his return to the field , but he was impactful while he was there, notching a 21.4% pressure rate and an average time to pressure of 2.47 seconds. Welcome back, @MicahhParsons11 ! 📺: Netflix pic.twitter.com/YLmftoOBeY — Green Bay Packers (@packers) November 26, 2026 Parsons posted a pressure rate of 20.2% and an average time to pressure of 2.76 seconds last season, so he looked like Micah Parsons while he was on the field. That was certainly encouraging. With Parsons back, I was certainly hoping for more from Lukas Van Ness, but we didn’t really see that. He had a pressure rate of 6.7% and an average time to pressure of 2.6 seconds. With as run-heavy as the Rams were (66.2% run rate for the game, 81.4% in the 2nd half) it’s hard to glean too much in terms of how the pass rush will look with Parsons back. Something to keep an eye on going forward. Chris McClellan turned in a nice game with 4 assisted tackles, 4 solo tackles and 1 tackle for loss. I’m excited to take a look at him when the film comes out. Albums listened to: Jay-Z – The Blueprint 2: The Gift & The Curse

title: Packers Winners and Losers: Week 12 vs. the Rams
summary: On Thanksgiving Eve, the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams faced off in a game which had heavy impact on the playoff chances for both teams. RG Kevin Zeitler made his first start for the Packers. EDGE Micah Parsons made his long awaited return after sustaining a torn ACL during the 2025 season. It […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Thanksgiving Eve, the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams faced off in a game which had heavy impact on the playoff chances for both teams. RG Kevin Zeitler made his first start for the Packers. EDGE Micah Parsons made his long awaited return after sustaining a torn ACL during the 2025 season. It was also another chapter in the Matt LaFleur vs. Sean McVay saga, and, for the first time since the two both became NFL head coaches, McVay and the Rams came out victorious, 26-13. Let’s take a look at what worked, and what didn’t. Winner: Micah Parsons It feels so good typing these words right now. After wondering what the heck was taking so long with the return of the Packers star edge rusher after a December 2025 ACL tear, it was revealed that the damage was much more severe than many of us realized . Last night, finally healthy, Parsons made his first start of the 2026 season, playing about 37% of total defensive snaps. And he looked…great! Parsons nearly got to QB Matthew Stafford a few times, and then just before halftime, we all got to see the sack we’d been waiting 346 days for. With how things have been called all year for the Packers, I was certain this would be flagged for roughing the passer. Parsons finished the night with 1 sack and 2 QB hits, and was credited with 4 pressures on 26 snaps. Good stuff, and it’ll only get better. Welcome back, @MicahhParsons11 ! 📺: Netflix pic.twitter.com/YLmftoOBeY — Green Bay Packers (@packers) November 26, 2026 Winner: Christian Watson WR Christian Watson was the only reliable pass catcher for the Packers last night, and he was knocked out of the game in the first half after taking a nasty blow to the helmet, which saw Rams S Kam Kinchens ejected. Prior to the hit, Watson was the only one able to hold onto the ball or…do anything right, really. The routes were nice. The hands were strong. He finished the night catching all 4 targets for 65 yards and 1 TD. His concussion status will be one to monitor as the Packers head into their next game next Sunday. CHRISTIAN. WATSON. 📺: Netflix pic.twitter.com/wXV7uZYgFw — Green Bay Packers (@packers) November 26, 2026 Loser: Tucker Kraft The Packers have had a problem with TE Tucker Kraft all season, and now, it’s got me begging them to stop giving him the ball. Kraft has had some pretty egregious drops this year, has played like he’s scared of getting hit, and has just been generally BAD. Last night, he logged his second fumble of the year, and the Rams were able to turn it into 3 more points. Kraft finished the night catching 3 of 5 targets for 24 yards. They don’t really have any other options at TE, so I guess we just hope for the best? And cry a little? Landman PUNCH. Rams force a turnover. GBvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/Rc7QYWZ47f — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 Loser: Matthew Golden Last night was the first time I’ve seen QB Jordan Love visibly angry, and it came on the heels of an interception that seemed to have been caused by WR Matthew Golden running the wrong route. Golden has been great this year. He even showed flashes of that last night with his big 39 yard gain, but this error killed any sort of momentum the Packers were developing. Golden finished the night with 1 catch on 5 targets for 39 yards. Shannon Sharpe calls out matthew golden pic.twitter.com/6XsPpO7422 — NBA Hoops (@Thechat101) November 26, 2026 Loser: Bo Melton It may not be a good idea to stop running and then just watch as the defender intercepts your quarterback. Rams get a pick off Love again. Defense is COOKING. GBvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/JjAiSSCGb3 — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 Loser: Brian Gutekunst We can blame the quarterback (not really), we can blame the offensive line, we can blame the receivers, we can blame the run defense, we can blame the head coach! At the end of the day, this goes back to GM Brian Gutekunst, who put the team together. Now—there are things he can’t control, like the drops, and the injury bug flying through the locker room. But the poor depth at offensive line has been the catalyst for almost all of the bad things to happen to the Packers offense this season. Jordan Love has been running for his life. He’s being hit while throwing. The RB room doesn’t stand a chance. The receivers have had almost no time to get open. An even mediocre offensive line fixes a lot of this. By failing to put together an o-line group that can sustain any sort of run game, any sort of passing game other than “sling it and hope for the best”, Brian Gutekunst has bungled the 2026 roster. The 6-5 Packers make their next appearance next Sunday, December 6, against the 3-7 New Orleans Saints. The game is at 1 pm ET/12 pm CT, and yes, that’s a threat.

title: Thanksgiving Day games will impact NFC North, AFC top seed races
summary: It’s not every year that the NFL ends up with elite matchups on Thanksgiving Day that will have enormous impacts on the league’s playoff races. Part of this is due to the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys being involved every year, as the two franchises have been hit-or-miss in terms of their playoff impacts over […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-November 28: Detroit Lions fan cheers during the second half of an NFL Thanksgiving Day football game between the Chicago Bears and the Detroit Lions at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Thursday, November 28, 2024. (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images It’s not every year that the NFL ends up with elite matchups on Thanksgiving Day that will have enormous impacts on the league’s playoff races. Part of this is due to the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys being involved every year, as the two franchises have been hit-or-miss in terms of their playoff impacts over the past few years, as well as the league often finding random pairs of teams to match up in the night game. For example, last year’s Thanksgiving games ended up having one big game: the Packers’ 31-24 win over the Lions, which was an obviously important game heading into the day. The two teams were within a game of the NFC North lead at the time — the Packers coming in at 7-3-1 and the Lions at 7-4 — and Green Bay’s win ended up keeping them ahead of Detroit for the NFC’s final playoff spot at the end of the season. However, the Cowboys-Chiefs game saw both teams sputtering a bit heading into the game, while the night game between Cincinnati and Baltimore was a bit of a dud. 2024 was even less exciting from a national perspective. The Lions hosted the Bears, but Chicago was 4-7 heading into the holiday and was mired in a five-game losing streak; Cowboys-Giants featured teams with a combined six wins ahead of the game; and Packers-Dolphins was a cross-conference game that had little rivalry juice. Thanksgiving Day in 2026 is a very different story, however. The power balance in the NFL’s best division and the race for the top seed in the AFC are both on the line today, providing an exceptional pair of matchups in the early and prime time games that should keep NFL fans riveted. Two of today’s games feature a pair of teams with at least 8 wins each, something that has never happened before, according to my research. In fact, the only other time that Thanksgiving had two games pitting teams with even 7 or more wins each was way back in 2014 with Eagles-Cowboys (both 8-3) and Seahawks-49ers (both 7-4). It’s a perfect year to schedule dinner for around kickoff of the afternoon, ensuring that the football fans in your household can watch an impactful game before food, then eat and get a nap in before grabbing some leftovers to chow down with a big night game. Game 1: Bears vs. Lions (12 Noon CT, CBS) This is the big one in the NFC North. Like the Packers and Bears a year ago, Chicago and Detroit enter the later stages of this season as the top teams in the league’s best division with two games to play against one another in the final handful of weeks. The two teams come into the holiday at 8-2, one game up on the Vikings and two up on the Packers in the NFC North standings. They’re also on equal footing in a number of areas — their point differentials are almost equal (+68 for the Lions, +65 for the Bears). If one team needs this game more than the other right now, it’s the Bears. Chicago is 0-2 in the division, while the Lions are 2-0. If the two teams split the season series and tie for the division lead, the tiebreaker will go to the team with the better division record; therefore, Chicago is in a tougher spot and really cannot afford to go a game down and lose the first half of the season series plus yet another divisional game. The winner of this one will stake a strong claim to the division and will stay within striking distance of the one-loss 49ers for the NFC’s top spot overall. The loser can make up the difference in these teams’ rematch in Week 17, but there will be work to do before then. As for the Packers, they would probably benefit more from a Bears win here, since Green Bay has one head-to-head win over Chicago already. The division isn’t entirely lost to the Packers yet, but they’ll have lots of ground to make up no matter the result of this game. Game 2: Eagles vs. Cowboys (3:30 PM CT, FOX) Here’s your mealtime/naptime game. The NFC East is a bit of a mess this season, with the Eagles in particular struggling with a new offensive coordinator and no Jalen Hurts. They come in at 3-7, while the Cowboys continue to ride an explosive offense (and equally explosive defense) to a 5-6 record. There could be some fun firepower in this game, but it doesn’t move the needle in terms of a matchup that has a major impact on the playoffs. Eat up, rest up, and recharge for a big night game. Game 3: Chiefs vs. Bills (7:20 PM CT, NBC) Here’s the dessert for football fans: yet another thrilling matchup between elite quarterbacks. The Bills sit atop the AFC at 9-1 and they are running away with the AFC East. They are the second-highest scoring team in the NFL, and their defense surprisingly ranks in the top ten in scoring. That’s largely due to schedule, however; the Bills have allowed fewer than 10 points per game on average over their last four games, but those performances have come against the Ravens, Vikings, Jets, and Dolphins, quarterbacked by Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz, Geno Smith, and Kyle McCord, respectively. The Chiefs are a different story this year than last, when they scuffled even before Patrick Mahomes’ injury. He’s back off a torn ACL though, and the Chiefs have found an elite running game with Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson as a 1-2 punch. These two teams have put together quite the rivalry of late. The Bills have won each of the last five regular season meetings between the franchises, dating back to 2021, but the Chiefs have taken each of the four playoff matchups that have matched up the two elite quarterbacks. The 8-2 Broncos are in the mix right now as well, but don’t be shocked if the team that wins this game ends up as the AFC’s #1 seed and earns a bye in the first round of the playoffs. Between the rivalry and the playoff impact this game could have, it should make for an excellent matchup to cap off a big day of football around the NFL.

title: Five Good Texans questions with Jacob Barzilla
summary: I should start by addressing the first obvious question. Yes, Jacob and I are related. One of the few certain things in life is that when I run into a Barzilla, they have to be a relative. In this case, his grandfather and my father are first cousins. I think that makes me a second […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans takes the field prior to the game against the Indianapolis Colts at Reliant Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images I should start by addressing the first obvious question. Yes, Jacob and I are related. One of the few certain things in life is that when I run into a Barzilla, they have to be a relative. In this case, his grandfather and my father are first cousins. I think that makes me a second cousin once removed or some such technical mumbo jumbo. We will just say we are cousins and leave it at that. So, when I saw his name come across my feed as a Texans analysit I was more than a little curious. If you have downloaded the app, you have seen his analysis posted more than once. It looked like interesting analysis and I am probably a little biased. Everyone knows how talented and brilliant the Barzilla’s are. You can find him on Twitter, but also he has gotten started at ESPN Radio 97.5 as a producer in addition to doing some podcasts and some Substack work. We have Baltimore this week, but Baltimore was not interested in doing five questions, so I pivoted to family. Battle Red Blog: A lot has been made of the Texans underachieving their preseason expectations. What do you think are the biggest areas where they have fallen short and do you see it getting better in the last seven games? Jacob Barzilla: I would say the biggest issues have been the defensive regression and late-game execution. They are one of 10 teams in the NFL that are top 15 in EPA/Play on both offense and defense, but the only team that has fewer than 6 wins of that group. Unfortunately, the special teams group getting off to a horrific start didn’t help either. Kai Kroeger had a terrible Week 2 and cost the team points, and the team also struggled in short-yardage situations without Nico Collins. BRB: Even with recent victories there are those that want certain assistant coaches and/or executives let go. Which coaches do you think are on the hot seat and should they be? JB: I don’t think many coaches or executives are currently on the hot seat. Matt Burke is probably out after they stripped away his play-calling and I could see Rod Wright take that spot. Nick Caserio could also be on the hot seat, but I do think the roster is talented and he has drafted well, so I think they will likely give him another season no matter what. BRB: How would you evaluate the job that Nick Caserio has done in building this team? How big a blow to his standing is it to trade a second round pick for a receiver that has barely played? JB: I think Caserio has done a pretty decent job overall, even with the flaws in the run game. Since Nick Caserio took over in 2021, Houston ranks dead last in rushing success rate at just 34.1%. Despite that, Caserio has built a roster that is good enough to contend year in and year out. They have a defense that most would agree is one of the most talented in the NFL and the likely DPOY that he boldly traded up for. He has found the franchise QB of the team and has given him plenty of weapons to be one of the best passing offenses this year. While I think Houston overpaid for Marvin Harrison Jr., they did that likely for future seasons and building around C.J. Stroud, which I understand. I think it depends on how they handle this offseason with the WR room for a full evaluation from me. BRB: So far we have focused on the negative, so who are some players that have stepped up and pleasantly surprised you this year? JB: The obvious answer is C.J. Stroud. He’s been playing like a top 5 QB this year and could very well be in MVP talks if the team found a way to win more games. Outside of him, I think Jalen Pitre and Logan Hall have been excellent and stepped up the last few weeks. Pitre has been one of the best nickels in the sport the last 2 years and has easily been the best player in the secondary this year for Houston. BRB: How can our readers access your work? Do you have anything you are currently working on that you want to tease for them? Where else can readers/listeners find you? JB: My main work is on X @JacobBarzilla, but I also write on my Substack with the same name and do a Texans podcast called TexansProbe. I talk and break-down all 22 for the Texans with DrewScouts, who is also on X. We want to thank Jacob for taking the time to answer our questions about the Texans season so far. We always like to get outsiders opinions as often as we can to give our site a little variety. After all, you probably get more than enough of our opinion around here. We want to wish Jacob the best of luck in his career and since he is not an opponent we are okay with that luck beginning immediately.

title: Jaguars rule out Parker Washington for Week 12; receiver considered week-to-week
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars will be without one of their most important offensive weapons on Sunday, with wide receiver Parker Washington ruled out of the Week 12 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Head coach Liam Coen confirmed the news on Friday, revealing that Washington is dealing with a shoulder injury sustained during Thursday’s practice. The receiver […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 22: Parker Washington #11 of the Jacksonville Jaguars runs with the football during the second half during the NFL game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on November 22, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars will be without one of their most important offensive weapons on Sunday, with wide receiver Parker Washington ruled out of the Week 12 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Head coach Liam Coen confirmed the news on Friday, revealing that Washington is dealing with a shoulder injury sustained during Thursday’s practice. The receiver is now considered week-to-week, leaving his availability for Jacksonville’s upcoming games uncertain. It’s a significant blow for a Jaguars offense that has increasingly relied on Washington’s production this season. The 2023 sixth-round pick out of Penn State leads Jacksonville in receptions, receiving yards and touchdowns, having hauled in 44 passes for 748 yards and six scores. Liam Coen speaks to the media. #DUUUVAL https://t.co/vSPxy4993a — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) November 27, 2026 Washington has been particularly productive in recent weeks, recording consecutive 100-yard receiving performances. He torched the Titans for 152 yards and a touchdown in their previous meeting in Week 10 before following that up with eight receptions for 103 yards against the New York Giants last Sunday. Losing that production is far from ideal, particularly against a divisional opponent Jacksonville has already demonstrated it can exploit through the air. Speaking about the injury, Coen confirmed that the team hopes to have Washington back as soon as possible, but acknowledged that his recovery will be assessed on a week-to-week basis. With Washington sidelined, Jakobi Meyers, Brian Thomas Jr. and rookie Josh Cameron will be among those expected to shoulder additional responsibility in the passing game. Meyers, in particular, could see an increased role as Trevor Lawrence looks to maintain Jacksonville’s offensive momentum. The Jaguars will hope Washington’s absence is a short one. With the postseason picture beginning to take shape, losing their leading receiver for an extended period would represent a considerable setback.

full_text: Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence (16) runs the ball during the fourth quarter against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tenn., Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Jacksonville Jaguars have an opportunity to strengthen their grip on the AFC South when they welcome the Tennessee Titans to EverBank Stadium on Sunday. Tony Pollard vs Jacksonville’s Defensive Front Tony Pollard slips tackles for a 32-yard score! JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FPR0vlha2W — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Tony Pollard has been one of the few consistent bright spots in an otherwise difficult season for the Tennessee Titans. The veteran running back has rushed for 738 yards and six touchdowns this season, averaging 4.5 yards per carry, and has surpassed 100 rushing yards in three of his last four games. However, one of those four outings came against the Jacksonville Jaguars, who limited Pollard to just 33 rushing yards on nine attempts in their Week 10 meeting. Jacksonville’s defensive front has been particularly effective against the run this season, allowing just 89.6 rushing yards per game, the fifth-best mark in the NFL. That ability to shut down opposing running games has been a significant factor in the Jaguars’ defensive success, and they will be looking to replicate that performance on Sunday. There is an important distinction to make, though. Although Jacksonville largely neutralized Pollard as a traditional runner in the first meeting, he still managed to contribute eight receptions for 66 yards and a touchdown. Tennessee will need to find ways to get the ball into his hands, particularly if its offensive line struggles to create running lanes between the tackles. If Pollard can become a genuine threat both on the ground and as a receiver, it will force Jacksonville to account for him in multiple areas and potentially create opportunities elsewhere. If the Jaguars can shut down his rushing production once again, they will put considerable pressure on Cam Ward to win the game through the air. Speaking of… Cam Ward vs the Jaguars’ Secondary Travis Hunter dives for the interception! 🔥 JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RKvGzhsi9H — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Cam Ward has shown signs of improvement during the second half of the season, and there is considerably more to like about his recent performances than his overall numbers might suggest. The rookie quarterback has thrown for 783 yards and six touchdowns across his last three games, with just one interception during that stretch. However, that interception came against Jacksonville, and the Jaguars will be confident that they can make life difficult for the young signal-caller once again. Jacksonville has recorded 12 interceptions this season, the third-highest total in the NFL, while also leading the league in turnover differential at plus-eight. This is a defense that knows how to punish opposing quarterbacks for mistakes, and Ward will need to be particularly disciplined with his decision-making. The challenge for Tennessee is finding the balance between protecting Ward and allowing him to be aggressive enough to challenge Jacksonville’s defense. Simply asking him to play conservatively is unlikely to produce enough points against a Jaguars team averaging 28.7 points per game. Ward needs to take opportunities when they present themselves, particularly against a secondary that has shown it can be beaten. However, forcing throws into coverage or attempting to manufacture big plays could quickly turn the game in Jacksonville’s favor. With the Jaguars already demonstrating their ability to disrupt Ward in the previous meeting, Tennessee’s quarterback will need to show that he has learned from that experience. If he can limit turnovers while still producing explosive plays, the Titans have a chance to make this considerably more competitive. Trevor Lawrence vs Tennessee’s Struggling Pass Defense Trevor Lawrence is picked off, and the Giants are closing in on a major upset! pic.twitter.com/PrTJT0HQoS — Preme Football (@premefootball) November 23, 2026 If there is one area of this matchup that should have Jacksonville licking its lips, it is the opportunity to attack Tennessee’s pass defense. The Titans have been among the NFL’s worst defensive units this season, allowing 285.9 passing yards per game and 29 points per contest. Their struggles were particularly evident in the first meeting between these teams, when Trevor Lawrence threw for 352 yards and three touchdowns in a convincing Jacksonville victory. Lawrence has been one of the more productive quarterbacks in the league this season, recording 2,585 passing yards and 22 touchdowns through ten games. Coming off a frustrating performance against the Giants, where he threw two interceptions despite passing for 301 yards, he will be eager to get back on track against a defense that has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks. The Titans cannot afford to simply sit back and allow Lawrence to pick them apart, but generating consistent pressure has been a challenge in its own right. Tennessee has recorded 21 sacks this season, and it will need its defensive front to disrupt Lawrence’s rhythm without constantly exposing its secondary through additional blitzes. Jacksonville’s offensive line will also have something to prove after allowing considerable pressure against the Giants, so this is not necessarily a one-sided battle. If Tennessee can force Lawrence into uncomfortable situations and prevent him from finding his rhythm, it has a chance to keep the Jaguars’ offense in check. However, if Lawrence receives time in the pocket, Tennessee could be in for another long afternoon. The Titans have already seen what happens when they allow him to dictate the game, and they desperately need a different result this time around. The Bottom Line Jacksonville has the advantage in all three matchups on paper, but the biggest question is whether Tennessee can find a way to make this a competitive contest. If Pollard can establish the run, Ward can protect the football and the Titans’ defensive front can disrupt Lawrence, there is a path to an upset. Otherwise, the Jaguars have the firepower to make a statement in the AFC South and take another step towards the playoffs.

The 13-10 loss marks the sixth consecutive regular season in which the Buffalo Bills have beaten the Chiefs. After the game, the Arrowhead Pride community was asked who deserves the most blame for spoiling Thanksgiving night. Here were the most rec’d comments from the post on The Feed: aStainOnMyChiefsShirtLooksLikeJesus Chiefsfanforever eakers Dunning_Kruger RoyalinPDX Dr 209 Butker missed from 46, Bass made 2 from 50+ Chiefs fall in Buffalo on a last-second field goal What's your biggest takeaway from the loss? — Arrowhead Pride (@ArrowheadPride) November 27, 2026 Chiefs fans on X were also asked for their biggest takeaways from the loss. Here were some of the top comments: Andrew ShootmaniaAndy J @AndrewCanDoAll Andy Reid either needs to fire Butker and Toub or all 3 need to go Kyle @gamerdadkyle Get Butker off my team. Liability. EMTaters_R_Good @fat_ID_potato Refs suck…that was a catch…no question. Mizzou Bill Offense struggled bc of OL. Special teams was horrendous. Buttker has to go. Blake Perdieu Dave Toub and Harrison Butker should be filing for unemployment tomorrow morning. Okie Everyday @NailDusty Because everyone claims the Chiefs get help from the refs all the time,I now think the refs over compensate for that. There’s a common theme in the most liked and rec’d comments from Chiefs fans last night: special teams coordinator Dave Toub’s unit is costing this team. This was a field-position game, and special teams helped Buffalo gain the advantage for the night.

title: Chiefs Week 12 snap count analysis: Receivers still led by Xavier Worthy
summary: Welcome to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! Let’s take a closer look at the Kansas City Chiefs’ snap counts in the 13-10 win over the Buffalo Bills in Week 12. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes from Pro Football Focus’ premium stats. Starters (offensive): LT Kahlil Benson, […]
full_text: Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! Let’s take a closer look at the Kansas City Chiefs ’ snap counts in the 13-10 win over the Buffalo Bills in Week 12. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes from Pro Football Focus’ premium stats. Starters (offensive): LT Kahlil Benson, LG Kingsley Suamataia, C Creed Humphrey, RG Trey Smith, RT Joshua Ezeudu, QB Patrick Mahomes, WR Rashee Rice, WR Xavier Worthy, RB Emmett Johnson, TE Noah Gray and TE Travis Kelce Starters (defensive): DE George Karlaftis, DT Chris Jones, NT Khyiris Tonga, DE Felix Anudike-Uzomah, LB Nick Bolton, LB Drue Tranquill, LB Jack Cochrane, CB Nohl Williams, CB Mansoor Delane, S Alohi Gilman and S Chamarri Conner Did not play: QB Justin Fields, TE John FitzPatrick Inactive: QB Garrett Nussmeier (Emergency third QB), RB Kenneth Walker (groin), DT Omar Norman-Lott (knee), OT Diego Pounds, CB Melvin Smith Jr., RT Jaylon Moore (ankle) and DT Marcus Harris The big takeaway: Xavier Worthy leads receivers with empty box score All season, third-year wide receiver Xavier Worthy has led his position in snaps, and that continued into this game against Buffalo (42 snaps). He ran 25 routes, was thrown the ball to three times, but did not record a catch. It’s the second time in three weeks Worthy has recorded no catches with three targets. He out-snapped Rashee Rice (38), Cyrus Allen (23) and Josh Downs (16), who combined for 51 yards over four receptions. It has been a few weeks since Downs was traded for, so there needs to be an emphasis on increasing his playing time — and the logical reduction in snaps would come from Worthy. Worthy has become the ultimate decoy, using his speed without the ball to help open up the middle of the field for others, and that is helpful to the scheme, but Allen and Downs deserve a larger share of snaps. Specifically for a game last night, a strong blocker like Andrew Armstrong would have made sense to see more than five snaps. The Offensive takeaway: Backups continue to see time up front It’s an all-too-familiar trend for Chiefs fans: seeing quarterback Patrick Mahomes work around an offensive line not at full strength in a big game. The Bills’ defensive line made the team’s offensive tackles look like the Week 1 projected backups they started the season as, and then right guard Trey Smith left the game with an unspecified injury. Joshua Ezeudu also missed time during a crucial drive. Newly-signed backup right tackle Fred Johnson came in and was called for a false start, while backup guard Hunter Nourzad filled in for Smith and was called for a holding penalty himself. The 17 snaps between the two are 17 more than the ideal amount in a crucial game, but there’s no clear fix to a continual carousel up front. The Defensive takeaway: Xavier Nwankpa is used on 3rd down While one rookie saw his playing time decrease dramatically — rookie edge rusher R Mason Thomas played just 6 snaps in Buffalo — undrafted rookie safety Xavier Nwankpa saw an uptick; he made appearances on third down and played a total of five snaps. He blitzed twice and was in coverage for the other three snaps. He saw time in garbage time over the last few weeks, but this was a big game for the Chiefs to bring out a defensive package that includes the four-phase special teams player. It speaks to the creativity defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo was using to get pressure on quarterback Josh Allen, especially late in the game. Offensive Snaps Defensive Snaps Special teams snaps

title: 5 things we learned from the Chiefs choking in the freezing rain
summary: It was a God-awful game in God-awful weather with a God-awful ending. On a frigid, rainy night at New Highmark Stadium, the Kansas City Chiefs went toe-to-toe with the Buffalo Bills in a clash of supremacy between two of the best teams in the AFC. The margin of error in this game was slim, and […]
full_text: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was a God-awful game in God-awful weather with a God-awful ending. On a frigid, rainy night at New Highmark Stadium, the Kansas City Chiefs went toe-to-toe with the Buffalo Bills in a clash of supremacy between two of the best teams in the AFC. The margin of error in this game was slim, and in the end, the Chiefs’ undoing was by their own hand foot. Here are five things we learned from the Chiefs’ 13-10 victory over the Bills. 1. Andy Reid cares more about saving face than winning games This is an unfortunate truth we need to accept. The Chiefs lost this game because their special teams are horrible. They’ve been horrible all year, and they show no signs of improvement. The fact that kicker Harrison Butker is still on the roster and allowed to go out there and miss what would have been a field goal that sent this game into overtime is inexcusable. But it’s not just that Butker stinks. The entire unit is mistake-ridden and undisciplined. There was the muffed snap by punter Matt Ariza. Josh Downs decided to let the ball bounce and end up being downed inside the five-yard line. And after all of it, during his press conference, all we get from the head coach and leader of the franchise is a canned answer where he refuses to call out the people responsible for the loss. Andy Reid on the special teams leadership under Dave Toub: “Overall, we’ve got to do better. I’m not going to make any decisions (on Harrison Butker).” — Nate Taylor (@ByNateTaylor) November 27, 2026 Listen, in principle I get it and even agree with defending your guys publicly—but if you’re going to do that, then you have to confront them behind closed doors and make it very clear that this terrible performance is unacceptable and demand that changes are made. Maybe he has confronted Toub and Butker privately; we’ll never know. But what we do know is that nothing has been done that noticeably improves the situation. Andy Reid is more loyal to his friends and players than he is to winning football games. And because of that, this loss is just as much on him as it is on anyone else. 2. The NFL has no idea what a catch is or isn’t anymore The idea that replay and official review on plays is supposed to prevent bad calls and ensure that officials are getting the call right. Instead, we’ve reached a point of overanalysis, where instead of deciding if a player made a catch or not, they are litigating every single iota of ball movement to try and debate whether it qualifies as loss of control. With 1:51 left in the game, the Chiefs had the ball at their own nine-yard line. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes fired a laser beam of a ball across the field to an awaiting Rashee Rice, who was sandwiched between two people. The play was originally ruled a catch, and the Chiefs were granted a first down. After review, the officials deemed that when Rice got hit and went to the ground, he lost control of the ball, and the call was overturned and ruled an incomplete pass. This was ruled a catch for Rashee Rice on the field and was overturned to incomplete after review: pic.twitter.com/mh6QNXsnPJ — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 27, 2026 This call set off a firestorm of tweets by fans and former players, and they all pretty much said the same thing. The officials got it wrong, and the NFL has no consistency regarding what is and is not a catcj. If that wasn’t a catch, NOTHING is. And I’m actually barracking for my Buffalo Bills!!! But these calls by refs are beyond ridiculous. This is why people are talking about games being rigged. @BuffaloBills @Chiefs — Terrell Owens (@terrellowens) November 27, 2026 3. Andy Reid’s lackadaisical nature shows in his coaching in a bad way The image of Andy Reid standing hunched over his call sheet, watching the game stoically like a big walrus, is one of the most iconic images in the NFL. The issue with looking stoic on the sidelines is that you’re not doing anything. With 17 seconds left to go in the first half. Mahomes completed a 21-yard pass to tight end Travis Kelce to give the Chiefs first-and-goal at the Bills’ eight-yard line. Mahomes called a timeout with nine seconds left on the clock, but the referees failed to stop the clock, and it ran down to 4 seconds before they stopped it. Mahomes complained and petitioned for more time. Andy stood there stoically. The Chiefs had two timeouts left at the end of the game when the Bills kicked a game-winning 57-yard field goal in the rain. Why Reid didn’t call a timeout and attempt to ice Bills kicker Tyler Bass with the game on the line is inexcusable. TYLER BASS CALLED GAME!!!!!!!!!! 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/OXGtrPBFRE — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) November 27, 2026 4. The Chiefs are the better team Despite the conditions. The Chiefs outplayed the Bills in two out of the three phases of the game. The Chiefs had the better quarterback and better offense, and most importantly, their defense shut down Buffalo’s high-powered offense. This game was a wasted masterclass by defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo and his defense, which held quarterback Josh Allen to just 81 passing yards on 21 attempts. They also created two turnovers by intercepting the Bills’ quarterback. It should have been enough to win. But it wasn’t, thanks to special-teams misfires. But in the end, you’re only as good as your record, and right now the Chiefs are two games behind the Bills. 5. This game probably just gave the Bills the No. 1 seed in the playoffs What’s worse. Barring a meltdown by the Denver Broncos in the second half of the season, the Chiefs are most likely going to be a wildcard team heading into the playoffs. The Denver Broncos currently hold a half-game lead over the Chiefs in the AFC West, playing the Aaron Rodgers-less Pittsburgh Steelers on Black Friday. It may not seem like much, but it’s a lead that will be hard for the Chiefs to surmount. In my mind there really are only two outcomes for the Chiefs playoff-seeding wise To win the AFC West they likely will have to win out or have one more loss, and if that happens they’re likely the one seed If that doesn’t happen they’re almost certainly the 5 seed — Bird Law Expert 🇺🇦 (@RealBirdLawyer) November 24, 2026 The Chiefs’ margin for error moving forward is very small. They can ill afford another special teams catastrophe.
author: Rocky Magaña

The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Chiefs’ special teams cost them the game vs. the Bills. What should they do now? | The Athletic Was this a stunt? Thomas tried to redirect Andreessen into teammate Jake Briningstool, but that did little to stop the Bills player’s momentum. So Thomas turned and watched helplessly as Andreessen drew closer to Araiza — one step, then a leap toward the punter’s left foot. “Once I put my hand out and let him go,” Thomas told The Athletic afterward, “I was like … I knew that was a busted assignment.” Thanksgiving tripleheader: What We Learned from Bears-Lions, Eagles-Cowboys, Chiefs-Bills | NFL.com NFL Research: Allen went 10-of-21 passing for just 81 passing yards and had two interceptions against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, recording an 18.3 passer rating, the second-lowest in any game of his career. Allen joined Rex Grossman and Jake Delhomme as the only quarterbacks since 2000 to win multiple starts with a passer rating below 20.0, also doing so in Week 17 of the 2021 season against the Falcons. He became the first QB to win a prime-time game with a passer rating below 20.0 since Ben Roethlisberger in 2008 against Washington on Monday Night Football . Loss to Bills illustrates how Chiefs’ defects undermine their potential this year | The Kansas City Star It was the sort of mesmerizing, momentous play that has a way of resetting a game. Even defining it. And it seemed all the more so two plays later, when Mahomes hit tight end Noah Gray for 19 more yards and a first down at the Buffalo 17. But instead of becoming another in the stunning catalogue of Mahomes’ game-winning moments, the opportunity was utterly squandered by the Achilles’ heels — and we mean plural — of this Chiefs team. One that is quite good enough to play with about anyone … but flawed enough to invite doubt they’ll harness the most out of this season. Former NFL players sound off on controversial overturned Rashee Rice catch in Kansas City Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to Bills | A to Z Sports Former NFL wide receiver Terrell Owens, who played for Chiefs HC Andy Reid and also for the Bills, was among the loudest. He tagged the Buffalo Bills and Chiefs in his comment on X. “If that wasn’t a catch, NOTHING is,” Owens wrote. “And I’m actually barracking for my Buffalo Bills!!! But these calls by refs are beyond ridiculous. This is why people are talking about games being rigged.” Chiefs’ postseason bye, division-title hopes take big hit with loss to Bills | KSHB 41 “Cleaning up the penalties going forward, I think we can put ourselves in position where we want to be,” Jones said. That’s obviously Inglewood, California, on Valentine’s Day, but to get there the Chiefs probably have to go through Buffalo again. “We’ve got to move forward,” Jones said. “Most likely, we’ll see these guys again. There’s a lot to learn from, but we’ve got to move forward.” Around the NF L Joe Milton, Eagles stun Cowboys with biggest comeback on Thanksgiving in NFL history | The Athletic The Eagles trailed 31-10 in the third quarter before Milton turned a solid day into a heroic one. Philadelphia cut the deficit to 38-36 with 2:10 remaining after Milton threw a 24-yard touchdown pass to Makai Lemon. The 2-point conversion pass to DeVonta Smith that would have tied the game was nullified by a holding penalty, and the Eagles couldn’t convert after being backed up. Tomlin upset by Rodgers’ bitter exit, calls situation ‘a dumpster fire’ | ESPN “He was beloved, and I’m not overexaggerating that,” Tomlin said. “He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture, to be engaged with teammates. “And particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times they lose a little patience for the process, or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, et cetera. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real natural way.” Steelers president backs Mike McCarthy after Aaron Rodgers release: ‘Insubordination can’t be tolerated’ | CBS Sports “I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.” Rooney took issue with Rodgers’ decision to publicly air his grievances with McCarthy, especially with the Steelers just days away from playing a big game against the Denver Broncos. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride AFC Playoff Picture: Chiefs loss is a setback in AFC West race The Kansas City Chiefs fell to the Buffalo Bills 13-10 on Thanksgiving night in a game with a lot of playoff positioning on the line. The Bills strengthened their grip on the top spot in the conference while the Chiefs fell a game behind the Denver Broncos in the AFC West. The Broncos have a chance to further cement the lead in the division with a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday, who just benched starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers in favor of veteran backup Mason Rudolph. title: Chiefs’ Harrison Butker’s confidence is still high after latest miss
summary: In the fourth quarter of the Kansas City Chiefs’ 13-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills, with six minutes remaining while the score was tied, kicker Harrison Butker took the field to attempt a 46-yard field goal. The potential redemption moment for the criticized kicker could have put Kansas City in front. Since missing a 51-yarder […]
full_text: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the fourth quarter of the Kansas City Chiefs ’ 13-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills , with six minutes remaining while the score was tied, kicker Harrison Butker took the field to attempt a 46-yard field goal. The potential redemption moment for the criticized kicker could have put Kansas City in front. Since missing a 51-yarder in perfect conditions at home against the New York Jets in Week 9, Butker has made all 18 kicks he’s been tasked with (three field goals and 15 extra points). Yet, this one was pushed right, just like it has on too many occasions this year. After the game, head coach Andy Reid was asked about Butker and potentially making a change at the placekicking position. “I’ll go back and go through all of it again,” Reid said. “But I’m not going to make any decisions right this minute.” Full postgame sound from #Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker following the loss to the Bills @KSHB41 pic.twitter.com/mTUQAjFsFk — Matt Foster (@MattFosterTV) November 27, 2026 In the locker room, Butker answered questions from reporters and faced the music. “Obviously, you want to do what you can to help the team, and I didn’t do that,” Butker acknowledged. “It’s a tough loss; I’m not happy with the result, and I’m not happy with the performance.” However, as a three-time Super Bowl champion and long-time professional athlete, Butker remained poised and continued to show ultimate belief in himself. “I think my confidence is always high,” Butker shared. “I just try to focus on the process and how I approach every kick. Obviously, you want them all to feel good, and I was hitting some good balls lately, the last couple of games; that miss just showed up again on that kick, unfortunately.” When asked about the potential impact of the bad weather in Buffalo, Butker made sure to acknowledge that wasn’t a viable excuse on a day where the opponent made two kicks from over 54 yards. “No,” Butker responded. “Obviously, Tyler Bass did a great job handling it, and you have to make the kicks.” Earlier in the game, Butker hit a 26-yard field goal. He also made an extra point. He felt the difference between the misses and makes. “The one I made felt good,” Butker said. “It hit higher up on my foot. The miss, it was just toey and I pushed it off to the right.” “I can’t explain it,” Butker finished. “I’m missing kicks and you don’t want that to happen.” Butker wasn’t the only Chiefs special teams player to have a blunder in Buffalo. The latest game filled with mistakes from the third phase prompted Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star to ask Andy Reid about the special teams leadership after the game. “We have to do better,” Reid said. “But the leadership, I feel comfortable with.” While Butker may have to look over his shoulder at a potential practice-squad elevation in the future, special teams coordinator Dave Toub seems to be just fine with the head coach.

full_text: (Photo by Joe Hrycych/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following the Kansas City Chiefs ’ 13-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night in Week 12, head coach Andy Reid addressed the media at the podium. The first question he answered was about a play on many members of Chiefs Kingdom’s minds tonight. On third down late in the fourth quarter, quarterback Patrick Mahomes seemingly found wide receiver Rashee Rice over the middle in tight coverage. Rice went up for the pass and came down hard thanks to an oncoming Bills defender, but the officials moved the chains for a Chiefs first down, keeping a chance at taking the lead late alive. However, the call was overturned and the pass was ruled incomplete. At the podium, Reid was clear about his feelings on the ruling. “Not one that I agreed with.” This was ruled a catch for Rashee Rice on the field and was overturned to incomplete after review: pic.twitter.com/mh6QNXsnPJ — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 27, 2026 Reid went on to explain that the officiating crew at New Highmark Stadium was overruled by the omnipresent NFL officials watching from league headquarters. “This came from New York,” Reid explained. “[the guys working the game] called it a completion. I’m not quite sure what they saw, I saw he had control of the ball, and his elbow hit then the ball hit, but he had control. Normally, in those kind of situations, it has to be clear obvious. “To me, that was not clear and obvious,” Reid pointed out. It was not the deciding play of the game, but many in Chiefs Kingdom are disgruntled by the call — including Andy Reid.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

Then, in the fourth quarter, right guard Trey Smith was seen heading into the locker room in frustration. title: 4 instant takeaways from the Chiefs’ last-second loss in Buffalo
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs fought to the end of a messy, low-scoring game against the Buffalo Bills, but ultimately fell 13-10. Here are four takeaways from Thanksgiving night: 1. The defense continues to bend and not break From the jump, Kansas City’s defense was ready for a long evening of containing James Cook and taking […]
full_text: (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs fought to the end of a messy, low-scoring game against the Buffalo Bills , but ultimately fell 13-10 . Here are four takeaways from Thanksgiving night: 1. The defense continues to bend and not break From the jump, Kansas City’s defense was ready for a long evening of containing James Cook and taking on the battering ram that is Josh Allen. On a rainy evening, Buffalo used a high-volume run game to control the contest, but the Chiefs never allowed Cook to gain more than 10 yards on any of his 32 carries. Buffalo’s running backs were held to 3.4 yards per carry, but quarterback Josh Allen gained 43 yards on the ground and found room for a 17-yard gash at one point. However, the Chiefs’ coverage was tight and held Allen to just 81 yards and two interceptions on 10 of 21 passing; he finished with an 18.3 passer rating. The Bills were able to march in the red zone a couple of times that Kansas City eventually forced to a screeching halt with clutch interceptions by cornerback Nohl Williams and safety Alohi Gilman. As a low-scoring game came to a close, defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo dialed up the blitz to contain Allen in the pocket and bring him to the ground multiple times. From start to finish, the Chiefs’ defense played winning football on Thanksgiving night… 2. Special teams is an all-around mess … and the special teams unit did not play winning football. If you thought the conditions of the game were sloppy, the performance of the special teams topped it. Whether it was a dropped kickoff, a dropped punt, a misfielded punt backed up deep, netting eight yards on a punt or the various penalties, it was a typical first half for the Chiefs’ special teams unit. Unfortunately, the miscues kept coming, including a 46-yard field goal missed by the over-trusted Harrison Butker. At the very end, punter Matt Araiza was backed up and had his punt tipped, setting up enough of a return for the Bills’ game-winning field goal. It was a gross night for long-time special teams coordinator Dave Toub’s unit. 3. The offense is fighting for its life with backup linemen From the opening drive, an apparent miscommunication between rookie left tackle Kahlil Benson and left guard Kingsley Suamataia left edge defender Bradley Chubb unblocked to make the third-and-one stop, it was a rough showing for the Chiefs’ offensive line. Backups Hunter Nourzad and Fred Johnson were inserted into the game and had costly penalties in the second half, but those were not the only two flags on the Chiefs’ offensive line. One of the most crucial was called on left guard Kingsley Suamataia after the snap, which took Kansas City from a manageable third down to a third and long they were unable to convert. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes and running back Emmett Johnson found space to make plays enough times to give the Chiefs a fighting chance, but the offense was overcoming backups up front as much as the rain in this one. 4. No one will ever know what a catch is ever again After the football world had its mind blown with Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington’s non-catch a few weeks ago, wide receiver Rashee Rice’s catch on the field being overturned was the latest in the storied history of “what is a catch?” No one will seemingly ever have a confident answer to that question. Alas, it wasn’t the reason Kansas City lost this game, just an insane call.
