title: Final Score: Chiefs fall to Bills on Thanksgiving night
summary: Tyler Bass drilled a 57-yard field goal with four seconds remaining to hand Kansas City a Thanksgiving loss in Buffalo. Greg Dortch’s 15-yard punt return set up the decisive kick after the Chiefs’ offense failed to move out of its own territory. Kansas City took a 10-7 lead on its opening possession of the second […]
full_text: (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tyler Bass drilled a 57-yard field goal with four seconds remaining to hand Kansas City a Thanksgiving loss in Buffalo . Greg Dortch’s 15-yard punt return set up the decisive kick after the Chiefs’ offense failed to move out of its own territory. Kansas City took a 10-7 lead on its opening possession of the second half. Jalen Royals’ 37-yard kickoff return provided favorable field position, and Emmett Johnson finished the seven-play, 56-yard drive with a one-yard touchdown run. The defense gave the Chiefs opportunities to win. Alohi Gilman and Nohl Williams intercepted Josh Allen in the red zone, and Kansas City recorded two sacks while holding him to 81 passing yards. James Cook carried Buffalo’s offense with 117 rushing yards and its only touchdown. But penalties repeatedly stalled Kansas City’s offense. Harrison Butker missed a potential go-ahead 46-yard field goal with 6:01 remaining, and the Chiefs punted on their final two possessions. Join Arrowhead Pride on game day! Stay on top of every Chiefs update and debate every snap with other members of Chiefs Kingdom. Game-day discussion is smoother in the SB Nation app. Fewer ads Jump easily between conversations Faster commenting and posting Download on iOS or Android . First Quarter Buffalo wins the toss and elects to receive. Buffalo opened with an eight-yard completion to James Cook III, who later converted third-and-1 with a three-yard run. Josh Allen’s 10-yard scramble moved the Bills into Kansas City territory, but the drive stalled after a short run and consecutive incompletions intended for Ray Davis and Khalil Shakir. Tommy Doman Jr.’s 42-yard punt went into the end zone for a touchback, giving the Chiefs possession at their own 20. Kansas City went three-and-out on its opening possession, handing off to Emmett Johnson three straight times. Johnson gained nine yards on his first two carries, but Bradley Chubb dropped him for a two-yard loss on third-and-1. Matt Araiza punted 43 yards, and Jadon Canady limited Greg Dortch to a one-yard return, giving Buffalo the ball at its own 31. The Chiefs forced a three-and-out after James Cook III gained four yards on first down. Ashton Gillotte and George Karlaftis stopped Josh Allen for no gain on a run around right end, and Allen’s deep third-down pass intended for DJ Moore fell incomplete. Tommy Doman Jr.’s 61-yard punt was downed by Tyrell Shavers at the Kansas City 4. Pinned at its own 4, Kansas City gained five yards on a Jalen Royals catch and four on an Emmett Johnson run. But Terrel Bernard stopped Noah Gray for no gain on a third-and-1 reception, forcing the Chiefs’ second straight three-and-out. Matt Araiza’s 37-yard punt went out of bounds at midfield, giving Buffalo a short field. Second Quarter Buffalo leaned on James Cook III during a 12-play, 49-yard scoring drive. Cook broke off a 10-yard run and converted fourth-and-1 near the goal line, while Josh Allen found Khalil Shakir for 17 yards on third-and-5. Replay overturned an apparent Cook touchdown, and a false start pushed Buffalo back to the 5, but Cook scored up the middle on the next snap. Tyler Bass’ extra point gave the Bills a 7-0 lead with 14:36 left in the second quarter. Patrick Mahomes found Travis Kelce for 16 yards to produce Kansas City’s first first down, but the Chiefs gained just three more yards before a third-down incompletion. Matt Araiza then fumbled the snap and managed a 13-yard punt that went out of bounds at the Kansas City 44. An ineligible-downfield-kick penalty added five yards, giving Buffalo possession at the Chiefs’ 39. Buffalo drove from the Chiefs’ 39 to the Kansas City 6, helped by James Cook III’s running and a defensive offside penalty. Nick Bolton dropped Cook for a three-yard loss before George Karlaftis deflected Josh Allen’s pass intended for Dawson Knox. Alohi Gilman intercepted it in the end zone, keeping Buffalo from adding points and giving Kansas City possession at its own 20 with 7:55 left in the half. Emmett Johnson gained five yards on second down and converted third-and-1 with a three-yard run, but Kansas City’s drive stalled after Patrick Mahomes recovered his own fumble for a two-yard loss. Mahomes threw incomplete to Josh Downs, then found Johnson for six yards on third-and-12. Matt Araiza punted 55 yards, and Greg Dortch’s 15-yard return gave Buffalo the ball at its own 24 with 4:44 left in the half. James Cook III opened Buffalo’s drive with runs of four and nine yards, but the Chiefs held Ray Davis to no gain on the next play. Josh Allen found DJ Moore for four yards before throwing incomplete to Keon Coleman on third-and-6. Tommy Doman Jr.’s 23-yard punt went out of bounds at the Kansas City 36, giving the Chiefs possession with 1:56 left in the half. Kansas City overcame an opening holding penalty as Patrick Mahomes found Travis Kelce for gains of 10 and 24 yards. Mahomes later scrambled for two yards on fourth-and-1, then connected with Kelce for 21 more to reach the Buffalo 8. After an incompletion intended for Rashee Rice, Harrison Butker made a 26-yard field goal, cutting the Bills’ lead to 7-3 going into the half. Third Quarter Jalen Royals’ 37-yard kickoff return set the Chiefs up at their own 44 to open the second half. Emmett Johnson started with runs of 13 and 12 yards before Patrick Mahomes found Rashee Rice for 10. Johnson added seven yards, and Josh Downs’ 13-yard reception put Kansas City at the Buffalo 1. After an incompletion, Johnson punched it in on the ground to cap the seven-play, 56-yard drive. Harrison Butker’s extra point gave the Chiefs their first lead, 10-7, with 11:31 remaining in the third quarter. Buffalo opened with two incompletions before Josh Allen scrambled for 17 yards on third-and-10. A 10-yard completion to Khalil Shakir converted another third down, and Dalton Kincaid’s six-yard catch helped move the Bills deeper into Kansas City territory. Allen added a nine-yard scramble and a two-yard third-down run to reach the Chiefs’ 14. But Nohl Williams intercepted his next pass intended for Shakir at the 13 and returned it seven yards, giving Kansas City possession at its own 20 with 5:48 left in the third quarter. It was Allen’s second red-zone interception. Kansas City couldn’t turn the interception into points. Emmett Johnson opened with a seven-yard run, then was stopped for no gain before an unnecessary roughness penalty on Kingsley Suamataia backed the Chiefs up 13 yards. Facing third-and-16, Patrick Mahomes was sacked by Greg Rousseau for a seven-yard loss, forcing Kansas City to punt from its own 7. Matt Araiza’s 60-yard kick was downed by James Winchester at the Buffalo 33 with 3:59 left in the third quarter. Fourth Quarter James Cook opened with runs of five and four yards before Josh Allen converted third-and-1 with a three-yard keeper. Buffalo continued leaning on Cook to move into Chiefs territory, eventually reaching the Kansas City 26 on Dalton Kincaid’s seven-yard catch. But Dawson Knox’s holding penalty erased Allen’s third-down scramble, and an incompletion forced a long field goal attempt. Tyler Bass connected from 54 yards to tie the game 10-10 with 12:02 remaining. After an opening incompletion, Patrick Mahomes found Emmett Johnson for 12 yards, and Johnson added five on the ground. Travis Kelce’s offensive pass interference penalty erased a 16-yard catch, but Mahomes rescued the drive with a 19-yard third-down completion to Cyrus Allen. Noah Gray’s 19-yard reception later moved Kansas City to the Buffalo 17. Hunter Nourzad’s holding penalty then wiped out Johnson’s 10-yard run, and Fred Johnson’s false start pushed the Chiefs farther back. Harrison Butker missed the ensuing 46-yard field goal wide right with 6:01 remaining. Buffalo leaned on James Cook, who opened with runs of three and five yards before converting third-and-2 with a three-yard gain. Cook added two more yards, and Josh Allen’s two-yard keeper brought up…

title: The Rams’ lost star that doesn’t get talked about
summary: The 2026 season for the Los Angeles Rams is one that will be trademarked for the injuries and adversity it brought. The Rams have mostly fought through it and held water on their way to a 7-4 record. It’s quite the turnaround from their 2-4 start. Puka Nacua is out for the year—as are Terrance […]
full_text: The 2026 season for the Los Angeles Rams is one that will be trademarked for the injuries and adversity it brought. The Rams have mostly fought through it and held water on their way to a 7-4 record. It’s quite the turnaround from their 2-4 start. Puka Nacua is out for the year—as are Terrance Ferguson, Poona Ford, and Jaylen Watson. Davante Adams has missed significant time. So did Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, Trent McDuffie and Steve Avila. Los Angeles has gone from “super team” to an injured reserve list that could probably compete for the playoffs. But perhaps the most surprising outcome for the Rams this year is decline from a player who has been healthy and on the field for 100% of the games this season: Matthew Stafford. LA has lost a ton of stars this season: Nacua, Ferguson, Ford, Watson, and others. We also must account for the fact that Stafford is no longer playing at a star level . Most will take issue with me saying that. The Rams are on a five-game win streak, after all. But this is a team that was built to compete for a championship. The Rams did little to reinforce the offense and spent most of their offseason resources on the defensive side of the ball. The issue with that? This is no longer the safe offense capable of reaching the same ceiling. The bottom has fallen out as well. LA bet on Stafford being able to replicate his MVP season from a year ago. They figured a rising tide on defense would lift the boat overall to new heights. Instead, the Rams are now a defensive-first team that doesn’t ask its quarterback to do much at all. The proof is in the pudding: Game Opponent Result Rushing Yards Passing Yards (net) Total Yards Week 12 vs. Packers W 26-13 241 132 373 Week 10 @ Cardinals W 34-6 202 234 436 Week 9 @ Commanders W 20-13 124 219 343 Week 8 vs. Chargers W 24-9 129 152 281 Week 7 @ Raiders W 35-21 199 187 386 The advanced metrics are not kind to Stafford either. After applying a 20% minimum dropback threshold, Stafford currently ranks 25th of 38 signal callers in Pro Football Focus (PFF) passing grade. He’s behind the likes of Jacoby Brissett (benched & traded), Cam Ward, Joe Milton (backup), Kirk Cousins (traded), Kyler Murray (benched), and Tanner McKee (backup). Here are Stafford’s rankings in individual metrics versus the rest of the pack: Positive play rate: 12.9% (28th) Negative play rate: 9.2% (24th) Big-time throw (BTT) rate: 3.4% (27th) Turnover-worthy play (TWP) rate: 3.6% (24th) BTT to TWP ratio: 0.88 (26th) Adjusted completion rate: 76.3% (15th) Completion rate over expected (adj for ADOT): +0.3 (20th) Average depth of target (ADOT): 7.6 yards (31st) Time to throw (TTT): 2.55 seconds (2nd) EPA per play: +0.090 (17th) Non-screen EPA per play: +0.110 (17th) Non-play action EPA per play: +0.110 (14th) The main takeaways? Stafford is no longer generating big-time throws to offset the above average rate in which he puts the ball in harm’s way. He used to win in this tradeoff, but the positive play creation has fallen off a cliff. Also, he has been slightly better without play action despite the Rams recently committing heavily to the ground game. Is he still a fit for the Sean McVay offense if that is the case? So why have the big-time throws disappeared from Stafford’s game? Well, it’s something I wrote about often early in the season . Defenses are intent on taking away explosive plays, which is both McVay and Stafford’s bread and butter. Stafford is being asked to get rid of the ball quickly and hit underneath targets. It’s not the best part of his game and the quick passing attack is something LA has struggled with since McVay and Stafford paired together in 2021. Simply put, this is not really the ideal world they want to live in. Defenses are forcing them into it. And Stafford, admittedly, is a quarterback of an era gone by. Mobility is now required at the position. If you can’t be patient and chip away at the defense, you will get burned. Mobility also helps in this facet because it allows signal callers to buy time and wait for more vertical lanes to open. The Rams do not have access to this part of modern football. Looking at the second-fastest time to throw in the NFL coupled with the an ADOT towards the bottom of the league, this seems to be an offense tailor made for what we saw from Ty Simpson in the preseason. It’s a stark juxtaposition between a rookie quarterback in his first three games versus one who has played in the NFL for nearly two decades. The encouraging sign? Simpson can bring a much-needed element of mobility to McVay’s offense when he eventually takes over. The Rams have effectively built an offense that doesn’t work well for Matthew Stafford. It’s a requirement with how defenses are approaching the game in 2026. He has been below average by nearly any objective measure, and he has been worse this season than quarterbacks who have been sent to the bench. Loyalty is a dangerous commitment in professional football. If the Rams are going to make good on Super Bowl expectations, they need Stafford to outright perform better. His back will be against the wall with limited offensive firepower, but he wasn’t even good when Nacua and Adams were on the field. All signs are pointing towards this being the end for Stafford. He’s the Rams’ lost star that no one is talking about.
author: JB Scott

title: Rams-Packers was fun, Thanksgiving games were wild
summary: The Los Angeles Rams won an exciting game over the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday, and that might feel like a week ago to some because the Thanksgiving games that followed were absolutely legendary. The Chicago Bears downed the Detroit Lions in the last seconds, the Philadelphia Eagles downed the Dallas Cowboys in the final […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams won an exciting game over the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday, and that might feel like a week ago to some because the Thanksgiving games that followed were absolutely legendary. The Chicago Bears downed the Detroit Lions in the last seconds, the Philadelphia Eagles downed the Dallas Cowboys in the final moments, and the Buffalo Bills found a way to beat the Kansas City Chiefs as time expired. Each game on Thursday came down to the wire, and each game was a blast to watch. Factor in the Washington Commanders beating the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday and this has been an even wilder week of Thanksgiving and football. The Rams win was big, but unless you are a Rams fan, you’ve probably moved on because Thursday’s games were outrageous, and now we get a Friday game with the Pittsburgh Steels vs. the Denver Broncos. A normal Black Friday Game. Nothing to see here, folks, outside of just regular old football featuring two classic franchises. Enjoy the football. Best Thanksgiving NFL games ever? Historic Turkey Day by the numbers (nfl.com) “Thursday’s games featured 174 combined points but were decided by just eight, and each one came down to a game-winning play in the last three seconds or less. Bears beat Lions, 39-35 , on a 6-yard Rome Odunze touchdown reception with three seconds left. Eagles upset Cowboys, 39-38, on a 59-yard Jake Elliott field goal with two seconds remaining. Bills defeated Chiefs, 13-10 , on a 57-yard Tyler Bass field goal with no time left on the clock. How rare was Thursday’s three-peat of fantastic finishes? Per NFL Research, this was just the second Thanksgiving slate in NFL history that featured three games decided by fewer than five points, with the other coming in 1926. Who could forget the dueling 0-0 draws between the Canton Bulldogs and Akron Indians, and Chicago Cardinals and Chicago Bears, plus the Los Angeles Buccaneers’ thrilling 9-6 win over the Detroit Panthers? Even better, this was the first Thanksgiving to feature three games decided in the final seconds, per NFL Research.“ NFL Thanksgiving slate: Two must-know storylines for each of five games (nfl.com) “ Can Steelers bounce back after chaotic turn of events? Pittsburgh was sitting pretty at 6-2 heading into its Week 9 bye. The season has taken a dramatic turn since then, though, with a two-game losing streak preceding Tuesday’s stunning late night announcement that Aaron Rodgers has been benched in favor of Mason Rudolph , one day after Mike McCarthy told reporters he was sticking with Rodgers at quarterback. Things spiraled further on Wednesday, leading the team to waive Rodgers . He re-signed with Pittsburgh in the offseason to reunite with McCarthy for one last ride in what the QB had declared would be his final NFL season. Clearly, things didn’t go according to plan, with the soon-to-be 43-year-old ranking 28th in EPA per dropback (-0.17) among the 31 qualified passers in 2026, per Next Gen Stats. Now we’re left to wonder if he’s played his final snap, and if the career backup Rudolph can keep the Steelers’ season from going off the rails.“ Thanksgiving tripleheader: What We Learned from Bears-Lions, Eagles-Cowboys, Chiefs-Bills (nfl.com) “ Bazooka Joe Milton III leads stunning Eagles comeback vs. Cowboys. The Eagles looked dead in the water, missing starters all over the field, playing with a backup QB, and were down 31-10 deep in the third quarter. Then the largest comeback in Thanksgiving history began with Joe Milton’s big arm. The QB splashed fearless bombs over and over again to puncture a limp Cowboys defense. With Saquon Barkley out early with an injury, Milton diced up the Dallas defense, completing 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards, three TDs and an INT. Several of his heaves to DeVonta Smith (11 catches, 200 receiving yards, two TDs) were perfectly dropped in the bucket. Milton might not yet have consistent touch underneath or on intermediate throws, vacillating from laser to a ball four feet off the mark (see: fourth quarter INT ). However, he throws a beautiful deep ball, particularly on the move. Case in point: 188 yards and all three TDs came on passes of 20-plus air yards (56.8%). Milton’s rushing ability also provides pizzazz to an offense that couldn’t get off the ground until Week 12. The Eagles switched to Bazooka Joe to inject explosives into a bland turkey of an offense. Boy, did that come to fruition on Thursday. He brings a cannon arm and athletic ability to overcome blocking deficiencies. He still has strides to make, and he will have to do it against a defense better than Dallas’ to prove he can be a legit starter in 2027. But he jolted a sleepy game and turned it on its head. Milton makes the four-win Eagles immensely more watchable the rest of the way.“ Jerry Jones to ‘question everything’ after Cowboys’ ‘damning’ Thanksgiving loss (nfl.com) “The Cowboys owner said he did not anticipate making any coaching changes ahead of Dallas’ next game, a Week 13 game at the Seattle Seahawks 11 days away, but that didn’t mean Schottenheimer was free from criticism. “These are setbacks and they’re damning setbacks, there’s no question about it,” Jones said, via ESPN . “And especially when we feel like that we can look at parts of the game where it was ours to take and we didn’t. So when you look at every bit of it, then you have to question everything.” Jones called Thursday’s loss to the Philadelphia Eagles — a 39-38 defeat in which Dallas led by 21 points deep into the third quarter — “numbing.” Will that feeling preclude Jones from making the rare call of dismissing his underperforming coach midseason? Schottenheimer was not worried about his job status after the loss. “I worry about the guys in that locker room, and it doesn’t affect me,” he said.“ Matt LaFleur Failed Packers in Loss to Sean McVay’s Rams (si.com) “Is it hard to replace a premier receiver like Watson? Of course it is. He’s third in the league with 981 receiving yards and probably would have blown past 1,000 yards on Wednesday. Rams Found a Way Against Packers But look at what his good friend, Rams coach Sean McVay, overcame in leading his team to a fifth consecutive win. What’s harder than replacing one premier receiver? How about replacing two. Puka Nacua, who led the NFL in receptions and yards last season, is on injured reserve following knee surgery. Davante Adams, who led the NFL in touchdown receptions last season, is on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. He might not be an elite receiver with his 34th birthday approaching but had two huge games this season.“ Are the LA Rams back? How good are the Chicago Bears? – Six things we learnt from the NFL on Thanksgiving (dazn) “ NFL fans were treated to four spectacular games across Thanksgiving and the evening before. Opening with the Los Angeles Rams running through the Green Bay Packers , followed by three one-score games, two decided by last-second field goals and one by a final-play touchdown, these games had everything. There was a 21-point comeback, elite running back play, a disappointing showdown between Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen and a first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game. Here are some of the key things to take away from this year’s slate of games from Thanksgiving.“ ‘GMFB’ revisits NFC Playoff Picture following Rams’ first win over Packers since 2018 (nfl.com) “Good Morning Football” breaks down who’s in and who’s out of the NFC Playoff Picture following the Los Angeles Rams’ emphatic win over the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve.“ Rams are more likely to extend Stetson Bennett than fans might think (ramblinfan) “Don’t fret. General manager Les Snead had constructed Stafford’s contract in such a way as to force both team and player to revisit it. That strategy allows either side to opt out of another year without the adversarial confrontations that typically come with a thanks-but-no-thanks negotiation. What about Bennett’s future? The fourth-year quarterback remains a man of mystery.…
author: Danny Stone

title: Sean McVay shapeshifts the Rams once again
summary: In another in transformation form, the Los Angeles Rams morphed into a different era to grind down the Green Bay Packers 26-13 on Thanksgiving Eve. L.A. coach Sean McVay took his team back in time to the early 70’s. The days of three yards and a puff of poly turf. The Rams ran the ball, […]
full_text: In another in transformation form, the Los Angeles Rams morphed into a different era to grind down the Green Bay Packers 26-13 on Thanksgiving Eve. L.A. coach Sean McVay took his team back in time to the early 70’s. The days of three yards and a puff of poly turf. The Rams ran the ball, played tough defense, and were nattily attired in old-school blue on white uniforms. But McVay is not a paunchy flat topper with a chaw of tobacco, he’s a modern-day shaman, buffed out with a boy band coiff. He’s a shapeshifter, continuously transforming the Rams since taking the reins in 2017. It’s a sorcerer’s alchemy of motion, formational subterfuge, and a heavy dose of traditional football thinking. In his eleven years, there’s been constant metamorphosis, but basically L.A. has gone from a fairly traditional West Coast offense and bend, but don’t break defense to duo/gap downhill run with multiple tight ends and an attacking defense that relies heavily on sub-packages. Last night, the Rams almost completely shelved their three wide receiver formations, shapeshifting into multiple tight ends and/or an extra offensive lineman on 83 percent of reps. Another 24 percent of snaps had two running back sets. Without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, Sean McVay has completely shifted the Rams' offensive personnel tendencies: More running backs, tight ends and offensive linemen and fewer receivers over the past two weeks. https://t.co/vTuomr0Xlr pic.twitter.com/tSxCAYcnuO — SūmerSports (@SumerSports) November 26, 2026 These changes, somewhat predicated by a litany of injuries have the snap counts in a state flux from week-to-week. Here’s the weekly review of the snap counts from the big win. Players, their snap counts and percentage of play time in bold. Quarterback Matthew Stafford (78, 100%) In Staff’s 250th career start, gritty is the best descriptor for his effort. He’s been a little off in his accuracy all season, but he’s finding ways to win. For the second time this season, he was able to post a victory without throwing a touchdown and also giving away an interception (per Next Gen Stats). That matches his previous career output. Running back Blake Corum (58, 74%) Kyren Williams (38, 49%) For the third time this season, the Rams have grossed over 200 yards rushing. During this five-game win streak, L.A. has out-rushed opponents at a clip of 895 yards to 261 and have scored eight more touchdowns (8-0). For the first time in his career, Corum was the go-to guy and responded with 184 yards on the ground. His 32 carries were the most in the Sean McVay/Rams era. Wide receiver Konata Mumpfield (70, 90%) Xavier Smith ( 18, 23%) CJ Daniels (17, 22%) Tutu Atwell (6, 8%) Even in a game where the Rams ran the football 47 times, six targets to the wide receiver unit is a paltry sum. Mumpfield created separation at medium depth and hauled in four of five targets for a desirable 17.3 yards per catch. Smith caught the only other target for a short gain. Reps for Daniels and Atwell were substantially down from the Arizona game. Gorgeous route from Mumpfield. GBvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/IgMO6MGy9y — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 Tight end Colby Parkinson (65, 83%) Max Klare (43, 55%) Tyler Higbee (40, 51%) Davis Allen (16, 21%) Pretty much a night of grunt work. These guys are certainly tough as a cutter grade steak and beat down by injuries. There answer, “just get a little dirt and spit, rub it in and repeat as necessary.” Seriously, how might the Rams offense shift now, if Allen and Higbee miss any time? Luckily they have another 10 days to get rehabbed. Look at Max Klare, career high reps in street fight. Offensive line Alaric Jackson, Beaux Limmer, Kevin Dotson (78, 100%) Warren McClendon (74, 95%) Bill Murray (57, 73%) Justin Dedich (21, 27%) David Quessenberry (19, 24%) Keagan Trost ( 4, 5%) It didn’t start out dominating with 12 carries for 46 yards in the first half, but the Rams stayed with the run game and were eventually able to impose their will in the second half. The blitz gave them some trouble, but in the end Green Bay only got one sack. Mostly bully ball work, only a couple of outside zone runs and a jet sweep, the big uglies were in road grade mode, between the tackles. Murray went out late and Dedich got work on his first game back and the offense didn’t miss a beat. Love the Rams use of six offensive linemen, a goal line offense at any point on the field. Fans were holding their collective breath when McClendon went down, but it was only cramps. It diid allow Trost to get his feet wet, if only a toe. Special teams How ‘bout them apples? All units, return, coverage, and FG/PAT served up a solid all-around performance. Biggest takeaway? Kicker Josh Karty getting all his corkscrew kickoffs into the landing zone. Of his seven kickoffs, only once were the Packers able to start across the 30 yard line and just one yard past it at that. I hate to be a wet blanket, but it should be noted that the Pack’s Special team Points Over Expected ranking is 31st while the Rams hover at 28th. Defensive line Aaron Donald (30, 65%) Braden Fiske (27, 54%) Kobie Turner (23, 50%) Tyler Davis (14, 30%) Ty Hamilton (9, 20%) Created good push rushing up the middle and generally formed a wall against the run. Turner was quiet in his return, but good to see him Start back into game shape. Donald is playing more disciplined than his glory days and still a handful. Davis and Hamilton will have to get used to the back seat with the interior at full strength. Edge Byron Young (37, 80%) Myles Garrett (32, 70%) Josaiah Stewart (20, 43%) Wesley Bailey (13, 28%) I honestly expected a little more pressure from the group, but Packer quarterback Love was clearly forced out his game and it’s always great to see plays behind the line of scrimmage. L.A. must have game planned the big three of Garrett, Young, and Stewart to see a lot of reps, Bailey’s workload percentage was down from last week. Off-ball linebacker Nate Landman (25, 54%) Omar Speights (10, 22%) Shaun Dolac (7, 15%) Using Landman and Speights basically as package players is showing promise, against predominantly passing teams, like Green Bay, using them in run/early down situations allows them to do what they do best and not square peg/round hole them in coverage. Interesting to see Dolac in the game late, as a spy on the quarterback. NATE LANDMAN WITH THE PEANUT PUNCH!! 🥊 #RamsHouse | 📺 @NetflixSports pic.twitter.com/z8BD5Nl68E — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 26, 2026 Safety Quentin Lake (46, 100%) Kamren Curl (46, 100%) Kamren Kinchens (25, 54%) Jaylen McCollough (17, 37%) Maximus Pulley (1, 2%) Strong outing by the safeties, each one made stellar individual plays. They took tight end Tucker Kraft, a very good receiver, out of the game. The Pack likes to take deep contested catch shots and the Rams safeties were stellar getting back to blanket those. The could have 3-4 interceptions with just a shade of luck. Kinchens was just four inches too high on the sideline hit. He is known for being an enforcer, but I don’t believe the ouster was warranted. A catch and extra 15 yards on the penalty are castigation enough. Cornerback Trent McDuffie (46, 100%) Josh Wallace (43, 93%) Emmanuel Forbes (35, 76%) McDuffie is the real deal. The Packers have an outstanding passing offense, holding them 200 yards through the air is a fine outing. Christian Watson is a tough cover and his going out was a huge break, but it was late (under two minutes left) in the first half and the Rams had the ball for 24 minutes in the final 30. I thought the way they all three played physical defending runners was very good. Inactives: QB Ty Simpson, OL Coleman Shelton, OL Steve Avila, DL Larell Murchison, E Desjuan Johnson, E Darryl Peterson The race to 11 wins The Rams come through in a “must win” game. With the margins so thin, grabbing a wildcard seed may end up being a back door effort, knocking off the Packers and thus gaining a head-to-head advantage…
author: Venie Randy Soares

title: Rams on verge of 6-game winning streak
summary: The Los Angeles Rams beat the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday, their fifth win in a row since starting 2-4. But this is one of the strangest five-game winning streaks of recent NFL history because somehow confidence has waned even as the Rams continue to win. Will beating the Kansas City Chiefs next week — […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams beat the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday , their fifth win in a row since starting 2-4. But this is one of the strangest five-game winning streaks of recent NFL history because somehow confidence has waned even as the Rams continue to win . Will beating the Kansas City Chiefs next week — which would tie for the second-longest winning streak of the Sean McVay era — have fans believing that L.A. doesn’t need a star wide receiver in order to make a Super Bowl run? The Packers still have a winning record, but Green Bay could be the worst team with a winning record in the NFL this season. Gorgeous route from Mumpfield. GBvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/IgMO6MGy9y — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 Are the Packers good? No. The Packers are bad. It will be stunning if Green Bay makes the playoffs, but for some reason the organization continues to reward the mediocrity of Matt LaFleur and Jordan Love with continued seasons at their respective job. The Packers at least need a new something , because Green Bay is on the verge of their sixth season in a row without reaching the NFC Championship. LaFleur has only won 10+ games once in the last five years. That season, they got beat handily by the Eagles in the wild card round. The Rams had a phenomenal day on the ground against the Packers and that can’t be taken lightly with an offensive coordinator like Sean McVay. Blake Corum is a star in the making . Hard for me to fault the Packers' trenches getting abused right now. This is what happens when your offense goes flat and can't move the ball. Trotting out an exhausted defense every few minutes and asking them to stop Blake Corum and Kyren Williams isn't realistic. — Zach Jacobson (@zachjacobson) November 26, 2026 And also it’s true that Jonathan Gannon is a nothing defensive coordinator who is unlikely to have a long-term job in the NFL at that role. He couldn’t beat McVay in Arizona and he can’t do it in Green Bay. The Packers probably aren’t even the best team that the Rams have beaten on this winning streak. That would likely be the Washington Commanders. Green Bay is on the verge of completely falling apart, and the Rams have won five in a row. Six in a row would feel a lot more comforting. The Chiefs are better than these teams The Rams have beaten these teams: Raiders Chargers Commanders Cardinals Packers Las Vegas, L.A. and Arizona are three of the worst teams in the NFL. And to the Rams’ credit, they beat them easily, as a good team should. The Commanders game was close throughout and Washington has won three of their last four, including wins over the Giants and Bengals. They’ve also beaten the Seahawks this season. Kansas City is better than these teams, albeit despite their 8-2 record they’ve had some setbacks. Kenneth Walker III will be out. Kenneth Walker's groin injury considered grade 2 which requires 2-3 weeks of rest, per @jeffrichadiha . https://t.co/b6YCB5GOzM — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) November 25, 2026 Rookie Emmett Johnson has rushed for over 100 yards in each of the last two games though. Kansas City has not beaten a good team in 2026, except for the Broncos in Week 1. They’ve had a similar story to the Rams. Winning convincingly against bad teams, an MVP quarterback who doesn’t have a clear star weapon at WR/TE, and the need to put another strong mark on their resume. 6-game winning streak? The Rams started 3-2 last season and then won six in a row. That winning streak was stopped by the Carolina Panthers, and then the Rams went 5-4 over those next nine games, including playoffs. In 2018, the Rams started 8-0, the longest winning streak of the Sean McVay era. They went 7-4 over the next 11 games, including playoffs. A win over the Chiefs will tie for McVay’s second-longest winning streak. That will help the playoffs. Consistency? That will help with the goal of winning a Super Bowl.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Rams PFF grades: Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett turn back clock
summary: The first NFL pre-Thanksgiving game brought a delicious victory for the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night. LA defeated the Green Bay Packers 26-13 to move to 7-4 on the season. After starting 2-4, winning five-straight didn’t seem to be in the cards. Their fortune seems to be shifting even in the face of injury. […]
full_text: The first NFL pre-Thanksgiving game brought a delicious victory for the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night. LA defeated the Green Bay Packers 26-13 to move to 7-4 on the season. After starting 2-4, winning five-straight didn’t seem to be in the cards. Their fortune seems to be shifting even in the face of injury. Who stood out on an individual level from this game? Let’s review the Pro Football Focus (PFF) grades and data in order to lean into some analytical takeaways. *Final grades are not currently available as of the writing of this post. Due to the Thanksgiving holiday I am going to run with the data still under review. Close enough. Top five grades on offense 1 – Konata Mumpfield, WR: 77.0 Mumpfield was the Rams’ passing offense on Wednesday night. He earned 69 yards on four catches and provided the only threat vertically. The next closest pass catchers in terms of yardage were Blake Corum at 21 and Kyren Williams at 19. Xavier Smith was the only other receiver to catch a pass and his solo reception went for four yards. Is that a reliable way to play offense and win games? Not really. The Rams must find better answers from their receiver group. They cannot rely on Davante Adams to completely reverse their fortunes on his own, especially coming back from a significant injury this late into his career. Gorgeous route from Mumpfield. GBvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/IgMO6MGy9y — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 2 – Justin Dedich, LG: 76.2 Dedich filled in for the injured Bill Murray who had replaced Steve Avila in the starting lineup. Dedich always seems to fare well in terms of PFF grading, and it’s encouraging to see him pickup where he left off after suffering an injury this summer that has limited his availability. Dedich is undersized. That may prevent him from ever becoming a full-time starter. He still has value in a reserve role. 3 – Tyler Higbee, TE: 75.2 Veteran tight end Tyler Higbee’s most important contributions came as a run blocker where he earned a mark from PFF of 70.2. He added one catch for 14 yards and came close to another big play. Higbee played roughly half the game before suffering an injury and being ruled out. Davis Allen was also ruled out. The statuses of both are worth monitoring moving forward. 4 – Blake Corum, RB: 71.6 What more is there to say about Blake Corum’s performance not just Wednesday night but over the last seven weeks? Against the Packers he grinded out 184 yards and a score for an average of 5.80. PFF credited the back with 103 yards after contact (3.22 average). The offensive line was road grading as well, as they generated 2.58 yards before contact on Corum’s carries. Not a bad day at the office. BLAKE CORUM COMING THROUGH. GBvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/vxYuIWEU93 — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 5 – Beaux Limmer, C: 70.9 It would be a welcome development—given the amount of players across the Rams’ roster that need new contracts—if Limmer could takeover the starting center job on a going forward basis. Injured starter Coleman Shelton is approaching the end of his 2025 free agent deal. Limmer has one year left on his rookie contract. He continues to excel in pass protection in the middle of the offensive line. Other notes on offense Matthew Stafford finished 17th in grades out of the 19 players who appeared on offense. PFF graded him at a mark of 54.2. The outlet did not credit the veteran quarterback with a single big-time throw. He had one turnover-worthy play that resulted into an interception that could have proved costly; however, Jordan Love made a mistake of his own just two plays later. Stafford has now thrown an interception in all but two of 11 games this season. He’s at 11 on the year, so averaging one per game in the aggregate. If the Rams are going to be limited offensively and lean into ball control into order to constrict the opposition into submission, one requirement of that is taking care of the football. Can the Rams trust Stafford in this area? His track record so far this year suggests not. Rams fans are waiting for Stafford to turn his season around. It hasn’t happened yet. He’s still the 21st-graded quarterback by both offensive grade and passing grade. It’s clear he has taken a major step back this year. The end could be nearer than expected. It’s difficult to say anything other than 2027 seems to be Ty Simpson’s year to takeover. Matthew Stafford with a meatball sub One of the WORST INTs of the season. pic.twitter.com/D56tKeTSDy — Dov Kleiman (@NFL_DovKleiman) November 26, 2026 Top five grades on defense 1 – Aaron Donald, DT: 93.5 Donald and Garrett each had five total pressures on Jordan Love even though neither finished with a sack. The Rams only brought down Love once (Bryon Young), although the pressure did ultimately force three turnovers by the Pakcers’ offense. Love easily could have finished with at least five interceptions—including dropped picks by Quentin Lake and Trent McDuffie and a takeaway by Kam Curl that was reversed because of penalty. 2 – Kamren Kinchens, DB: 90.5 Kinchens forced a major collision along the sideline with receiver Christian Watson that dramatically altered the rest of the game. Kinchens was ejected, which resulted in controversy. Watson entered concussion protocol and was ruled out for the second half. The Rams seemingly had no answers for the dynamic receiver up to that point, and the Packers had little going through the air in the second half without Watson. Closer look at the hit that Kamren Kinchens was ejected for pic.twitter.com/SZERA2rlI0 — Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 26, 2026 3 – Myles Garrett, EDGE: 90.2 4 – Nate Landman, MLB: 89.9 Make it another hallmark punch out for Nate Landman. He stole the ball away from tight end Tucker Kraft for a key takeaway. The veteran linebacker played just 25 snaps. Omar Speights had 10. Shaun Dolac played seven. The roles of these players are changing as Lake took over the green dot duties. That isn’t necessarily a bad thing. The defensive line is limiting opposing rushing attacks on their own. The Rams are able to pivot more towards additional safeties to focus on tightening up through the air. It’s working. Stick with it. 5 – Quentin Lake, DB: 89.4 Lake finished with the second-highest coverage grade on the defense (87.0) behind only Landman (90.5). He dropped an interception that likely would have scored and put the Packers away even earlier. In total he finished with two pass breakups. Other notes on defense The Packers went after reserve corners Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes often with mixed results. Each had four targets into their coverage. Wallace allowed three receptions for 15 yards and the touchdown to Watson. Forbes gave up three catches for 79 yards (36 after the catch) and he caught the interception that effectively sealed the game. While their PFF marks were low relative to the other members of the defense (18th and 19th out of 20), these coverage numbers aren’t something that will get you beat. The standard is not perfection for these players as they look to replace injured starter Jaylen Watson. There will be negative moments. The Rams must hope that the positives—like Forbes’ interception—outweigh the bad.
author: JB Scott

title: Blake Corum is the Rams’ best running back
summary: Blake Corum was incredible for the Los Angeles Rams in their Week 12 win over the Green Bay Packers. He was nearly unstoppable as he gashed through the Green Bay defense, carrying the offense in a 26-13 victory. Not only was Corum the best player in the game, he solidified himself as RB1 for the […]
full_text: Blake Corum was incredible for the Los Angeles Rams in their Week 12 win over the Green Bay Packers. He was nearly unstoppable as he gashed through the Green Bay defense, carrying the offense in a 26-13 victory. Not only was Corum the best player in the game, he solidified himself as RB1 for the Rams going forward. Los Angeles has the luxury of rotating between two starting-caliber running backs in Corum and Kyren Williams. If you don’t think that’s an enviable place to be, go look at the Rams’ opponents from Wednesday night, whose leading rusher was a wide receiver in a losing effort. Williams has been a positive contributor for the Rams for years and still is right now. But when push came to shove in the biggest game of the season so far , Sean McVay put his faith in Corum. Blake Corum celebrated his 26th birthday with the best game of his NFL career against Green Bay. 32 CAR, 184 RUSH YDS, 1 TD, 2 REC, 21 REC YDS. With a rushing attack like this, the Rams have everything they need to make a Super Bowl run. https://t.co/ihXa9lX4LH pic.twitter.com/LF8VibPU0E — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) November 26, 2026 Clearly, he was rewarded for his belief. This season, Corum has tallied more yardage on fewer carries than Williams, and he was the go-to option in a game the Rams truly could not afford to lose. The third-year pro posted 33 carries for 184 yards in the win over the Packers; that’s the highest number of carries for a Ram since Zac Stacy in 2013, and it’s the most single-game yardage for a Ram since Todd Gurley in 2018. It should be noted that Corum was doing this behind a depleted offensive line, too, with a pair of starters out (not to mention the holes due to injury across the rest of the offensive roster). Part of that is the Packers’ porous run defense, which has now given up the two highest individual rushing totals of the season, but still, it’s not as if he had wide-open running lanes all night. According to Next Gen Stats, Corum had 150 yards after contact on Wednesday night. The Rams becoming a successful service academy offense with multiple backup offensive linemen just because Blake Corum just doesn’t go down at first contact is so wild — Tej Seth (@tejfbanalytics) November 26, 2026 There’s something to be said for riding the hot hand, and that’s definitely part of what went into Wednesday’s Corum-heavy second half. After all, Ronnie Rivers had a turn being the workhorse last time out in a win over the Arizona Cardinals. But this is back-to-back weeks that Corum has out-touched Williams. And, as mentioned above, his full-season stats have been even more efficient while scoring at a nearly identical clip (Corum has six rushing touchdowns, Williams has seven after Week 12). Most rush yards in a game this season Bijan Robinson 194 (Week 3) Blake Corum 184 (Week 12) ⬅️ Kenneth Walker III 177 (Week 4) Kenneth Walker III 173 (Week 1) Bucky Irving 170 (Week 8) pic.twitter.com/Cwo2yfFgQU — PFF (@PFF) November 26, 2026 Williams should still play plenty of snaps down the stretch, obviously. He’s still a good player, it’s not like he’s chopped liver compared to Corum. And by splitting the snaps between two backs, you’re ideally keeping both a bit fresher for a potential postseason run. Just ask the Seattle Seahawks and Kenneth Walker III about how much of a boon it is to have a fresh running back in January and February. But as things stand today, the best running back the Rams have is Blake Corum. For a running game that is not just efficient but can also completely take over a game like we just saw, the focal point right now should be Corum, no matter what the other back in the rotation has accomplished before.
author: Brendan Dzwierzynski

title: RAMalytics: 3 stats that defined Rams’ win over Packers
summary: A 26-13 win isn’t exactly a blowout. Then again, the Los Angeles Rams completely suffocated the Green Bay Packers by dominating time of possession—especially in the second half. Blake Corum was the boa constrictor. He amassed over 200 total yards on the game with at least 180 and a score on the ground alone. The […]
full_text: A 26-13 win isn’t exactly a blowout. Then again, the Los Angeles Rams completely suffocated the Green Bay Packers by dominating time of possession—especially in the second half. Blake Corum was the boa constrictor. He amassed over 200 total yards on the game with at least 180 and a score on the ground alone. The Rams’ rushing attack was productive despite Davis Allen, Tyler Higbee, Warren McClendon, and Bill Murray all leaving the game due to injury. The Rams can hang their hat on this impressive victory, although the slate does not let up any time soon. Before we turn the page, these are 3 stats that defined LA’s win over Green Bay: #1 – Defense is leading the way Sure, it helps that across LA’s five-game winning streak the first four victories came against middling-at-best competition. Still, in their last six outings, the Rams allowed just four touchdowns. Myles Garrett wasn’t available for that full stretch. Trent McDuffie either. They are still finding a way to get the job done. The biggest tell that LA dominated Jordan Love and company? The Packers offense finished with 244 total yards while Corum accumulated 205 himself. Kyren Williams added another 65 yards and a score. #2 – Blake Corum’s takeover It was jarring to see Corum open the game in the backfield. I’ve grown accustomed to seeing Kyren Williams earn the start, even if running back workload has been fairly split in recent years. The Rams have come to understand that Corum gives them a more dynamic option on the ground. When they needed an offensive spark this season, Corum provided that while very little else is working. LA is taking the path of least resistance and leaning on their best playmaker. The most impressive part of Corum’s performance? He finished with 99 yards after contact against the Packers. If those were all of his yards on Wednesday night, that is a strong individual performance. He broke tackles and created yardage that wasn’t readily there to a final output of 184 rushing yards. According to SumerSports, Corum had an EPA per rush of +0.19. It’s rare to see an EPA per rush that isn’t negative across the NFL. #3 – Dominating time of possession For the full game, the Rams held the ball for 40:40 versus the Packers’ 19:20 . On the surface that lends itself to winning. When you split the time of possession by half (23:45 to 6.55) , you realize Green Bay really had no opportunity to mount a comeback. Corum and the Rams were playing keep away. The defense was also able to force turnovers even when Love and the Packers offense was on the field. Green Bay’s offense largely watched their demise from the sidelines. The Rams similarly dominated the second half against the Arizona Cardinals last week. This is their second-straight game—and only the second game across the entire NFL season so far—where a team accumulated more than 24 minutes of possession in the second half. You can’t win if you can’t score. By playing complimentary football, the Rams aren’t even giving opposing offenses a chance to do so.

title: Raiders’ wide receivers Week 11 snap and production review
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders lost 38-24 at the Denver Broncos in Week 11. Let’s review how their wide receivers fared: Jalen Nailor: He played 83 percent of the snaps a week after playing a season high 86 percent. He had one catch for 16 yards on five targets. He has two catches for 15 yards […]
full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders lost 38-24 at the Denver Broncos in Week 11. Let’s review how their wide receivers fared: Jalen Nailor: He played 83 percent of the snaps a week after playing a season high 86 percent. He had one catch for 16 yards on five targets. He has two catches for 15 yards on nine targets the past two games. Tre Tucker Tucker played 80 percent of the snaps. He had two catches on 10 targets. He had two big drops. Tucker has seven catches for 114 yards on 23 targets in the past four games. Jack Bech: The 2025 second-round pick played a career-high 55 snaps and he had a career best eight catches for 88 yards on nine targets. It was a nice bounce back after he had three catches for 19 yards in three games since returning from the injured reserve. Bech helped make up for the absence of star tight end Brock Bowers in Denver. Cody White: White played 12 snaps. He was not targeted. Dareke Young: He played three offensive snaps. He didn’t have any targets. Conclusion: Bech was the shining light. Tucker needs to find a way to make a bigger impact again.
author: Bill Williamson

title: Raiders defense is doing well in this area
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders’ defense, overall, has been having a rough season. However, the unit is doing one thing very well — creating turnovers. Las Vegas has 17 takeaways, which is tied for the third most in the NFL. Many of the Raiders’ takeaways are coming when it counts. According to this X Post, Las […]
full_text: (Photo by Edward Monigan IV/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders’ defense, overall, has been having a rough season. However, the unit is doing one thing very well — creating turnovers. Las Vegas has 17 takeaways, which is tied for the third most in the NFL. Many of the Raiders’ takeaways are coming when it counts. According to this X Post, Las Vegas has 10 takeaways in the fourth quarter of games. That leads the league by three. NFL defenses ranked by 4th quarter takeaways: pic.twitter.com/WPp6dQq4Hd — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 24, 2026 Las Vegas has compiled those 10 fourth-quarter takeaways in six of their 11 games. They got fourth-quarter takeaways in all four of their wins this season and two came in defeats. Of course, they had four against the New Orleans Saints in a Week 3 win. So, this is a heck of a formula for the Raiders to find a way to win. If they can get their opponents to cough up the ball late, Las Vegas has a real chance to win. Let’s see if they can force the Cleveland Browns into a late turnover on Sunday night.
author: Bill Williamson

title: Raiders-Browns Week 12: 5 things to watch
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders play at the Cleveland Browns on Sunday night. Kickoff is set for 5:20 p.m. PT. Here are five keys to victory for the Raiders: Run the ball: The Raiders had one of their most successful games on the ground this season in Week 11. They ran for 143 yards during the […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders play at the Cleveland Browns on Sunday night. Kickoff is set for 5:20 p.m. PT. Here are five keys to victory for the Raiders: Run the ball: The Raiders had one of their most successful games on the ground this season in Week 11. They ran for 143 yards during the loss to Denver. It was the first time since Week 3 where Las Vegas had 100 yards rushing. The opportunity will be there for more success in Cleveland. The Browns have allowed 34 run plays of 10 plus yards this season. Protect Fernando Mendoza: Raiders’ rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza has been sacked a total of 11 times in his first two NFL starts. That’s way too many and it puts unnecessary stress on a young player. The Browns will be coming after him. Play cleaner: After not being penalized in Week 10, the Raiders were flagged nine time at Denver. That must improve this week. Start fast: The Dawg Pound is going to be wild for this prime-time game. The Raiders need to start fast and take an early lead to quiet down the crowd. Play well in fourth quarter: The Raiders haven’t been playing well late in games recently. Meanwhile, the Browns have been comeback kings. Las Vegas has to find a way to finish in what should be a close game.
author: Bill Williamson

title: Raiders’ special teams can ill afford adding to the team’s overall woes
summary: Considering the team’s defense ranks dead last in points allowed and yielding the second-worst amount of yards allowed, the Las Vegas Raiders special teams can ill affording adding to the overall woes. Field position comes at a premium in the NFL and for the Silver & Black, a disadvantage of that nature puts Rob Leonard’s […]
full_text: (Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images Considering the team’s defense ranks dead last in points allowed and yielding the second-worst amount of yards allowed, the Las Vegas Raiders special teams can ill affording adding to the overall woes. Field position comes at a premium in the NFL and for the Silver & Black, a disadvantage of that nature puts Rob Leonard’s defense in dire straits. Which makes the pair of times Raiders punter AJ Cole III’s boots were blocked by the Denver Broncos in the Week 11 38-24 loss a cause for concern. “I have to watch the tape,” Las Vegas head coach Klint Kubiak said when asked about the punt protection in the postgame press conference. “Two punts were huge. They were big,” Denver head coach Sean Payton said after the game. “One of them I know was a rush. When you look at what that does field position-wise and just say it’s a 40-yard swing, it’s almost like a turnover.” Even a day later, when the NFL statisticians officially marked the two punts as deflected and not blocked — due to the ball crossing the line of scrimmage — a sour taste remains in the Raiders special teams room. The first deflection occurred in the opening quarter when Denver’s Sai’Vion Jones bull rushed up the middle and changed the trajectory of Cole’s boot with his forearm. The ball eventually settled two yards past the line of scrimmage. The second occurred a quarter later with Dondrea Tillman tipping Cole’s punt limiting the boot to just 27 yards. It was indeed a forgettable Mile High outing for not only Cole, but special teams coordinator Joe DeCamillis. BLOCKED‼️ 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/9WKuW8iZYF — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 22, 2026 Shoring up the blocking and protection assignments on punts is a must as the Raiders’ Week 12 matchup with the Cleveland Browns was flexed to the Sunday night primetime slot instead of the standard afternoon affair it was originally was. Everything gets amplified under the lights in front of a national audience and repeating the lack of protection which resulted in Cole’s normally booming punts ricocheting off a defender’s appendage isn’t ideal. Where They Stand With 40 punts on the season, Cole is ranked 12th amongst his punting brethren in the league. The 2,029 yards his kicking foot has amassed ranks ninth while his 50.7 yards per punt average is third-best in the NFL. Cole’s 43.8 net yards per punt — average that subtracts return and touchback yards — is seventh-best as the league average on average yards per boot and net yards per punt are 47.7 and 42.2, respectively. The 31-year-old punter has four touchbacks which puts him at fifth-most and with 15 of his boots landing inside or being downed in the opponent’s 20-yard line puts him right in the middle at 16th overall. That’s the area where Cole is under the league average of 39.9 percent of kicks pinning opponents deep with his being 37.5 percent. In comparison, the Philadelphia Eagles’ Braden Mann leads the league in punts (53) and yardage (2,566) and he also owns the longest boot of the season with an 86-yard blast. The New York Giants’ Jordan Stout tops the yards per punt average at 51.7 — the Kansas City Chiefs’ Matt Araiza is second at 51.0 — while the G-Men’s boot specialist is atop the league with a 44.7 net yards average per boot. Mann also leads the NFL with 24 of his 53 punts pinning opponents within their own 20-yard line. Place kicking-wise, Matt Gay has certainly rekindled the accurate and dependable ways with DeCamillis in Las Vegas, much like the duo had during their respective time with the Los Angeles Rams. Matt Gay's two best seasons arrived in 2021 and 2022 with Joe DeCamillis as special teams boss with the Rams. Trying to recapture those 2 years where Gay was 94.1 and 93.3 percent in field goals (32-of-34 & 28-of-30). #Raiders #RaiderNation https://t.co/usCH2a5EKS — Ray Aspuria (@AsukalAspuria) March 10, 2026 As noted in the tweet above, Gay’s two best seasons in his eight seasons in the NFL were with DeCamillis in Los Angeles. The initial skepticism of Gay being a productive replacement for long time kicker Daniel Carlson have been certainly allayed. At 22-of-24 on field goals this season, the 32-year-old kicker has the sixth-best accuracy percentage at 91.7 percent. Gay’s long of 59 yards gives him the sixth-longest boot amongst his contemporaries and going 25-for-25 on extra points gives him the third-best percentage in that department. Gay’s misses this season were from 49 yards and 51 yards out — both in the month of October. The first occurred in Week 5 against the New England Patriots (Gay finish 1-for-2 on field goals that game) and the second a Week 7 miss against the Rams (he finished 3-for-4 that day). With the 22 field goals and 25 extra points made so far during the Raiders’ 2026 campaign, Gay (unsurprisingly) leads the team in points scored at 91. For comparison’s sake, there’s only one kicker who hasn’t missed a field goal attempt this season: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ Chase McLaughlin who is 22-for-22. A total of 12 kickers are perfect on extra points heading into Week 12 action. The NFL average for field goal percentage is 84.7 percent while it’s 95.5 percent on extra points. Return game-wise, Las Vegas boasts one of the top kick returners in running back Dylan Laube. Raiders RB Dylan Laube is the first player in the NFL this season to return a kickoff for a touchdown. pic.twitter.com/nhu44RpO5j — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 1, 2026 The 27-year-old reserve tailback is one of two return men in the league to house a kickoff. The 95-yard burst Laube had against the New York Jets in the Raiders’ Week 8 38-33 victory was the first end zone visit on a kick return this season. Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Devontez Walker housed a kickoff (86-yard gallop) in Week 11. Laube currently ranks second in average yards per return at 29.9. He trails Buffalo Bills running back Ray Davis (30.1 average) in that department. In terms of total kick return yards, Laube is third at a tally of 956. Tennessee Titans wideout Chimere Dike and Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Dohnte Meyers are ahead at 1,112 and 968 yards, respectively. The Raiders punt return game hasn’t been as explosive. Rookie wide receiver Malik Benson has seven returns for 94 yards while veteran wideout Deven Thompkins has one for 18 yards and Laube has two for 13 yards. Las Vegas is more apt to signal fair catch than return punts.
author: Ray Aspuria

title: Why isn’t the Las Vegas Raiders defense good enough
summary: Stop me if you’ve heard this before, but the Las Vegas Raiders defense has got a lot of growing to do to catch up with the offense. They have come within one score of, or surpassed, the 40-point threshold for the sixth time in 11 games. Pointing fingers Head coach Klint Kubiak said they win […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Stop me if you’ve heard this before, but the Las Vegas Raiders defense has got a lot of growing to do to catch up with the offense. They have come within one score of, or surpassed, the 40-point threshold for the sixth time in 11 games. Pointing fingers Head coach Klint Kubiak said they win as a team and lose as a team; refusing to point fingers is noble and expected of the head coach. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard elected not to take the high road, instead making a snide comment: “Fatigue makes cowards of us all…when you’re on the field a long time, mistakes tend to happen more often.” But here, we aren’t limited by nobility; Leonard would have gotten a pass until he decided to open his mouth and speak on an offense ranking 29 th in time of possession but 6 th in total points. So let us start by looking at who has been truly responsible for this lackluster defense. Leonard is the one calling the defensive plays and maintaining a league-worst defensive efficiency allowed, a paltry 48.1% defensive success rate and a 15.9% explosive play rate. No rush at all No one is doing jack up front for the Raiders defensive line outside of Maxx Crosby. Over the last three weeks, the Raiders defensive line has 2.5 sacks, five tackles for loss, seven quarterback hits, 1 forced fumble and two pass breakups. Crosby is the owner of every single one of those stats except one quarterback hit from Kwity Paye, Malcolm Koonce and Tonka Hemingway, along with the 0.5 sack, forced fumble and two pass breakups that Folorunso Fatukasi has produced. Kwity Paye , a high-priced free agent acquisition, hasn’t had a sack since Week 6 at home against the Buffalo Bills. Coincidentally, that happened to be the date of his last tackle for loss as well. His last quarterback hit was against Brock Purdy in Week 9. Hardly worthy of his lofty three-year, $48 million ($16 million average) contract. Cutting him with a June-1 designation saves roughly $6.01 million, with $16.824 million (one year’s salary) dead cap. At the rate of one sack every 5-6 weeks, one quarterback hit roughly every 2-3 weeks and a tackle for loss every six weeks, the rubber is going to have to meet the road at some point. Malcolm Koonce, last year Koonce got a pass for coming off an injured knee and was kept over a more deserving K’Lavon Chaisson. After receiving a good-faith one-year $11.01 million contract, his good start to the 2026 season has faded into oblivion along with his productivity. Over the last three games, he has two tackles and a quarterback hit. This season, he has accounted for 12 tackles, seven quarterback hits, three sacks, two forced fumbles and 1 tackle for loss. His last 0.5 sack was in Week 5 against the New England Patriots; the quarterback hit against the Denver Broncos on Sunday was his first impact as a rusher in six weeks. Adam Butler , according to Pro Football Focus, ranks 84 th out of 134 qualified interior defensive linemen. Strangely enough, Butler’s best grade is as a run defender, ranking 49 th of 134 and then comes the fall. His 21 total tackles are outside the Top 50 defensive tackles; his 0.5 sacks are outside the Top 75 defensive tackles; his seven total quarterback pressures are in the bottom third of qualifying defensive interiors. Defensive backfield Eric Stokes has played so poorly as of late that it is baffling how he is still starting. At this point, he has been every opponent’s favorite target; more so than even the rookies. When he isn’t giving up on plays, he is getting beaten like a drum. Stokes is allowing a passer rating of 115.2, making him the 9th-worst cover corner in the league coming out of week 10. What’s worse is that number has been steadily climbing over the last three weeks. In weeks 8-10, he posted a passer rating of 116.1. Additionally, when it comes to penalties, he has four accepted pass interference calls resulting in 58 yards; the first being tied for 5th most and the latter being the 5th most in the league. Stokes may have five pass breakups this season, but he still hasn’t recorded an interception since week 4 of his rookie season. Hezekiah Masses, Jermod McCoy, Darien Porter: All three are rookie cornerbacks who must be afforded an opportunity to learn their craft and experience bumps and bruises along the way. Before blaming them for all the explosive plays generated, we have to understand they are being asked to cover for a league-worst 3.0 seconds to throw and 4 th -worst in pocket time allowed, 2.72 seconds. Individually, they have all experienced success in one way, shape, or form. All of these young defensive backs need to get in the weight room and transform their bodies from college to the pros. Getting acclimated to the league is a process and all of these young players have shown promise. Masses has three interceptions this year but is still searching for a permanent positional home. Slightly undersized, he has the heart of a lion but needs a good NFL strength and development plan in the offseason. Out wide, he has three interceptions, but his productivity in the slot has been an improvement over veteran Taron Johnson, which offers positional versatility. He is a better man-coverage corner than soft zone but can do both. A ferocious blitzer who can get home when activated but is still too small to be a nickel linebacker. One of the few blemishes has been his ability to hold contain when he’s the last defender on the line. Porter the second-year cornerback, is a bit of an enigma. Unable to keep his starting job locked down from Masses and McCoy, he hasn’t been bad and has proven that, if utilized correctly, he can be an asset to the defense. Porter is a converted wide receiver with size, speed and length who specializes in press-man coverage. However, the main issue is the press-bail and zone technique he is being asked to play is a style which isn’t conducive to what he does best. He is a good and willing tackler, better suited to larger, less quick-twitch receivers. Opposite of Stokes, he is the second-best tackler out past the edges. McCoy , when healthy, has the tools to be the best of the bunch. Watching him stay balanced, controlled and locate the football was a sight for sore eyes. Playing the ball all the way through the catching process and being able to punch the ball out is what the Raiders need. Tackling in the run game was a problem against the Broncos. All in all, for a rookie making his second start, there are some encouraging signs but also plenty of room for improvement. Defending the run Enough can’t be said about how disappointing the run defense has been. This season, the 16 rushing touchdowns allowed are tied for the most in the league. The Raiders are allowing 149.5 yards per game, ranking 31st, and 4.82 yards per carry, ranking 30th in the league. Surprisingly, the 51 missed tackles are middle of the pack, so the reality is they are getting outmuscled. Against the Broncos, the Raiders lost three defensive tackles to injury. Whether they are able to play in the Sunday Night Game against the Cleveland Browns remains to be seen. If they are not, the run defense stands to be even worse.
author: Philip Robinson

title: 4 things about Browns heading into Week 12
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders play at the Cleveland Browns on Sunday night. Kickoff is at 5:20 p.m. PT. Here are three things to know about the Browns: Coach is doing work: When the Browns hired longtime NFL assistant Todd Monken as their head coach this offseason it really didn’t move the radar. It wasn’t considered […]
full_text: (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders play at the Cleveland Browns on Sunday night. Kickoff is at 5:20 p.m. PT. Here are three things to know about the Browns: Coach is doing work: When the Browns hired longtime NFL assistant Todd Monken as their head coach this offseason it really didn’t move the radar. It wasn’t considered a sexy pick. But the no -nonsense offensive minded job has his team playing well at 6-4. He seems to be a fit for the city and for team franchise. The first-time NFL head coach, 60, is a dark horse NFL Coach of the Year candidate Playoff history: The Browns known for being a woebegone franchise that has never been to a Super Bowl. But there are looking to go to the payoffs for the third time this decade. Nothing much was expected from this team, but they are winning more than they are losing. Tough at home and in the fourth quarter: The Browns have had six fourth-quarterback comebacks and they are a perfect 4-0 at home. Do you think the Dawg Pound will be fired up for their first Sunday Night Football game in five years? Defense can be run on: The Browns’ defense is solid, but it can give up big plays on the ground. They have allowed 34 run plays of 10 plus yards this season. The Raiders have struggled against the run for much of this season, but there is an opportunity for some chunk plays.

title: Raiders tight ends quiet with Brock Bowers out
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2024 draft class fared in a 38-24 road loss at the Denver Broncos on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the Cleveland Browns: Brock Bowers: The first-round pick didn’t play due to an ankle injury that kept him to just 11 snaps in […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2024 draft class fared in a 38-24 road loss at the Denver Broncos on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the Cleveland Browns: Brock Bowers: The first-round pick didn’t play due to an ankle injury that kept him to just 11 snaps in Week 10 against Seattle. In Bowers’ absence, Las Vegas tight ends Ian Thomas and Michael Mayer combined for just two catches for 23 yards and a touchdown. The Raiders are hopeful Bowers can play at Cleveland and he’s clearly needed. Jackson Powers-Johnson: The second-round pick remained on the bench for the sixth straight game. He played four snaps on special teams. D.J. Glaze: The third-round pick started at right tackle as usual. Tommy Eichenberg: The fifth-round pick from Ohio State played just four defensive snaps. It was the second straight game he didn’t play much after playing extensively for three straight games. He did play 29 snaps on special teams. Dylan Laube: The sixth-round pick had had six kickoffs for 134 yards and he had a punt return for 13 games. He is averaging 29.9 a kick return, which is second in the NFL. He had been leading the league for several weeks.

title: 5 Things I Think I Think About the Miami Dolphins After Week 11
summary: Stop me if you’ve heard this one before: Despite a herculean defensive effort, the Miami Dolphins lost another game due to mental mistakes and what is statistically the worst offense in all of football in points scored. I love the effort and the budding stars on an underappreciated defense, but man, this offense is hard […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Derrick Moore #8 of the Detroit Lions rushes Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins during the first half of the game at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images Stop me if you’ve heard this one before: Despite a herculean defensive effort, the Miami Dolphins lost another game due to mental mistakes and what is statistically the worst offense in all of football in points scored. I love the effort and the budding stars on an underappreciated defense, but man, this offense is hard to watch. Here are five things I think I think about the Dolphins’ loss in Buffalo. The Defense Played Better Than the Final Score Would Suggest So sure, allowing 26 points and more than 400 total yards doesn’t sound especially impressive. But you do a little digging, and Miami’s defense turned in another quality performance. First, the Dolphins intercepted Josh Allen twice, sacked him three times and limited the future Hall of Famer to a passer rating under 70. That’s a solid defensive performance. Buffalo’s rushing attack was held under 100 yards on 27 carries (3.5 yards per carry). They also forced the Bills to settle for field goals rather than touchdowns on multiple red-zone trips. And this is all without Zack Sieler, Jordan Phillips and Zeek Biggers. And then there’s this: Since Oct. 4, Buffalo has scored more than 30 points against every team except two: The Minnesota Vikings, whose defense this season is ridiculously good Your Miami Dolphins. In fact, the Dolphins have given up 30+ points only twice all year, and that was against two of the NFL’s elite offenses in the 49ers and Bengals. Sure, you could argue that the Dolphins’ lackluster offense is allowing teams to ease up on the gas, and I wouldn’t disagree with you. Still, for a defense missing key contributors and facing one of the league’s top offenses, that’s an accomplishment worth recognizing. If Miami had received even modest offensive support, this game could have looked very different. The Passing Game Failed Kyle McCord as Much as Kyle McCord Failed the Passing Game We all know Kyle McCord shouldn’t be starting NFL games at this point in his young career. McCord completed just 12 of 33 passes on Sunday for 102 yards, plus an interception. Several throws sailed high, others were late, and the offense never established any rhythm through the air. That said, the Dolphins finished with just 12 receptions on 33 targets. Twelve! Caleb Douglas caught only two of his 10 targets while dropping multiple catchable passes, including a potential red-zone scoring opportunity. (The game was probably out of reach by that point, but his drop against the Lions essentially ended any hopes of a comeback then too.) It’s worth mentioning there’s a solution for this: By comparison, the Bills caught 28 of their 44 targets and consistently converted opportunities when the ball arrived in catchable locations. Miami’s passing offense wasn’t sabotaged by one player – it was a collective failure. Ollie Gordon Is Playing Better Than His Box Scores After an explosive couple of games upon replacing De’Von Achane in the backfield, Gordon’s production lately has been a little more … pedestrian. 20 carries for 76 yards against the Colts. 16 for 55 against the Lions. What often gets overlooked is the environment he’s operating in. Opposing defenses have spent weeks loading the box, daring Miami’s struggling passing attack to beat them through the air. According to Kyle Crabbs of Locked On Dolphins , Gordon has consistently faced one of the league’s highest rates of eight-man boxes since the bye week. Yet despite that reality, Gordon turned 11 carries into 69 yards against Buffalo, averaging 6.3 yards per attempt and ripping off a 24-yard run. Maybe not a dominant performance, but it was another reminder that Gordon can still be productive despite facing unfavorable circumstances. Right Tackle Is a Gaping Hole of Awful Do you remember early in the season, when Austin Jackson was getting lit up like a Christmas tree? At the time, we said, “Sure, but he’s facing Pro Bowlers Maxx Crosby and Nick Bosa, let’s wait and see how he does against less accomplished defensive linemen.” Folks, it hasn’t gotten any better. Against Buffalo edge rusher Greg Rousseau, who currently has [checks notes] zero Pro Bowl nods, Jackson had a PFF grade of 34.6. (For context, a grade of 60 is considered average, a 50 is below average and a 40 is bad.) That’s not only the lowest of all the offensive linemen, or even anyone on the offense – it’s the lowest of anyone on the team on Sunday not named “Herring.” Rousseau finished with two sacks and constantly disrupted the pocket. Jackson hasn’t been this bad all season, but even at his best, he hasn’t been “good.” I’ve been reluctant to move Proctor out of left guard, mostly because he’s been so good where he is and I still have flashbacks of what poor guard play looks like from Jonah last season. But man. We need to do something. Let’s All Root Against the Patriots This Week When a team is 1-9, it’s easy to start looking ahead at next season’s draft and dreaming of Jeremiah Smith rocking the aqua and orange. If you want Smith, you’ll probably need the No. 1 spot overall. Currently, the Dolphins are third in the draft order, tied by record with the Titans and Chargers but losing out on strength of schedule. (Per the NFL, the team that played the schedule with the lowest winning percentage will be awarded the higher pick — pretty much, losing to bad teams is worse than losing to good teams, and the Dolphins have faced a lot of good teams.) Can the Dolphins sneak ahead of those other two teams? Maybe: Five of the Titans’ losses have been within a touchdown, and they still have another game against the Colts coming up. With a home game against the imploding Steelers and a matchup against the Raiders still coming up, I think they can finish with 3-4 wins. The Chargers will be tougher. I think they can beat the Dolphins Christmas weekend. Can the Chargers beat the Drake Maye-less Patriots at home this weekend? That’s the key – the rest of their schedule looks like a bunch of Ls to me. If we can get the Titans and Patriots to 3 wins, then we can afford to beat the Jets this weekend and still land the No. 1 pick in the draft. Sweeping the Jets in a 2-15 season would be rewarding in its own way. That’s my Christmas wish. Let’s make it happen! In the meantime, happy Leon Lett Day everyone!
