Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Vikings, a little more clarity in Thursday’s injury report. title: Patriots vs. Chargers: Who has the edge in Week 12?
summary: What a difference a few months can make. When the New England Patriots took on the Los Angeles Chargers in the wild card playoff round in January, it was billed as a matchup between two of the best quarterbacks in football. On Sunday, Drake Maye will be out after fracturing his fibula while Justin Herbert […]
full_text: What a difference a few months can make. When the New England Patriots took on the Los Angeles Chargers in the wild card playoff round in January, it was billed as a matchup between two of the best quarterbacks in football. On Sunday, Drake Maye will be out after fracturing his fibula while Justin Herbert remains in concussion protocol and is also far from a lock to play in the game. We might have a good old-fashioned Battle of the Backups on our hands, folks. Tommy DeVito versus D.J.Uiagalelei, one for the true connoisseurs. Who will have the edge when all is said and done, though? After initially favoring the home team , the oddsmakers have since changed their stance and now see the Patriots as 1.5-point favorites — a line we can agree with when looking at our head-too-head comparison between the two teams. Passing game Patriots pass offense vs. Chargers pass defense: There is no sugar-coating it: Tommy DeVito was not good after entering the game against the Lions in place of Drake Maye two weeks ago. However, the circumstances did him no favors so he’s getting a mulligan on that one. And with two weeks to prepare and the Patriots possibly getting Alijah Vera-Tucker and Romeo Doubs back, we do like his chances to play a lot more competitively this time around. As an added factor, a Chargers pass defense ranked just 22nd in EPA per dropback has been without five starters in both of its practices thus far this week. Even in the unlikely case that all of them will be ready to go come Sunday, L.A. might find itself in a more challenging position than one would suspect against a team fielding its backup quarterback. And so, we are giving a slight edge to DeVito and company. | Edge: Patriots Patriots pass defense vs. Chargers pass offense: Even with Justin Herbert in the lineup, the Chargers passing offense has been truly abysmal in its first year under coordinator Mike McDaniel. Not only has the unit turned thrown 11 interceptions (t-27th), it also has posted a dropback EPA of -0.117 (30th). Things have not looked good, and they might get even worse if the inexperienced D.J. Uiagalelei — he of seven career pass attempts — is thrown into the water. Luckily for him and his team, New England’s once-highly-touted pass defense has struggled mightily over the last few games as well. Still, with two weeks to find its mojo again and potentially going up against a player originally starting the season as the Chargers’ QB3, this is a chance at a “get right” game for the unit. Then again, if it doesn’t turn out that way, the Patriots defense might just be broken beyond repair. | Edge: Patriot s Patriots fans, join the game-day huddle! Follow every snap and discuss every decision with fellow fans on the SB Nation app. Connect through our live game chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Running game Patriots rushing offense vs. Chargers run defense: With Tommy DeVito under center, the Patriots will have to rely on their running game to show some significant improvement from the form it displayed leading up to last week’s bye. Will it be able to do so, though? Even with Reggie Gilliam back in the fold and Alijah Vera-Tucker nearing a return, that will not be easy. The Chargers, after all, will likely try to hone in on stopping the run to force DeVito to beat them. Luckily for the Patriots, Los Angeles’ run defense is ranked near the bottom of the league in EPA given up per run (-0.015) and as noted above might miss some key personnel including starting defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson and leading run tackler Daiyan Henley. | Edge: Patriots Patriots run defense vs. Chargers rushing offense: Even after getting gushed by Jahmyr Gibbs the last game, the Patriots defense is still ranked 15th in the NFL in both EPA per run (-0.051) and yards per carry (4.1) surrendered. However, the group will face another serious challenge this week in second-year man Omarion Hampton and a unit running the ball at one of the highest rates in football. New England needs to be ready to slow the run down and essentially do what L.A. will try on offense, if Justin Herbert is out: make the backup quarterback beat you. However, Hampton’s quality and the inconsistency of the Patriots run defense might make it hard to actually execute the plan as intended. | Edge: Chargers Special teams Neither team has been particularly good returning kickoffs and the Patriots do have a slight edge in the punt return game thanks to Marcus Jones lining up deep. However, every other category tilts toward the Chargers. Their coverage teams have performed at a high level this year, while kicker Cameron Dicker has a combined 5.6% miss rate on field goals and extra points compared to Andy Borregales’ 10.3%. In a game that could be decided by its oftentimes anonymous third phase, L.A. has the advantage. | Edge: Chargers Coaching The Patriots haven’t been able to consistently duplicate their success from last season, and part of it appears to fall on a coaching staff that will now have its work cut out for it given the quarterback situation. That said, Josh McDaniels has proven himself quite adaptable over his career — something that cannot be said yet about his Chargers counterpart, Mike McDaniel. When it comes to getting a new starting quarterback up to speed, and the two teams’ general performances so far this year, we still see New England as the better-equipped of the two teams in that regard. | Edge: Patriots Verdict The Patriots are the better team overall, have played the better football this year, and even at 5-5 clearly have a superior record. And yet, it all comes down to how well their backup quarterback can perform with the spotlight on him start to finish, and whether or not a much-maligned defense can get its mojo back. Given that the. Chargers are faced with all kinds of questions themselves, however, we still believe that both are possible — as is New England winning its sixth game of the year.

title: Patriots mailbag: How will the offense evolve for Tommy DeVito?
summary: The New England Patriots are back from their bye week as preparation begins for Tommy DeVito to take over at quarterback for the injured Drake Maye. So, let’s get into this week’s edition of the #PostPulpit Mailbag. How do you expect the Pats to alter the offense to fit Devito’s abilities, compared to Maye? How […]
full_text: The New England Patriots are back from their bye week as preparation begins for Tommy DeVito to take over at quarterback for the injured Drake Maye. So, let’s get into this week’s edition of the #PostPulpit Mailbag. How do you expect the Pats to alter the offense to fit Devito’s abilities, compared to Maye? How do they get the run game going? – Maye The Force Be With You Josh McDaniels and the Patriots coaching staff have had two weeks to figure out how to shape the offense around DeVito moving forward. It’s a process McDaniels has experience with , and one he says requires remaining fluid as they determine what DeVito is confident and comfortable doing. The biggest expectation here is that the Patriots offense will be less vertical moving forward. Drake Maye is an elite deep-ball thrower, ranking second in the league in both deep completions and average depth of target (10.1 yards). By comparison, DeVito averaged just 6.2 yards per target across two seasons in New York and attempted only 16 deep passes during that span. While DeVito showcased an impressive deep ball throughout training camp and the preseason, it’s unrealistic to expect him to replicate Maye’s success in that area. The deep shots can’t completely be removed from the call sheet, but DeVito has been at his best as a starter operating in the quick game and attacking the middle of the field. And while not necessarily a schematic change to the offense itself, establishing a more effective ground game would help DeVito by allowing the offense to stay on schedule and avoid obvious passing situations. It could also create opportunities for easier completions off play-action. Theoretically, a backup QB needs to be ready to go at the drop of a hat (or the snap of a fibula), but I’d be curious just how “ready” a backup QB usually is. DeVito certainly struggled, but at the same time the backup QB doesn’t take reps with the #1’s do they? Or if they do, they don’t get as many as the starting QB. I suspect he’s building chemistry with his line & receivers now that just wasn’t possible before Drake went down. – kwizzer As DeVito acknowledged this week, it is his job to be ready to go at the drop of the hat. It is a hard job, however, to get thrown into the fire especially without taking extensive line reps since the preseason (which is a different story in itself). Then besides getting reacclimatized to the game speed, you must adjust to little things like taking snaps from a different center. DeVito explained this week how different it is entering a week in which you know you’re the starter: “I think just more reps. Getting reps during practice, getting the actual reps of the game plan. And like I said, no excuses. That’s your job to be ready and do all of that. There are no words to really explain the feeling of what that is, knowing you’re going into that week, you’re about to go battle with these guys. Just the extra little attention to detail from everybody and the communication. ‘Hey, I see this this way, I see this that way.’ They speak to me and it’s a good conversation.“ Ok. What’s our best o-line combination down the stretch and to build for next year? – Chu With Alijah Vera-Tucker nearing his return from injured reserve, the Patriots have four of their week one starters available up front in Will Campbell, Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson and Morgan Moses. That leaves the big question at right guard. Matt Pryor has been solid while filling in but Ben Brown has also been back at practice this week. Will we win the game and a few more, or will we, well, y’know… – Marmalade32 The Patriots have no excuse to lose to this 1-9 Chargers team if Justin Herbert (concussion) is sidelined . From there, they should still beat the Dolphins in Week 18 and likely would be the pick over the Jets. It’s tough then to see a game the Patriots will be favored in in the remaining group of Bills, Vikings, Chiefs, and Broncos. Maye will push to return for the Denver game, while hosting the Vikings struggling offense on a short week is probably the game to steal to potentially make the Wild Card at 9-8. Who is your favorite 1st round player in the draft who would potentially be available pick 12 or later? – XGhost-PepperX As of November, I’d project some of the Patriots biggest needs in the draft to be wide receiver and then the spine of the defense (DT, LB, S). Indiana’s Charlie Becker is the consensus No. 2 wide receiver in the draft and would be a great fit with Drake Maye. However, New England might have won too many games already to land Becker, so LSU’s wide receiver Jackson Harris is another favorite of mine. On defense, Georgia linebacker Chris Cole has long been another favorite. That’s all for this week’s #PostPulpit mailbag. If you have questions you’d liked to be answered next week, submit them online in our weekly submission post on the Feed. Make sure to follow @iambrianhines and @PatsPulpit as well.

title: Patriots defense preparing for every Chargers quarterback possibility
summary: The New England Patriots are not the only team facing quarterback questions heading into Week 12. The Los Angeles Chargers, their opponent on Sunday, are in the same boat. Starting QB Justin Herbert remains in concussion protocol and was a no-show at practice both Wednesday and Thursday. With his status in question, backup D.J. Uiagalelei […]
full_text: The New England Patriots are not the only team facing quarterback questions heading into Week 12. The Los Angeles Chargers, their opponent on Sunday, are in the same boat. Starting QB Justin Herbert remains in concussion protocol and was a no-show at practice both Wednesday and Thursday. With his status in question, backup D.J. Uiagalelei might be elevated into the starting role. Given that uncertainty, the Patriots defense is faced with a question: who to prepare for? “That’s a question that gets asked a lot: ‘You don’t know if a quarterback’s going to play or not, do you prepare for all of them?’ It’s lot about us,” defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr explained earlier this week. “Obviously, we know a lot more about Herbert’s play style than the next two guys, D.J. and Jake [Browning], if they make Jake active. But they are aware of their play styles. Obviously, there’s a lot more tape of Herbert, but everybody’s aware of the contingency plans. We went over that again [Wednesday], the contingency plans if we get news if something else changes.” Kuhr likened the situation to preparing for Denver Broncos backup quarterback Jarrett Stidham ahead of last year’s AFC Championship Game. That contest came two weeks after New England’s most recent meeting with Herbert, whose offense was held to three points in the wild card round. Uiagalelei was inactive as a member of the Chargers’ practice squad that day. Now, 10 months later, he is in line to potentially get his first career start and add to a résumé consisting of a mere 21 regular season snaps — all of them in a loss to the Texans earlier this season — as well as two pass completions on seven attempts for 24 yards and a touchdown. Despite the limited output so far, the Patriots have to familiarize themselves with the 25-year-old former undrafted free agent. And in the process of doing so, they have seen some differences to Los Angeles’ regular starter. “Strong arm. I would say more from the pocket than Herbert,” Kuhr said about his game. “Obviously, some inexperience. But he made some plays in college; obviously, he’s made a roster. So, I would say he’s a professional, he’s going to take advantage of his opportunity just like every backup quarterback does.”

title: Ex-Patriots quarterback Joe Milton steals the show on Thanksgiving
summary: With one former New England Patriots quarterback in the broadcast booth, another played the game of his life. Joe Milton, under the watchful eye of Tom Brady, led the Philadelphia Eagles to a 39-38 road victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. And even on a day that saw the likes of Patrick Mahomes, Josh […]
full_text: With one former New England Patriots quarterback in the broadcast booth, another played the game of his life. Joe Milton, under the watchful eye of Tom Brady, led the Philadelphia Eagles to a 39-38 road victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. And even on a day that saw the likes of Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, Caleb Williams, Jared Goff and Dak Prescott all line up under center, it was the third-year QB that stole the show. Milton completed 21 of 31 pass attempts for 331 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. He also led the game-winning drive when he marched Philadelphia’s offense into kicker Jake Elliott’s field goal range in the late fourth quarter, helping the Eagles overcome what was a 21-point deficit in the late third quarter. In addition, he proved why his “Bazooka Joe” nickname was well earned: he threw some truly spectacular passes. Every time Joe Milton made the craziest throw of the year vs the Cowboys 5 different times. pic.twitter.com/lVuL46DCmH — Cam (@42Cyc) November 27, 2026 Milton completed six of his 11 deep pass attempts versus the Cowboys, gaining 188 yards and scoring three touchdowns. He finished the game with 0.308 expected points added per play, a completion percentage 12.1 points over expectation, and an average of 17.3 air yards — ranking first among all six of the quarterbacks taking the field on Thursday. Whether he can build on the successful outing in front of a national audience will be seen. For Milton, however, it was a high point on what had been a rollercoaster of a career so far. That rollercoaster, of course, that started when the Patriots selected him in the sixth round of the 2024 draft. Milton was brought in in the same draft class as third overall pick Drake Maye, whose status as the Patriots’ future face of the franchise was never questioned. This, in turn, put his fellow then-rookie on a path to backup duty; but with veteran Jacoby Brissett also under contract at the time, not even that materialized. He ended up playing just one game as a rookie, the season finale against Buffalo a mere hours before head coach Jerod Mayo was fired. Milton completed 22 of 29 passes in that contest for 241 yards and a touchdown, leading New England to its fourth game of the year (and to drop out of the first overall draft pick). With a new regime under Mike Vrabel coming in, however, his days were numbered. In April of 2025, Milton and a seventh-round pick were sent to Dallas for a fifth-rounder. Through a series of follow-up trade, Patriots turned that selection into kicker Andy Borregales, long snapper Julian Ashby and cornerback Kobee Minor. Milton, meanwhile, played four games in his first season as a Cowboy but lost the QB2 competition this summer. He started his 2026 campaign on the Dallas practice squad, but was signed off of it by the Eagles in October. A month later, and with him now serving as Philadelphia’s starter in place of the injured Jalen Hurts, he now got the best of his former team.

title: Patriots vs. Chargers weather forecast for NFL Week 12
summary: SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA, is an indoor arena and therefore unbothered by the elements. This means that any weather forecast for Sunday’s game between the New England Patriots and their hosts, the Los Angeles Chargers, will be irrelevant and have no bearing on the outcome of the Week 12 contest. full_text: SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA, is an indoor arena and therefore unbothered by the elements. This means that any weather forecast for Sunday’s game between the New England Patriots and their hosts, the Los Angeles Chargers, will be irrelevant and have no bearing on the outcome of the Week 12 contest. For a 5-5 Patriots team currently outside of the playoff picture but well within striking range — particularly considering some recent developments elsewhere in the AFC — that should be a positive. Why? Because a controlled environment without any meteorological challenges means one less factor of uncertainty surrounding backup quarterback Tommy DeVito, who is set to start his first game in place of the injured Drake Maye. In addition, no weather impact also should help the Patriots in the kicking game; Andy Borregales has made just 11 of 14 field goal tries and also missed one of his 25 extra points this season. With wind not a significant factor, however, he will not have to worry about this part of the operation being an issue. In what might end up as a close game, any help he and the Patriots as a whole can get in that regard is welcome. As for the conditions outside the stadium, the temperature at kickoff is projected as mostly sunny with a high of around 74°F by the National Weather Service . No precipitation is in the forecast. Kickoff between the Patriots and Chargers at SoFi Stadium on Sunday was flexed from primetime to 4:05 p.m. ET .

title: Patriots vs. Chargers Thursday injury report for Week 12
summary: After practicing for three straight days coming out of their bye week, the New England Patriots opted to give their players a day off for Thanksgiving. Accordingly, the injury report released on Thursday is merely an estimation what it would look like had the team practiced. And if it did, the list would look exactly […]
full_text: After practicing for three straight days coming out of their bye week, the New England Patriots opted to give their players a day off for Thanksgiving. Accordingly, the injury report released on Thursday is merely an estimation what it would look like had the team practiced. And if it did, the list would look exactly like it did on Wednesday . As opposed to the Patriots, their Week 12 opponent did hold a practice on Thursday even though there were no major changes for the Los Angeles Chargers either. And with that said, let’s take a look at the two teams’ second injury reports leading up to Sunday’s 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff at SoFi Stadium. Did not participate Patriots QB Drake Maye (fibula) WR A.J. Brown (hamstring) OL Walter Rouse (concussion) CB Carlton Davis III (knee) Chargers QB Justin Herbert (concussion) RB Keaton Mitchell (knee) WR Brenen Thompson (hamstring) TE David Njoku (shoulder) DT Dalvin Tomlinson (knee) ED Tuli Tuipulotu (ankle) ED Akheem Mesidor (ankle) LB Daiyan Henley (knee) CB Tarheeb Still (ankle) The Patriots projected no changes to their list of absentees, with Drake Maye headlining the group after fracturing his fibula in Week 10 versus the Detroit Lions. The expectation is that the MVP runner-up will miss most if not all of the remaining regular season, with backup Tommy DeVito being prepared to take over as the starter in his absence. More interesting that New England’s estimation, however, is the Chargers’ report after they practiced Thursday. The first name that stands out is Justin Herbert, the team’s starting quarterback who remains in concussion protocol and has now missed both sessions this week; seemingly in anticipation of him being inactive, L.A. promoted practice squad QB Jake Browning to the 53-man roster on Thursday. Browning would serve as QB2 behind second-year passer D.J. Uiagalelei in case Herbert is unable to go. Herbert is joined on the DNP list by four defensive starters: defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson, edge Tuli Tuipulotu, linebacker Daiyan Henley and cornerback Tarheeb Still. Limited participation Patriots FB Reggie Gilliam (knee) WR Romeo Doubs (shoulder — IR return) LG Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring — IR return) Chargers S Kendall Williamson (calf) The Patriots estimated a limited level of participation from both of their recent designees to be brought back from injured reserve, Romeo Doubs and Alijah Vera-Tucker. This leaves their status for Sunday’s game in question; New England still has a respective 20 and 18 days to activate them to the 53-man roster. One of Los Angeles’ injured players, meanwhile, graduated from sidelined to limited participation: reserve safety Kendall Williamson. Full participation Patriots OL Ben Brown (knee) Chargers DT Teair Tart (not injury related — rest) LB Khalil Mack (not injury related — rest) Ben Brown would have been a full practice participant again on Thursday, which suggests he is on track to factor into the interior offensive line mix this week. Depending on Alijah Vera-Tucker’s outlook, Brown could either start at left or at right guard, or serve as a versatile backup behind whoever gets first billing on Sunday. For the Chargers, veteran. defenders Teair Tart and Khalil Mack were back in action on Thursday. Both were given a veteran’s day of rest on Wednesday and are in line to play on Sunday. After taking the day off on Thursday, the Patriots will return to the practice fields at Gillette Stadium on Friday morning for another regular session. They will fly out to Los Angeles later that same day.

title: Patriots rooting guide for Thanksgiving weekend
summary: Happy Thanksgiving weekend, everybody. While the rest of us are going to enjoy some days with family and food, the NFL is quite busy: a total of 16 games will be played between Wednesday and Monday, with at least one game on on five of the next six days. One of those will be played […]
full_text: Happy Thanksgiving weekend, everybody. While the rest of us are going to enjoy some days with family and food, the NFL is quite busy: a total of 16 games will be played between Wednesday and Monday, with at least one game on on five of the next six days. One of those will be played by the New England Patriots, who are going to take on the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET. There are no questions about who to root for in this specific game, but how about the others? Let’s take a look. Once again, a quick explainer: as long as the Patriots are still theoretically alive in the race for a playoff spot, we will root with that possibility in mind. Thursday 1 p.m. ET Chicago Bears (8-2) at Detroit Lions (8-2) : Go good game! The Patriots lost to both teams already this year, so this really makes no difference whatsoever. | CBS 4:30 p.m. ET Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) at Dallas Cowboys (5-6) : Go good game! Two NFC East rivals going against one another with no impact on the Patriots. Time to enjoy a second slice of pie. | FOX 8:20 p.m. ET Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) at Buffalo Bills (9-1) : Go… Bills? Okay, stay with us here. If we are being honest with ourselves, the Patriots can probably kiss their dreams of defending the AFC East title this season goodbye. However, the playoffs are still a possibility. Other teams are more realistic candidates to drop behind New England — looking at you, Pittsburgh — but if the Chiefs have no games on their schedule where it would be essential for us to root for rather than against them. So, in an ideal scenario, they kick off a losing streak on Thursday night that might just allow the Patriots to overtake them further down the road. Of course, the chances of that actually happening are fairly low, but one can dream. | NBC Friday 3 p.m. ET Denver Broncos (8-2) at Pittsburgh Steelers ( 6-4 ) : Go Broncos! Now this is a game that truly matters. The Steelers are the current seventh seed in the AFC and as such the Patriots’ closest rival in the race for a postseason spot. In fact, if they lose to the Broncos and New England wins in L.A. then the Patriots are suddenly ahead of them in the standings. Luckily for the Patriots, the Steelers are doing their best these days to at least play their part in that. | Prime Video Sunday 1 p.m. ET New Orleans Saints (3-7) at Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) : Go Saints! Somebody has to win the AFC North, and the Bengals are the best bet right now. That said, it would be good if they had to fight for playoff positioning until the very last week of the season, just in case the Patriots need them to beat the Browns in Week 18. With. that in mind, we are rooting for the Saints in this one. | CBS Baltimore Ravens (4-7) at Houston Texans (4-6) : Go Ravens! Another somewhat important game from a Patriots point of view. Neither team is currently in the playoff picture, but the Texans have seemingly started hitting their stride and a loss to the moribund Ravens would help break their momentum and make a late push harder. | CBS New York Giants (6-3-1) at Indianapolis Colts (3-8) : Go Colts! Indianapolis entering the playoff race seems like a long shot, meaning that this can be a game where we root with draft position in mind. Don’t forget: the Jets earn the Colts’ first-rounder next year. | FOX Tennessee Titans (1-9) at Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) : Go Titans! With games against the Steelers and Texans still on their schedule, the Patriots will want the Jaguars to have to bring their A-game in both contests. Maybe some heat applied from a loss to their division rivals can help with that. | FOX New York Jets (3-8) at Miami Dolphins (1-9) : Go Dolphins! We are rooting for the worse-positioned AFC East team in this one, once again from a draft perspective. | CBS Atlanta Falcons (3-7) at Minnesota Vikings (7-3) : Go Vikings! Four words: strength of schedule tiebreaker. Will it matter? Unlikely. Is it better to be safe than sorry, though? Absolutely. | FOX 4:25 p.m. ET Washington Commanders (4-5-1) at Arizona Cardinals (3-8) : Go Commanders! We would rather see top draft picks end up with an NFC team like the Cardinals over, for example, the Dolphins or Jets. Sorry, Arizona, it’s nothing personal. | FOX Seattle Seahawks ( 6-4 ) at San Francisco 49ers (9-1) : Go Seahawks! Once again, strength of schedule makes the difference here. | FOX 8:20 p.m. ET Las Vegas Raiders (4-7) at Cleveland Browns ( 6-4 ) : Go Raiders! A big one for the Patriots on Sunday night. New England has a clear edge over Las Vegas, but is looking up in the standings to the Browns. A Raiders win would therefore be important for two reasons: it would drop Cleveland to 6-5 and also give them a negative result in a common game with the Patriots. That tiebreaker might just end up being important with no head-to-head between the two teams. | NBC Monday 8:15 p.m. ET Carolina Panthers (5-5) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7): Go good game! An all-NFC South battle will close out Thanksgiving weekend on Monday night. It’s a low-stress affair from a Patriots perspective. | ESPN The following games have already been played. title: Saints Draft Position: NFL Week 12
summary: After yet another loss, the New Orleans Saints are in the top 10 and project to select number 8 overall in the NFL Draft. I will warn you, you may not like the conversation I’m about to have, and honestly, I’m not sure I do either. Let’s start with talking about Tyler Shough. I do […]
full_text: TEMPE, AZ - NOVEMBER 21: Oklahoma State Cowboys quarterback Drew Mestemaker (17) warms up before the college football game between the Oklahoma State Cowboys and the Arizona State Sun Devils on November 21, 2026 at Mountain America Stadium in Tempe, Arizona. (Photo by Kevin Abele/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After yet another loss, the New Orleans Saints are in the top 10 and project to select number 8 overall in the NFL Draft. I will warn you, you may not like the conversation I’m about to have, and honestly, I’m not sure I do either. Let’s start with talking about Tyler Shough. I do not think the Saints should make a QB change after this season. His play has been bad of late, but that happens sometimes with QBs, and it matters more how they can bounce back from it. I blame coaching for a lot of the issues Shough is going through because we have seen how good he can be. 2028 would be the likely offseason when a QB change could happen because we will see what Shough can do in 2027. Hopefully that can happen with a new staff, because if it’s not, Shough’s regression will only continue, which will be one of the biggest missed opportunities in a long time. Shough has the potential to be a top-10 QB in the NFL, and he will likely thrive somewhere else if that happens. Hopefully it doesn’t, and finally Shough can be put in a position to succeed. There is also a way it happens sooner. If a new head coach comes in and falls in love with a prospect, they may want to draft their guy. Shough is Kellen Moore’s guy, and although I do think any head coach candidate would love to work with him, there’s a future that they may not want to. Because of the potential, even if very unlikely, I wanted to take this week’s draft positions to talk about a few options in 2027. At the top of the draft, Drew Mestemaker will likely be the #1 QB off the board. He had a really good season, has ideal measurements for the NFL, and can carry an offense. CJ Carr is another option that is more realistic for pick #8. Then you have Arch Manning and Austin Simmons, but they may stay in college and wait for 2028. The options are not great in this year’s draft, and giving up on Shough makes little sense. Hopefully it doesn’t happen.

title: Saints vs. Bengals: Key Matchups
summary: The New Orleans Saints have fallen to 3-7 on the season after a loss to the Chicago Bears. New Orleans was completely outmatched in the loss, losing in their key matchups. The Saints are now up against another one of the league’s best teams with the Cincinnati Bengals coming to town. If New Orleans can […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 22: Travis Etienne Jr. #3 of the New Orleans Saints rushes the ball against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints have fallen to 3-7 on the season after a loss to the Chicago Bears. New Orleans was completely outmatched in the loss, losing in their key matchups. The Saints are now up against another one of the league’s best teams with the Cincinnati Bengals coming to town. If New Orleans can come away with a win, it will likely be due to winning these key matchups. CB Kool-Aid McKinstry vs. Ja’Marr Chase The Saints have been efficient in limiting receivers in recent weeks. Tetairoa McMillan was limited to 35 receiving yards, and New Orleans limited Rome Odunze and Luther Burden to 55 combined. Despite their recent success, they haven’t faced a superstar quite like Ja’Marr Chase. While Chase is coming off an off day, logging just 31 yards, the superstar was on a tear before that, logging 527 yards in the three-game span before that. Cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry hasn’t had the breakout season we all hoped for, but has been better than the public perceives him. Staley trusts McKinstry in coverage, and he’s had good film against opposing WR1s. With the Saints’ offensive struggles, their defense must keep them in games. That all starts with slowing down Chase. If New Orleans can take the star wide receiver out of the game, they can continue to keep themselves in contention with one of the league’s best. RB Travis Etienne Jr. vs. the Bengals’ run defense The Bengals have had a recent struggle against the run, highlighted in their loss to the Washington Commanders. In the loss, Cincinnati allowed 140 rushing yards, with 55 coming from Jayden Daniels and 95 from their running back tandem of Jacory Crosky-Merritt and Austin Ekeler. Crosky-Merritt and Ekeler were efficient in their running, with Crosky-Merritt averaging 4.2 yards per carry and Ekeler going for a strong 5.9 yards per carry. Running back Travis Etienne finally broke free for an explosive year, logging a 46-yard long against the Chicago Bears. Etienne finished the day with 76 yards on 14 carries. While his averages drop significantly if you take away his big run, hopefully his big run was an eye-opener for Kellen Moore and the rest of the coaching staff that their $48 million running back deserves more carries. The Saints are the worst running team in the league, and it’s mostly due to poor play design and predictable play calling. Luckily, New Orleans is facing a team that has struggled to slow down the run and is the 11th-worst run defense in the league. If they want any chance to win against the 7-3 Bengals, they’ll have to control the game on the ground. Chris Olave and Jordyn Tyson vs. the Bengals’ secondary The Saints defense is facing one of, if not the best, wide receiver duos in the league against Chase and Tee Higgins. New Orleans is looking to form an impressive wide receiver duo of their own with Chris Olave and Jordyn Tyson. Olave started the season strong but has slowed down recently, while Tyson has proven to be a reliable complement. But the Bengals defense has come a long way from their poor pass defense from a year ago. Cincinnati’s secondary has had a respectable season, ranking 15th in the league. With seven games remaining, Olave is on pace for a monster year, already logging 866 receiving yards this season. The introduction of Tyson in the Saints’ offense has opened up space for Olave, and he is coming off a strong performance against the Bears, logging 9 receptions for 102 yards. With Tyler Shough’s recent struggles, a bounce-back game where he could rely on his two first-round receivers would be big for his confidence.
author: Kyle Besson

title: Our Defense vs. Their Offense: Cincinnati Bengals
summary: Here is the side of the matchup all New Orleans Saints fans should be concerned about. The Saints will have to slow down former national champion and current MVP favorite Joe Burrow. Not to mention the matchup between the best receiver in the league, Ja’Marr Chase, and the Saints’ secondary. Oh, and Tee Higgins is […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 22: Chase Young #99 of the New Orleans Saints during the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is the side of the matchup all New Orleans Saints fans should be concerned about. The Saints will have to slow down former national champion and current MVP favorite Joe Burrow. Not to mention the matchup between the best receiver in the league, Ja’Marr Chase, and the Saints’ secondary. Oh, and Tee Higgins is a problem as well. The Bengals are currently sixth in the NFL in total offense, averaging 383 yards per game. They are averaging 289 passing yards per game, which ranks first in the NFL. The weakness of the Bengals’ offense is their rushing attack, as they are just as bad as the Saints at running the ball. The Bengals only average 84 yards per game on the ground, which ranks 30th in the NFL. The Saints rank 27th in total defense, allowing 355 total yards per game. As poorly as the Bengals run the ball on offense, the Saints are just as bad at stopping the run on defense. The Saints’ defense is allowing 131 rushing yards per game, which ranks 28th in the NFL. This will be a matchup of weakness against weakness. If the Saints allow the Bengals to establish offensive balance, this game will become significantly more difficult for them to defend. Entering their Monday night matchup, the Bengals were averaging 36.2 points per game during their five-game winning streak, so this offense is rounding into midseason form. Burrow is on pace to become the first QB in NFL history to finish a season with over 5,000 passing yards, 50 TDs, and a 70% completion percentage. The Saints have one advantage they can proudly lean on, and that is the pass-rushing ability of their two edge rushers, Chase Young and Carl Granderson. Now, this does not mean it will be easy for them because, unlike in years past, the Bengals have been able to improve the protection of their franchise QB. The Bengals have allowed only 16 sacks this season. This places a premium on being able to generate pressure on Burrow with just four rushers. If Brandon Staley has to bring more than four, Burrow, Higgins, and Chase will be more than willing to take advantage. How do you think the Saints’ defense will match up against the Bengals’ offense? Do you think they can affect Joe Burrow and force him into making some poor decisions? Share your thoughts in the comments. .

However, with each passing week, the margin for error continues to shrink. The odds may be stacked against New Orleans, but anything can happen on any given Sunday. title: Saints Rookie Report: Week 11 review vs. the Bears
summary: Another loss and another pretty quiet day for the Saints’ rookies, even Jordyn Tyson. WR Jordyn Tyson Speaking of Tyson, let’s start with him. This was a weird game for him. When the ball got in his hands, he did really well once again, but it only happened once in the air and once on […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 22: Jordyn Tyson #0 of the New Orleans Saints during the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Another loss and another pretty quiet day for the Saints’ rookies, even Jordyn Tyson. WR Jordyn Tyson Speaking of Tyson, let’s start with him. This was a weird game for him. When the ball got in his hands, he did really well once again, but it only happened once in the air and once on the ground. That is not good enough, and the Saints need to do a better job getting him involved. Next, I want to talk about the play that has gotten a lot of attention. When Tyler Shough was sacked for a safety, Kellen Moore and Shough said that Tyson was supposed to chip the pass rusher. That was likely a rookie mistake that looks much worse because it gave up points, but also, relying on the guy who has barely played in the NFL to do that does have some risk. I’m really hoping Tyson can get more involved this week. DT Christen Miller Miller is currently on IR. TE Oscar Delp We did get some more involvement from Delp in the passing game, but once again, not enough. The Saints still won’t fully commit to him, which is unfortunate because I do think it will help. G Jeremiah Wright Wright did not play this week, and it was probably for the best. He needs more time to develop, and the interior needs the veterans to step in. Not sure if Erik McCoy will play this week, but no matter what, Wright will likely not play. WR Bryce Lance Another game of Lance not really doing much on offense and not having the best game on special teams. Besides blocking, which has also been inconsistent, Lance has not had a positive impact when on the field, and the Saints might as well just commit to Lance being WR6. WR Barion Brown Brown had a really good return in this game, but that’s really the only impact he made. It was an important day for him because former LSU teammate Zavion Thomas is in a very similar situation to Brown, but he ended up getting outplayed. He’s really improving as a returner, and I know that touchdown is coming soon.

title: Giants-Colts matchup: When the Giants have the ball
summary: The New York Giants are coming off of a fantastic win at home in Week 11, but now need to turn the page to focus on the Indiana Colts. This is not the Colts team that many were expecting when the schedule was released. The Colts looked like one of the best teams in the […]
full_text: ﻿The New York Giants offense before a play. | Getty Images The New York Giants are coming off of a fantastic win at home in Week 11, but now need to turn the page to focus on the Indiana Colts. This is not the Colts team that many were expecting when the schedule was released. The Colts looked like one of the best teams in the AFC for the first half of the 2025 season, and it was widely expected that they’d return to form with Jones’ return from injury. That, however, didn’t happen and the 3-8 Colts are well out of the AFC’s playoff picture. The Giants’ 23-18 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars preserved their lead at the top of the NFC East, and this game is being looked at as a brief reprieve before the toughest stretch of the Giants’ schedule. Can the Giants maintain their level of play and not overlook Colts? Stats that matter The Colts’ defensive scheme The Colts’ defense is designed and called by a familiar face in defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo. He was the Giants’ defensive backs coach in 2018 before being hired as the Cincinnati Bengals defensive coordinator in 2019 and then becoming the Colts’ DC in 2025. Anaroumo is a well-regarded defensive mind who has been in consideration for the Giants’ head coaching job. His scheme is built around a “multiple” 4-3 front and he primarily calls zone coverages on the back end, though their rate of zone coverage is one of the lowest in the NFL, while their man coverage rate is among the highest. The Colts call more coverages with single-high safeties, usually mixing Cover-1 and Cover-3 looks. When they use two-deep safety looks it’s usually Cover-4, with some Cover-6 mixed in. Recall, Cover-6 is a hybrid coverage that blends Cover-4 and Cover-2 shells, or “Quarter-Quarter-Half”. The Cover-4 is called to the passing strength, matching more DBs to the side of the offense with more receiving threats. The Colts primarily rely on a 4-man rush, though it remains to be seen how Anaroumo will adapt now that DeForest Buckner has been traded. The Colts’ defense hasn’t been good this year, but they’ve been better against the pass than the run. Their passing EPA allowed is 0.082 per play (19th in the NFL), and their passing success rate allowed is 42.5 percent (8th best). Their rushing EPA allowed, however, is -0.010 per play, which is 29th in the NFL, with a rushing success rate allowed of 43.9 percent (23rd). The centerpiece of their defense is now CB Sauce Gardner, acquired from the Jets last year. Gardner has rare athletic traits for the position with exceptional length and athleticism, and is one of the best corners in the NFL at forcing tight window throws. Gardner is allowing just 2.1 yards of separation as the closest defender (per NextGenStats). For comparison, that’s less than the Giants’ own Deonte Banks, who’s allowing 2.3 yards of separation on average. That said, Banks has been much better at the catch point, forcing -4.7% catch rate below expected, while Gardner’s opponents are catching passes at a rate of 11.1% higher than expected. Gardner’s presence allows the Colts to play more man coverage than they have in the past, but he can be had in coverage. Answers for the blitz The Giants’ offense has struggled against the blitz over the last two weeks. Both the Washington Commanders and Jaguars dialed up the blitz on key downs, and they were generally successful in disrupting the Giants’ offense when they did so. Whether by getting a free runner in run defense or sending pressure against J.J. McCarthy on passing downs, the Giants’ opponents were able to generate pressure and disrupt the Giants’ offense. The good news is that the Colts don’t blitz all that often. They’re 31st in the NFL in blitz rate at 16.7%. Their four-man rush had been adequate, generating pressure and hitting the quarterback at (roughly) league-average rates. But that was, for the most part, with DeForest Buckner. He was one of the Colts to go in their trade deadline fire sale. Now, their best pass rusher is DL Adetomiwa Adebawore, who leads the team in sacks (5.0) and QB hits(12). Edge defender Laiatu Latu is a potential problem as well, but it remains to be seen just how much pressure the Colts will be able to generate with just their front four. It’s possible that they could attempt to play a more blitz-heavy style of defense in light of how the Commanders’ and Jaguars’ defenses were able to disrupt J.J. McCarthy. However, that isn’t really in their defensive DNA, and playing outside of their scheme and preferred philosophy could create opportunities for the Giants. The Giants’ running backs are all capable receivers, and it might be a good idea to ask them to chip before releasing into routes as opposed to purely blocking. If McCarthy can quickly recognize the blitz, slowing a pass rusher and immediately giving him a quick answer could help the offense be more consistent. Attacking the Colts’ defense The Giants will almost certainly look to get their rushing attack on track and lean on their running game against the Colts. Not only have the Colts fielded one of the worst run defenses in the NFL this year, ranking 29th in yards per carry allowed (4.7 per carry), but they also rank 30th in rushing EPA allowed (16.47 EPA allowed). That was before the Colts traded away their best defensive lineman in DeForest Buckner, and the Colts gave up 167 yards on the ground to the Texans without Buckner. When the Giants aren’t running the ball, they can attack the vulnerable flats and seams inherent in the Colts’ favored Cover-3 looks. J.J. McCarthy has plenty of arm strength to hit square-outs in the flat to either sideline, and those routes would use Malik Nabers and Darnell Mooney’s quickness to generate separation. Likewise, the Giants have been trying to hit on explosive plays down the middle of the field. The seams in Cover-3 defenses could be good targets for deep passes to tight ends Isaiah Likely or Theo Johnson, or wide receivers Mooney, Nabers, and Jalin Hyatt. Finally, the Giants could also look to their 11-personnel package more often. Malik Nabers has proven to be an absolutely devastating slot receiver, and the Giants should look for opportunities to use him in that capacity. Darnell Mooney might not be an ideal outside receiver, however using him as an outside receiver not only adds another speed threat to stretch the defense but allows Nabers to move into the slot. The Giants have flashed a dangerous offense that’s equally capable of being explosive and suffocating — as well as ineffective and inefficient. The Colts’ defense presents them with an opportunity to truly put it all together for the first time this season.

title: New York Jets News: A Miracle run to the Playoffs? Are you Saying There’s a Chance?
summary: The New York Jets are 3-8. According to the NFL Playoff Picture (via the NFL Media Group), the Jets currently have a 1% chance of making the playoffs. If they lose to the Miami Dolphins in Week 12, that’ll reduce their chances to less than 1%. However, if they beat the fish, their playoff chances […]
full_text: Jan 9, 2010, Cincinnati, OH, USA; New York Jets coach Rex Ryan is interviewed by NBC sideline reporter Tiki Barber after the 2010 AFC Wild Card playoff game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paul Brown Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee/Image of Sport-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Jets are 3-8. According to the NFL Playoff Picture (via the NFL Media Group), the Jets currently have a 1% chance of making the playoffs. If they lose to the Miami Dolphins in Week 12, that’ll reduce their chances to less than 1%. However, if they beat the fish, their playoff chances will double to 2%. Are you saying there’s a chance? There’s a section of the fan base that would prefer to see the Jets lose to both improve their draft positioning and to lessen the chances of Aaron Glenn returning in 2027. The problem, according to some of those fans, is that there are too many winnable games down the stretch for the Jets. On paper, the Jets will be or could be facing at least three backup quarterbacks (Carson Beck or Josh Johnson, Kyle McCord, and Tommy DeVito). Also, depending on whether the Buffalo Bills have anything left to play for in Week 18, that could be a fourth backup QB. Instead of complaining, why don’t we take advantage? This opens up a favorable pathway to go on a winning streak. Now, how likely is that? Well, that’s a different conversation altogether. The Jets haven’t won back-to-back games all season. They haven’t really upset anyone, and they haven’t consistently beaten teams that folks assume they should be able to beat. Both of those things would be necessary to even have a hint of the postseason. The other thing helping the Jets’ potential path is that the bottom of the AFC is falling apart. Pittsburgh is crumbling; the Jets have the head-to-head tiebreaker over Cleveland; they play New England; and Baltimore has a backup in at QB. I’m not saying it’s likely; I’m not guaranteeing it’s going to happen; all I’m saying is there’s a chance, and maybe that’s what Jets fans should be rooting for. The Indianapolis Colts are self-destructing. The Jets control their first-round pick. That pick has a great chance to be a top-three selection. The Jets don’t need to tank; the Colts can tank for them. So… playoffs?! Maybe I’m food drunk from Thanksgiving, but I’m starting to see the light! J-E-T-S! Take the game-day conversation with you! summary: The Jets have played eight times on Thanksgiving in the past. They are an even 4-4 in those games. Below we will take a look at them. November 24, 1960: New York Titans 41 Dallas Texans 35 The American Football League played games on Thanksgiving, and the Jets played on Turkey Day in each their […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - JANUARY 03: Brad Smith #16 of the New York Jets runs in a touchdown in the second quarter against Frostee Rucker #92 of the Cincinnati Bengals at Giants Stadium on January 3, 2010 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jets have played eight times on Thanksgiving in the past. They are an even 4-4 in those games. Below we will take a look at them. November 24, 1960: New York Titans 41 Dallas Texans 35 The American Football League played games on Thanksgiving, and the Jets played on Turkey Day in each their first three years of existence. They were called the Titans at that point. Playing against the future Kansas City Chiefs , Don Maynard caught 10 passes for 179 yards and a touchdown, while Art Powell added 8 catches for 110 yards and a touchdown. November 23, 1961: New York Titans 21 Buffalo Bills 14 Al Dorow threw for 223 yards and a touchdown, and Dick Felt returned an interception 55 yards for a touchdown to provide the Titans with the winning margin at the Polo Grounds. November 22, 1962: New York Titans 46 Denver Broncos 45 A wild game in Denver saw the Titans blow a 24-7 lead and then overcome a 45-32 fourth quarter deficit on Johnny Green’s fourth and fifth touchdown passes of the game, one to Dick Christy and the other to Art Powell. November 23, 1972: Detroit Lions 37 New York Jets 20 Entering the fourth quarter, the Lions led 23-20, but they blew the game open with a field goal and touchdown runs by Greg Landry from 6 yards and Altie Taylor from 38. November 28, 1985: Detroit Lions 31 New York Jets 20 Eric Hipple threw four touchdown passes, three to Leonard Thompson as the Lions jumped out to a 24-3 lead and never looked back. November 22, 2007: Dallas Cowboys 34 New York Jets 3 It was an ugly afternoon in a lost season for the Jets. The Cowboys owned a 21-3 lead at halftime on a Marion Barber touchdown run, a Jason Witten reception from Tony Romo, and a Terrence Newman interception off Kellen Clemens returned for a score. November 25, 2010: New York Jets 26 Cincinnati Bengals 10 In the third meeting between these teams in eleven months, the Jets erased a 10-7 halftime deficit. Brad Smith was the star with a 53 yard touchdown run in the first minute of the second half and an 89 yard kickoff returned for a score in the fourth quarter. November 22, 2012: New England Patriots 49 New York Jets 19 This game is best remembered for the Buttfumble. What people don’t remember was that was part of a 52 second span where New England scored an offensive touchdown, a defensive touchdown, and a special teams touchdown to turn a 7-0 lead into a 28-0 rout.

title: Even in a lost Eagles season, greatness can happen
summary: I’m going to tell you something you already know. The Philadelphia Eagles are not going to win the Super Bowl this year. In fact, they are almost certainly not going to make the playoffs, even though their epic 39-38 back-from-the-dead victory over the Cowboys in Dallas on Thanksgiving afternoon increased their odds of doing so […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS- NOVEMBER 26: Joe Milton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates after an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’m going to tell you something you already know. The Philadelphia Eagles are not going to win the Super Bowl this year. In fact, they are almost certainly not going to make the playoffs, even though their epic 39-38 back-from-the-dead victory over the Cowboys in Dallas on Thanksgiving afternoon increased their odds of doing so just a tad. #Eagles playoff odds according to @benbbaldwin 's playoff simulator. 74% if 10-7 28% if 9-8 w/loss not to NYG 11% if 9-8 w/loss to NYG 4% if 8-9 w/neither loss to NYG https://t.co/qUMVWewYEn — Deniz Selman (@denizselman33) November 27, 2026 We’ve known for more than a month that this was a lost season. When Jalen Hurts was lost for the year with blood clots, Lane Johnson retired, half the team got injured and the front office traded away Cam Jurgens and Jordan Davis, it became obvious the franchise was punting on 2026 and looking to the future. After winning their second Super Bowl two years ago and reaching the postseason five straight seasons under Nick Sirianni, that’s OK. Lost seasons happen. Not every season has to be about winning the Super Bowl. I know that’s easier to say as fans of a franchise that now has two of them in the last decade, but it’s the truth. Fans of prior generations who had to live through not just lost seasons, but lost decades, had to learn how to unearth greatness while trudging through the muck of a depressing campaign. The Eagles’ scintillating victory over the Cowboys yesterday was just such a moment. It probably won’t result in the team making the playoffs, but it is a victory that will be remembered by every fan of this team for the rest of their lives. Their rally from 21 points down is the largest deficit overcome in NFL history on Thanksgiving, and they did it against their most hated rival, in their building. They did it with incredible plays from the unlikeliest, and likeliest, corners of the roster. Consider Joe Milton, III, the Eagles’ fourth quarterback of the season, who began 2026 as Dallas’ third-stringer and was signed by Howie Roseman off their practice squad back in October. After being thrust into the starting job following Tanner McKee’s struggles as the back-up, Milton has thrived in the team’s two games after the bye. On Thursday afternoon in Dallas, he was electric. Every time Joe Milton made the craziest throw of the year vs the Cowboys 5 different times. pic.twitter.com/lVuL46DCmH — Cam (@42Cyc) November 27, 2026 Milton finished 21-of-31 passing for 331 yards, 3 TDs, one interception, and one rushing score on a 15 yard scramble to the end zone. He’s making quite a case to be considered the team’s back-up QB once Hurts is back next year. His favorite target on the day, DeVonta Smith, had the game of his life. Connecting on multiple deep hook-ups against an awful Dallas secondary, Smith caught 11 balls on 14 targets for a career-high 200 yards and two TDs. It’s unclear if he’ll be available for the Eagles’ next game in Arizona after being landing hard on his tailbone late in the 4th quarter of the Birds’ comeback, but his efforts on Thursday were nothing short of heroic. DeVonta Smith has only played six games this year (3 with Hurts, 1 with McKee, 2 with Milton) and is on 17-game pace of: 190 targets 119 receptions 1,560 yards 11 TDs Only three WRs have more PPR PPG than him this season: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Puka Nacua, and CeeDee Lamb. As a… pic.twitter.com/0kT29ne211 — Addison Hayes (@AddisonHayes_) November 27, 2026 Ty Robinson, a name no one could have been expected to utter much heading into the game, was responsible for two of the afternoon’s biggest plays. Trailing 31-17 early in the 4th quarter, Robinson’s blocked punt allowed Kenny Moore to pick the ball up inside the five yard line and waltz into the end zone for a momentum-shifting score. Ty Robinson blocked it, Kenny Moore II recovered it. One-score game 🦅 PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2eHqQp1ujh — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 And then, with less than a minute to play and Dallas going for a game-sealing 4th-and-1 conversion, Robinson (with the help of Quinyon Mitchell’s terrific defense on Cee Dee Lamb denying a slant pattern that was Dak Prescott’s first option) sacked Prescott at midfield to put the Eagles a mere 10 yards out of field goal range. EAGLES SACK DAK ON 4TH DOWN PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/HUyLQrz2c5 — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 Robinson finished with three QB pressures, two hurries, the aforementioned sack and blocked punt. The trade of Jordan Davis earlier this month has allowed Robinson to get more playing time, and he’s taking advantage of it. And how about Jake Elliott? After struggling over the last two seasons, especially from long distance (5-for-15 from beyond 50 yards), he has suddenly re-discovered his deep stroke and is enjoying a late-career renaissance. Overall, he’s 13-for-14 this season, including a perfect 5-for-5 from beyond 50. If you haven’t heard the Dallas radio call of Elliott’s 60-yarder yesterday, as well as the final two seconds of the game, enjoy this. How Jake Elliott's eventual 60-yard game-winning FG and the last :02 of the game sounded on Cowboys radio pic.twitter.com/MYHcpA4mKR — Nick Piccone (@_piccone) November 27, 2026 There were other performances worth remembering, too. Will Shipley stepped up and rushed for 46 yards on 10 carries after Saquon Barkley left the game with a stinger. Makai Lemon hauled in five balls for 51 yards, including a terrific 24-yard touchdown catch in the 4th quarter. Elijah Moore caught three balls for 57 yards. Jeremiah Trotter, Jr. led all players with 12 tackles (no other player on either team had more than nine, Byron Young). And Braden Mann continued pounding punts into the stratosphere, consistently helping the Eagles with field position whenever possible. And kudos must be given to the much-maligned head coach and offensive coordinator. After failing to score more than 24 points in a single game this year, the offense put up 22 in the 4th quarter alone and 39 overall. Yes, it was against a porous Dallas defense, but we’ve seen Sean Mannion’s offense struggle against the worst defenses in the league, including this very same Cowboys squad in late October when they lost 38-21 at the Linc. I didn’t love Sirianni’s histrionics after the game. Stop jawing with fans, get yourself under control, and go give the opposing head coach a proper post-game handshake. Also, the decision to go for two points after drawing to 38-30 made no sense to me, either. But all that being said, Sirianni’s players never folded the tents after getting behind 31-10 in the second half, and credit must be giving to the head coach for that. Eagles fans haven’t had to deal with many lost seasons over the last quarter century. Thankfully, we’re not used to this. So it’s easy to forget that, even in a season where nothing has gone your way, a legendary moment can be birthed from its ashes. Sometimes, sports is just about moments and memories. And while there likely won’t be a banner raised at Lincoln Financial Field at the beginning of next year, The Joe Milton Thanksgiving Game of 2026 will be remembered as an Eagles classic forever. And that is something to be thankful for.
author: John Stolnis

title: 10 Eagles things I think I think after incredible comeback vs. Cowboys
summary: Incredible. There’s no other way to describe the Philadelphia Eagles’ comeback victory over the Dallas Cowboys — which was way more enjoyable than any meal you could consume on Thanksgiving. This is an Eagles game that’s going to be remembered forever, just like the Christmas Day win over the Cowboys in 2006 and the Miracle […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 26: Joe Milton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles walks off the field with the Madden Thanksgiving MVP trophy after an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Incredible. There’s no other way to describe the Philadelphia Eagles’ comeback victory over the Dallas Cowboys — which was way more enjoyable than any meal you could consume on Thanksgiving. This is an Eagles game that’s going to be remembered forever, just like the Christmas Day win over the Cowboys in 2006 and the Miracle at the Meadowlands comeback in 2010. The victory is that improbable, especially when the Eagles were down 31-10 with 3:35 left in the third quarter. They had no business being in this game, yet they found their way back to make it a game — and stole a victory away from the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. This was a game the Cowboys should have won handily. Instead they choked it away, thanks to the hands of a resilient Eagles team that didn’t let their 3-7 record stand in the way of what seemed to be an insurmountable deficit. No matter how the rest of this season goes, that was one heck of a win. This victory will be talked about amongst generations of Eagles fans. A Thanksgiving miracle — that may have ended the Cowboys season. The Eagles are good at ruining seasons all of a sudden. 1. What else can you say about Joe Milton? Milton delivered one of the greatest performances my a quarterback in Eagles history. What Milton did against the Cowboys was absolutely incredible, and this was more than a quarterback showing off his ridiculous arm talent. The final stat line: 21-of-31, 311 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT, 10.7 YPA — 121.8 rating. 3 carries, 15 yards, TD. There are only two quarterbacks in Eagles history with 300+ passing yards, 3+ passing TD, 1+ rushing TD, and average 10+ YPA in a game — Milton and Michael Vick (2010 at Commanders). That’s how well Milton played on Thanksgiving — in just his third career start. Once the Eagles trailed 31-10, Milton went 11-of-16 for 181 yards with 2 TD, 1 INT and a 120.1 rating (averaging 11.3 YPA). He also had 15 yards and a rushing touchdown in that stretch to bring the Eagles back from three scores. This level of play was throughout the game. Milton used his arm strength to keep the Eagles offense moving, going 11-of-19 for 278 yards with 3 TD, 1 INT and 14.6 YPA on throws that traveled 10+ air yards — finishing with a 120.1 passer rating. He was 2-of-6 for 95 yards and 2 TD with 0 INT for a 121.5 passer rating on throws that traveled 25+ air yards. Any completion on passes that traveled 25+ air yards was a touchdown. The Eagles had some exciting performances from Jalen Hurts over the years, but that was arguably the most exciting passing performance by a quarterback since Nick Foles threw for 471 yards against the Houston Texans in 2018 (and that was an Eagles’ win too). Impressive performance by Milton, finally giving life to an Eagles offense that badly needed it. 2. The most impressive feat of Joe Milton’s day? Milton had a touchdown pass that traveled 64.4 yards in air distance, and that wasn’t the most impressive aspect of his performance. He threw an interception into triple coverage with 7:14 to play when the Eagles were trailing 38-3, which seemed to be the backbreaker with how the defense was playing. The Eagles got the ball back and Milton goes 4-of-4 for 70 yards and a 24-yard touchdown to Makai lemon on the ensuing drive — netting a perfect 158.3 passer rating. The poise and ability to forget that interception immediately following the interception spoke more volumes about who Milton is as a player than anything else he accomplished on Thanksgiving. When Milton made a boneheaded play, he responded in the way winning quarterbacks respond. He hasn’t even been on his team for two months and was able to shake that play off and perform at an even higher level. Since the interception, Milton finished 6-of-9 for 84 yards with a touchdown and a 133.6 passer rating. He led the Eagles to victory with a touchdown drive and set Jake Elliott up with his game-winning field goal. Want to know how to stick around as a starting quarterback in the NFL? Moments like that. 3. Joe Milton might have locked up QB2 One of the few things I wanted to see in the remainder of the season was if Milton could play well enough to be the QB2 next year. Judging Milton through two starts was tough, given the state of the offense and the changes the Eagles were making to accomondate his game. Milton didn’t get to throw the deep ball much, and he missed when he had his opportunity last week to DeVonta Smith. He didn’t miss any of those opportunities on Thanksgiving, hitting two of them for 95 yards and two touchdowns. On throws that traveled 20+ air yards, Milton went 6-of-11 for 188 yards and 3 TD with 0 INT — a 139.2 passer rating. The arm strength was clearly on display, along with the accuracy on the deep ball. Milton was relentless facing pressure too, finishing 7-of-10 for 154 yards with 3 TD and 0 INT for a 152.1 passer rating — while also being sacked five times. He was 6-of-8 for 145 yards with 3 TD and 0 INT on throws from outside the pocket — 156.3 rating. Backup quarterbacks don’t have games like this. QB5’s — which is what Milton was when he signed — really don’t have games like this. This performance may have locked up QB2 for Milton next year. If Milton can stack up good-to-solid performances, he’ll be the QB2 on the Eagles (at least). Milton may get a starting opportunity elsewhere too (he is a restricted free agent), but the Eagles can control his fate there as well. The situation needs to play itself out, but Milton is certainly on the radar around the league. He’s earned it. 4. That victory had to be bittersweet for Joe Milton When Milton was making incredible throws against the Cowboys, I couldn’t help but think of his journey to get to this point. Over the last four months, Milton was cut by the Cowboys after losing the QB2 job to Sam Howell —toiling on the practice squad for five weeks. Any team could have claimed Milton when he was waived, and no team did. Any team could have signed Milton from the Cowboys practice squad to the active roster, and no one did. The Eagles signed Milton to the active roster when Jalen Hurts was lost for the season due to blood clots in his lungs. If Hurts wasn’t done for the year, the Eagles wouldn’t have brought in Milton. He literally was their QB5, the fifth quarterback to make the active roster. Tanner McKee got three starts before the Eagles turned to Milton, Andy Dalton told the Eagles he had a better opportunity with the Atlanta Falcons. Milton wasn’t considered by the Cowboys and 31 other teams until the Eagles needed a quarterback. To have a performance like that against a team that cut him and chose Sam Howell over him had to be bittersweet — especially since he led the Eagles to a 21-point comeback on the road against that team on Thanksgiving in just his third start. Certainly Milton will soak that all in at some point, but the battle to succeed and have a moment like that are why sports are so great. Even when Milton was counted out, he wasn’t. 5. Legendary performance from DeVonta Smith There were questions whether DeVonta Smith was a WR1 earlier this season. There shouldn’t be any following Thanksgiving. Smith finished with 11 catches for 200 yards and two touchdowns in the win over the Cowboys, the first Eagles’ player to get 200+ receiving yards in a game since DeSean Jackson in 2010. He had the most receiving yards on Thanksgiving since 1945 — and the second-most by any player on the holiday in NFL history. Smith had two touchdown catches of 45+ yards, the first player to do that on Thanksgiving since Randy Moss in 1998. He had more receiving yards on Thanksgiving (200) than A.J. Brown has the whole season (128). How good was the Milton-Smith connection? Milton…
