title: What was going on with the heated Nick Sirianni-Will Shipley exchange during Eagles-Cowboys?
summary: Last week, there was fiery exchange between coaches on the Eagles sideline, and on Thursday against the Cowboys, there was a heated moment caught on camera between head coach Nick Sirianni and RB Will Shipley. The coach and player were seen yelling back and forth after the Eagles failed to convert on fourth down after […]
full_text: Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images | Getty Images Last week, there was fiery exchange between coaches on the Eagles sideline , and on Thursday against the Cowboys, there was a heated moment caught on camera between head coach Nick Sirianni and RB Will Shipley. The coach and player were seen yelling back and forth after the Eagles failed to convert on fourth down after choosing to hand the ball to Saquon Barkley instead of calling a QB sneak. Nick Sirianni And Will Shipley Getting Heated On The Sideline. Saquon Barkley Was Part Of This One Too. Not Exactly A Peaceful Thanksgiving In Philly. Something Clearly Has Them All Fired Up. pic.twitter.com/pCzsNMqcnz — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 26, 2026 Sirianni wasn’t asked about the situation during his post-game press conference, but has likened similar moments to two guys being passionate about the game. These things do happen, but it’s still notable considering suggestions that the head coaches job is on the line this season — there’s been little to suggest that this is true from the organization’s perspective, but the rumors won’t subside as the team claws back from a 2-7 start to the year. As for Shipley, after the game, he chalked it up to any other disagreement that families have on Thanksgiving, but said it will all just make them closer. “I got so much love for Coach Nick and as the leader of this football team. Emotions were running high and there was no love lost…We got after it for a little bit, but it’s just going to allow our relationship to continue to grow. With that being said, I love him to death.” Still, Shipley wouldn’t get into exactly what the conversation was about. Regardless, the RB ended up getting a majority of the carries the rest of the game as Saquon Barkley was sidelined with a stinger, and there didn’t seem to be any lingering negativity to worry about.
author: Alexis Chassen

title: DeVonta Smith’s performance in the Eagles’ win over the Cowboys was heroic
summary: The Eagles WR1 gave everything he had on Thanksgiving against the Cowboys, and late in what would become a career-high game, DeVonta Smith went down hard on his tailbone and stayed on the ground well after the play ended. He rolled over to his front while gesturing toward his back, but despite being looked at […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles WR1 gave everything he had on Thanksgiving against the Cowboys, and late in what would become a career-high game, DeVonta Smith went down hard on his tailbone and stayed on the ground well after the play ended. He rolled over to his front while gesturing toward his back, but despite being looked at by trainers, he was able to return to finish the game. Smith ended the holiday matchup against the Eagles rival with 11 catches for 200 yards, both career-high numbers, and two touchdowns. As he celebrated the team’s miraculous 39-38 comeback win, even FOX’s Erin Andrews addressed how much Smitty needed to get back to the locker room to treat his back pain. The WR quipped that it’s easier to deal with knowing the result was a win, but PhillyVoice’s Jimmy Kempski noted that Smith could barely walk an hour after the game ended. DeVonta Smith can barely walk, barely move. It’s remarkable that he was able to finish the game. — Jimmy Kempski (@JimmyKempski) November 27, 2026 Thankfully, the Eagles will now get a bit of a mini-bye after a four-day short week ahead of the Thanksgiving game. With some additional days of rest, hopefully Smith is able to get some pain relief in his back and isn’t out long term. For as bad as this 4-7 has been for the Birds, it does feel like the momentum is shifting, and Smith being on the field has a lot to do with that.
author: Alexis Chassen

title: Eagles vs. Cowboys Thanksgiving: The good, the bad, and the ugly
summary: Nick Sirianni had to be redirected away from the stands more than a few times by the Eagles’ media relations team at AT&T Stadium. He tried to high five everyone wearing midnight green Thursday afternoon. The Eagles were dead two times, three times, 10 times, it seemed, and they managed to stage the largest Thanksgiving […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS- NOVEMBER 26: Joe Milton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates after an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Nick Sirianni had to be redirected away from the stands more than a few times by the Eagles’ media relations team at AT&T Stadium. He tried to high five everyone wearing midnight green Thursday afternoon. The Eagles were dead two times, three times, 10 times, it seemed, and they managed to stage the largest Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history, overcoming a 21-point deficit (31–10) to beat the Dallas Cowboys, 39-38, in one of the most improbable victories in Eagles’ memory. It sets the Eagles up to now become NFC East contenders, considered where the Eagles were two weeks ago. Credit has to go to Sirianni. The Eagles never gave up. They were banged up, without Cooper DeJean, Dallas Goedert, and Saquon Barkley, and instead relied on Ty Robinson’s blocked punt, and pivotal nine-yard sack that turned the ball over and set up Jake Elliott’s game-winning 59-yard field goal with 2 seconds left. But the game belonged to Joe Milton . The pickup from the Cowboys’ practice squad hauled the Eagles from a 31-10 deficit to complete 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards and three touchdowns being named MVP of the game. DeVonta Smith was amazing in a career-high game, catching a career-high 11 passes for a career-high 200 yards on 14 targets. It is a signature victory in Sirianni’s six years. The Eagles are now 4-7 with the lowly Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts next, two teams with a combined 6-16 record, which could bring the Eagles to 6-7 with Seattle coming to Lincoln Financial Field on Dec. 19. The Eagles are still at the bottom of the NFC East, but in a position to push the 6-3-1 New York Giants, and the 4-5-1 Washington Commanders for supremacy in the division. The Eagles’ 20 fourth-quarter points exceeded the 17-points per game the Eagles were averaging this season. The Eagles continued playing hard for Sirianni. He still made dubious choices, like the decision to go for a two-point conversion after Milton’s 15-yard TD run with 9:09 left to play, and the Eagles trailing 38-30. It does not matter now—the Eagles won. The Eagles were down at one point 31-10 with 3:35 left in the third quarter, then proceeded to score on four of their next five drives. There was a lot of good, some bad and some ugly in the Eagles’ 39-38 win over the Dallas Cowboys. The Good Joe Milton exploding on national TV—and causing Tom Brady’s head to explode—in completing 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards and three touchdowns. He just had a habit of coming up in clutch situations to make big plays. He probably made himself a pile of money from some NFL team, too, whether the Eagles are in his future or somewhere else. Wherever he goes, no Eagles’ fan will forget what he did on Thanksgiving Day 2026 against the Dallas Cowboys, bringing a dead team back to life. Ty Robinson’s blocked punt and Kenny Moore’s 3-yard scoop and score suddenly made what looked like a blowout into a game. Robinson came slicing through the line and dove at Dallas punter Bryan Anger to catch the punt with his right hand, and Moore ran after the loose ball and gathered it in for a three-yard score. Robinson later came up with a huge nine-yard sack at the Eagles’ 48 with 55 seconds left, setting up the Elliott game-winner. Jake Elliott coming through big again. He was 2-for-2 on a 48- and 59-yard game-winning field goal. This came after Elliott went 4-for-4 the previous week against Pittsburgh with field goals of 41, 29, 53 and 55 yards. Elliott is 13 of 14 on field goal attempts, and 21 of 21 on extra points—including 5-for-5 on field goals attempts of 50 yards or more. Sirianni is going to have to think more of Elliott kicking field goals instead of trying to go for it on fourth down. What sometimes gets lost is Elliott is a two-time Super Bowl champion who has made huge field goals in huge games. DeVonta Smith seemed to be the only weapon the Eagles had, and despite added attention, he caught a game-high 11 passes for a game-high 200 yards on 14 targets, including 50- and 45-yard touchdown catches. It was Smith’s 45-yard TD catch with 15 seconds left in the third quarter that continued to make the game intriguing pulling the Eagles within 31-17. Milton’s 50-yard rainbow to DeVonta Smith for the Eagles’ only touchdown in the first half. Milton was about the only thing the Eagles had going in the first half. Otherwise, it was bad. Two of Milton’s first three passes converted third downs. They were the first two good signs the Eagles might be able to move the ball against the NFL’s 31st defense. Milton’s first completion was a nine-yard completion to Dallas Goedert on a second-and-eight to the Eagles’ 17. Three plays later. Milton connected with Smith for a 16-yard reception to the Eagles’ 35. Of course, the Eagles blew it by going for it on fourth-and-one at the Dallas 37. Money on third down. Milton completed eight of his first 11 passes, three of which came on third down. On the Eagles’ first drive, he hit Smith for 16 yards on a third-and-8, and on third drive, he hit Makai Lemon for 20-yard pass on a third-and-12 to the Dallas 34. It led to Elliott’s 48-yard field goal. Byron Young with nine tackles from the defensive tackle position. He had five solo tackles, assisting on four. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. continues to lead the defense. Every time the linebacker out of St, Joe’s Prep and Clemson has started this season, he has led the Eagles in tackles. Thanksgiving against Dallas was no different, with a game-high 12 tackles, seven solo, with a sack and two tackles for loss. Trotter is now second on the Eagles in tackles with 64 tackles, although has a team-high 41 solo tackles. The Bad Cobie Durant’s interception with 7:05 to play seemed to seal the victory for the Cowboys after the Eagles’ fourth stop of the game. Brandon Aubrey missed a gimme 40-yard field goal attempt bailed out the Eagles. The Eagles losing Cooper DeJean, Saquon Barkley and Dallas Goedert to injury in the first quarter. Not that it mattered. The Ugly Cornerback Quinyon Mitchell flagged with pass interference on the very first play of the game. The 17-yard call took the ball from the Dallas 23 to the Cowboys’ 40 and jumpstarted one of the NFL’s most potent offenses. Mitchell was called for two pass interferences penalties for a total of 46 yards. It was not a good game for Mitchell, who was later burned for a 39-yard completion on a second-and-16 right after the Eagles’ blocked punt score. The quick euphoria the Eagles had after the blocked punt was quickly zapped on a Dak Prescott 14-yard touchdown scramble with 10:11 to play. The Eagles first half. Everyone may have given up by then and began eating their Thanksgiving Day dinner. The Cowboys scored on four of their first five drives. They had outgained the Eagles, 245 to 169, had 17 first downs to the Eagles’ eight, and the Eagles committed penalties for 71 yards, including Quinyon Mitchell’s second interference call for 29 yards, and Riq Woolen’s 10-yard interference call leading to the Cowboys’ last touchdown in the first half. The Cowboys converted 6 of 7 third downs to the Eagles’ 2 of 5. With 5:09 left in the first half, the Cowboys scored on three of their four possessions, had amassed 208 total yards of offense, averaging 8.3 yards a play, 12.9 yards a pass and 5.3 yards a rush. Zak Prescott was 6 of 10 for 129 yards and a touchdown. Dak Prescott’s 31-yard touchdown pass to Kavontae Turpin for a Cowboys’ 14-0 lead with 36 seconds left in the first quarter. It looked like the route was on. The Cowboys’ second drive. This time,the Cowboys needed just five plays to score. But they came up with a big third-down play again, this time, on a third-and-16, when Prescott hit George Pickens for a 36-yard completion to the Eagles’ 33. Riq Woolen made…
author: Joseph Santoliquito

title: Eagles-Cowboys final score: Joe Milton leads comeback victory over Dallas!
summary: HAPPY THANKSGIVING, PHILADELPHIA EAGLES FANS! The Eagles are 4-7 after beating the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday. Final score: 39 to 38. HAHAHAHAHAHAHA. Man, I can’t believe the Eagles won that game! The Birds were looking left for dead after going down 31 to 10 with about three minutes remaining in the third quarter. Their defense […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS- NOVEMBER 26: Joe Milton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles throws a pass during second half of an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images HAPPY THANKSGIVING, PHILADELPHIA EAGLES FANS! The Eagles are 4-7 after beating the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday. Final score: 39 to 38. HAHAHAHAHAHAHA. Man, I can’t believe the Eagles won that game! The Birds were looking left for dead after going down 31 to 10 with about three minutes remaining in the third quarter. Their defense was getting carved up by the Cowboys’ high-powered offense. But Joe Milton never said die! The Eagles’ quarterback led his new team to a winning effort against his former team, ultimately finishing 21/31 for 331 yards, three touchdowns, one interception, and a 121.8 passer rating. A lot of that production came through DeVonta Smith, who had 11 catches for 200 yards (!) and two touchdowns. Ty Robinson, who blocked a punt to create an Eagles touchdown earlier in the game, came through with a much-needed fourth down sack that ultimately set up a game-winning Jake Elliott field goal! WHAT A WIN! And suddenly the Eagles’ season is not totally dead?! Could they actually win the NFC East?! Probably not … but they weren’t supposed to win this game, either! Next up for the Eagles: a road game against the Arizona Cardinals, which the Eagles will probably be favored in! Read on for a recap and stay tuned for BGN’s postgame coverage. FIRST QUARTER The Eagles won the coin toss and elected to defer, per usual. The Cowboys took over at their own 23-yard line and Quinyon Mitchell was flagged for pass interference on the first snap from scrimmage. Tacky call on Q going up against George Pickens, who was also pretty handsy on that play. Facing 3rd-and-3, a quick dump off to Javonte Williams resulted in a first down. Cooper DeJean was hurt after tackling Williams. The Cowboys picked up another first down into field goal range with Andrew Mukuba missing a tackle in the hole. Facing 3rd-and-8, Dak Prescott’s first down scramble was called back by Jonathan Greenard drawing a holding penalty on Terence Steele. Facing 3rd-and-18, Prescott hit CeeDee Lamb wiiiiide open in the middle of the field for an easy first down at the seven-yard line. Great resistance there. Not! Jihaad Campbell seemed to get lost in coverage. The Cowboys then went with three straight runs to reach the end zone. 11 plays, 77 yards, 6:10 off the clock. EAGLES 0, COWBOYS 7. The Eagles started at their own 6-yard line after Britain Covey mishandled Brandon Aubrey’s bouncing kickoff. The Eagles picked up their first first down with a Joe Milton completion to Dallas Goedert. Facing 3rd-and-7 after a blitz forced a Milton incompletion, Milton ripped a nice ball to DeVonta Smith for another first down. A Cowboys player signaled incomplete, though, and Brian Schottenheimer threw his red flag to challenge the play. After commercial, it was announced that the Cowboys did not challenge in time before the Eagles got a play off. I don’t know if the review would have been conclusive enough to overturn the ruling on the field anyway. Milton hit Elijah Moore (!) in rhythm for a 25-yard completion to put the offense past midfield. Milton balling early! Facing 3rd-and-6 after two Saquon Barkley runs, Milton hit DeVonta just shy of the sticks. Facing 4th-and-short, the Eagles seemed like they might go Brotherly Shove but they instead tried a fullback dive with Barkley and it was stopped for a loss. The decision to go for it was correct. Overthought it on the play call. Just use the tush push. Disappointing end to an otherwise encouraging 11-play, 57-yard drive. The Cowboys took over at their own 37-yard line. Prescott’s deep shot to Pickens with Riq Woolen trailing bounced off of the receiver for an incompletion. Fortunate break for the Eagles’ defense. Facing 3rd-and-6, Prescott took off running for a first down but it was wiped out by another holding penalty on Javonte Williams grabbing Marcus Epps. Facing 3rd-and-16, Prescott hit Pickens for a contested grab against Woolen. Another favorable opportunity for the defense to get off the field and they just can’t do it. One play later, Prescott hit KaVontae Turpin for a 31-yard catch-and-run touchdown. Too easy. Meanwhile, Nick Sirianni was shown arguing with Will Shipley on the sideline. OK, then. EAGLES 0, COWBOYS 14. KAVONTAE TURPIN IS TOO FAST PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0MqBAQPtHh — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 Nick Sirianni And Will Shipley Getting Heated On The Sideline. Saquon Barkley Was Part Of This One Too. Not Exactly A Peaceful Thanksgiving In Philly. Something Clearly Has Them All Fired Up. pic.twitter.com/pCzsNMqcnz — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 26, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 15-yard line. Milton hit Zach Ertz (!) for a catch that got wiped out with the Eagles accepting a Cowboys illegal contact penalty to end the first quarter. SECOND QUARTER Facing 3rd-and-5, Milton ran out of bounds for no gain. Three-and-out. Honestly, should’ve gone for it there, even though it was on the Eagles’ own 25-yard line. The Cowboys over at their own 35-yard line after a 24-yard punt return by Turpin. Facing 3rd-and-5 after Jihaad Campbell had good coverage on Lamb (!), Prescott hit Turpin to beat an Eagles blitz for a first down. Turpin bobbled the ball, though, and Sirianni threw his red flag to challenge the play. After review, the call was overturned and the Cowboys had to punt. Hey, a stop! If only barely. The Eagles took over at their own 18-yard line. DeVonta made a nice leaping catch against tight coverage from the Cowboys for 24 yards and a first down near midfield. Facing 3rd-and-12 after Markel Bell had a real rough rep to allow a Rashan Gary sack, Milton rolled right and hit a wide open Lemon for a first down! Milton got the juice?! Facing 3rd-and-6, Milton was blitzed and threw behind DeVonta for an incompletion. Jake Elliott came in for the 48-yard field goal make. I would’ve gone for it there, you’re not beating the Cowboys by kicking FGs. But not a bad nine-play, 52-yard drive. EAGLES 3, COWBOYS 14. The Cowboys took over at their own 40-yard line after their special teams made a smart play to draw an Eagles penalty. They picked up a first down with two runs, with Mukuba getting blocked out of the play on one. The Cowboys quickly moved into field goal range. And then into the red zone. Williams then went 12 yards easily up the gut for a touchdown. Zero resistance. EAGLES 3, COWBOYS 21. TD, Cowboys. They take a 21-3 lead. This is the second-most points the Eagles have allowed in a 1st half since Vic Fangio became the defensive coordinator. You have to go back to W4 of the 2024 season vs. TB for the last time a team scored more. That was 24 points. — Zach Berman (@ZBerm) November 26, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 30-yard line. Ertz drew a pass interference penalty to give the Eagles a first down. Milton roll left and unleashed a rocket down the field to DeVonta for a 50-yard touchdown! Hell yeah! That was fun. JOE MILTON GOES DEEP TO DEVONTA SMITH PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ZcKIPvq6jS — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 JOE MILTON'S ARM TALENT IS RIDICULOUS 🎯 PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2MLAir7i29 — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 That Joe Milton TD throw traveled 64.4 yards in air distance, according to NextGen. It’s the longest TD throw by an Eagles QB since stat began being tracked in 2016. — Tim McManus (@Tim_McManus) November 26, 2026 The Cowboys took over at their own 29-yard line after a nice special teams tackle by Darius Cooper. Facing 3rd-and-inches, Williams got enough on a first down run to then bleed the clock the two-minute warning. Q got flagged for illegal contact to allow another first down. Then Prescott hit Pickens for yet…

title: Eagles vs. Cowboys Thanksgiving game live chat
summary: Happy Thanksgiving! The Philadelphia Eagles are back on the road Thursday for a Thanksgiving Day game against the Dallas Cowboys. title: Steelers vs. Broncos Week 12 picks
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming off the one of the most embarrassing weeks in franchise history. But, the NFL season stops for no one, as Pittsburgh will host the Denver Broncos. The Steelers have yet to lose a home game this season, while the Broncos have won six straight. Who will come out on top? […]
full_text: (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming off the one of the most embarrassing weeks in franchise history. But, the NFL season stops for no one, as Pittsburgh will host the Denver Broncos. The Steelers have yet to lose a home game this season, while the Broncos have won six straight. Who will come out on top? Our staff weighs in. Mike Nicastro : Sometimes, a quarterback change can provide a spark that a team desperately needs. I think Rudolph will embrace the opportunity, play with confidence and give his teammates something to rally behind. I don’t expect it to be pretty, and I certainly don’t think many people will see this result coming. But I have a feeling this Steelers team will come together when it matters most. Steelers 23, Broncos 20. Ryan Parish: Hard to believe the team will be focused and prepared with all of the dramatics of the last few days. Then of course, they haven’t looked prepared on gamedays the past few weeks. It’s too bad, Denver seems like a winnable game, and there is talent on this team despite recent performances. For head coach Mike McCarthy’s sake, he’d better hope the Steelers rally together and show a spark. The Rooneys are a patient family, and they seem to be supporting the coach publicly so far, but if this season falls into complete disarray and McCarthy loses the locker room, his time on the job might be shorter than we could have imagined. I have a hard time being optimistic about this week. Broncos 23, Steelers 16 . Ryland Bickley : Denver is a good but not elite team, and if this was a normal season for the Steelers, I’d think they’d have a good chance at winning this one in Pittsburgh. But on a short week, after two demoralizing losses, and following Aaron Rodgers’ highly-publicized, dramatic exit, it’s hard to be optimistic about the Steelers’ chances against the 8-2 Broncos. Even if the team is more focused on the game than we expect, suddenly losing a starting quarterback just two days before a game would make any team’s game preparation chaotic. Pittsburgh isn’t helpless in this one, but the Denver defense is a tough opponent and Sean Payton should have some success scheming against the Steelers’ defense on the other side of the ball. Broncos 30, Steelers 20. Joey Bray : After one of the most unbelievable weeks in franchise history, the Pittsburgh Steelers have the tall task of taking on the AFC West-leading Broncos on Black Friday. I have a bad feeling that all of this off the field banter will leak onto the field. Consider me a skeptic of the idea that Mason Rudolph can provide this major spark to the offense that Mike McCarthy is hoping he can provide. Sure, Rudolph will probably be more open to play action and be able to move a bit better, but this is a team that has problems offensively well beyond that in their struggling running game. The Steelers defense will probably look about the same, but the strong rushing attack of Denver will eventually wear them down as their offense will once again struggle to find consistency. I’ll take the Broncos to dominate a game that will have many questioning the direction of the Steelers franchise. Broncos 28, Steelers 6. Jarrett Bailey: The Steelers are going to win. Because they have to. After spending all week as the laughing stock of the NFL and being ridiculed, their terrific defense keeps the Broncos’ offense from scoring more than one touchdown, and they eek out a low-scoring win under the leadership of Mason Rudolph at quarterback. title: Mike Tomlin calls Steelers a ‘dumpster fire’ after Aaron Rodgers release
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have been in the headlines for all of the wrong reasons this week ahead of their Black Friday showdown with the Denver Broncos. Late Tuesday night, Aaron Rodgers was benched, which led to him going on the Pat McAfee Show and going scorched earth, making some wild accusations against Steelers head coach […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have been in the headlines for all of the wrong reasons this week ahead of their Black Friday showdown with the Denver Broncos. Late Tuesday night, Aaron Rodgers was benched, which led to him going on the Pat McAfee Show and going scorched earth, making some wild accusations against Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy. Rodgers was waived by Pittsburgh on Wednesday after his comments. During halftime of the Bills vs. Chiefs Thanksgiving Night game, longtime Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin sat down with NBC play-by-play broadcaster Mike Tirico to give his thoughts on the developing situation in Pittsburgh. When Tomlin was asked about the eomtions he was feeling seeing this happen to the team he coached for nearly two decades, he offered a simple but interesting response. “I’m upset about it,” Tomlin told Tirico. “You know, it’s a dumpster fire, and I don’t say that in a judgmental way. I’ve presided over a few dumps to fires in my 19 years. But, it certainly is upsetting, and I’m sure Steeler Nation is upset.” Although Tomlin made it clear his use of the words “dumpster fire” were not judgmental, it feels appropriate given the events of the last 48 hours. It feels like this situation is far from over. McCarthy and his team will have to look to quiet the noise after a tumultuous week to take on one of the AFC’s best in the Broncos. title: Mike Tomlin says Aaron Rodgers is beloved in Steelers locker room
summary: The last 48 hours have been some of the most insane in the history of the Pittsburgh Steelers. Just two weeks after defeating their division-rival Browns 27-6 to take sole possession of first place in the AFC North, the Steelers announced they were benching quarterback Aaron Rodgers. That announcement was followed by the quarterback making […]
full_text: (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The last 48 hours have been some of the most insane in the history of the Pittsburgh Steelers. Just two weeks after defeating their division-rival Browns 27-6 to take sole possession of first place in the AFC North, the Steelers announced they were benching quarterback Aaron Rodgers. That announcement was followed by the quarterback making an impromptu appearance on The Pat McAfee Show calling out head coach Mike McCarthy. This led to the Steelers releasing him. Speaking to Mike Tirico at halftime of Bills vs. Chiefs, former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin was asked about his firsthand experience coaching Rodgers and how the four-time MVP was perceived in the locker room. “He was beloved,” Tomlin said. “And I’m not over exaggerating that. He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steelers culture, to be engaged with teammates. And particularly from my perspective, I work with a lot of veteran players over the years, and at times, they lose a little patience for the process, or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, et cetera. He seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real natural way.” Tomlin and Rodgers’ relationship was highlighted by Rodgers as a reason he came to Pittsburgh in 2025. title: Steelers President Art Rooney expresses full confidence in Mike McCarthy
summary: Wednesday was one of the wildest days in the history of the Pittsburgh Steelers. After benching Aaron Rodgers late Tuesday night, the four-time MVP went on The Pat McAfee Show and aired out a lot of grievances largely pertaining to head coach Mike McCarthy. full_text: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Wednesday was one of the wildest days in the history of the Pittsburgh Steelers. After benching Aaron Rodgers late Tuesday night, the four-time MVP went on The Pat McAfee Show and aired out a lot of grievances largely pertaining to head coach Mike McCarthy. Among the issues Rodgers put on blast were McCarthy routinely falling asleep in meetings, being late for walkthroughs and meetings, not knowing the gameplay, and breaking down a team huddle vs. the Eagles by saying, “1-2-3 Packers.” Several insiders have noted that players have backed up these claims made by Rodgers, which led many to believe McCarthy’s days in Pittsburgh could and should be numbered. However, Team President Art Rooney II expressed faith in the Steelers’ head coach. “I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney said via Gerry Dulac . “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.” The Steeles will face the Broncos on Black Friday in their first home game since they defeated the Cleveland Browns 27-6 to secure a 6-2 record. Oh how much has changed since then. Let us know what you think in the comments . full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) Ahead of a must-win NFC West rematch, the Seattle Seahawks’ offense appears set to get their starting left tackle, Charles Cross, back. Cross has been out since the Week 7 game against the Kansas City Chiefs with an ankle injury, but was a full participant in practice on Thursday. Cross’ return could come at a crucial time as the Seahawks are already planning to be without star guard Quenton Nelson and starting right tackle Abe Lucas, both of whom did not practice on the holiday. Signs continue to trend positively for the return of Seahawks’ quarterback Sam Darnold, who was a full go in practice for the second day in a row. On the other side of the field, San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy did not practice with an ankle injury on Thursday, setting the table for a potential Mac Jones start on Sunday. Sticking with the offense, prolific wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba was once again limited in practice with an ankle injury. JSN has been the Seahawks’ entire offense, so even the potential of him missing this game is enough to give any Seahawks fan a miniature heart attack at minimum. Seahawks guard Anthony Bradford was also limited with a knee injury and an illness. Bradford has been battling injuries all season, but served in a key role of holding back disaster up front with Nelson out. Star linebacker Ernest Jones continued to be limited in practice with a knee injury, while edge rusher DeMarcus Lawrence was upgraded to limited, some welcome good news for the Seahawks front-7. The “Dark Side” defense will likely be without Jarran Reed, who missed practice for the second day in a row with a toe injury. title: The Seahawks have one weakness that the 49ers can exploit
summary: The San Francisco 49ers look to continue their quest for perfection in the NFC West with their home tilt against the Seattle Seahawks. The two met in October in a turnover-heavy game that ended 32-29 in Seattle. While both teams are dealing with ailing quarterbacks, it looks like Sam Darnold is on track to play […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers look to continue their quest for perfection in the NFC West with their home tilt against the Seattle Seahawks. The two met in October in a turnover-heavy game that ended 32-29 in Seattle. While both teams are dealing with ailing quarterbacks, it looks like Sam Darnold is on track to play on Sunday, while as of Thursday night, Brock Purdy’s status is unclear. While Mac Jones started eight games in 2025, none came against the Seahawks, and that defense is a tough draw for any backup quarterback. But as we wait to know if Purdy is good to go, these are the numbers to know for Sunday’s NFC West clash: 26.8 Pressure rate. The Seahawks offense has allowed a 26.8 pressure rate, the third-highest rate in the league (according to Pro Football Reference). The 49ers defensive line has been turning up the heat on opposing quarterbacks over the past few weeks, a welcome sight for a group that struggled for most of the first half of the season. After combining for 15 pressures against Atlanta and Las Vegas, the San Francisco front had 26 pressures against Dallas and 21 against Minnesota last week. And while those 47 pressures only translated to two sacks, Seattle doesn’t allow too much of that pressure to get to Sam Darnold. Seattle has allowed only 22 sacks this season (12th-fewest) and a 6.7 sack rate (14th-best); however, pressure might be enough against Darnold, who appears on track to play Sunday. When under pressure (according to Pro Football Focus), Darnold completes 37.2 percent of his passes with a pair of touchdowns to five interceptions, good for a passer rating of 34.4, 34th of 37 qualified passers this season. Darnold threw a pair of interceptions in Week 5 against 23 San Francisco pressures. Maybe the 49ers front can squeeze out a bit more production on Sunday to force another multi-turnover game from the Seattle quarterback. 4.5 Yards per pass attempt. The Seahawks defense allows 4.5 yards per pass attempt, the league’s best average. The 49ers offense is predicated on the run game staying ahead of the sticks, and using the pass game for the explosive plays. San Francisco’s 9.0 yards per pass attempt is the top in the league, and if that pace continues, it would become the 24th offense in NFL history (1920-present day, per Pro Football Reference) to average more than nine yards per attempt. But Seattle’s defense does not allow much in the passing game, allowing half of what the 49ers gain per pass attempt. Seattle has allowed more than 200 passing yards in only one game this season and has already held the 49ers to a season-low 175 passing yards in San Francisco’s Week 5 win. The Seattle pass defense will be tricky enough with a healthy Brock Purdy, but a less-than-healthy or even a Mac Jones spot start might prove to be too tough for the 49ers offense. 69.6 Red zone touchdown percentage. Seattle’s defense allows a touchdown on 69.6 percent of red zone chances, the fourth-highest rate in the league. Another week, another tough red zone defense for the 49ers offense to handle. Last week, it was a Minnesota team where it was tough to both enter the red zone and score from inside it. San Francisco went four-for-four from the final 20 yards against the feared Vikings defense. With Seattle, it might be tough to enter the red zone, but once in, the Seahawks are among the worst in the league at allowing red zone touchdowns. After the 49ers’ four red zone entries against the Vikings, Seattle jumped Minnesota into the top spot, tied with Pittsburgh with only 23 red zone attempts allowed this season. But where Seattle’s defense falls off is stopping the touchdown. While the 16 red zone touchdowns allowed is among the ten fewest in the league, 16 touchdowns on 23 entries comes out to 69.6 percent, placing the elite Seattle defense ahead of only Carolina, Washington, and Las Vegas. The 49ers offense went three-for-three against Seattle in Week 5, adding to their first-ranked 84.8 red zone touchdown percentage entering Week 11. The Seahawks might make life hell for the 49ers in the first 80 yards, but if San Francisco can get to the final 20, you have to like their chances to come out with six points.

full_text: The Daily Slop – 27 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders shift to Duo run scheme pays off vs Bengals They entered the year looking to become more of a zone run team and while they had a promising start, they soon had issues that took a while to figure out. But in the second half against the Giants, they found some success switching up the run scheme and using more duo runs instead of zone runs . Offensive coordinator David Blough took that success and leaned into it even further against the Bengals on Monday night. The Commanders ran almost exclusively duo schemes and variations of duo against the Bengals and had one of their best rushing performances of the season. Running backs Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Austin Ekeler had combined stats of 20 carries for 95 yards and a touchdown at an average of 4.75 yards per carry. There was a clear cohesive plan with the duo run schemes, with Blough mixing in a few different variations. The Commanders found some success shifting their base run scheme from zone to duo vs the Giants a few weeks ago. They continued that trend with even more success vs the Bengals. I broke down the layers of their duo run schemes: https://t.co/N9sfam01kd pic.twitter.com/LRvLxzi1AE — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) November 27, 2026 [ Note: The play discussed below is the same one embedded in the tweet above ] Patrick and Cosmi do a great job against Lawrence again here, Lawrence tries to get aggressive and split the double team, but almost jumps in the air trying to break through. Patrick makes initial contact and prevents Lawrence from breaking through but Cosmi comes in and supports him too. The pair of them effectively catch Lawrence in the air and are able to almost lift him and drive him backwards. Ekeler runs up the middle initially, following behind Chirs Paul and Brandon Coleman, who work a good double team on Jonathan Allen before Paul works up to the linebacker. I think Ekeler could have just hit this run right behind Paul the whole way, but he sees a potential lane behind Cosmi to cut into. He initially makes his cut before then deciding to hit the run inside behind Paul. He is a bit late to hit the hole but he gets in there and manages to pick up another seven yards before being brought down. It was a nice game plan from Blough, implementing a bunch of different variations of duo to keep the defense honest while still leaning into those strong double teams inside. Those double teams were very effective all game long, even against two premier defensive tackles in Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen. Full credit to Blough and the coaching staff for identifying duo as a scheme that might work better for them than zone and leaning all the way into it very quickly. It was impressive to see them layer in the different variations so quickly, though it helped that these were all schemes that this group ran last year under Kliff Kingsbury. Riggo’s Rag 7 unsung Commanders heroes who became impossible to ignore against Bengals Jacory Croskey-Merritt – Commanders RB The Washington Commanders received a boost before prime time [on Monday night] when running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt was activated after a spell on injured reserve. However, there were concerns about how much he could contribute after a month out of action. It was clear that the Commanders wanted to manage Croskey-Merritt’s reps, which was the correct call. Their struggling ground game needs him at the business end of the campaign, but the 2025 seventh-round pick looked pretty sharp under the national spotlight. Croskey-Merritt gave the Commanders’ ground game purpose and urgency it lacked in his absence. He was decisive, physical after contact, and elusive in tight windows. He also gave quarterback Jayden Daniels a useful pass-catching outlet out of the backfield, which the Bengals had to account for on every snap. Despite this being his first game back, Croskey-Merritt gained 77 yards from scrimmage — 54 rushing and 23 receiving — and scored on the ground. Considering it was his first game back in the lineup, these numbers give him a solid platform to build on over Washington’s remaining seven contests. And if Croskey-Merritt can pick up these numbers in the coming weeks, the Commanders will have a well-balanced offense for offensive coordinator David Blough to call as he sees fit. And if he hits, he can become the No. 1 receiver in 2027 with Terry McLaurin’s future in Washington uncertain. McLaurin tore the patellar tendon in his left knee in Week 6 and has a $34 million cap hit next season. Not only is his return date unknown, but so will be his ability to play at a certain level. That’s why they need to explore their options to find someone who can provide some help now but be a top option in 2027 and beyond. One team source said they know how hard it can be to find an elite receiver in free agency so they need to be creative, whether through trades, the draft or a signing like this one. If they’re fortunate, he can contribute down the stretch for a team that became more interesting after a 22-20 win over Cincinnati on Monday night. At 4-5-1 the Commanders can contend for a playoff spot over the final seven games; perhaps he can contribute at some point to help them achieve that goal. How does Aiyuk fit with the Commanders’ offense? Aiyuk has the route-running traits to play a productive role in coordinator David Blough’s system. With West Coast elements and reduced formations, Aiyuk will see targets on quicks and in-breakers, while Blough can set him up on play-action throws from Daniels. These are defined reads that create open voids in the coverage. Catch and go. Plus, with Aiyuk’s ability to shake press coverage and track the ball vertically, he would add a much-needed playmaking presence, generating matchups as a boundary X target, which complements the skill sets of Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams in the Commanders’ route tree. When Aiyuk is game-ready (conditioning, scheme), he can boost the Washington passing game. — Bowen Quinn said there’s no timetable for Aiyuk to play. He has to learn the terminology of the offense, get used to the route combinations and show that he’s in football shape. title: Washington Commanders vs Arizona Cardinals Week 12: Five Questions with Revenge of the Birds
summary: It’s week 12 of the NFL season and the 4-5-1 Washington Commanders will be facing a 3-8 Arizona Cardinals team on the road at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, AZ this coming Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET. The Cardinals are a team in transition; they only had a placeholder QB to start the season in […]
full_text: It’s week 12 of the NFL season and the 4-5-1 Washington Commanders will be facing a 3-8 Arizona Cardinals team on the road at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, AZ this coming Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET. The Cardinals are a team in transition; they only had a placeholder QB to start the season in Jacoby Brissett. They traded him away to the Ravens in week 9, backup QB Gardner Minshew sustained a season-ending injury after his first start, and now the Cardinals are deciding between rookie 3rd-round pick Carson Beck (who is injured) and recently-signed 40-year old journeyman Josh Johnson to lead the offense. The Cardinals are in their 4th year of GM Monti Ossenfort (formerly of the Titans) and 1st year of HC Mike LaFleur (formerly of the Rams, and younger brother of Packers’ HC Matt LaFleur). On offense, the Cardinals are coached by HC Mike LaFleur and OC Nathaniel Hackett, with LaFleur calling the plays. As a McVay disciple, LaFleur runs a McVay/Shanahan style offense that is built on formation shifts, pre-snap motion, and play-action passing to confuse opposing defenses. As part of this tree, the offense is built around an outside-zone run offense with pin-and-pull concepts designed to move defenders with angles and set up play-action and bootlegs. Arizona’s primary weapon in the passing game has been TE Trey McBride, who has 689 receiving yards on 87 receptions so far this year. Given how many receptions Washington seems to give up to TEs, this should be a matchup to watch. Overall, Arizona’s offense ranks 23rd in passing yards/game and 27th in rushing yards/game . Note that 3rd-overall pick in the 2026 draft Jeremiyah Love is still on injured reserve, which no doubt impacts the running game. On defense, the Cardinals had been led by DC Nick Rallis, a holdover from Jonathan Gannon’s coaching staff. However, Rallis was fired after giving up 34 points to the Chiefs. Teryl Austin, former DC of the Steelers, will be taking over as defensive playcaller and interim DC. It’s anyone’s guess what Austin’s defense will look like, but he is taking over a defense ranked 19th against the pass and 27th against the run . DE Josh Sweat has ranked 13th in the NFL in pass rush win rate and the Cardinals overall have been ranked 13th in pass rush win rate and 22nd in run stop win rate. I asked Seth Cox of Revenge of the Birds five questions about the state of the Cardinals and what to look for in this game. 1) The Cardinals have just fired DC Nick Rallis. What did you think of Rallis, how much of the problems on defense were due to him vs personnel, and what do you think will change with Teryl Austin replacing him? I think Rallis was terrible at his job and should have been fired with all of the Jonathan Gannon staff, but no one wanted this job. He had great ideas, but they are unable to execute them because of their talent, and that makes you bad at your job. If you are continually doing the square peg, round hole thing and continually terrible, that is on you to not make changes and instead put new pieces out there and fail the same way. I think Rallis’ schemes are excellent, but he needs the right personnel to get it to work. 2) What are the early returns on HC Mike LaFleur and what do you think of the Cardinals’ coaching staff in general? Hard to tell. Terrible defense. Terrible quarterback situation. Terrible roster construction from the general manager. So, let’s just say it’s unfair to judge him, but his offensive scheme is awful thus far and that is super disappointing. But is it because the roster is awful? Likely. Could his scheme also be awful? Absolutely. 3) What do you think of GM Monti Ossenfort and how he is building the team? He legitimately may be the worst GM in NFL history if they lose out this season. Seriously, think about all the bad GM’s and we are approaching the point where if Ossenfort loses out, his win percentage as GM would be worse than Matt Millen’s. Things have not been going well in Arizona and Ossenfort is a massive reason why. 4) It’s currently unclear if Carson Beck or Josh Johnson will start at QB this week. What have you seen out of each of them and what will the offense look like with them at the helm? Bad? I mean Josh Johnson had been here 12 days so I guess you can make an exception, but Beck was mostly bad, then has been dealing with a recurring back injury. It makes the entire situation for the Cardinals and their fans even harder to understand and stomach because you can’t even get to enjoy watching Beck play because his back is so bad. So instead, we get 40-year old Josh Johnson and I guess we will see if newly brought back Kedon Slovis will be the young player we get to watch and hope turns into something. This place sucks. 5) How should Washington gameplan for this matchup on both sides of the ball? Show up? Seriously, Teryl Austin will be calling the defense for the first time, but the talent is what it is. So, when you look at what the Cardinals defense has done well, it wasn’t terrible in pass coverage, but mainly that’s because it is so awful at stopping the run that other teams don’t throw the ball much. When you actually want to throw the ball, you’ll see no pass rush, and that “good enough” coverage is really tough to maintain when you are covering for more than 3.5 seconds. On offense, nothing. They don’t run the ball well, they don’t throw the ball well. It’s genuinely miserable to watch. Outside of a miraculous quarter and some time against Dallas, the Arizona Cardinals have five touchdowns scored since the Detroit Lions loss. Five touchdowns in six games and three quarters. Three touchdowns in one quarter against the Cowboys (I know you guys will enjoy that nugget). This offense stinks. Anyways, Commanders win and cover unless Austin is somehow a wizard. Commanders 31 Cardinals 10 Good luck and good health in this one to you all. There will be no companion article to this one, as Seth is enjoying Thanksgiving and probably scouting new GM candidates, so it was generous of him to answer our questions here. Thanks again to Seth Cox for taking time out of his day to answer our questions about the Cardinals.

title: Commanders fans see Vikings as toughest remaining game – survey results
summary: Climbing out of an early hole Not so long ago, for many Commanders fans, the 2026 season felt like it might slip away before Halloween. Washington stumbled out of the gate to a 1-3 start, absorbing frustrating losses to the Eagles, Cowboys, and Colts while fans questioned whether the players and coaching staff could stabilize […]
full_text: MEXICO CITY, MEXICO - NOVEMBER 22: Kirk Cousins #8 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up prior to the game against the San Francisco 49ers at Estadio Banorte on November 22, 2026 in Mexico City, Mexico. (Photo by Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Climbing out of an early hole Not so long ago, for many Commanders fans, the 2026 season felt like it might slip away before Halloween. Washington stumbled out of the gate to a 1-3 start, absorbing frustrating losses to the Eagles, Cowboys, and Colts while fans questioned whether the players and coaching staff could stabilize the ship. Fast forward to the end of November, and the view from Northwest Stadium looks markedly different. Over the past four games, the Commanders have gone 3-1, taking down two division leaders in the New York Giants (24-21) and Cincinnati Bengals (22-20), getting a useful divisional win against the Eagles, and losing only to a tough opponent in a tight 20-13 loss to the 7-4 Los Angeles Rams. Currently standing at 4-5-1, Washington is far from a finished product, and nobody is booking Super Bowl flights just yet. Still, the trajectory has shifted, and the schedule ahead opens up considerably compared to the front-loaded gauntlet the burgundy & gold has had to take on and survive. This week’s Reacts survey: Confidence roars back In our Week 12 Hogs Haven Reacts survey, we opened with our standard barometer question: Are you confident about the direction of the team? The numbers reflect a dramatic mood swing across the community: 80% voted “Yes,” while just 20% voted “No.” That 34-point leap from last week’s 46% mark represents the highest confidence rating since Week 2 (83%) and a sharp reversal from the 14% nadir recorded two weeks ago. Reading through the comments section of the survey article and Feed post surveys, the drivers behind that optimism are clear. First-year defensive coordinator Daronte Jones earned widespread praise for orchestrating Monday night’s shutdown of Joe Burrow and Cincinnati. Despite missing key front-seven pieces like Javon Kinlaw and Daron Payne (both on injured reserve and out for the balance of the regular season), Washington held the Bengals to 31 rushing yards on 14 carries and limited Ja’Marr Chase to 31 receiving yards. Commenters like MikeDHTTC and WashNDUNC pointed directly to Jones’ two-high safety looks and late-game pressure — culminating in Nick Cross’s third-down sack on Cincinnati’s final drive — as evidence that the defense has, at last, found its identity. On offense, fans have rallied around Jayden Daniels’ late-game poise and the emergence of young playmakers. Daniels engineered a 64-yard drive in 34 seconds, without timeouts, to set up rookie kicker Drew Stevens’ walk-off field goal on Monday night, leaning on rookie receiver Antonio Williams (nine catches, 122 yards) and tight end Chig Okonkwo (66 yards) in the latter portions of the game. As Rook6980 noted, seeing a young core — including Williams, Sonny Styles, Trey Amos, and Josh Conerly Jr. — produce alongside Daniels gives the fanbase tangible proof of a sustainable foundation. Even among the 20% who voted “No”, the skepticism wasn’t rooted in despair; rather, they want to see offensive coordinator David Blough string together cleaner first halves against inferior opponents before fully buying in to the idea that the team is on-track. Which remaining opponent poses the toughest test? Our second question asked readers which of Washington’s remaining opponents will be the toughest to beat. The results broke down heavily toward one NFC North contender: Visit our partners at FanDuel The Vikings loom large In reviewing the comments, I found the logic behind the 56% vote for Minnesota was virtually unanimous: Brian Flores’ defense. Readers like evarigan , OMG-WTF , and Redskins75 cited the Vikings’ league-best scoring defense (allowing just 16.1 points per game) and aggressive blitz packages as a nightmare matchup on the road at U.S. Bank Stadium in Week 16. Respondents also pointed out the intriguing chess match between Flores and his former pupil, Daronte Jones, alongside the storyline of facing former Washington quarterback Kirk Cousins. Are the Jaguars being overlooked? Because the Jaguars play in the AFC South, many NFC-focused fans may simply be less familiar with Liam Coen’s squad — and may have been swayed by Jacksonville’s surprising 23-18 loss to the Giants last week. When you stack Minnesota’s full body of work against that of the Jacksonville Jaguars, an interesting pattern emerges. Statistically, the 7-3 Jaguars could actually be the more complete team: While Minnesota has been “winning ugly” behind an elite defense and a 28th-ranked scoring offense, Jacksonville boasts a top-six scoring attack to go with a top-three scoring defense. Commenters evarigan and Alex Rowsey nailed that distinction, noting that traveling to Jacksonville in Week 17 to take on that balanced AFC juggernaut could ultimately prove even more daunting than the trip to Minneapolis. A note about the Simple Rating System: You may not be aware of the SRS, so I thought I’d include an explanatory note here about what it is and where it comes from: Simple Rating System (SRS) is a statistical metric created and maintained by Pro-Football-Reference (Sports Reference) that evaluates a team’s overall quality using only two inputs: point differential and strength of schedule. An SRS rating of 0.0 represents a league-average team. A team’s score tells you how many points better or worse than an average team they are on a neutral field. For example, an SRS of +9.89 means a team is roughly 10 points better than an average NFL squad, whereas a +4.31 rating puts a team about four points above average. How it works The formula is straightforward: SRS = Average Margin of Victory + Strength of Schedule Because strength of schedule depends on the quality of opponents—whose own ratings depend on their opponents—Pro-Football-Reference solves a system of linear equations across all 32 teams simultaneously so that every team’s rating accounts for the exact point differentials of every opponent they have played. For an explanation of EPA per play in the NFL, CLICK HERE The NFC East picture after Thanksgiving The Cowboys in Week 18 Interestingly, 13% of voters pegged the Dallas Cowboys as the toughest hurdle left on the slate, with WashingtonFMJ_Bulletskins and IronMike66 predicting the Week 18 finale will decide the division. Notably, our survey closed before Thursday’s Thanksgiving action, when Dallas blew a 21-point lead and fell 39-38 to the Eagles on a late Jake Elliott field goal. I’m not sure whether that outcome might have changed a few votes in the survey. That Dallas stumble leaves the NFC East standings tightly bunched heading into Sunday: Because Washington’s record includes a tie, and the Commanders have played one fewer game than Dallas, a victory in Arizona on Sunday pulls the Commanders even with the Cowboys at five wins and keeps Washington ahead of Dallas in the division race. Over the final seven games, the math is straightforward: Washington needs to outpace Dallas by at least one win and make up two wins on the Giants in order to finish with at least the same number of wins as both divisional rivals, claiming the NFC East crown. What’s right in front of us: Commanders at Cardinals Before worrying about Minnesota, Jacksonville, or Dallas, Washington has to handle business in the desert against the 3-8 Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. Under head coach Mike LaFleur, Arizona has struggled on both sides of the ball, ranking 29th in scoring offense (17.4 points per game) and 31st in scoring defense (29.4 points per game) while dropping three straight. Even so, tight end Trey McBride (63 receiving yards per game) remains a focal point that will test Washington’s linebackers and safeties. The Cardinals have beaten both the Rams and the Cowboys this season, and can’t be taken lightly by the Commanders if…

full_text: Treylon Burks has been bothered with a foot injury for several weeks. The veteran Commanders receiver initially suffered the injury weeks ago and Washington has been trying their best to manage it while keeping him in the lineup. He missed the Rams game but has found a way to play in every other game, and the strategy of limiting his practice work has been effective in getting him ready for game day. It’s clearly limiting his production, but his presence is key to keeping this offense moving. Cornerback Amik Robertson missed a second straight day with an ankle injury that kept him out of the Bengals game. If he can’t go on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, we’ll see a combination of Rasul Douglas/Trey Amos on the outside and Mike Sainristil and possibly Quan Martin and Fabian Moreau on the inside. Defensive lineman Charles Omenihu (rib) was limited for a second straight day. Everyone else on the active roster was a full-go. title: Washington Commanders officially sign Brandon Aiyuk to practice squad
summary: UPDATE: The Commanders have officially announced the signing of receiver Brandon Aiyuk to their practice squad. They also added cornerback Ambry Thomas to the practice squad, and released receiver Malik Heath from the practice squad in a corresponding move. It’s clear that Aiyuk will need some time to get used to the Commanders’ offensive system […]
full_text: UPDATE: The Commanders have officially announced the signing of receiver Brandon Aiyuk to their practice squad. They also added cornerback Ambry Thomas to the practice squad, and released receiver Malik Heath from the practice squad in a corresponding move. It’s clear that Aiyuk will need some time to get used to the Commanders’ offensive system and to get into NFL game shape, and he’ll also need to help run the Washington scout team. His activation will come in time and then he will try to help the Commanders down the stretch in their attempt to win the NFC East. We have made the following roster moves: – Signed WR Brandon Aiyuk and CB Ambry Thomas to the practice squad – Released WR Malik Heath from the practice squad — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 26, 2026 The Commanders have signed receiver Brandon Aiyuk to their practice squad, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday. The free agent, who was released by the San Francisco 49ers and formally cleared waivers, met with the Commanders at the team’s complex on Wednesday . Per Schefter, Aiyuk signed contract to join the team’s practice squad. Free-agent WR Brandon Aiyuk is signing with the Washington Commanders practice squad, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus. Aiyuk once again becomes teammates with his Commanders QB Jayden Daniels. pic.twitter.com/jt8diY95o3 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 25, 2026 This move was telegraphed somewhat, with the Tuesday release of running back Craig Reynolds to open up a spot. Aiyuk will have an opportunity to work himself back into game shape after more than two years on the shelf. The Commanders can elevate him when ready, or they can sign him to the active roster at a time of their choosing. He can be elevated three times before Washington has to formally activate him. Washington has been Aiyuk’s preferred destination, a point that was clear when he started wearing Commanders gear in social media posts over the summer. Some quick background: The 49ers drafted Aiyuk in the first round back in 2020 and then inked him to a four-year, $120-million contract in 2024. Then things got messy. Aiyuk suffered a serious knee injury during the 2024 campaign and didn’t play after that. The 49ers took issue with Aiyuk’s choice to rehab away from their facility, and it created a schism and a rift that was never repaired. The 49ers voided Aiyuk’s guarantees and placed him on the exempt/did not report list. Then Aiyuk went on a social media tirade, torching 49ers GM John Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan. He also took some shots at Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels – Aiyuk and Daniels were good friends and teammates at Arizona State – and his mother. They have reportedly mended fences, which set the stage for this signing. Commanders GM Adam Peters was also involved in the Aiyuk draft pick when he was in San Francisco. Aiyuk had 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns in 2023, shockingly his last full season in the NFL. There’s no doubting Aiyuk’s talent, though it has been some time since that has led to production. How long it takes for Aiyuk to get ready is to be determined, but Washington needs him to get prepared fast to keep this good thing going. It’s hard to imagine he’ll be ready for Sunday’s road game against the Arizona Cardinals, especially with his need to catch up learning the Commanders system. And there’s great shape and football shape, which are two totally different things. Let us know your thoughts about this Brandon Aiyuk signing in the article comments below:

Commanders links Feeling thankful 🤍 pic.twitter.com/uw1Fcist1j — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 26, 2026 Articles The Athletic (paywall) Commanders to sign Brandon Aiyuk to practice squad: ‘You can never have enough good players’ The timing of the agreement — two days after the 49ers waived him and 12 weeks into the season — leaves Aiyuk, 28, and the Commanders little time to see if and how much he can contribute before this season’s end. If Aiyuk is anything close to the player he was in 2023, when he earned second-team All-Pro honors and, in Peters’ words, “was a true No. 1 receiver,” Washington will have added a first-round talent at a bargain rate. If Aiyuk appears to have lost a step after two-plus years out of the game or otherwise does not work out, Washington can easily cut ties at minimal cost; he’s not taking a spot on the active roster and he’ll be paid a minimal weekly salary. If the Commanders elevate him for as many as three games, the limit for a practice-squad player, his total salary for the rest of the season would max out at roughly $306,000, a bargain rate for a player viewed as a No. 1 receiver and a far cry from what he was slated to earn in the remainder of his deal with the 49ers. Any further elevations would require that they sign him to the active roster. Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told reporters earlier this month that the veteran receiver is fully healthy after suffering a multi-ligament knee injury in 2024. But Aiyuk hasn’t played a snap, in a game or practice, since Oct. 20, 2024 — 766 days to be exact. Aiyuk will likely need a significant ramp-up period to get back into football conditioning and get acclimated to the Commanders’ offense, and as a practice-squad player, he’ll be afforded fewer practice reps than the receivers on the active roster. With Brandon Aiyuk expected to sign with Washington tomorrow, I asked GM Adam Peters about the move, why he was willing to look past the noise on social media, and whether this sets a precedent for the organization moving forward. pic.twitter.com/trpuRbMLM6 — Marshall Kramsky (@marshallkramsky) November 26, 2026 Considering Brandon Aiyuk’s availability was an open secret for months, I asked Adam Peters how long he's imagined signing the WR. (The "local" part means he really did buy a house!) pic.twitter.com/YpcM9SIw8R — Ben Standig (@BenStandig) November 25, 2026 To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) What WR Brandon Aiyuk brings to the Washington Commanders What I can offer you that others can’t is a look at what kind of receiver he was when he was last on the field prior to getting hurt. It’s very hard to say what he is now because we’ve just nott seen him on a football field in two years, but we can look at what he was before the injury as a glipse of what his ceiling might be. So what was Aiyuk before the injury? In no uncertain terms, Aiyuk was an elite receiver in 2023, racking up 1342 yards and seven touchdowns on 75 catches, with the second highest average yards per catch in the league that year with 17.9. What made him so good in 2023? The list is long but lets cover the basics. His biggest strength is his route running. Aiyuk, at least in 2023, was one of the top route runners in the league, giving him the ability to separate against even the best corners in the league. The Commanders are finally signing WR Brandon Aiyuk. It's uncertain what kind of player he is now, but I went back and watched his tape in both 2023 and 2024 to see what the upside is to this move. Full breakdown: https://t.co/TVqQYsOMYa pic.twitter.com/4uga6BwSu2 — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) November 25, 2026 Aiyuk understands that he can’t always run every single route the same way, so he has different methods of running routes that he can go to in order to keep things fresh, but he’s also capable of making different routes look very similar, which is the real sign of an elite route runner. full_text:
The NFL on Thanksgiving is a classic tradition, and the uniforms are as much a part of the games as a celebratory turkey leg. But, this year a game was played on Thanksgiving Eve for the first time. And it's only right that the matchup included the debut of a uniform, too. 

 

 The Los Angeles Rams  wore their "Fearsome White" threads against the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday. The all-white look is inspired by the Rams' "Fearsome Foursome" defensive line from the 1960s and early 1970s. A modern "Rams Royal" lid includes white horns, white facemask, new 3D bumper logos and "Rams" on the front. Royal blue stripes run over the shoulder to mirror the curve of the helmet horn, alongside accenting sleeve numbers.

 The fifth annual John Madden celebration was held on Thanksgiving, and a patch featuring a silhouette of Madden was included on the jersey of each player at all of the Wednesday and Thursday games.

 

 A Thanksgiving tripleheader meant throwback threads, led by the Dallas Cowboys who rocked their 1960s-era uniforms against the Philadelphia Eagles . Dallas brought this combination back in 2022 following a nine-year hiatus. The navy and white look includes a clean lid with a navy star on the side and a stripe down the middle. 

 On Black Friday, the Pittsburgh Steelers  dressed for the occasion with their color rush threads against the Denver Broncos . The all-black look includes gold numbers and stripes on the sleeves, with a similarly colored stripe down the pants. Pittsburgh owns a 9-3 record in the uniform.

title: NFL Week 12 arrivals: Cameron Heyward leads arrivals ahead of Steelers-Broncos
summary: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
full_text:
The Thanksgiving menu includes an extra helping of NFL style, with Week 12 arrivals getting started before the turkey hits the table.

 
 The Green Bay Packers visited the Los Angeles Rams on a warm Wednesday in Inglewood, California.

 Thursday brings the Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions together in Detroit, and morning temperatures in the 40s could lead to giving statement coats their moment. The Philadelphia Eagles visit the Dallas Cowboys in Arlington, Texas, where a sunny afternoon in the 50s calls for sweater weather.

 The Kansas City Chiefs face the Buffalo Bills on Thursday night in Orchard Park, New York, to close out the tripleheader with temperatures in the 30s and rain in the forecast. Friday's meeting between the Denver Broncos and Pittsburgh Steelers in Pittsburgh brings another opportunity for layers, with temperatures around the low 40s and possible showers.

 Sunday offers a little of everything: jacket weather around the Great Lakes, warmer conditions in South Florida and potential rain in the Bay Area. Whether players are bundling up or keeping things breezy, there's plenty of room to serve a look.

 Here are the standout arrivals from Week 12.

 

 Black Friday fashion 
 The Steelers and Broncos brought a variety of fits to the tunnels of Acrisure Stadium for their Friday afternoon showdown, with the highlight likely being  Cameron Heyward breaking out a sleek -- but still cozy -- turtleneck and chain look.

 

 

 Thanksgiving threads 
 
 Chris Jones brought the style to Buffalo through the inclement weather and all. The Kansas City Chiefs defensive tackle wore a cream double-breasted suit with a black turtleneck. 
 
 
 
 CeeDee Lamb donned a long black double-breasted overcoat, charcoal trousers and chunky lace-up boots. The Dallas Cowboys wide receiver accessorized with a leather tote and silver jewelry. Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons embraced fall fashion in a camel-colored coat with plush shearling-style lapels, layered over a plum plaid suit and matching turtleneck. 
 
 Wednesday's looks 
 Aaron Donald kept it sleek in a black zip-up jacket and matching pants, accessorizing with gold-tinted shades and a checkered designer pouch. His blue, white and yellow sneakers added a pop of Rams colors to the look.

title: 2027 NFL draft order projections for Round 1, chances for top pick, more
summary: ESPN's Football Power Index projects the 2027 NFL draft order for Round 1, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.
full_text:
The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

 What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

 So where do things stand? Here are the full sortable projections, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.

 What we're hearing on the Steelers:  The Steelers are reeling from the events of the week and rolling to Friday's game with Mason Rudolph as their new signal caller and leader. He helped the team go 3-0 in the final three games of 2023 when he was given the starting job over Mitch Trubisky and Kenny Pickett . "We have a job to do as players and as men and we're going to love each other," Rudolph said Wednesday. We're going to support our coach, and it's pointless for me to try to play mediator or decipher between what was said. Really it's important to block the noise out and go play a football game, and as cliche as it sounds, support the black and gold."  -- Brooke Pryor

 Bold prediction: Broncos RB  Jonah Coleman  will record at least five receptions, which would be a career high. RBs catch passes at a higher rate against zone coverage, and the Steelers run more zone than anyone.
